Job 42:15 In all the lande were none found so fayre, as the doughters of Iob, & theyr father gaue them enherytaunce amonge theyr brethren.
Job 42:16 After this lyued Iob .xl. yares, so that he sawe his children, & his children children to the fourthe generacyon.
Job 42:17 And so he dyed, beynge olde & of a perfecte age.

BOOK: Psalms

CHAPTER: 1

Psalms 1:1 O blessed is the man, that goeth not in the counsayll of the vngodly: that abydeth not in the waie of sinners and sitteth not in the seate of the scorneful.
Psalms 1:2 But deliteth in the lawe of the Lord, and exercyseth hym self in hys lawe, bothe daye and nyght.
Psalms 1:3 Suche a man is lyke a tree planted by the watersyde, that bringeth forthe hys frute in due season. His leaues shall not fall af, & loke whatsoeuer he doth, it shall prospere.
Psalms 1:4 As for the vngodly, it is not so with them but they are lyke the dust, wych the wynde scatered awaye from the grounde.
Psalms 1:5 Thefore the vngodly shall not be able to stande in the iudgement, nether the synners in the congregacyon of the ryghtuous.
Psalms 1:6 For the Lorde aloweth the waye of the righteous, but the waye of the vngodly shal peryshe.

CHAPTER: 2

Psalms 2:1 VVhy do the Heathen grudge? why do the people ymagyne vayne thinges?
Psalms 2:2 The kynges of the earth stande vp, and the rulers are come to gether, agaynste the Lorde and agaynste hys anoynted.
Psalms 2:3 Let vs breake their hondes a sunder, and cast away their yock from vs.
Psalms 2:4 Neuerthelesse he that dwelleth in heauen, shall laughe them to scorne: yea euen the Lorde hym selfe shall haue them in derysyon.
Psalms 2:5 Then shal he speake vnto them in hys wrath, and vexe them in hys sore displeasure.
Psalms 2:6 Yet haue I sette my kyng vpon my holy hyll of syon.
Psalms 2:7 As for me, I wyll preache the law, wherof the Lord hath sayde vnto me: Thou arte my sonne, this day haue I begotten the.
Psalms 2:8 Desyre of me, and I shall geue the Heathen for thyne enherytaunce. Yea the vttermost partes of the worlde for thy possessyon.
Psalms 2:9 Thou shalt rule them wyth a rodde of yron, and breake them in peces lyke an earthen vessell.
Psalms 2:10 Be wyse nowe therfore, O ye Kinges, be warned, ye that are iudges of the earthe.
Psalms 2:11 Serue the Lorde wyth feare, and reioyse before hym wyth reuerence.
Psalms 2:12 Kysse the sonne, lest the Lorde be angrye and so ye peryshe from the ryght way. For his wrath shalbe kindled shortly: blessed are all they that put their trust in hym.

CHAPTER: 3

Psalms 3:1 A Psalme of Dauid when he fledde from the face of Absalom. Why are they so many, O Lord that trouble me? a great multytude are they that ryse agaynst me.
Psalms 3:2 Yea many one ther be that say of my soule: there is no helpe for hym in God Selah.
Psalms 3:3 But thou, O Lord, arte my defender, my worshippe, and the lifter vp of my head.
Psalms 3:4 I call vpon the Lord wyth my voyce, and he heareth me out of hys holy hyll. Selah.
Psalms 3:5 I layed me downe and slepte, but I rose vp agayne, for the Lorde sustayned me.
Psalms 3:6 I am not afrayed for thousandes of the people, that compasse me rounde aboute.
Psalms 3:7 Vp Lorde, and helpe me O my God for thou smitest al mine enemyes vpon the cheke bones and breakest the teeth of the vngodly.
Psalms 3:8 Helpe belongeth vnto the Lorde, therfore let thy blessynge be vpon thy people.

CHAPTER: 4

Psalms 4:1 To the Chanter in Neginoth, a Psalme of Dauid. Heare me when I call, O God of my ryghteousnes: thou that comfortest me in my trouble: haue mercy vpon me, herken vnto my praier.
Psalms 4:2 O ye sonnes of men, howe longe wyll ye blaspheme myne honour? why haue ye suche pleasure in vanytye, and seke after lyes? Selah.
Psalms 4:3 Knowe thys, that the Lorde dealeth maruelously wyth hys saynt: and when I cal vpon the Lorde, he heareth me.
Psalms 4:4 Be angrye, but synne not: comen wyth youre owne hertes vpon youre beddes, and remember youre selues. Selah.
Psalms 4:5 Offer thy sacrifyce of ryghtuousnes, and put your trust in the Lord.
Psalms 4:6 There be many that saye: who wyll do vs any good? Lord lift vp vpon vs the lyghte of thy countenaunce.
Psalms 4:7 Thou reioyseste myne herte, thoughe their encrease be great both in corne & wyne.
Psalms 4:8 Therfore wyll I laye me downe in peace, and take my rest: for thou Lorde only settest me in a sure dwellynge.

CHAPTER: 5

Psalms 5:1 To the Chaunter by Nehiloh, a Psalme of Dauid. Heare my wordes (O Lorde) consyder my callynge.
Psalms 5:2 O marke the voice of my petition my Kynge and my God, for vnto the wyl I make my prayer.
Psalms 5:3 Heare my voyce by tymes (O Lorde) for early in the mornyng wyll I get me vnto the, yea and that with diligence.
Psalms 5:4 For thou art not the God that hath pleasure in wickednesse, ther may no vngodly person dwel with the.
Psalms 5:5 Suche as be cruell maye not stande in thy syght, thou art an enemye vnto all wycked doers.
Psalms 5:6 Thou destroiest the lyers: the Lord abhorreth the bloude thursty and disceatful.
Psalms 5:7 But as for me, I wyl come into thy house euen vpon the multytude of thy mercy: and in thy feare wyll I worshippe towarde thy holy temple.
Psalms 5:8 Lede me (O Lord) in thy ryghtuousnesse; because of myne enemyes, & make thy waye playne before me.
Psalms 5:9 For there is no faithfulnesse in their mouthes: they dessemble in their hertes: their throt is an open sepulcher: with their tonges thy disceaue.
Psalms 5:10 Punysh them (O God) that they may perysh in their owne ymaginacions: cast them out because of the multytude of their vngodlynesse, for they rebell agaynste the.
Psalms 5:11 Agayne, let all them that put their truste in the, reioyse: yea let them euer be geuynge of thankes, because thou defendest: them: that they whyche loue thy name, be ioyfull in the.
Psalms 5:12 For thou Lord geuest thy blessynge vnto the ryghtuous: and with thy fauorable kindnes thou defendest him, as wyth a shylde.

CHAPTER: 6

Psalms 6:1 To the chaunter by Negynoth vpon Sheminith, a Psalme of Dauid. Oh Lorde rebuke me not in thyne anger: Oh chasten me not in thy heuy dyspleasure.
Psalms 6:2 Haue mercye vpon me (O Lorde) for I am weake: O Lorde heale me for all my bones are vexed.
Psalms 6:3 My soule also is in great trouble, but lord how longe?
Psalms 6:4 Turne the (O Lord) and deliuer my soule Oh saue me for thy mercyes sake.
Psalms 6:5 For in death no man remembreth the: Oh who wyll geue the thankes in the hell?
Psalms 6:6 I am wery of gronyng euery nyght wash I my bedde, and water my couche wyth my teares.
Psalms 6:7 My countenance is chaunged for verye inwarde grefe. I consume awaye I haue so many enemyes.
Psalms 6:8 Awaye fro me all ye wicked dors, for the Lorde hath hearde the voyce of my wepyng
Psalms 6:9 The Lord hath hearde myne humble petycyon, the Lorde hath receaued my prayer.
Psalms 6:10 All myne enemies shalbe confunded and sore vexed: yea they shalbe turned backe and put to shame, and that ryght soone.

CHAPTER: 7

Psalms 7:1 Sigaion of Dauid, whych he sang for the wordes of Cus the sonne of Iemini. O Lord my god, in the do I trust: saue me from al them that persecute me, and delyuer me.
Psalms 7:2 Lest he deuoureth vp my soule lyke a lion and teare it in peces whyle ther is none to helpe,
Psalms 7:3 O Lorde my God, if I haue done anye suche thyng, if there be any vnrightuousnes in my handes:
Psalms 7:4 If I haue rewarded euyl vnto them that dealt frendly wyth me, or hurt them that wyth out any cause are myne enemies.
Psalms 7:5 Then let myne enemye persecute my soule, and take mo: ye let hym treade my life downe in the earth, and laye myne honour in the dust. Selah.
Psalms 7:6 Stande vp (O Lorde) in thy wrath, lyft vp thy selfe ouer the furyous indygnacyon of myne enemyes: aryse vp (for me) in the vengeaunce that thou hast promysed.
Psalms 7:7 That the congregacion of the people maye come about the, for their sakes therfore lyfte vp thy selfe agayne.
Psalms 7:8 The Lord is iudge ouer the people: auenge me then (O Lord) accordynge to my ryghtuousnes and innocency.
Psalms 7:9 Oh let the wickednes of the vngodly come to an ende: but maynteyne the iust, thou rightuous God, that triest the very hertes and the reynes.
Psalms 7:10 My helpe commeth of God, which preserueth them that are true of herte.
Psalms 7:11 God is a ryghtuous iudge, and God is euer threatnynge,
Psalms 7:12 If men wyll not turne, he hath whette his swearde: he hath bent his bowe and made it ready.
Psalms 7:13 He hath prepared hym the weapens of death, & ordeined his arrowes to be destroied.
Psalms 7:14 Beholde, he trauyleth wyth mischefe, he hath conceaued vnhappinesse, and broughte forth a lye.
Psalms 7:15 He hath grauen & digged vp a pyt, but he shall fall hym selfe into the pitte that he hath made.
Psalms 7:16 For hys vnhappinesse shall come vpon hys owne head, and hys wyckednes shal fal vpon hys owne pate.
Psalms 7:17 As for me, I wyll geue thankes vnto the Lorde for hys ryghtuousnes sake, and wyll prayse the name of the Lorde the most hyest.

CHAPTER: 8

Psalms 8:1 To the chaunter vpon Githith, a Psalme of Dauid. O Lord our gouernour: how wonderfull is thy name in all the worlde? howe excellente is thy glory aboue the heauens?
Psalms 8:2 Out of the mouth of the very babes and sucklynges thou haste ordeyned prayse, because of thyne enemyes, that thou mightest destroye the enemye & the auenger.
Psalms 8:3 For I considre thy heauens, euen the worke of thy fingers: the moone & the starres which thou hast made.
Psalms 8:4 Oh what is man, that thou art so myndfull of hym? either the sonne of man that thou visitest hym?
Psalms 8:5 After thou haddest for a season made him lower then the aungels, thou crounedest him with honour and glory.
Psalms 8:6 Thou haste set him aboue the workes of thy handes: and thou hast put all thynges in subiection vnder his fete.
Psalms 8:7 All shepe and oxen, yea, and the beastes of the felde.
Psalms 8:8 The foules of the ayre, the fish of the sea, and whatsoeuer walketh thorow the wayes of the sea.
Psalms 8:9 O Lorde our gouernoure, how wonderfull is thy name in all the worlde?

CHAPTER: 9

Psalms 9:1 To the chaunter vpon Almuth Laben, a Psalme of Dauid. I wyll geue thankes vnto the (O Lord) with my whole hert I will speake of all thy meruelous workes.
Psalms 9:2 I will be glad, and reioyse in the, yea, my songes wil I make of thy name O thou moost hyest.
Psalms 9:3 Because thou hast dryuen myne enemyes abacke, they were disconfited, and perished at thy presence.
Psalms 9:4 For thou hast maynteyned my right and my cause: thou sittest in the throne that arte the true iudge.
Psalms 9:5 Thou rebukest the Heythen, & destroyest the vngodly, thou puttest out their name for euer and euer.
Psalms 9:6 The enemyes sweardes are come too an ende, thou haste ouerthrowen their cytyes, their memorial is perished with them.
Psalms 9:7 But the Lorde endureth for euer, he hath prepared his seate vnto iudgement.
Psalms 9:8 He gouerneth the worlde with righteousnes, and ministreth true iudgement vnto the people.
Psalms 9:9 The Lorde is a defence for the poore, a defence in the tyme of trouble.
Psalms 9:10 Therfore they that know thy name, putte their trust in the: for thou (Lorde) neuer faylest them that seke the.
Psalms 9:11 O prayse the Lorde, whiche dwelleth in Syon, shewe the people of hys doynges.
Psalms 9:12 And why? he maketh inquisicion for their bloude, and remembreth theym: he forgetteth not th complaynte of the poore.
Psalms 9:13 Haue mercy vpon me (O Lord) considre the trouble that I am in amonge myne enemyes, thou that liftest me vp from the gates of death.
Psalms 9:14 That I maye shewe all thy prayses within the portes of the daughter of Sion, and reioyse in thy sauynge health.
Psalms 9:15 As for the Heathen, thei are suncken doune in the pytte that they made: in the same nette which they spred out priuely, is their owne feete taken.
Psalms 9:16 Thus the Lord is knowen to execute true iudgemente, when the vngodly is trapped in the woorkes of hys owne handes. Selah.
Psalms 9:17 The wicked must be turned vnto hell, & all the Heythen that forget God.
Psalms 9:18 But the poore shall not all waye be oute of remembraunce, the pacyent abydynge of suche as be in trouble shall not peryshe for euer.
Psalms 9:19 Vp Lorde, let no man haue the vpperhand let the Heythen be condemned before the.
Psalms 9:20 O Lorde set a scholemaster ouer them, that the Heathen maye knowe theim selfes to be but men. Selah.

CHAPTER: 10

Psalms 10:1 Why arte thou gone so far of, O Lord? wylt thou hyde thy selfe in tyme of trouble?
Psalms 10:2 While the vngodlye hath the ouer hand, the pore must suffer persecutyon. O that they were taken in the ymagynacion which they go aboute.
Psalms 10:3 For the vngodly maketh bost of his owne hertes desyre, the couetous blesseth him selfe and blasphemeth the Lorde.
Psalms 10:4 The vngodlye is so proude and full of indignacyon, that he careth not mether is God before hys eyes.
Psalms 10:5 Hys wayes are al waye filthye, thy iudgementes are farre out of his sight, he defyeth all his enemyes.
Psalms 10:6 For he sayth in hys herte: Tushe, I shall neuer be cast downe, ther shal no harme happen vnto me.
Psalms 10:7 His mouth is ful of cursyng, fraude & disceate vnder hys tonge is trauayle and sorowe.
Psalms 10:8 He sytteth lurckynge in the gardens, that he may pryuely murther the innocente, hys eyes are set vpon the poore.
Psalms 10:9 He lyeth waytynge secretlye, as ti were a lyon in hys denne. He lurketh that he maye rauyshe the pore, yea, to rauysh the poore, when he hath gotten him into hys net.
Psalms 10:10 Then smyteth he, then oppresseth he and casteth downe the pore with his authoritye.
Psalms 10:11 For he sayeth in hys herte: Tushe, God hath forgotten, he hath turned awaye hys face, so that he wyll neuer se it.
Psalms 10:12 Aryse Lorde God, lyfte vp thyne hande and forget not the poore.
Psalms 10:13 Wherfore should the wycked blaspheme God and saye in his herte: tush, he careth not for it:
Psalms 10:14 Thys thou seyst, for thou consyderest the mysery and sorowe. The poore geueth him selfe ouer into thy hande, and committeth hym vnto the, for thou art the helper of the frendlesse.
Psalms 10:15 Breake thou the arme of the vngodly and malycyous, search out the wickednes which he hath done, that he maye perysh.
Psalms 10:16 The Lord is kynge for euer, the Heithen shal perish out of his land.
Psalms 10:17 Lord, thou hearest the desyrous longing of the poore: theyr hert is sure, that thine eare herkeneth therto.
Psalms 10:18 Helpe the fatherlesse and poore vnto their ryght, that the vngodlye be no more exalted vpon earh.

CHAPTER: 11

Psalms 11:1 To the chaunter, of Dauid. In the Lord put I my trust: how will ye then saye too my soule: that she shoulde fle as a byrde vpon your hyll?
Psalms 11:2 For lo, the vngodly haue bent their bowe, and made ready their arrowes in the quyuer, that they maye priuely shute at them, which are true of hert.
Psalms 11:3 The verye foundacion haue they caste doune, what can the righteous then do with all?
Psalms 11:4 But the Lorde is in hys holy temple, the Lordes seate is in heauen: He considereth it with hys eyes, hys eye lyddes beholde the chyldren of men.
Psalms 11:5 The Lorde seith bothe the righteous and vngodly, but who so delyteth in wickednes, hym hys soule abhorreth.
Psalms 11:6 Vpon the vngodly he shall rayne snares, fyre, brymstone, storme and tempest: thys rewarde shall they haue to drynke.
Psalms 11:7 For the Lord is righteous, and he loueth righteousnes: hys countenaunce beholdeth the thinge that is iust.

CHAPTER: 12

Psalms 12:1 To the chaunter vpon Sheminith, a Psalme of Dauid. Helpe Lord, for there is not one saincte more: very fewe faythfull are there amonge the chyldren of men.
Psalms 12:2 Euery man telleth lyes too his neyghbour, they do but flatter with their lyppes and dissemble in their herte.
Psalms 12:3 O that the Lorde wolde rote out all disceatfull lyppes, and the tonge that speaketh proude thynges.
Psalms 12:4 Which saye: oure tonge shoulde preuayle we are they that oughte too speake, who is Lord ouer vs?
Psalms 12:5 Now for the troubles sake of the oppressed, and because of the complainte of the poore I will vp (sayeth the Lord) I wil helpe them, & set them at rest.
Psalms 12:6 The wordes of the Lord are pure wordes euen as the siluer, which from earth is tryed and purified .vij. tymes in the fyre.
Psalms 12:7 Kepe them therfore (O Lorde) and preserue vs from this generacion for euer.
Psalms 12:8 And why? when vanite & ydelnes getteth the ouerhande among the chyldren of men, all are full of the vngodly.

CHAPTER: 13

Psalms 13:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. How longe wilt thou forget me O Lorde? for euer? howe longe wilt thou hyde thy face fro me?
Psalms 13:2 Oh how long shal I seke counsayl in my soule? how longe shall I be so vexed in myne hert? howe longe shall myne enemye triumphe ouer me?
Psalms 13:3 Considre, & heare me, O Lorde my God: lighten myne eyes, that I sleape not in death.
Psalms 13:4 Lest myne enemye saye: I haue preuayled agaynst hym: for if I be cast doune, they that troble me will reioyse at it.
Psalms 13:5 But my trust is in thy mercy, & my herte is ioyfull in thy sauynge health.
Psalms 13:6 I will singe of the Lorde, that dealeth so louingly with me. (Yea, I wil prayse the name of the Lorde the moost hyest.)

CHAPTER: 14

Psalms 14:1 To the chaunter, of Dauid. The folyshe bodyes saye in their hertes: tushe, there is no God. They are corrupt, & become abhominable in their doynges, there is not one that doth good.
Psalms 14:2 The Lorde loked doune from heauen vpon the chyldren of men, too se if there were any that wolde vnderstande and seke after God.
Psalms 14:3 But they are all gone out of the waye, they are altogether become vnprofitable: there is none that doeth good, no not one.
Psalms 14:4 How can they haue vnderstandinge, that worke mischiefe, eatynge vp my people, as it were bread, & call not vpon the Lord?
Psalms 14:5 Therfore shall they be brought in greate feare, for God standeth by the generacion of the righteous.
Psalms 14:6 As for you ye haue made a mocke at the counsail of the poore, because he putteth hys trust in the Lorde.
Psalms 14:7 Oh that the sauynge healthe were geuen vnto Israel out of Sion. Oh that the Lord wolde deliuer his people out of captiuitie. Then shoulde Iacob reioyse, & Israell should be right glad.

CHAPTER: 15

Psalms 15:1 A Psalme of Dauid. Lorde, who shal dwel in thy tabernacle? who shall reste vpon thy holy hyl?
Psalms 15:2 Euen he that leadeth an vncorrupt life: that doth the thing which is right, and that speaketh the trueth from hys hert.
Psalms 15:3 He that vseth no disceat in his tongue: he that doth no euell to hys neyghbour, & sclaundreth not hys neyghbours.
Psalms 15:4 He that setteth not by the vngodly, but maketh muche of them that feare the Lorde: he that sweareth vnto his neyghbour, & dispoynteth hym not.
Psalms 15:5 He that geueth not his money vpon vsury, and taketh no rewarde agaynste the innocent. Who so doth these thinges, shall neuer be remoued.

CHAPTER: 16

Psalms 16:1 Michtam of Dauid. Preserue me (O God) for in the do I trust.
Psalms 16:2 I haue saide vnto the Lord: thou art my God, my goodes are nothing vnto the.
Psalms 16:3 All my delytes is vpon the saynctes that are in the earth, and vpon suche lyke.
Psalms 16:4 But they that runne after another, shall haue greate trouble. Their drinckoffringes of bloude will not I offre, neither make mencion of their name in my mouth.
Psalms 16:5 The Lorde him selfe is my good and my porcion, thou mayntaynest myne enherytaunce.
Psalms 16:6 The lot is fallen vnto me in a fayre ground, yea, I haue a goodly heritage.
Psalms 16:7 I will thanke the Lorde for geuynge me warnynge: my reynes also haue chastened me in the night season.
Psalms 16:8 Afore hand sawe I God alwayes before me, for he is on my righte hande, that I should not be moued.
Psalms 16:9 Therfore dyd my hert reioyce, & my tunge was glad, my flesh also shal rest in hope.
Psalms 16:10 For why? thou shalt not leaue my soule in hell, neither shalt thou suffre thy saincte to se corrupcion.
Psalms 16:11 Thou hast shewed me the wayes of lyfe: thou shalte make me full of ioye wyth thy countenaunce. At thy ryght hande there is pleasure and ioye for euermore.

CHAPTER: 17

Psalms 17:1 A prayer of Dauid. Heare the right (O Lord) considre my complaynte: herken vnto my prayer, that goeth not oute of a fayned mouth.
Psalms 17:2 Let my sentence come forth from thy presence: and loke vpon the thinge that is equall.
Psalms 17:3 Thou hast proued & visited myne herte in the night season: thou hast tryed me in the fyre: & hast founde no wickednes in me: for I vtterly purposed that my mouthe shoulde not offende.
Psalms 17:4 Because of the woordes of thy lippes, I haue kepte me from the workes of men, in the waye of the murtherer.
Psalms 17:5 Oh ordre thou my goinges in thy pathes: that my fote steppes slippe not.
Psalms 17:6 For vnto the I crie: heare me O God: encline thine eares to me: & herken vnto my woordes.
Psalms 17:7 Shewe thy maruelous louing kindnesse, thou that sauest them whiche put their trust in the, from suche as resist thy right hande.
Psalms 17:8 Kepe me as the apple of an eye, defende me vnder the shadow of thy wynges.
Psalms 17:9 From the vngodly that trouble me, fro myne enemyes which compasse my soule round about.
Psalms 17:10 Which manteyne their owne welthinesse with oppression, and their mouthe speaketh proude thynges.
Psalms 17:11 They lye wayting in our waye on euery side, turnyng their eyes doune to the ground.
Psalms 17:12 Like as a Lyon that is gredy of his pray, and as it were a Lyons whelpe lurkynge in hys denne.
Psalms 17:13 Vp Lord, disapoynte hym and cast him doune: deliuer my soule with thy swerde from the vngodly.
Psalms 17:14 From the men of thy hande (O Lord) from the men of the worlde, which haue theyr porcion in this lyfe: whose bellyes thou fyllest with thy treasure. They haue chyldren at theyr desyre, and leaue the rest of of theyr substaunce for their babes.
Psalms 17:15 But as for me, I wil beholde thy presence in righteousnes: and when thy glory appeareth, I shall be satisfied.

CHAPTER: 18

Psalms 18:1 To the chaunter of Dauid, seruaunt of the Lorde, whiche sayde vnto the Lorde the woordes of thys songe, on the daye in which the Lorde delyuered hym from the hande of all hys enemyes, and from the hande of Saul, and sayde. I wyll loue the (O Lorde) my strength.
Psalms 18:2 The Lorde is my succour, my refuge, my sauyoure: my God, my helper in whome I trust: my buckler, the horne of my health, and my proteccion.
Psalms 18:3 I will prayse the Lorde, and call vppon hym, so shall I be safe fro myne enemyes.
Psalms 18:4 The sorowes of deathe compassed me, and the brokes of vngodlynes made me afrayed.
Psalms 18:5 The paynes of hell came aboute me, the snares of death toke holde vpon me.
Psalms 18:6 Yet in my trouble I called vpon the Lord, and complayned vnto my God. So he hearde my voyce out of hys holye temple, and my complaynte came before hym ye euen into hys eares.
Psalms 18:7 Then the earth trembled and quaked, the verye foundacyones of the hylles shoke and were remoued, because he was wroth.
Psalms 18:8 There wente a smoke oute of hys nostrels and a consuming fyre out of his mouth so that coales were kyndled at it.
Psalms 18:9 He bowed the heauens & came downe, and it was darke vnder his fete.
Psalms 18:10 He rode vpon the Cherubyns & dyd fle: he came flyenge wyth the wynges of the wynde.
Psalms 18:11 He made darcknesse his pauylion rounde aboute hym, wyth darcke water and thycke cloudes to couer him.
Psalms 18:12 At the brightnes of his presence the cloudes remoued, wyth hayle stones and coales of fyre.
Psalms 18:13 The Lord also thondred out of the heauen and the heygth gaue his thonder wyth haile stones and coales of fyre.
Psalms 18:14 He sente oute hys arrowes and scattered them, he cast sore lyghtenynges, and destroied them.
Psalms 18:15 The sprynges of waters were sene, and the foundacyons of the rounde worlde were discouered at thy chidynge (O Lorde) at the blastynge and breth of thy displeasures.
Psalms 18:16 He sente doune from the heygth to fetch me, and toke me out of greate waters.
Psalms 18:17 He delyuered me fro my stronge enemies & fro my foes whych were to myghtye for me
Psalms 18:18 They preuented me in the time of my trouble, but the Lorde was my defence.
Psalms 18:19 He broughte me forthe also into lybertye: and delyuered me, because, he had a fauoure vnto me.
Psalms 18:20 The Lorde shall rewarde me after my righteous dealynge, and accordynge to the clennesse of my handes shall he recompense me.
Psalms 18:21 For I haue kepte the wayes of the Lord: and haue not behaued my selfe wickedly agaynst my God.
Psalms 18:22 I haue an eye vnto all hys lawes, and caste not oute hys commaundementes fro me.
Psalms 18:23 Vncorrupte wyll I be before him, and will eschue myne owne wyckednes.
Psalms 18:24 Therfore shall the Lorde rewarde me after my ryghtuous dealynge, and accordinge vnto the clennesse of my handes in his eye sighte.
Psalms 18:25 With the holye thou shalte be holye, and wyth the innocente thou shalte be innocente.
Psalms 18:26 With the cleane thou shalt be cleane, and with the frowarde thou shalte be frowarde.
Psalms 18:27 For thou shalte saue the poore oppressed, and brynge doune the hye lokes of the proude.
Psalms 18:28 Thou lyghtest my candell, O Lorde my God: thou maketh my darcknesse to be light
Psalms 18:29 For in the I can dyscomforte an hoste of men: yea in my God I can leape ouer the walle.
Psalms 18:30 The waye of God is a perfecte waye: the wordes of the Lorde are tryed in the fire: he is a shylde of defence, for all them that truste in hym.
Psalms 18:31 For who is God, but the Lord? Or who hath any strength, but our God?
Psalms 18:32 It is God that gyrded me with strength, and made my way vncorrupt.
Psalms 18:33 He hathe made my fete lyke hertes fete, and set me vpon hye.
Psalms 18:34 He teacheth myne handes to fyght, & maketh myne armes to breake euen a bowe of stele.
Psalms 18:35 Thou haste geuen me the defence of thy healthe, thy ryghte hande vpholdeth me, and thy louynge correctyon maketh me greate.
Psalms 18:36 Thou hast made roume ynough vnder me for to go, that my fote steppes shuld not slyde.
Psalms 18:37 I wyll folowe vpon myne enemyes, and take them: I wyll not turne tyll they be dyscomforted.
Psalms 18:38 I wyll smyte them, they shall not be able to stand, but fal vnder my fete.
Psalms 18:39 Thou hast gyrded me with strength vnto the battel, thou hast throwen them al downe vnder me that rose vp agaynst me.
Psalms 18:40 Thou hast made myne enemyes to turne heir backes vpon me, thou haste destroyed them: that hated me.
Psalms 18:41 They cryed, but there was none to helpe them: yea euen vnto the Lorde, but he heard them not.
Psalms 18:42 I wyll beate them as smalle as the duste claye in the wynde, I wyll cast them out as the clay in the stretes.
Psalms 18:43 Thou shalt delyuer me from the striuynges of the people, thou shalt make me the head of the Heathen. A people whom I haue not knowne shal serue me.
Psalms 18:44 As soone as they heare of me, they shall obey me, but the straung chyldren dyssemble with me.
Psalms 18:45 The straunge chyldren are waxen olde, and go haltynge out of their pathes.
Psalms 18:46 The Lorde lyueth: and blessed be, my helper, praysed be the God of my health.
Psalms 18:47 Euen the God which seyth that I be auenged, and subdueth the people vnto me.
Psalms 18:48 It is he that delyuereth me from my cruell enemyes: thou shalt lyfte me vp from them that ryse against me, thou shalt rid me from the wycked man.
Psalms 18:49 For this cause I wyll geue thankes vnto the (O lorde) among the gentiles, and synge prayses vnto thy name.
Psalms 18:50 Greate prosperitye geueth he vnto hys Kynge: and sheweth louynge kyndnesse vnto Dauyd hys anoynted yea & vnto his sede for euermore.

CHAPTER: 19

Psalms 19:1 To the chaunter, a Psalm of Dauid. The very heauens declare the glory of God, and the very firmament sheweth his handy worcke.
Psalms 19:2 One daye telleth another, and one nyght certifyeth another.
Psalms 19:3 There is neyther speach ner language, but their voices are hard among them.
Psalms 19:4 Their sounde is gone oute into all landes, and their wordes into the endes of the worlde.
Psalms 19:5 In them hathe he sette a tabernacle for the Sunne, whych commeth forthe as a brydegrome out of his chamber, and reioyseth as a giaunt to runne his course.
Psalms 19:6 It goeth forth from the one ende of the heauen, and runneth aboute vnto the same ende agayne, and there maye no man hyde hym selfe from the heate therof.
Psalms 19:7 The lawe of the Lorde is a perfecte lawe it quickeneth the soule. The testimonye of the Lorde is true, and geueth wisdome euen vnto babes.
Psalms 19:8 The statutes of the Lord are ryght, and reioyse the hert: the commaundement of the lord is pure, and geueth lyght vnto the eyes.
Psalms 19:9 The feare of the Lorde is cleane, and endureth for euer: the iudgementes of the Lord are true and ryghtuous altogether.
Psalms 19:10 More pleasaunt are they then golde, yea then much fyne golde: sweter then hony and the hony combe.
Psalms 19:11 These thy seruaunt kepeth, & for kepynge of them there is great reward.
Psalms 19:12 Who can tell, how oft he offendeth? Oh clense thou me fro my secrete fautes.
Psalms 19:13 Kepe the seruaunt also from presumptuous synnes, lest they get the dominion ouer me: so shall I be vndefyled and innocent from the greate offence.
Psalms 19:14 Yea the words of my mouth and the meditacion of my herte shalbe acceptable vnto the, O Lorde, my helper and my redemer.

CHAPTER: 20

Psalms 20:1 To the chanter, a Psalme of Dauid. The Lorde heare the in the tyme of trouble, that name of the God of Iacob defend the.
Psalms 20:2 Send the helpe from the Santuary, and strength the oute of Sion.
Psalms 20:3 Remembre all thy offerynges, and accept thy brent sacrifice, Selah.
Psalms 20:4 Graunte the thy hertes desyre, and fulfill all thy mynde.
Psalms 20:5 We wyll reioyse in thy health, & triumphe in the name of the Lorde our God: the Lord perfourme all thy peticion.
Psalms 20:6 Now knowe I, that the Lord helpeth hys anoynted, and will heare hym from his holy heauen: myghtye is the helpe of hys ryghte hande.
Psalms 20:7 Some put their trust in charettes, & some in horses: but we will remembre the name of the Lorde oure God.
Psalms 20:8 They are broughte doune and fallen, but we are rysen and stande vp right.
Psalms 20:9 Saue, Lorde, and helpe vs, O kyng, when we call vpon the.

CHAPTER: 21

Psalms 21:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. Lorde, how ioyfull is the kyng in thy strength? O how exceadyng glad is he of thy sauynge health?
Psalms 21:2 Thou haste geuen him hys hertes desyre, and hast not put him from the request of hys lippes. Selah.
Psalms 21:3 For thou hast preuented him with liberal blessinges, and set a croune of golde vpon hys head.
Psalms 21:4 He asked lyfe of the, and thou gauest him a longe lyfe, euen for euer and euer.
Psalms 21:5 His honour is great in thy sauing health, glory and great worship shalt thou laye vpon hym.
Psalms 21:6 For thou shalt geue hym euerlastinge felicitie, and make hym glad with the ioye of thy countenaunce.
Psalms 21:7 And why? because the kynge putteth hys trust in the Lord, and in the mercy of the most hyest he shall not miscary.
Psalms 21:8 Let all thyne enemyes fele thy hande: let thy right hande fynde out all theym that hate the.
Psalms 21:9 Thou shalt make them like a fyry ouen in tyme of thy wrath: the Lorde shall destroye them in hys displeasure, and the fyre shal consume them.
Psalms 21:10 Their frute shalte thou rote oute of the earth, and their sede from amonge the chyldren of men.
Psalms 21:11 For they intended mischief agaynst the, & ymagined suche deuyces, as they were not able to perfourme.
Psalms 21:12 Therfore shalte thou put them to flighte, & with thy strynges thou shalte make ready thyne arrowes agaynst the faces of them.
Psalms 21:13 Be thou exalted, Lorde in thyne owne strength, so wyll we synge and prayse thy power.

CHAPTER: 22

Psalms 22:1 To the chaunter vppon Aieleth of the dawnyng, a Psalme of Dauid. My God, my God: why haste thou forsaken me? the wordes of my complaynte are farre fro my health.
Psalms 22:2 O my God, I crye in the daye tyme, but thou hearest not: and in the night season also I take no rest.
Psalms 22:3 Yet dwellest thou in the sanctuarye, O thou worshyppe of Israel.
Psalms 22:4 Oure fathers hoped in the, they trusted in the, and thou dyddest deliuer them.
Psalms 22:5 They called vpon the, & were helped: they put their trust in the, & were not confounded.
Psalms 22:6 But as for me, I am a worme & no man: a very scorne of men and the outcaste of the people.
Psalms 22:7 Al they that se me, laugh me to scorne: thei shute out their lippes, & shake their heades.
Psalms 22:8 He trusted in God, let hym delyuer hym: let him helpe hym, if he will haue hym.
Psalms 22:9 But thou art he that toke me out of my mothers wombe: thou waste my hope, when I hanged yet vpon my mothers brestes.
Psalms 22:10 I haue bene left vnto the euer sence I was borne, thou art my God, euen fro my mothers wombe.
Psalms 22:11 O go not fro me then, for trouble is harde at hande, and here is none to helpe me.
Psalms 22:12 Great bulles are come about me, fatte oxen close me in on euery syde.
Psalms 22:13 They gape vpon me with their mouthes, as it were a rampynge and roarynge Lyon.
Psalms 22:14 I am poured out lyke water, all my boones are out of ioynt: my herte in the middest of my body is euen lyke meltyng waxe.
Psalms 22:15 My strength is dryed vp lyke a potsherde, my tunge cleueth to my goomes, & thou haste brought me into the dust of death.
Psalms 22:16 For dogges are come about me, the counsail of the wicked hath layed seage against me. They pearsed my handes and my fete,
Psalms 22:17 I might haue tolde all my bones: as for them, they stode staryng and lokyng vpon me.
Psalms 22:18 They haue parted my garmentes among them, and cast lottes vpon my vesture.
Psalms 22:19 But be not thou farre fro me, O Lorde: thou art my succoure, haste the to helpe me.
Psalms 22:20 Delyuer my soule from the swearde, my dearlyng from the power of the dogge.
Psalms 22:21 Saue me from the Lyons mouth, & heare me from amonge the hornes of the Vnicornes.
Psalms 22:22 So wyll I declare thy name vnto my brethren, in the middest of the congregacion wyl I prayse the.
Psalms 22:23 O praise the Lord ye that feare him: Magnify hym all ye sede of Iacob, and let al the sede of Israel feare hym.
Psalms 22:24 For he hath not despised nor abhorred the miserable estate of the poore: he hath not hid hys face fro me, but when I called vnto him he herde me.
Psalms 22:25 I wyll prayse the in the great congregacion, and perfourme my vowes in the sighte of all them that feare the.
Psalms 22:26 The poore shall eate & be satisfied: they that seke after the Lord shal prayse hym: our hert shall lyue for euer.
Psalms 22:27 All the endes of the worlde shall remembre them selfes, and be turned vnto the Lorde: & all the generacions of the Heithen shal worshippe before hym.
Psalms 22:28 For the kyngdom is the Lordes, & he shal be the gouernour of the Heythen.
Psalms 22:29 All such as be fat vpon earth, shall eate also and worshippe. All they that lye in the dust, and lyue so hardly, shall fall doune before hym.
Psalms 22:30 The sede shall serue hym, and preache of the Lord for euer.
Psalms 22:31 They shall come, and declare hys ryghteousnes: vnto a people that shallbe borne, whome the Lorde hath made.

CHAPTER: 23

Psalms 23:1 A Psalme of Dauid. The Lord is my shepherde, I can want nothynge.
Psalms 23:2 He fedeth me in a grene pasture, and ledeth me to a freshe water.
Psalms 23:3 He quickeneth my soule, and bryngeth me forth in the waye of righteousnes for his names sake.
Psalms 23:4 Though I should walke now in the valley of the shadow of death, yet I feare not euel for thou arte with me: thy staffe & thy shepehoke comforte me.
Psalms 23:5 Thou preparest a table before me agaynste myne enemyes: thou anoyntest my head with oyle, and fyllest my cuppe ful.
Psalms 23:6 Oh let thy louing kyndnes and mercy folowe me all the dayes of my life, that I may dwell in the house of the Lorde for euer.

CHAPTER: 24

Psalms 24:1 A Psalme of Dauid. The earth is the Lordes, & all that therin is: the compase of the world, & al that dwell therein.
Psalms 24:2 For he hath founded it vpon the seas, and buylded it vpon the floudes.
Psalms 24:3 Who shall go vp into the hyll of the Lord? Or who shal remayne in his holy place?
Psalms 24:4 Euen he that hath innocent handes and a cleane hert: which lifteth not vp his minde vnto vanite, and sweareth not to disceaue.
Psalms 24:5 He shal receaue the blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his sauiour.
Psalms 24:6 This is the generation of them that seke hym, of them that seke thy face, O Iacob. Selah.
Psalms 24:7 Open your gates (O ye princes) lette the euerlastynge dores be opened, that the kyng of glory may come in.
Psalms 24:8 Who is this kyng of glory? It is the Lorde strong and myghtie, euen the Lorde myghty in batell.
Psalms 24:9 Open youre gates (O ye princes) let the euerlastynge dores be opened, that the kyng of glory may come in.
Psalms 24:10 Who is this king of glory? It is the Lord of Hoostes, he is the kynge of glorye. Selah.

CHAPTER: 25

Psalms 25:1 Of Dauid, Vnto the (O Lorde) I lyft vp my soule.
Psalms 25:2 My God, I trust in the: Oh lette me not be confounded, leste myne enemyes tryumphe ouer me.
Psalms 25:3 For all they that hope in the shall not be ashamed: but suche as be scornefull despysers without a cause they shall be put to confucyon.
Psalms 25:4 Shewe me thy wayes, O Lord, & teach me thy pathes.
Psalms 25:5 Lede me in thy trueth and learne me, for thou art the God of my healthe, and in the is my hope al the day long.
Psalms 25:6 Call to remembrance, O Lorde, thy tender mercyes and thy louynge kyndenesses, which haue bene euer of olde.
Psalms 25:7 Oh remembre not the synnes and offences of my youth, but accordynge vnto thy mercye thynke vpon we, O Lord, for thy goodnesse.
Psalms 25:8 O how frendly & rightuous is the Lord, therfore will he teach synners in the way.
Psalms 25:9 He ledeth the symple a right, & suche as be meke them lerneth he his wayes.
Psalms 25:10 All the wayes of the Lord are verye mercy and faythfulnes, vnto suche as kepe hys testament and couenaunte.
Psalms 25:11 For thy names sake, O Lorde, be mercyfull vnto my synne, for it is greate.
Psalms 25:12 Whatsoeuer he be that feareth the Lorde he shall shewe hym the waye that he hathe chosen.
Psalms 25:13 Hys soule shall dwell at ease, and his sede shal possesse the lande.
Psalms 25:14 The secrete of the Lorde is amonge them that feare him, and he sheweth them hys couenaunt.
Psalms 25:15 Myne eyes are euer lokynge vnto the Lorde, for he shall plucke my fete oute of the net.
Psalms 25:16 Turne the vnto me and haue mercy vpon me, for I am desolate and in misery.
Psalms 25:17 The sorowes of my herte, are greate, O brynge me out of my troubles.
Psalms 25:18 Loke vpon myne aduersyty and misery, & forgeue me all my synnes.
Psalms 25:19 Consyder how myne enemyes are many, and beare a malicious hate against me.
Psalms 25:20 O kepe my soule, and delyuer me: let me not be confounded, for I haue put my trust in the.
Psalms 25:21 Let inocencye and ryghtuous dealynge walie vpon me, for my hope is in the.
Psalms 25:22 Delyuer Israell, O God oute of all hys trouble.

CHAPTER: 26

Psalms 26:1 Of Dauid. Be thou my iudge, O Lord, for I walke innocently: my trust is in the Lorde therfore shal I not fal.
Psalms 26:2 Examen me. O Lorde, and proue me: trye out my raines and my hert
Psalms 26:3 For my louynge kindnesse is before mine eyes, and I walke in thy truth.
Psalms 26:4 I syt not amonge vayne personnes, & haue no feloshippe with the disceatfull.
Psalms 26:5 I hate the congregacyon of the wycked, and I wyll not syt amonge the vngodlye.
Psalms 26:6 I wash my handes with innocencye, O Lorde, and so go I to thyne alter.
Psalms 26:7 That I may shewe the voice of thy praise and tell of all thy wonderous workes,
Psalms 26:8 Lorde, I loue the habitacion of thy house, and the place where thy honoure dwelleth.
Psalms 26:9 O destroy not my soule wyth the sinners nor my lyfe with the bloudthursty.
Psalms 26:10 In whose handes is wyckednesse, and their right hande is full of gyftes.
Psalms 26:11 But as for me I wyll walcke innocentely: O deliuer me, and be mercyfull vnto me.
Psalms 26:12 My fote standeth right: I wyll prayse the (O Lorde) in the congregations.

CHAPTER: 27

Psalms 27:1 Of Dauid. The Lorde is my lyghte and my health: whome then shoulde I feare? the Lorde is the strength of my life, for whom then shuld I be afraied?
Psalms 27:2 Therfore when the wycked, euen myne enemies and my foes, came vpon me, to eate vp my flesh, stombled and fell.
Psalms 27:3 Thoughe an hooste of men were layed agaynst me, yet shall not my hert be afrayed: and though there rose vp warre agaynst me, yet wyll I put my trust in him.
Psalms 27:4 One thynge haue I desyred of the Lorde, which I wyll requyre: namelye, that I maye dwel in the house of the Lorde all the dayes of my lyfe, to beholde the fayre beutye of the Lorde, and to viset his temple.
Psalms 27:5 For in the tyme of trouble he hath hydde me in his tabernacle, yea in the secrete place of his dwellynge hath he kept and set me vp vpon a rocke of stone.
Psalms 27:6 And now hath he lift vp my head aboue myne enemyes, that compassed me rounde aboute. Therfore wyll I offer in hys dwellynge. the oblacyon of thankesgeuynge: I wil singe and speake prayses vnto the Lorde.
Psalms 27:7 Herken vnto my voyce, O Lorde, when I crye vnto the: haue mercye vpon me and heare me,
Psalms 27:8 My hert speketh vnto the, my face seketh the, yea Lorde, thy face wyll I seke.
Psalms 27:9 O hyde not thou thy face fro me, caste not in thy seruaunt of displeasure. Thou art my succour, leaue me not, nether forsake me, O God my sauioure.
Psalms 27:10 For my father and my mother haue forsaken me, but the Lord hath taken me vp.
Psalms 27:11 Shewe me thy waye O Lord and lede me in the right path, because of myne ennemye
Psalms 27:12 Delyuer me not into the wyles of myne aduersaryes, for there are false wytnesses risen vp against me, and they ymagyne myschyefe.
Psalms 27:13 Neuerthelesse I beleue verelye to se the goodnesse of the Lorde in the lande of the lyuynge.
Psalms 27:14 O tary thou the Lordes leisure, be strong let thyne hert be of good comfort, and wayte thou still for the Lorde.

CHAPTER: 28

Psalms 28:1 Of Dauid. Vnto the wil I crye, O my strong defence: thinke no scorne of me, leste if thou make the as thoughe thou herdeste not, I be come lyke them, that go downe in to the pyt.
Psalms 28:2 Heare the voyce of my humble peticyon, when I cry vnto the, and hold vp my handes toward thy holy temple.
Psalms 28:3 O plucke me not awaye amonge the vngodly and wickeddoers, which speake frendly to their neyghboure, but ymagin mischefe in their hertes.
Psalms 28:4 Rewarde them accordynge to their dedes and wyckednesse of their owne inuencyons. Recompence them after the worckes of their handes, paye them that they haue deserued.
Psalms 28:5 For they regarde not the worckes of the Lorde, nor the operacyon of his hands: therfore shall he breake them down, and not bild them vp.
Psalms 28:6 Praysed be the Lorde, for he hath herd the voyce of myne humble petycyon.
Psalms 28:7 The Lord is my strength and my shylde: my hert hoped in hym, and I am helped: therfore my hert daunseth for ioy, and I wil sing praises vnto hym.
Psalms 28:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, he is the defender and Sauioure of his anoynted.
Psalms 28:9 O helpe thy people, geue thy blessyng vnto thyne enheritaunce: fede them, and set them vp for euer.

CHAPTER: 29

Psalms 29:1 A Psalme of Dauid. Ascribe vnto the Lorde, O ye mightie, ascribe vnto the Lord worship and strength.
Psalms 29:2 Geue the Lord the honour of his name bow your selues to the holy magesty of the Lord,
Psalms 29:3 It is the Lorde that commaunded the waters: It is the gloryus God that maketh the thonder: it is the Lorde that ruleth the sea.
Psalms 29:4 The voyce of the Lorde is mighty in operacyon, the voice of the Lorde is a glorius voyce.
Psalms 29:5 The voyce of the Lorde breaketh the Cedre trees: yea the Lorde breaketh the Ceders of Libanus.
Psalms 29:6 He maketh them to skyppe lyke a calfe: Libanus and Sirion lyke a younge vnicorne
Psalms 29:7 The voyce of the Lorde deuydeth the flames of fyre:
Psalms 29:8 the voice of the Lorde shaketh the wylderuesse, yea the Lorde shaketh the wildernesse of Cades.
Psalms 29:9 The voyce of the Lorde moueth the hyndes and discouereth the thicke bushes: in hys temple shall euerye man speake of hys honoure.
Psalms 29:10 The Lord stilleth the water floud, and the Lord remaineth a king for euer.
Psalms 29:11 The Lorde shall geue power vnto hys people, the Lord shall geue his people the blessyng of peace.

CHAPTER: 30

Psalms 30:1 A Psalme and songe of the dedicatiou of the house of Dauid. I wyll magnifye the, O Lord, for thou hast set me vp, and not suffred my foes to triumphe ouer me.
Psalms 30:2 O Lord my God, I cried vnto the, and thou hast healed me.
Psalms 30:3 Thou Lord hast brought my soule out of hell: thou hast kepte my lyfe, where as they go downe to the pyt.
Psalms 30:4 Singe prayses vnto the Lord (O ye saintes of hys) geue thankes vnto hym for a remembraunce of hys holynesse.
Psalms 30:5 For his wrath endureth but the twincling of an eie, and his pleasure is in lyfe: heuinesse may well endure for a nyght, but ioye commeth in the morning.
Psalms 30:6 As for me, when I was in prosperytye, I sayd: Tush I shal neuer fall more.
Psalms 30:7 And why? thou Lord of thy goodnesse hadest made my hyll so stronge. But as soone as thou turnedest thy face fro me, I was brought in feare.
Psalms 30:8 Then cryed I vnto the, O Lorde, yea vnto the Lord made I my praier.
Psalms 30:9 What profyt is ther in my bloude, if I go downe to corruption? May the dust geue thankes vnto the? Or shal it declare thy faythfulnesse?
Psalms 30:10 Heare, O Lorde, and haue mercye vpon me: Lord be thou my helper.
Psalms 30:11 And so thou hast turned my heuynesse into ioye: thou haste put of my sacke cloth, & gyrded me with gladnesse.
Psalms 30:12 That mine honoure myght synge praises vnto the without ceasyng: O Lord my God, I wil geue thankes vnto the for euer.

CHAPTER: 31

Psalms 31:1 To the chaunter a Psalme of Dauyd. In the O lord, is my trust: let me neuer be put to confusyon, but delyuer me in thy rightuousnesse.
Psalms 31:2 Bow downe thyne eare to me, make haste to delyuer me: be thou my strong rocke and a house of defence, that thou mayest saue me.
Psalms 31:3 For thou arte my stronge holde and my castel: O be thou my gide and lede me for thy names sake.
Psalms 31:4 Drawe me out of the nette that they haue layed pryuelye for me, for thou arte my strength
Psalms 31:5 In to thy handes I commende my spirite: thou hast delyuered me O Lorde thou God of truth.
Psalms 31:6 I hate them that holde of vanites, and my trust is in the Lord.
Psalms 31:7 I wil be glad and reioyse in thy mercy for thou hast consydered my trouble, thou haste knowne my soule in aduersity.
Psalms 31:8 Thou hast not delyuered me ouer into the handes of the enemye, but hast set my fete in a large rowme.
Psalms 31:9 Haue mercy vpon me, O Lorde, for I am in trouble, myne eye consumed for verye heuynesse, yea my soule and my body.
Psalms 31:10 My lyfe is waxen olde with heuines, and my yeares with moornyng. My strength fayleth me because of mine aduersitie, and my bones are corrupt.
Psalms 31:11 I am become a verye reprofe amonge all myne enemyes, my neyghbours and they of myne owne aquayntaunce are afraied of me they that se me in the streate, conueye them selues fro me.
Psalms 31:12 I am cleane forgotten and oute of mynde as a dead man: I am become lyke a broken vessell.
Psalms 31:13 For I haue harde the blasphemy of the multytude: euerye man abhorreth me: they haue gathered a councell together agaynste me, and are purposed to take awaye my lyfe.
Psalms 31:14 But my hope is in the Lord, and I say thou art my God.
Psalms 31:15 My tyme is in thy hande: deliuer me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.
Psalms 31:16 Shewe thy seruaunte the lyghte of thy countenaunce, helpe me for thy mercyes sake.
Psalms 31:17 Let me not be confounded, O Lorde, for I calle vpon the: lette the vngodlye rather be put to confusyon, and broughte vnto the hell.
Psalms 31:18 Let the lieng lippes be put to silence which cruely, disdainefully, and despitefully speake against the rightuous.
Psalms 31:19 O howe greate and manyfolde is thy good, whyche thou haste hyd for them that feare the? O what thinges bringest thou to passe for them, that put their truste in the, euen before the sonnes of men?
Psalms 31:20 Thou hydest them priuely by thyne owne presence from the proude men, thou kepeste them secretly in thy tabernacle, from the strife of tonges.
Psalms 31:21 Thankes be to the Lorde, for he hath shewed me maruelous greate kyndenesse in a strong cytye.
Psalms 31:22 For when the suddaine feare cam vpon me I said: I am cast out of thy sighte. Neuerthelesse, thou herdest myne humble prayer, when I cried vnto the.
Psalms 31:23 O loue the Lorde (all ye hys saynctes) for the Lorde preserueth the faythfull, and plenteusly rewardeth he the proud doer.
Psalms 31:24 Be strong therfore and take a good herte vnto you, all ye that put your trust in the Lord.

CHAPTER: 32

Psalms 32:1 An instruccyon of Dauid. Blessed are they, whose vnryghtuousnes is forgeuen, and whose sinnes are couered.
Psalms 32:2 Blessed is the man, vnto whom the Lord imputeth no synne, in whose, spirite ther is no gyle.
Psalms 32:3 For while I helde my tonge my bones consumed awaye thorowe my daylye complaynynges.
Psalms 32:4 And because thy hand was so heuy vpon me both daye and nyght, my moysture was lyke the drouth in Sommer. Selah.
Psalms 32:5 Therfore I confessed my sinne vnto the & hyd not myne vnryghtuousnes. I sayde: I wyll knowledge myne offence and accuse my selfe vnto the Lord, & so thou forgauest me the wickednesse of my synne Selah.
Psalms 32:6 For thys shall euerye sayncte make hys prayer vnto the in due season, therfore shall not, the great water fludes, come nie hym.
Psalms 32:7 Thou art my defence in the trouble that is come aboute me, O compasse thou me about also with the ioy of deliuerance. Selah
Psalms 32:8 I wyl enforme the, and shew the the waie wherin thou shalt go I wyll fasten myne eyes vpon the.
Psalms 32:9 Be not ye now like horses & mules, which haue no vnderstandyng. Whose mouthes thou must hold with bit and bridle, if they wil not obey the.
Psalms 32:10 Great plages shal the vngodly haue, but who so putteth hys trust in the Lorde, mercy shall compasse him on euery syde.
Psalms 32:11 Be glad, O ye ryghtuous, and reioyse in the Lord, be ioyful al ye that are true of herte.

CHAPTER: 33

Psalms 33:1 Reioyse in the Lord, O ye righteous, for it becommeth well the iust to be thankefull.
Psalms 33:2 Prayse the Lord with harpe: singe psalmes vnto him wyth the lute and instrument of ten strynges.
Psalms 33:3 Singe hym a new songe, yea, sing lustely vnto hym, and with a good corage.
Psalms 33:4 For the woorde of the Lorde is true, & all hys workes are faythful.
Psalms 33:5 He loueth mercy and iudgement, the earth is full of the goodnesse of the Lorde.
Psalms 33:6 By the worde of the Lorde were the heauens made, and all the hoostes of theym by the breth of hys mouth.
Psalms 33:7 He gathereth the waters together as it were in a bottell, and layeth vp the depe in secret.
Psalms 33:8 Let all the earth feare the Lorde, and lette all them that dwell in the worlde, stande in awe of hym.
Psalms 33:9 For loke what he sayeth, it is done: and loke what he commaundeth, it standeth fast.
Psalms 33:10 The Lorde bryngeth the counsayl of the Heythen to naught, and turneth the deuyces of the people.
Psalms 33:11 But the counsayll of the Lorde endureth, and the thoughtes of his herte from generacion to generacion.
Psalms 33:12 Blessed are the people that holde the Lorde for their God, & blessed are the folke whome he hath chosen to be hys heretage.
Psalms 33:13 The Lorde loketh doune from heauen, & beholdeth all the chyldren of men:
Psalms 33:14 from hys stronge seate he considreth all them that dwell in the worlde.
Psalms 33:15 He onely hath fashyoned all the hertes of them, and knoweth all their workes.
Psalms 33:16 A kynge is not helped by hys owne great hoost, neyther is a giaunte saued thorow the myght of hys owne strength.
Psalms 33:17 A horse is but a vayne thing to saue a man, it is not the power of hys strengthe that can delyuer hym.
Psalms 33:18 Beholde, the eye of the Lorde loketh vnto them that feare hym, & put their trust in hys mercy.
Psalms 33:19 That he maye delyuer their soules frome death, & to fede them in the deare tyme.
Psalms 33:20 Let oure soule paciently abyde the Lord, for he is oure helpe and shylde.
Psalms 33:21 So shall oure hert reioyse in him, because we haue hoped in hys holy name.
Psalms 33:22 Let thy mercifull kyndnesse, O Lorde, be vpon vs, lyke as we put our trust in the.

CHAPTER: 34

Psalms 34:1 Of Dauid, when he fayned hym self too be madde before Abimelech: whyche droue hym awaye, and he departed. I wyll alwaye geue thanckes vnto the LORD, hys prayse shall euer be in my mouth.
Psalms 34:2 My soule shall make her boast in the Lord: the humble shall heare therof, & be glad.
Psalms 34:3 O prayse the Lord wyth me, and let vs magnyfye hys name together.
Psalms 34:4 I sought the Lorde, and he herde me, yea he delyuered me out of all my feare.
Psalms 34:5 They that haue an eye vnto hym, shalbe lightened, & ther faces shal not be ashamed.
Psalms 34:6 This poore man cryed vnto the Lorde, & he hearde hym, yea, and delyuered hym oute of all hys troubles.
Psalms 34:7 The Aungel of the Lorde pytcheth hys tente rounde aboute hym that feare hym, & delyuereth them.
Psalms 34:8 O taste and se how frendly the Lorde is, blessed is the man that trusteth in hym.
Psalms 34:9 O feare the Lord, ye that be hys sayntes: for they that feare hym, lacke nothyng.
Psalms 34:10 The ryche shall wante and suffre hunger, but they which seke the Lord, shal want no maner of thyng, that is good.
Psalms 34:11 Come hyther, O ye chyldren, herken vnto me, I wil teache you the feare of the Lorde.
Psalms 34:12 Who so lysteth to lyue, and wolde fayne se good dayes.
Psalms 34:13 Let hym refrayne his tonge from euell, & hys lyppes that they speake no gyle.
Psalms 34:14 Let hym eschue euell, and do good: Lette hym seke peace and ensue it.
Psalms 34:15 For the eyes of the Lorde are ouer the righteous, and his eares are open vnto theyr prayers.
Psalms 34:16 But the face of the Lorde beholdeth them that do euell, to destroye the remembraunce of them out of the earth.
Psalms 34:17 When the righteous crye, the Lorde heareth them, & delyuereth them out of all theyr troubles.
Psalms 34:18 The Lorde is nye vnto them that are contryte in hert, and will helpe suche as be of an humble sprete.
Psalms 34:19 Great are the troubles of the righteous, but the Lorde delyuereth them out of all.
Psalms 34:20 He kepeth all their bones, so that not one of them is broken.
Psalms 34:21 But misfortune shall slaye the vngodly, & they that hate the righteous shalbe gylty.
Psalms 34:22 The Lorde deliuereth the soules of hys seruauntes, and all they that put their truste in hym, shall not offende.

CHAPTER: 35

Psalms 35:1 Of Dauid. Stryue thou with them, O lord, that stryue with me, fight thou against them that fight against me.
Psalms 35:2 Laye hande vpon the shylde and speare, and stande vp to helpe me.
Psalms 35:3 Drawe out thy swearde, and stoppe the waye agaynst them that persecute me, saye vnto my soule: I am thy helpe.
Psalms 35:4 Let them be confounded & put to shame, that seke after my soule: let theym be turned back and brought to confusion, that ymagin mischiefe for me.
Psalms 35:5 Let them be as the dust before the winde, and the aungel of the Lord scateryng them.
Psalms 35:6 Let their waye be darcke and slippery, & the aungell of the Lorde to persecute them.
Psalms 35:7 For they haue priuely layed their nette to destroye me without a cause, yea, & made a pytte for my soule, which I neuer deserued.
Psalms 35:8 Let a soden destruccion come vpon hym vnwares, & the nette that he had layed pryuely, catche hym selfe, that he maye fall into hys owne mischief.
Psalms 35:9 But let my soule be ioyfull in the Lorde, and reioyse in hys helpe.
Psalms 35:10 All my bones shall saye: Lorde who is lyke vnto the? which deliuerest the poore from those that are to strong for him, yea, the poore and the nedy from hys robbers.
Psalms 35:11 False witnesses are rysen vp, and laye to my charge thinges that I know not.
Psalms 35:12 They rewarde me euell for good, too the great discomforte of my soule.
Psalms 35:13 Neuerthelesse, when they were sycke, I put on a sacke cloth: I humbled my soule with fastyng, and my prayer turned into myne owne bosome.
Psalms 35:14 I behaued my selfe as though it had bene my frende or my brother, I went heuely, as one that mourneth for hys mother.
Psalms 35:15 But in myne aduersitie they reioyse, & gather them together. Yea, the very lame come together agaynste me vnwares, makynge mowes at me, and ceasse not.
Psalms 35:16 With the gredy and scorneful hypocrites they gnasshed vpon me with their teeth.
Psalms 35:17 Lorde, whan wilt thou loke vpon thys? O restore my soule from the wycked rumoure of them, my dearlynge from the lyons?
Psalms 35:18 So will I geue the thanckes in the great congregacion, and prayse the among muche people.
Psalms 35:19 O let them not triumphe ouer me, that are myne enemyes for naught: O let them not winke with their eyes, that hate me without a cause.
Psalms 35:20 And why? their comening is not for peace but they ymagyn false wordes agaynste the outcastes of the lande.
Psalms 35:21 They gape vpon me with their mouthes, saying: there, there: we se it with our eyes.
Psalms 35:22 This thou seist, O lorde: holde not thy tonge then, go not farre fro me, O lorde.
Psalms 35:23 Awake lorde, and stande vp: auenge thou my cause, my God, and my lorde,
Psalms 35:24 Iudge me, O lorde my God, accordynge to thy righteousnesse, that they triumphe not ouer me.
Psalms 35:25 O let them not saye in their hertes: there there, so wolde we haue it: O let them not saye: we haue ouercome hym.
Psalms 35:26 Let them be put to confusion & shame, that reioyse at my trouble: let them be clothed wt rebuke and dishonoure, that boost them selfes agaynst me.
Psalms 35:27 Let them also be glad and reioyse, that fauoure my righteous dealynge: yea, let them saye alwaye: blessed be the lord, whiche hath pleasure in the prosperitie of hys seruaunt.
Psalms 35:28 And as for my tonge, it shalbe talkyng of thy righteousnes and of thy prayse, all the day longe.

CHAPTER: 36

Psalms 36:1 To the chaunter, of Dauid the seruaunt of the Lorde. My hert sheweth me the wickednesse of the vngodly, that there is no feare of God before hys eyes.
Psalms 36:2 For he dissembleth before his face, so longe tyll hys abhominable sinne be founde out.
Psalms 36:3 The woordes of hys mouth are vnrighteousnes and disceate, he will not be learned to do good.
Psalms 36:4 He ymagineth mischief vpon his bedde he wil come in no good waye, nor refuse the thyng that is euel.
Psalms 36:5 Thy mercy, O Lorde, reacheth vnto the heauen, and thy faythfulnesse vnto the cloudes.
Psalms 36:6 Thy righteousnesse standeth lyke the strong mountaynes, and thy iudgemente lyke the great depe. Thou Lord preseruest both men and beastes.
Psalms 36:7 How precious is thy mercy, O God, that the chyldren of men maye put their trust vnder the shadowe of thy wynges?
Psalms 36:8 They shalbe satisfied with the plenteousnesse of thy house, and thou shalte geue them drynke of the ryuer of thy pleasures.
Psalms 36:9 For by the is the wel of lyfe, and in thy lyght, shall we se lyght.
Psalms 36:10 O sprede forth thy louing kyndnesse vnto them that knowe the, and thy ryghteousnesse vnto them that are true of hert.
Psalms 36:11 O let not the fote of pride ouertake me, O let not the hande of the vngodly caste me doune.
Psalms 36:12 As for wycked doers, they fall, they are cast doune, and are not able to stande.

CHAPTER: 37

Psalms 37:1 A Psalme of Dauid. Fret not thy selfe at the vngodly be not thou enuious agaynst the euel doers.
Psalms 37:2 For they shall soone be cutte doune lyke the grasse, & be wythered euen as the grene herbe.
Psalms 37:3 Put thou thy trust in the Lorde, and be doyng good: so shalt thou dwel in the lande, & verely it shall fede the.
Psalms 37:4 Delyte thou in the Lorde, & he shall geue the thy hertes desire.
Psalms 37:5 Committe thy waye vnto the Lorde, sette thy hope in hym, and he shall brynge it too passe.
Psalms 37:6 He shal make thy righteousnesse as cleare as the light, & thy iust dealynge as the noone daye.
Psalms 37:7 Holde the styl in the Lord, and abyde paciently vpon hym: but greue not thy selfe at one that hath prosperytie, and lyueth in abhominacion.
Psalms 37:8 Leaue of from wrath, let go displeasure, let not thy gelousy moue the also to do euell.
Psalms 37:9 For wycked doers shalbe roted oute, but they that paciently abyde the Lord, shall enheret the lande.
Psalms 37:10 Suffre yet a litle whyle, and the vngodly shalbe cleane gone: thou shalt loke after hys place, and he shalbe awaye.
Psalms 37:11 But the meke spreted shall possesse the earth, and haue pleasure in muche rest.
Psalms 37:12 The vngodly layeth wayte for the iust, & gnassheth vpon him with his tethe.
Psalms 37:13 But the Lord laugheth him to scorne, for he seyth that his daye is commyng.
Psalms 37:14 The vngodly drawe oute the swerde & bende their bowe, to caste doune the simple and poore, and to slaye suche as go the right waye.
Psalms 37:15 Neuertheles, their swerde shal go thorow their owne hert, and theyr bowe shalbe broken.
Psalms 37:16 A small thinge that the righteous hath, is better then great ryches of the vngodly.
Psalms 37:17 For the armes of the vngodly shalbe broken, but the Lorde vpholdeth the ryghteous.
Psalms 37:18 The Lord knoweth the dayes of the Godly and their inheritaunce endureth for euer.
Psalms 37:19 They shall not be confounded in the perlous tyme, and in the daies of derth thei shal haue ynough.
Psalms 37:20 As for the vngodly, they shall perysh: and when the enemyes of the Lorde are in theyr floures, they shall consume, yea, euen as the smoke shall they consume awaye.
Psalms 37:21 The vngodly boroweth and payeth not agayne, but the righteous is mercyfull and lyberall.
Psalms 37:22 Such as be blessed of hym, shall possesse the lande: and they whome he curseth, shalbe roted out.
Psalms 37:23 The Lorde ordreth a good mans goynge, and hath pleasure in hys waye.
Psalms 37:24 Though he fall, he shall not be hurte, for the Lorde vpholdeth him with his hande.
Psalms 37:25 I haue bene yonge, and now am olde: yet sawe I neuer the righteous forsaken, nor hys sede to seke their bread.
Psalms 37:26 The righteous is euer mercifull, and lendeth gently, therfore shal his sede be blessed.
Psalms 37:27 Fle from euell, and do the thynge that is good, so shalt thou dwell for euer.
Psalms 37:28 For the Lorde loueth the thynge that is ryght, he forsaketh not hys sainctes, but thei shalbe preserued for euermore: as for the sede of the vngodly, it shalbe roted out.
Psalms 37:29 Yea, the righteous shal possesse the land, and dwell therein for euer.
Psalms 37:30 The mouth of the righteous is exercised in wysdome, and hys tonge talketh of iudgement.
Psalms 37:31 The lawe of his God is in his hert, therfore shall not his fotesteppes slyde.
Psalms 37:32 The vngodly seyth the righteous, & goeth aboute to slaye hym.
Psalms 37:33 But the Lorde will not leaue him in hys handes, nor condempne him when he is iudged.
Psalms 37:34 Hope thou in the Lord, & kepe his waye, & he shal so promote the, that thou shalt haue the lande by enheritaunce, and se, when the vngodly shall perishe.
Psalms 37:35 I my selfe haue sene the vngodly in great power, & florishinge lyke a grene baye tree:
Psalms 37:36 but when I went by, lo, he was gone: I sought hym, but he coulde no where be founde.
Psalms 37:37 Kepe innocency, and take hede vnto the thynge that is ryghte, for that shall brynge a man peace at the last.
Psalms 37:38 As for the transgressours, they shall peryshe together, and the vngodly shall be roted out at the laste.
Psalms 37:39 The helpe of the righteous commeth of the Lorde, he is their strength in the tyme of trouble.
Psalms 37:40 The Lorde shall stande by them, and saue them: he shall delyuer them from the vngodly and helpe them, because they put their truste in hym.

CHAPTER: 38

Psalms 38:1 To the chaunter, to brynge too remembraunce. Pvtte me not too rebuke (Oh Lorde) in thyne anger: Oh chasten me not in thy heuy displeasure.
Psalms 38:2 For thyne arrowes stycke fast in me, and thy hande presseth me sore.
Psalms 38:3 There is no whole parte in my body, because of thy displeasure: there is no reste in my bones, by reason of my synnes.
Psalms 38:4 For my wyckednesses are gone ouer my head, and are like a sore burthen, to heuy for me to beare.
Psalms 38:5 My woundes styncke and are corrupte, thorow my folyshnesse.
Psalms 38:6 I am broughte into so greate trouble and mysery, that I go mournynge all the daye longe.
Psalms 38:7 For my loynes are cleane dryed vp, and there is no whole parte in my body.
Psalms 38:8 I am feble & sore smytten, I roare for the very disquietnes of my hert.
Psalms 38:9 Lorde, thou knowest all my desyre, & my gronynge is not hyd from the.
Psalms 38:10 My hert panteth, my strengthe hath fayled me, and the lighte of myne eyes is gone fro me.
Psalms 38:11 My louers and frendes stande lokynge vpon my trouble, and my kynsmen are gone afarre of.
Psalms 38:12 They that sought after my lyfe, and to do me euell, spake of lyes & ymagined disceate all the daye longe.
Psalms 38:13 As for me, I was lyke a deaf man & herde not: and as one that were domme, not openynge hys mouth.
Psalms 38:14 I am become as a man that heareth not: and that can make no resistaunce wyth hys mouth.
Psalms 38:15 For in the, O Lorde, is my truste, thou shalt heare me, O Lorde my God.
Psalms 38:16 My desyre is, that myne enemyes triumphe not ouer me: for if my foote slyppe, they reioyse greatly agaynst me.
Psalms 38:17 I am ready to suffre trouble, and my heuinesse is euer in my sight.
Psalms 38:18 For I confesse my wyckednesse, and my synne greueth me.
Psalms 38:19 But myne enemyes lyue, & are mightye: and they that hate me without a cause, are many in numbre.
Psalms 38:20 They that rewarde me euel for good, speake euell of me, because I folowe the thyng that good is.
Psalms 38:21 Forsake me not (O Lord my God) O go not farre fro me.
Psalms 38:22 Haste the to helpe me, O Lorde my succoure.

CHAPTER: 39

Psalms 39:1 To the chanter for Iduthun, a Psalme of Dauid. I sayde: I wyll kepe my wayes that I offende not in my tonge And so I shutte my mouthe whyle the vngodly layed wait for me.
Psalms 39:2 I helde my tonge, I was domme, I kept sylence, yea euen from good wordes, but it was payne and grefe to me.
Psalms 39:3 My hert was hote within me, and whyle I was thus musyng, the fyre kindled: so that I spake wyth my tong.
Psalms 39:4 Lorde, let me knowe myne ende, and the numbre of my dayes: that I may be certified what I want.
Psalms 39:5 Behold, thou hast made my dayes a span longe, and my lyfe as it were nothynge before the. O how vayne are all men liuing? Selah
Psalms 39:6 Yea euery man walketh as it were a shadow, and disquieth him selfe in vayne: he heapeth vp ryches, and can not tell to whome he gathereth them.
Psalms 39:7 And now Lorde wherin shall I comforte me? my hope is in the.
Psalms 39:8 Delyuer me from all myne offences, and make me not a scorne vnto the folish.
Psalms 39:9 I kepe sylence, and open not my mouthe, for thou hast done it.
Psalms 39:10 Turne thy plages awaye fro me, for I am consumed thorow the feare of thy hande.
Psalms 39:11 When thou punishest man for sinne. thou chastenest him: so that his beutye consumeth awaye, lyke as it were a moth. O how vayne are al men? Selah.
Psalms 39:12 Heare my prayer O Lorde, and consyder my callynge: shewe not thy selfe as though thou sawest not my teares. For I am a straunger and pilgrymme wyth the, as all my forefathers were.
Psalms 39:13 Oh spare me a lytle that I may refreshe my selfe, before I goo hence, and be no more sene.

CHAPTER: 40

Psalms 40:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. I waited pacyently for the Lord, which enclined hym selfe vnto me: and herd my callynge.
Psalms 40:2 He brought me out of the horryble pitte, out of the myre and claye: he set my fete vpon the rocke, & ordred my goinges.
Psalms 40:3 He hath put a newe songe in my mouthe, euen a thanckes geuynge vnto oure God. Many men seing this shal feare the Lord, and put their trust in hym.
Psalms 40:4 Blessed is the man that setteth his hope in the Lorde, and turneth not vnto the proud, & to such as go aboute with lyes.
Psalms 40:5 O Lorde my God, greate are thy wonderous worckes whiche thou haste done: and in thy thoughtes toward vs there maye none be likened vnto the. I wold declare them, and speake of them: but they are so manye, that they can not be tolde.
Psalms 40:6 Sacryfyce and offerynge thou wouldeste not haue but a bodye haste thou ordeyned me: burnt offerynges and sacrifyce for synne thou hast not alowed.
Psalms 40:7 Then sayde I: Lo, I come. In the begynnynge of the boke is it written of me,
Psalms 40:8 that I shoulde fulfyl thy wyl O my God, and that am I content to do: yea thy lawe is wythin my hert.
Psalms 40:9 I will preach of thy ryghtuousnesse in the great congregacyon: Lo. I wyl not refraine my lippes, O Lorde, and that thou knowest.
Psalms 40:10 I do not hyde thy ryghtuousnes in my hert, my talkinge is of thy trueth and sauing health: I kepe not thy louyng mercy & faythfulnesse backe from the greate congregacyon.
Psalms 40:11 Turne not thou thy mercy fro me O Lord but let thy louynge kyndnesse and trueth alwaye preseue me.
Psalms 40:12 For innumerable troubles are come about me: my synnes haue taken suche holde vpon me that I am not able to loke vp: yea they are mo in number then the heares of my head and my hert hath fayled me.
Psalms 40:13 O Lorde, let it be thy pleasure to delyuer me make hast (Lord) to help me.
Psalms 40:14 Let them be ashamed and confunded, that seke after my soule, to destroye it: let them fall backwarde and be put to confusion, that wish me euell.
Psalms 40:15 Let them soone be broughte to shame, that crye ouer me, there there.
Psalms 40:16 But let all those that seke the, be ioyfull and glad in the: & let al such as delyte in thye sauyng health, say alway: the Lord be praised.
Psalms 40:17 As for me, I am poore and in miserye, but the Lord careth for me. Thou art my helper and redemer, make no long tariyng, O my God.

CHAPTER: 41

Psalms 41:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid. Blessed is he, that consydereth the poore: the Lord shal deliuer him in the tyme of trouble.
Psalms 41:2 The Lord shal preserue him & kepe him aliue: he shall make him to prospere vpon earth, and shall not delyuer him into the wyl of his enemeyes.
Psalms 41:3 The Lord shal refresh him, when he lyeth sicke vpon his bed, yea thou makest hys bed in al his sicknesse.
Psalms 41:4 I sayd: Lord be mercifull vnto me, heale my soule, for I haue synned agaynst the.
Psalms 41:5 Myne enemyes speake euel vpon me: when shal he die, and his name perishe.
Psalms 41:6 Though he came in to se, yet meaned he falsede in his hert, heapyng myscheyfe vpon hym selfe.
Psalms 41:7 All they that hate me, runne together agaynst me, and ymagyn euell against me.
Psalms 41:8 They haue geuen a wycked sentence vpon me: when he lyeth, he shall ryse vp no more.
Psalms 41:9 Yea euen myne owne famylyer frende, whom I trusted, whiche dyd eate my breade hath lyfte vp his hele agaynste me.
Psalms 41:10 But be thou mercyful vnto me (O Lord) rayse thou me vp, and I shall reward them
Psalms 41:11 By this I know thou fauourest me, that. my enemy shal not triumphe ouer me.
Psalms 41:12 Thou hast vpholden me because of my innocency, and set me before thy face for euer.
Psalms 41:13 O blessed be the Lorde God of Israel, from hence forth and for euermore. Amen. Amen.

CHAPTER: 42

Psalms 42:1 To the chaunter, a monicion of the sonnes of Corah. Like as the hert desyreth the water brokes, so longeth my soule after the, O God.
Psalms 42:2 My soule is a thurste for God, yea euen for the lyuynge God: when shall I come, and behold the face of God?
Psalms 42:3 My teares are my meate daye and nighte whyle it is daylye sayed vnto me: where is now thy God?
Psalms 42:4 Now when I thincke ther vpon, I poure out my hert by my self: for I would faine go hence wyth the multytude and passe ouer wt them vnto the house of God, in the voyce of prayse and thankes geuynge, amonge suche as kepe holy daye.
Psalms 42:5 Why art thou so full of heuynes, (O my soule) and why arte thou so vnquyet wythin me? O put thy trust in God, for I wyl yet geue him thankes, for the helpe of his countenance
Psalms 42:6 My God, my soule is vexed wythin me: therfore I remembre the lande of Iordaine, and the litle hyl of Hermonim.
Psalms 42:7 One depe calleth another wyth the voyce of thy whistles, al thy waues and water floudes are gone ouer me.
Psalms 42:8 The Lorde hath promysed hys louynge kyndnesse daylye, therfore will I prayse him in the night season, and make my prayer vnto the God of my lyfe.
Psalms 42:9 I wyll say vnto God my stony rock: why host thou forgotten me? why go I thus heuely, whyle the enemye oppresseth me?
Psalms 42:10 Whyle my bones are broken, whyle mine enemyes cast me in the teeth, daylye saiynge vnto me: where is now thy God?
Psalms 42:11 Why art thou so heuy (O my soule) & why art thou so disquieted within me? O put thy trust in God, for I wyll yet thanke hym for the helpe of hys countenaunce, and because he is my God.

CHAPTER: 43

Psalms 43:1 Geue sentence vpon me (O God) and defende my cause agaynst the vnholy people: Oh delyuer me from the dysceatefull, and wycked man.
Psalms 43:2 For thou (O God) art my strength: why hast thou shut me from the? Why go I then so heuely, whyle the enemye oppresseth me?
Psalms 43:3 Oh sende out thy light any thy truth, that they maye leade me and brynge me vnto thy holy hyll, and to thy dwellyng.
Psalms 43:4 That I maye go into the aulter of God, euen vnto the God whyche is my ioye & pleasure, and vpon the harpe to geue thankes vnto the, O God, my God.
Psalms 43:5 Why art thou so heuy (O my soule) and why art thou so disquyeted wythin me? O put thy trust in God, for I wyll yet geue hym thanckes for the helpe of hys countenaunce, and because he is my God.

CHAPTER: 44

Psalms 44:1 To the chaunter an instruccyon of the sonnes of Corah. We haue herde with our eares (O God) our fathers haue told vs, what thou hast don in their tyme of olde
Psalms 44:2 Howe thou hast dryuen out the Heythen wyth thy hand, and planted them in: how thou hast destroyed the nacions and cast them out.
Psalms 44:3 For they gat not the lande in possessyon thorowe their owne swearde, neyther was it their owne arme that helped them. But thy ryght hande, thyne arme and the lyght of thy countenaunce, because thou haddest a fauoure vnto them.
Psalms 44:4 Thou arte the Kynge and my God, thou sendest helpe vnto Iacob.
Psalms 44:5 Thorow the, wyll we ouerthrow our enemyes: and in thy name wyll we treade them vnder, that ryse vp agaynst vs.
Psalms 44:6 For I wyll not trust in my bowe, it is not my sweard that shall helpe me.
Psalms 44:7 But it is thou that sauest vs from our enemyes: and puttest them to confusyon that hate vs.
Psalms 44:8 We wyll alway make our boast of God, and prayse thy name for euer. Selah.
Psalms 44:9 But now thou forsakest vs, and puttest vs to confusyon, and goest not forth wyth oure Hostes.
Psalms 44:10 Thou makest vs to turne oure backes vpon oure enemyes, so that they which hate vs spoyle our goodes.
Psalms 44:11 Thou lettest vs be eaten vp lyke shepe, & scaterest vs among the Heathen.
Psalms 44:12 Thou sellest thy people for naught, and takest no money for them.
Psalms 44:13 Thou makeste vs to be rebuked of oure neyghboures, to be laughed to scorne & had in derision, of them that are rounde about v
Psalms 44:14 Thou hast made vs, a very by word among the Heathen, and that the people shake their heades at vs.
Psalms 44:15 My confusion is dayly before me, and the shame of my face couereth me.
Psalms 44:16 For the voyce of the sclaunderer and blasphemer, for the enemye and auenger.
Psalms 44:17 All this is come vpon vs, and yet haue we not forgotten the ner behaued oure selues vnfaythfully in thy couenaunt.
Psalms 44:18 Oure herte is not turned backe, neyther our steps gone out of thy way.
Psalms 44:19 For thou hast smitten vs in the place of dragones, and couered vs with the shadow of death.
Psalms 44:20 If we had forgotten the name of our God and holden vp oure handes to any straunge God.
Psalms 44:21 Should not God fynde it out? for he knoweth the very secretes of the herte.
Psalms 44:22 But for thy sake we are kylled all the daye longe, and are counted as shepe apoynted to be slayne.
Psalms 44:23 Vp Lorde, why slepest thou? wake, and cast vs not of for euer.
Psalms 44:24 Wherfore hydest thy face? wylte thou cleane forget oure mysery and oppression
Psalms 44:25 For oure soule is brought low euen vnto the dust, and our bely cleueth vnto the ground
Psalms 44:26 Arise O Lord, helpe vs and delyuer vs for thy mercy sake.

CHAPTER: 45

Psalms 45:1 To the chaunter, vpon Sosanim, an instruccion of the chyldren of Corah, a songe of loue. Mi herte is endytinge of a godd matter, I speake of that, which I haue made of the kynge: My tonge is the penne of a ready wryter.
Psalms 45:2 Thou arte the fayrest amonge the chyldren of men, full of grace are thy lyppes, therfore God blesseth the for euer.
Psalms 45:3 Gyrde the with thy swerde vpon thy thyghe (O thou mightye) with worshippe and renowne.
Psalms 45:4 Good lucke haue thou with thyne honor, ryde on with the trueth, mekenesse & righteousnes: and thy righthand shall teach the wonderfull thynges.
Psalms 45:5 Thy arrowes are sharpe, the people shal be subdued vnto the, euen in the myddest amonge the kynges enemyes.
Psalms 45:6 Thy seate (O God) endureth for euer: the scepter of thy kyngdome is a right scepter.
Psalms 45:7 Thou hast loued righteousnesse, & hated iniquitie: wherfore God (which is thy God) hath anoynted the with the oyle of gladnes aboue thy felowes.
Psalms 45:8 All thy garmentes are lyke myrre, Aloes & Cassia, when thou commest out of thine yuerye palaces in thy beutifull glory.
Psalms 45:9 Kynges daughters go in thy goodly aray and vpon thy right hande standeth the quene in a vesture of the most fyne golde.
Psalms 45:10 Herken (O daughter) considre, & enclyne thyne eare: forget thyne owne people, & thy fathers house.
Psalms 45:11 So shall the kynge haue pleasure in thy beuty, for he is thy Lorde, & thou shalte worshyp hym.
Psalms 45:12 The daughters of Tire shalbe there with gyftes, the ryche amonge the people shall make their supplication before the.
Psalms 45:13 The kynges daughter is all glorious within, her clothyng is of wrought golde.
Psalms 45:14 She shalbe brought vnto the kyng in rayment of nedle worke, & maidens after her: such as be next her shalbe brought vnto the.
Psalms 45:15 Wyth ioye and gladnesse shall they be brought, & go into the kynges palace.
Psalms 45:16 In steade of thy fathers thou hast gotten chyldren, whome thou shalt make princes in all landes.
