Psalms 45:17 I wyll remembre thy name from one generacion to another: therfore shall the people geue thankes vnto the, worlde withoute ende.

CHAPTER: 46

Psalms 46:1 To the chaunter, a songe of the children of Corah vpon almuth. In oure troubles & aduersitye, we haue founde, that God is oure refuge, oure strength and helpe.
Psalms 46:2 Therfore wyl we not feare though the earth fell, and though the hylles were caryed into the myddest of the sea.
Psalms 46:3 Though the waters of the sea raged and were neuer so troublous, and thoughe the mountaynes shoke at the tempest of the same. Selah.
Psalms 46:4 For there is a floude, which with hys ryuers reioyseth the cytye of God, the holy dwellyng of the moost hyest.
Psalms 46:5 God is in the middest of her, therfore shal she not be remoued: for God helpeth her, & that right early.
Psalms 46:6 The Heythen are madde, the kingdomes make muche a do: but when he sheweth hys voyce, the earth melteth awaye.
Psalms 46:7 The Lord of hoostes is with vs, the God of Iacob is oure defence. Selah.
Psalms 46:8 O come hither, and beholde the woorkes of the LORD, what destruccions he hathe brought vpon the earth.
Psalms 46:9 He hath made warres to cease in all the worlde: he hathe broken the bowe, he hathe knapped the speare in sonder, and brente the charettes in the fyre.
Psalms 46:10 Be styll then and confesse that I am God I will be exalted amonge the Heythen, and I will be exalted vpon earth.
Psalms 46:11 The Lord of hostes is with vs, the God of Iacob is our defence. Selah.

CHAPTER: 47

Psalms 47:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of the chyldren of Corah. O clappe youre handes together (all ye people) O synge vnto God with the voyce of thankesgeuynge.
Psalms 47:2 For the Lord the most hyest is to be feared, and he is the great kyng vpon all the earth.
Psalms 47:3 He shal subdue the people vnder vs, and the Heythen vnder oure fete.
Psalms 47:4 He choseth vs for an heretage, the beutye of Iacob whome he loued. Selah.
Psalms 47:5 God is gone vp with a mery noyse, & the Lord with the sownde of the trompet.
Psalms 47:6 O singe prayses, singe prayses vnto God O singe prayses, singe prayses vnto oure kynge.
Psalms 47:7 For God is kyng of all the earth, O sing prayses vnto hym with vnderstandynge.
Psalms 47:8 God is kyng ouer the Heythen, God sitteth in hys holy seate.
Psalms 47:9 The prynces of the people are gathered together vnto the God of Abraham: for God is farre hyer exalted, then the mighty lordes of the earth.

CHAPTER: 48

Psalms 48:1 A songe of a Psalme of the chyldren of Corah. Greate is the Lorde & hyely too be praysed, in the cytye of oure God, euen vpon hys holy hyl.
Psalms 48:2 The hyll of Syon is lyke a fayre plante, whereof all the lande reioyseth: vpon the north side lyeth the cytye of the great kyng.
Psalms 48:3 God is well knowen in her palaces, that he is the defence of the same.
Psalms 48:4 For lo, kynges are gathered, and gone by together.
Psalms 48:5 They marueled, to se suche thynges: they were astonied, and sodenly cast doune.
Psalms 48:6 Feare came there vpon them, and sorow as vpon a woman in her trauayle.
Psalms 48:7 Thou shalt breake the shyppes of the sea, thorow the East wynde.
Psalms 48:8 Lyke as we haue herde, so se we in the cytye of the Lord of hoostes, in the citie of oure God. God vpholdeth the same for euer. Selah.
Psalms 48:9 We wayte for thy louynge kyndnesse (O God) in the middest of thy temple.
Psalms 48:10 O God, according vnto thy name, so is thy praise vnto the worldes ende: thy right hande is full of righteousnes.
Psalms 48:11 Oh let the mount Sion reioyse, and the daughters of Iuda be glad because of iudgementes.
Psalms 48:12 Walke about Sion, go rounde about her and tell her towres.
Psalms 48:13 Marke well her walles, sette vp her houses. that it may be tolde them that come after.
Psalms 48:14 For this God is our God for euer & euer, and he shall alwaye be oure guyde.

CHAPTER: 49

Psalms 49:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of the chyldren of Corah. O heare thys, all ye people: pondre it wel, all ye that dwel vpon the earth.
Psalms 49:2 Hye & lowe, & rych & poore, one wyth another.
Psalms 49:3 My mouth shall speake of wysdome, and my hert shall muse of vnderstandynge.
Psalms 49:4 I will enclyne myne eare to the parable, and shewe my darke speach vpon the harpe.
Psalms 49:5 Wherfore should I feare the euel dayes, when the wickednesse of my heles compaseth me rounde aboute?
Psalms 49:6 They that put their trust in their good, & boast theym selfes in the multitude of theyr ryches.
Psalms 49:7 No man may deliuer his brother, nor make agrement vnto hym for God.
Psalms 49:8 For it costeth more to redeme their soules so that he must let that alone for euer.
Psalms 49:9 Yea, though he liue longe, and se not the graue.
Psalms 49:10 For it shalbe sene, that such wyse men shal dye and perysh together, as wel as the ignoraunt and folysh, and leue their goodes for other.
Psalms 49:11 Loke what is in their houses, it contynueth still: their dwellyng places endure from one generacion to another, and are called after their owne names vpon the earth.
Psalms 49:12 Neuerthelesse man abydeth not in suche honour, but is compared vnto the brute beastes, and becommeth lyke vnto them.
Psalms 49:13 This waye of theirs is very folyshnesse, and yet their posteritie prayse it wyth theyr mouth. Selah.
Psalms 49:14 They lye in the hell like shepe, death shall gnawe vpon theim, and the righteous shall haue dominacion of theim in the mornynge by tymes: their strength shall consume, and hell shalbe their dwellynge.
Psalms 49:15 But God shall deliuer my soule from the power of hell, when he receyueth me. Selah.
Psalms 49:16 O be not thou afraied, when one is made ryche, & the glory of hys house increased.
Psalms 49:17 For he shall cary nothynge away wyth hym when he dyeth, neither shall his pompe folowe hym.
Psalms 49:18 Whyle he lyueth, he is counted an happy man: and so long as he is in prosperitie, men speake good of hym.
Psalms 49:19 But when he foloweth his fathers generacion, he shall neuer se light any more.
Psalms 49:20 When a man is in honour and hath no vnderstandinge, he is compared vnto the brute beastes, and becommeth lyke vnto them.

CHAPTER: 50

Psalms 50:1 A Psalme of Asaph. The Lord euen the mighty God hath spoken, & called the world from the risyng vp of the sunne vnto the goynge doune of the same.
Psalms 50:2 Out of Sion apeareth the glorious beuty of God.
Psalms 50:3 Oure God shal come, and not kepe silence there goeth before him a consuming fyre, and a mighty tempest round about him.
Psalms 50:4 He shall call the heauens from aboue, and the earth, that he may iudge his people.
Psalms 50:5 Gather my saynctes together vnto me, those that set more by the couenant then by any offering.
Psalms 50:6 And the heauens shal declare his rightuousnes, for God is iudge him selfe. Selah
Psalms 50:7 Heare, O my people: let me speake, let me testify among you, O Israell: I am God, euen thy God.
Psalms 50:8 I reproue the not because of thy sacryfice thy burnteofferynges are allwaye before me.
Psalms 50:9 I wil take no bullockes out of thy house, nor gotes out of thy foldes.
Psalms 50:10 For all the beastes of the felde are myne, and thousandes of cattell vppon the hylles.
Psalms 50:11 I know al the foules vpon the mountaynes, and the wylde beastes of the felde are in my sight.
Psalms 50:12 If I be hongry, I wyll not tell the: for the whole worlde is myne, & all that therein is.
Psalms 50:13 Thynkest thou, that I will eate the fleshe of oxen, or drynke the bloude of goates?
Psalms 50:14 Offre vnto God prayse and thankesgeuynge, and paye thy vowes vnto the most hyest.
Psalms 50:15 And call vpon me in the tyme of trouble, so wyll I heare the, that thou shalte thanke me.
Psalms 50:16 But vnto the vngodly sayeth God? Why doest thou preach my lawes, and takest my couenaunt in thy mouth?
Psalms 50:17 Where as thou hatest to be refourmed, and castest my woordes behynde the?
Psalms 50:18 If thou seist a thefe, thou runnest wyth him, and art partaker with the aduouterers.
Psalms 50:19 Thou lettest thy mouthe speake wickednesse, and thy tonge paynteth disceate.
Psalms 50:20 Thou sittest & speakest agaynste thy brother, yea, & sclaundrest thyne owne mothers sonne.
Psalms 50:21 This thou doest, whyle I holde my tonge and thynkest me to be euen suche one as thy self: but I wyll reproue the, and set my selfe agaynst the.
Psalms 50:22 O considre this, ye that forget God: lest I plucke you awaye, and there be none too delyuer you.
Psalms 50:23 Who so offreth me thankes and prayse, he honoureth me: & this is the way, wherby I wyll shewe hym the sauynge healthe of God.

CHAPTER: 51

Psalms 51:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauid, when the prophet Nathan came vnto hym, after he was gone into Bethsabe. Haue mercy vpon me (O God) after thy goodnes, & according vnto thy great mercyes, do awaye myne offences.
Psalms 51:2 Wash me well fro my wickednesse, and clense me fro my synne.
Psalms 51:3 For I knowledge my fautes, & my synne is euer before me.
Psalms 51:4 Agaynst the only, agaynst the haue I sinned, & done euel in thy sight: that thou mightest be iustified in thy saynges, and shouldest ouercome when thou art iudged.
Psalms 51:5 Beholde, I was borne in wickednesse, & in synne hath my mother conceyued me.
Psalms 51:6 But lo, thou hast a pleasure in the trueth, and hast shewed me secrete wisdome.
Psalms 51:7 O purge me with Isope, and I shall be cleane: wash thou me, and I shalbe whyter then snowe.
Psalms 51:8 Oh let me heare of ioye & gladnesse, that the bones which thou hast broken, maye reioyse.
Psalms 51:9 Turne thy face from my synnes, & put oute all my misdedes.
Psalms 51:10 Make me a cleane hert, O God, & renue a right sprete within me.
Psalms 51:11 Cast me not awaye from thy presence, & take not thy holy sprete from me.
Psalms 51:12 O geue me the comforte of thy helpe agayne, and stablish me with thy sprete.
Psalms 51:13 Then shall I teache thy wayes vnto the wicked, that sinners may be conuerted vnto the.
Psalms 51:14 Deliuer me from bloude giltinesse, O God, thou that art the God of my health, that my tonge may prayse thy righteousnesse.
Psalms 51:15 Open my lyppes, O LORD, that my mouth maye shewe thy prayse.
Psalms 51:16 For if thou haddest pleasure in sacrifice, I wolde geue it the: but thou delytest not in burntofferinges.
Psalms 51:17 The sacryfice of God is a troubled spirit a broken and a contrite hert, O God, shalte thou not despyse.
Psalms 51:18 O be fauourable gracyous vnto Syon, that the walles of Ierusalem maye be buylded,
Psalms 51:19 For when shalt thou be pleased wyth the sacrifice of ryghtuousnes, with the burntofferinges and oblations: then shal they laye bullockes vpon thine alter.

CHAPTER: 52

Psalms 52:1 To the chaunter, an exortacyon of Dauid when Doeg the Edomite came to Saul, and shewed hym, sayinge: Dauid is come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thy self, thou Tyrraunt, that thou canste do myschiefe? Wher as the goodnesse of God endureth yet dayly.
Psalms 52:2 Thy tonge ymagyneth wyckednesse, and with lyes it cutteth like a sharpe rasoure.
Psalms 52:3 Thou loueste vngratiousnesse more then good, to talke of lyes more then ryghtuousnesse. Selah.
Psalms 52:4 Thou louest to speake al wordes that may do hurte. O thou false tonge.
Psalms 52:5 Therfore shall God cleane destroye the, smyte the in peces, pluke the out of thy dwellynge, and rote the out of the lande of the lyuynge. Selah.
Psalms 52:6 The rightuous shal se this, and feare, and laugh him to scorne,
Psalms 52:7 Lo, this is the man, that toke not God for his strength but trusted vnto the multitud of his riches, & was myghty in his wickednes.
Psalms 52:8 As for me, I am lyke a grene olyue tree in the house of God: my truste is in the tender mercy of God for euer and euer.
Psalms 52:9 I wyll alwaye geue thankes vnto the, for that thou hast done: & wil hope in thy name, for thy sayntes lyke it wel.

CHAPTER: 53

Psalms 53:1 To the chaunter vpon Mahalath, an instruccyon of Dauid. The folysh bodyes saye in their hertes: Tush, there is no God. Corrupte are they & become abhomynable in their wyckednesse: there is not one, that doth good.
Psalms 53:2 God loked downe from heauen vpon the chyldren of men, to se if there were any that would vnderstand, or seke after God.
Psalms 53:3 But they are all gone out of the waye they are al become vnprofitable: ther is none that doth good, no not one.
Psalms 53:4 How can they haue vnderstandynge, that are the worckers of wyckednes, eatynge vp my people as it were breade, and call not vpon God?
Psalms 53:5 They are afrayed, where no feare is: for God breaketh the bones of them that beseige the: thou puttest them to confusion, for God despiseth them.
Psalms 53:6 Oh that the sauynge healthe were geuen vnto Israel out of Sion: Oh that the Lorde woulde delyuer his people out of captiuity. Then shoulde Iacob reioyse, and Israell should be ryght glad.

CHAPTER: 54

Psalms 54:1 To the chaunter in Neginoth, an instruccyon of Dauyd, when the Zephytes came and sayed vnto Saul: Dauid is hydde amongest vs. Helpe me (O God) for thy names sake, and deliuer me in thy strength.
Psalms 54:2 Heare my prayer (O God) considre the wordes of my mouth.
Psalms 54:3 For straungers are rysen vp agaynst me, and the mighty (which haue not God before their eyes) seke after my soule. Selah.
Psalms 54:4 But lo, God is my helper: it is he that vpholdeth my soule.
Psalms 54:5 He shall reward euel vnto myne enemies and in thy trueth shalt thou destroy them.
Psalms 54:6 A fre will offerynge will I geue the, and prayse thy name O Lorde, because it is so comfortable.
Psalms 54:7 For thou hast deliuered me out of all my trouble, so that myne eye seith his desire vpon myne enemyes.

CHAPTER: 55

Psalms 55:1 To the chaunter in Neginoth, an instruccion of Dauid. Heare my prayer, O God, and hyde not thy self fro my petycion.
Psalms 55:2 Take hede vnto me & heare me, how piteously I mourne and complayne.
Psalms 55:3 The enemye cryeth so, and the vngodly commeth on so fast: for they are mynded too do me some mischief, so maliciously are they set agaynst me.
Psalms 55:4 My hert is heuy within me, and the feare of death is fallen vpon me.
Psalms 55:5 Fearfulnesse and tremblynge are come vpon me, and an horrible drede hathe ouerwhelmed me.
Psalms 55:6 And I sayde: O that I had wynges lyke a doue, that I might fle somwhere, and be at rest.
Psalms 55:7 Lo, then wolde I get me awaye farre of, and remayne in the wildernesse. Selah.
Psalms 55:8 I wolde make haste to escape, from the stormy wynde and tempest.
Psalms 55:9 Destroye their tonges (O Lorde) and deuyde them, for I se vnrighteousnes & stryfe in the cytye.
Psalms 55:10 Thys goeth daye and nyght aboute the walles, mischief and vyce are in the middest of it.
Psalms 55:11 Wickednesse is therin, disceate and gyle go not out of her stretes.
Psalms 55:12 If it were myne enemye that reuyled me, I could beare it: or if one that ought me euel wyll dyd threaten me, I wolde hyde my self from hym.
Psalms 55:13 But it is thou my companyon, my gyde & myne owne familier frende.
Psalms 55:14 We had swete and secrete communicacion together in the house of God.
Psalms 55:15 Let death come hastely vppon them, and let them goo doune quyck into hell, for wickednes is amonge theym in their dwellynges.
Psalms 55:16 As for me, I will call vnto God, and the Lord shall helpe me.
Psalms 55:17 In the euenynge, mornyng and at noone daye will I mourne and complayne: and he shall heare my voyce.
Psalms 55:18 It is he that deliuereth my soule in peace, from them that laye wayte for me: for they are many agaynst me.
Psalms 55:19 Yea, euen God that endureth for euer, shall heare me, and bring them doune. Selah. For they will not turne: and why? they feare not God.
Psalms 55:20 Yea, they laye handes vpon such as be at peace with hym, & so they breake hys couenaunt.
Psalms 55:21 Their mouthes are softer then butter, & yet haue they battayll in theyr mynde: theyr wordes are smoother then oyle, and yet be they very swerdes.
Psalms 55:22 O cast thy burthen, or care, vpon the Lord he shall norysh the, and not leaue the ryghteous in vnquyetnesse.
Psalms 55:23 But as for them, thou (O God) shalt cast doune into the pytte of destruccion. The bloudthrustye & disceatfull shall not lyue out half their dayes. Neuerthelesse my trust is in the.

CHAPTER: 56

Psalms 56:1 To the chaunter, vpon the domme stock doue: whiche flyeth ferre of, Michtam of Dauid, when the Phylystynes toke hym in Geth. Be mercifull vnto me (O God) for men will treade me doune: they are dayly fightynge and troublynge me.
Psalms 56:2 Myne enemyes treade me dayly vnder their fete, for they be many that proudly fighte agaynste me.
Psalms 56:3 Neuerthelesse, when I am afrayed, I put my trust in the.
Psalms 56:4 I will comforte my selfe in Gods worde, yea, I will hope in God, & not feare: What can flesh then do vnto me?
Psalms 56:5 They vexe my dayly in my wordes: all that they ymagyne, is to do me euell.
Psalms 56:6 They holde alltogether, & kepe them selues close they marcke my steppes, how they may catch my soule.
Psalms 56:7 But in vayne, for it shall escape them: and why? thou (O God) in thy dyspleasure shalt cast doune suche people.
Psalms 56:8 Thou tellest my flytynges, thou puttest my teares in thy bottel, and numbrest them.
Psalms 56:9 When soeuer I call vpon the, myne enemyes are put to flight: whereby I knowe that thou art my God.
Psalms 56:10 In Goddes worde wyll I reioyse, in the Lordes worde wyll I comforte me.
Psalms 56:11 Yea, in God do I trust, and am not afraied what can man than do vnto me?
Psalms 56:12 Vnto the (O god) wil I paye my vowes, vnto the wyll I geue thankes and prayse.
Psalms 56:13 For thou haste delyuered my soule from death, and my fete frome fallynge, that I may walke before God in the lyght of the lyuyng.

CHAPTER: 57

Psalms 57:1 To the Chaunter destroy not Michtam of Dauid, when he fledde from Saull into the caue. Be mercyfull vnto me, O God, be mercyfull vnto me, for my soule trusteth in the: and vnder the shadow of thy winges shal be my refuge, vntyll wyckednes be ouer past.
Psalms 57:2 I call vnto God the moste hyest, euen the God that shal helpe me vp agayne.
Psalms 57:3 He shal send from heauen, and saue me from the reproue of him that would swalowe my vp. Selah. This shall God sende, for his mercye and faythfulnes sake.
Psalms 57:4 I lye wyth my soule among the cruel lions euen among the chyldren of men, whose teeth are speares and arrowes, and their tonge a sherpe sweard.
Psalms 57:5 Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thy glory aboue al the earthe.
Psalms 57:6 They haue layed a net for my fete, and pressed doune my soule: they haue dygged a pytte before me, and are fallen into it them selues. Selah.
Psalms 57:7 My hert is redy, O God, my herte is ready to synge and geue prayse.
Psalms 57:8 Awake, O my glorye, awake lute and harpe, I my selfe wil awake ryght early.
Psalms 57:9 I wil geue thanckes vnto the, O Lorde, amonge the people, I wyll synge prayses vnto the among the Heithen.
Psalms 57:10 For the greatnes of thy mercye reacheth vnto the heauens, and thy faythfulnes vnto the cloudes.
Psalms 57:11 Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thi glory aboue al the earth.

CHAPTER: 58

Psalms 58:1 To the chaunter Destroye not Michtam of Dauid. If youre myndes be vpon righteousnes in deede, then iudge the thyng that is ryght, O ye sonnes of men,
Psalms 58:2 But ye ymagyn mischefe in youre hertes and youre handes deale with wickednes.
Psalms 58:3 The vngodly are froward, euen from their mothers wombe: as soone as they be borne, they go a stray and speake lyes.
Psalms 58:4 They are as furyous as the serpent, euen lyke the deaf Ader that stoppeth her eares.
Psalms 58:5 That she shoulde not heare the voyce of the charmer, charme he neuer so wisely.
Psalms 58:6 Breake their teeth (O god) in their mouthes, smite the chaft bones of the lions whelpes in sonder, O Lord.
Psalms 58:7 That they maye fall awaye, lyke water that runneth a pace: and that when they shote their arrowes, they maye be broken.
Psalms 58:8 Let them consume away lyke a snaile, and lyke the vntymely frute of a woman, and let them not se the sunne.
Psalms 58:9 Or euer your thorns be sharpe, the wrath shall take them awaye quicke, like a stormy wynde.
Psalms 58:10 The ryghteous shal reioyse when he seith the vengeaunce, and shall washe hys fete in the bloud of the vngodly.
Psalms 58:11 So that men shall saye, verelye there is a rewarde for the righteous: doutles, there is a God that iudgeth the earth.

CHAPTER: 59

Psalms 59:1 To the chaunter destroye not Michtam of Dauid, when Saull sende to watche the house, to thintent to kyll hym. Delyuer me fro myne enemyes (O my God) and defende me from them that rise vp against me.
Psalms 59:2 O delyuer me from the wycked doers, and saue me from the bloudthursty men.
Psalms 59:3 For lo, they lye wayting for my soule: the mighty men are gathered together agaynste me, withoute any offence or faulte of me, O Lorde.
Psalms 59:4 They runne, & prepare them selfes, without my faute: Arise, come thou helpe me, and beholde.
Psalms 59:5 Stande vp O Lord God of hostes, thou God of Israel to viset all Heythen: be not mercifull vnto theym that offende of malicious wyckednesse. Selah.
Psalms 59:6 Let them go to and fro, and runne aboute the cytye, houlynge lyke dogges.
Psalms 59:7 Beholde, they speake (agaynste me) wyth their mouth, swerdes are vnder their lippes for who reproueth them?
Psalms 59:8 But thou (O Lorde) shalte haue theim in derision, thou shalte laugh all Heythen too scorne.
Psalms 59:9 My strength do I ascrybe vnto the, for thou (O God) art my defender.
Psalms 59:10 God sheweth me his goodnes plenteously, God letteth me se my desyre vppon myne enemyes.
Psalms 59:11 Slaye them not, leste my people forget it: but scatre them abroade with thy power, & put them doune, O Lord my defence.
Psalms 59:12 For the synne of their mouth, for the wordes of their lyppes, & because of their pryde, let them be taken: and why? their preachyng is of cursing and lyes.
Psalms 59:13 Consume them in thy wrath, consume them that they maye perishe, and knowe that it is God, whyche ruleth in Iacob and in all the worlde. Selah.
Psalms 59:14 Set them go to and fro, and runne aboute the cytye, houlyng lyke dogges.
Psalms 59:15 Let them runne here and there for meate, and grudge when they haue not ynough.
Psalms 59:16 As for me, I will synge of thy power, and prayse thy mercy by tymes in the mornyng: for thou art my defence & refuge in the tyme of my trouble.
Psalms 59:17 Vnto the (O my strengthe) wyll I singe, for thou (O God) art my defence, & my mercifull God.

CHAPTER: 60

Psalms 60:1 To the chaunter, vpon the rose of wytnesse Michtam of Dauid, for too teache when he fought agaynst Syria of Mesopotania, & Syria of Zoba: and when Ioab turned backe, and slue .xij. thousand Edomytes. in the valley of Salt. O God, thou that hast cast vs out and scatered vs abroade, thou that hast bene so sore displeased at vs, comforte vs agayne.
Psalms 60:2 Thou that hast remoued the lande & deuided it, heale the sores therof, for it shaketh.
Psalms 60:3 Thou hast shewed thy people heuy thinges, thou hast geuen vs a drynke of wyne, that we slombre with all.
Psalms 60:4 Yet hast thou geuen a token for suche as feare the, that they maye caste it vp in the trueth. Selah.
Psalms 60:5 That thy beloued myghte be delyuered, healpe them wyt thy ryghthande, and heare me.
Psalms 60:6 God hath spoken in his Sanctuary (which thing reioyseth me) I wyll deuyde Sichem, and meate aut the valley of Suchoth.
Psalms 60:7 Galaad is myne, Manasses is myne, Ephraim is the strength of myne head, Iuda is my Captayne.
Psalms 60:8 Moab is my washpotte, ouer Edom will I stretche oute my shoue, Phylystea shalbe glad of me.
Psalms 60:9 Who will leade me into the strong cytie? Who will bryng me into Edom?
Psalms 60:10 Shalt not thou do it O God, thou that hast cast out: thou God, that wenteste not out with our hostes?
Psalms 60:11 O be thou our helpe in trouble, for vayne is the helpe of man.
Psalms 60:12 Thorow God we shal do great actes, for it is he that shall treade downe oure enemies

CHAPTER: 61

Psalms 61:1 To the chaunter vpon Neginoth, of Dauid Heare my crying (O god) geue hede vnto my prayer.
Psalms 61:2 From the endes of the earth will I call vnto the, when my herte is in trouble:
Psalms 61:3 Oh sette me vp vpon an hye rocke. For thou art my hope, a strong tower for me agaynst the enemye.
Psalms 61:4 I wyll dwell in thy tabernacle for euer, that I maye be safe vnder the couerynge of thy wynges. Selah.
Psalms 61:5 For thou, O Lord, hast harde my desyres, thou hast geuen an heretage vnto those that feare thy name.
Psalms 61:6 Thou shalte graunte the Kynge a longe lyfe, that his yeares may endure thorow out all generacyons.
Psalms 61:7 That he maye dwel before God for euer: Oh let thy louynge mercy and faythfulnes preserue hym.
Psalms 61:8 So wyl I al away syng prayses vnto thy name, that I may dayly perfourme my vowes.

CHAPTER: 62

Psalms 62:1 To the chaunter, for by Iduthun a Psalme of Dauyd. My soule wayteth onely vpon God, for of hym commeth my helpe.
Psalms 62:2 He only is my strength, my saluation, my defence, so that I shal not greatly fall.
Psalms 62:3 How longe wyll ye ymagyn myschiefe agaynste euerye man? ye shalbe slayne all the sorte of you: yea as a tottrynge wall shall ye be, and lyke a broken hedge.
Psalms 62:4 Their deuyce is only how to put hym out, their delite is in lyes: they geue good wordes wyth their mouth, but curse wyth the herte. Selah.
Psalms 62:5 Neuerthelesse, my soule abideth only vpon God, for he is my God.
Psalms 62:6 He only is my strength my saluacion, and my defence: so that I shall not fal.
Psalms 62:7 In God is my helth, my glory, my might, and in God is my trust.
Psalms 62:8 O put your trust in him alway (ye people) poure oute youre hertes before hym, for God is our hope. Selah.
Psalms 62:9 As for men, they are but vayne, men are dysceatfull: vpon the weyghtes they are all together lyghter than vanitye it selfe.
Psalms 62:10 O trust not in wronge and robbery, geue not youre selues vnto vanitye: if ryches encrease, set not your herte vpon them.
Psalms 62:11 God spake once a worde, twyse haue I hearde the same: that power belongeth vnto God
Psalms 62:12 That thou Lorde arte mercyfull, and that thou rewardeste euerye man accordynge to his worckes.

CHAPTER: 63

Psalms 63:1 A Psalme of Dauid, when he was in the wildernes of Iuda. O God, thou art my God: earlye wyll I seke the. My soule thrusteth for the, my flesh longeth after the in a baren and drye lande wher no water is.
Psalms 63:2 Thus do I loke for the in thy Sanctuary, that I myght beholde thy power and glorye,
Psalms 63:3 For thy louynge kyndnesse is bettrr then lyfe, my lyppes shall prayse the.
Psalms 63:4 As longe as I lyue wyll I magnyfye the and lyft vp my handes in thy name.
Psalms 63:5 My soule is satisfied euen as it were with mary and fatnesse, when my mouth prayseth the with ioyful lyps.
Psalms 63:6 In my bedde wyll I remember the, and when I wake my talkynge shalbe of the.
Psalms 63:7 For thou hast bene my helper, and vnder the shadow of thy wynges wyl I reioyse.
Psalms 63:8 My soule hangeth vpon the, thy ryghte hande vpholdeth me.
Psalms 63:9 They seke after my soule, but in vayne, for they shall go vnder the earth.
Psalms 63:10 They shall fall into the swerd, and be a porcyon for foxes.
Psalms 63:11 But the Kynge shall reioyse in God: all they that sweare by him, shalbe commended for the mouth of lyers shalbe stopped.

CHAPTER: 64

Psalms 64:1 To the chaunter a Psalme of Dauid. Heare my voice, O God, in my complaynte, preserue my lyfe from feare of the enemye.
Psalms 64:2 Hide me from the gathering together of the frowarde, from the heape of wycked doers.
Psalms 64:3 Which whet their tonges lyke a sweard, and shote wyth their veneymous words like as with arowes.
Psalms 64:4 That they maye preuely hurt the innocent sodenly to hyt him wythout any feare.
Psalms 64:5 They haue deuysed myschefe, and communed amonge them selues, how they may laye snares: tush (saye they) who shall se them?
Psalms 64:6 They ymagyn wyckednes, and kepe it secrete amonge them selues, euerye man in the depe of his herte.
Psalms 64:7 But God shal sodenly shote wyth an arow that they shalbe wounded.
Psalms 64:8 Yea their owne tonges shall make them fall, in somuch that who so seyth them, shall laugh them to scorne.
Psalms 64:9 And all men that se it shal saye: thys hath God done, for they shall perceyue that it is hys worcke.
Psalms 64:10 The righteous shal reioyse in the Lorde, and put his trust in him: and all they that are true of hert, shalbe glad therof.

CHAPTER: 65

Psalms 65:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme and song of Dauid. Thou, O God art, praised in Syon, and vnto the is the vow perfourmed.
Psalms 65:2 Thou hearest the praier, therfore commeth all fleshe vnto the.
Psalms 65:3 Oure misededes preuaile agayust vs, Oh be thou mercyfull vnto our synnes.
Psalms 65:4 Blessed is the man whom thou chosest and receauest vnto the, that he may dwell in thy courtes: he shalbe satisfied wyth the pleasures of thy house, euen of thy holy temple.
Psalms 65:5 Heare vs, according vnto thy wonderfull rightuousnesse, O God oure saluation: thou that art the hope of all the endes of the earth, and of the broade sea.
Psalms 65:6 Which in his strength setteth fast the mountaynes, and is gyrded aboute wyth power.
Psalms 65:7 Which stilleth the ragynge of the sea, the roarynge of his waues, and the woodnes of the people.
Psalms 65:8 They that dwell in the vttermoste partes are afrayed at thy tokens, thou makest both the mornyng and euenyng starres to prayse the.
Psalms 65:9 Thou visitest the earth, thou waterest it. and makest it very plenteous. The riuer of god is ful of waters, thou preparest man hys corne, and thus thou prouydeste for the earth.
Psalms 65:10 Thou waters, her forowes, thou breakest the harde clottes thereof, thou makest it softe with the droppes of rayne, and blessest the increase of it.
Psalms 65:11 Thou crownest the yeare wyth thy good and thy fotsteppes droppe fatnesse.
Psalms 65:12 The dwellinges of the wildernes are fat also, that they droppe wyth all: and the lytle hylles are pleasaunt on euerye syde.
Psalms 65:13 The foldes are full of shepe, the valleyes stande so thicke with corne that they laughe and synge.

CHAPTER: 66

Psalms 66:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauyd. O be ioyfull in God, all ye landes,
Psalms 66:2 synge prayses vnto the honoure of his name, make hys prayse to be gloryous.
Psalms 66:3 Saye vnto God: O howe wonderful are thy worckes? thorowe the greatenesse of thy power shall thine enemyes be confounded.
Psalms 66:4 O that all the worlde woulde worshippe the, synge of the, and prayse thy name. Selah
Psalms 66:5 O come hyther and beholde the worckes of God, which is so wonderful in his doinges amonge the chyldren of men.
Psalms 66:6 He turned the sea into drye lande, so that they wente thorow the water on fote: therefore wyll we reioyse in him.
Psalms 66:7 He ruleth wyth hys power for euer, hys eyes beholde the people: the rennagates shall not be able to exalte them selues. Selah.
Psalms 66:8 O magnyfye oure God, ye people, make the voyce of his prayse to be hearde.
Psalms 66:9 Whych holdeth oure soule in life, and suffreth not our fete to slyppe.
Psalms 66:10 For thou, O God, hast proued vs, thou hast tryed vs lyke as syluer is tryed.
Psalms 66:11 Thou hast broughht vs into captyuyty, & layed trouble vpon oure loynes.
Psalms 66:12 Thou haste suffred men to ryde ouer oure heades, we went thorow fyre and water, but thou hast broughte vs out, and refreshed vs.
Psalms 66:13 Therfore wyll I go into thy house wyth brentoffrynges, to paye the my vowes,
Psalms 66:14 which I promysed with my lippes, and spake wyth my mouth, when I was in trouble.
Psalms 66:15 I wyll offer vnto the fat brentsacrifyces wyth the smoke of rammes, I wyl offer bullockes and goates. Selah.
Psalms 66:16 O come hither, and herken, all ye that feare God, I wyll tell you, what he hath done for my soule.
Psalms 66:17 I called vnto hym wyth my mouthe, and gaue hym prayses wyth my toung.
Psalms 66:18 If I enclyne vnto wyckednesse wyth my herte, the Lorde wyll not heare me.
Psalms 66:19 Therfore God hath herde me, and consydred the voyce of my prayer.
Psalms 66:20 Praysed be God, which hath not cast out my prayer, ner turned his mercy fro me.

CHAPTER: 67

Psalms 67:1 To the chaunter, in Neginoth, a Psalm and songe. God be mercyfull vnto vs, blesse vs, and shewe the lyght of hys countenaunce vpon vs. Selah
Psalms 67:2 That we maye knowe thy waye vpon earth, thy sauynge helth among al Heathen.
Psalms 67:3 Let the people prayse the, O God, yea let all people prayse the.
Psalms 67:4 O let the people reioyse and be glad, that thou iudgest the folke ryghtuouslye, and gouernest the nacions vpon earth.
Psalms 67:5 Let the people prayse the, O God, let al people prayse the.
Psalms 67:6 God, euen oure owne God, geue vs hys blessynge, that the earth maye brynge forth her encrease.
Psalms 67:7 God blesse vs, and let all the endes of the world feare hym.

CHAPTER: 68

Psalms 68:1 To the chaunter, a Psalm and song. of Dauid. Let God aryse, so shall hys enemyes be scattered, and they that hate hym, shall flee before hym.
Psalms 68:2 Lyke as the smoke vanysheth, so shalt thou dryue them away: and lyke as waxe melteth at the fyre so shal the vngodly perysh at the presence of God.
Psalms 68:3 But the ryghtuous shalbe glad and reioyce before God, they shalbe mery and ioyfull.
Psalms 68:4 Oh synge vnto God, synge prayses vnto his name: magnify hym that rydeth aboute the heauens (whose name is the Lord) & reioyce before hym.
Psalms 68:5 He is a father of the fatherlesse, he is a defender of widdowes: euen God in his holy habytacyon.
Psalms 68:6 He is the God that maketh men to be of one mynde in a house, and bryngeth the presoners out of captyuity in due season, but let the rennagates contynue in scarcenesse.
Psalms 68:7 O God, when thou wenteste forth before the people, when thou wentest thorowe the wyldernesse. Selah.
Psalms 68:8 The earth shoke, and the heauens dropped at the presence of God in Sinai, at the presence of God, whyche is the God of Israell.
Psalms 68:9 Thou O God sendest a gracyous raine vpon thyne enherytaunce, and refreshest it when it is dry.
Psalms 68:10 That thy beastes may dwel therin, which thou of thy goodnesse haste prepared for the poore.
Psalms 68:11 The Lorde shall geue the worde, wyth great hostes of Euangelystes.
Psalms 68:12 Kynges wyth their armyes shall fle, and they of the housholde shall deuyde the spoile
Psalms 68:13 If so be that ye lye amonge the pales, the doues fethers shalbe couered with syluer, & her wynges of the colour of golde.
Psalms 68:14 When the Almyghty setteth Kynges vpon the earth, it shalbe cleare euen in the darkne
Psalms 68:15 The hyll of Basan is Gods hyl, the hil of Basan is a plenteous hyl.
Psalms 68:16 Why hoppe ye so, ye greate hylles? It pleaseth God to dwell vpon thys hyll yea the Lorde wyll abide in it for euer.
Psalms 68:17 The charettes of God are many .M. tymes thousande, the Lorde is among them in the holy Sinai.
Psalms 68:18 Thou art gone vp an hye, thou hast ledde captiuitie captiue, and receyued gyftes for men: Yea, euen for thyne enemyes, that they might dwell with the Lord God.
Psalms 68:19 Praysed be the Lord dayly, euen the God whiche helpeth vs, & poureth hys benefites vpon vs. Selah.
Psalms 68:20 The God that is our sauiour, euen God the Lord by whome we escape death.
Psalms 68:21 The God that smyteth the enemies vpon the heades and vpon the heary scalpes: such as go on styll in their wickednes.
Psalms 68:22 The Lorde hath sayde: some wil I bryng agayne from Basan, some wyll I brynge agayne from the depe of the sea.
Psalms 68:23 That thy fote may be dipped in the bloud of thyne enemyes, and that thy dogges may licke it vp.
Psalms 68:24 It is well sene, O God, how thou goest, howe thou my God and kynge goest in the Sanctuary.
Psalms 68:25 The singers go before, and then the mynstrels amonge the maydens with the tymbrels.
Psalms 68:26 O geue thankes vnto God the Lorde in the congregacion, for the welles of Israel.
Psalms 68:27 There lytle Beniamin, the princes of Iuda, the princes of Zabulon, & the princes of Nephthaly beare rule amonge them.
Psalms 68:28 Thy God hath commytted strength vnto the, stablyshe the thynge, O God, that thou hast wrought in vs.
Psalms 68:29 For thy temples sake at Hierusalem shall kynges brynge presentes vnto the.
Psalms 68:30 Reproue the beastes amonge the reedes, the heape of bulles with the calues: those that dryue for money. Oh scatre the people that delite in battaile.
Psalms 68:31 The princes shall come out of Egipt, the Morians land shall stretch out her handes vnto God.
Psalms 68:32 Synge vnto God, O ye kyngedomes of the earth: O syng prayses vnto the Lorde. Selah.
Psalms 68:33 Which sitteth in the heauens ouer all from the beginnynge: Lo, he shall sende oute hys voyce, yea, and that a mighty voyce.
Psalms 68:34 Ascrybe ye the power vnto God, his glory is in Israel, and his might in the cloudes.
Psalms 68:35 God is wonderfull in his Sanctuary, he is the God of Israel, he will geue strength and power vnto hys people. Blessed be God.

CHAPTER: 69

Psalms 69:1 To the chaunter vpon Sosanim of Dauid. Helpe me, O god, for the waters are come in, euen vnto my soule.
Psalms 69:2 I stycke fast in the depe myre where no ground is: I am come into depe waters, and the floudes wyll drowne me.
Psalms 69:3 I am weery of crying, my throte is drye, my sight fayleth me, for waytinge so longe, vpon my God.
Psalms 69:4 They that hate me without a cause, are mo then the heeres of my head: they that are myne enemyes & wolde destroye me giltlesse are mighty: I am fayne to paye the thinges that I neuer toke.
Psalms 69:5 God thou knowest my simplenesse, and my faultes are not hyd from the.
Psalms 69:6 Let not them that trust in the, O Lord God of hoostes, be ashamed for my cause: let not those that seke the, be confounded thorowe me, O God of Israel.
Psalms 69:7 And why? for thy sake do I suffre reprofe, shame couereth my face.
Psalms 69:8 I am become a straunger vnto my brethren, and an aleaunt vnto my mothers chyldren.
Psalms 69:9 For the zele of thyne house hath euen eaten me, and the rebukes of them that rebuked the, is fallen vpon me.
Psalms 69:10 I wepte and chastened my selfe with fastyng, and that was turned to my reprofe.
Psalms 69:11 I put on a sacke cloth, and therefore they iested vpon me.
Psalms 69:12 They that sate in the gate, spake agaynste me, & the dronkardes made songes vpon me.
Psalms 69:13 But Lorde I made my prayer vnto the in an acceptable tyme. Heare me, O God, with thy great mercy and sure helpe.
Psalms 69:14 Take me out of the myre, that I sinke not Oh let me be deliuered from them that hate me, and out of the depe waters.
Psalms 69:15 Lest the water floud drowne me, that the depe swalowe me not vp, and that the pytte shut not her mouth vpon me.
Psalms 69:16 Heare me, O Lord, for thy louyng kyndnesse is comfortable: turne the vnto me according vnto thy great mercy.
Psalms 69:17 Hyde not thy face from thy seruaunt, for I am in trouble: O haste the to helpe me.
Psalms 69:18 Drawe nye vnto my soule, & saue it: Oh deliuer me because of myne enemyes.
Psalms 69:19 Thou knowest my reprofe, my shame & my dishonoure: myne aduersaries are all in thy sight.
Psalms 69:20 The rebuke breaketh my herte, and maketh me heuy: I loke for some to haue pytye vpon me, but ther is no man: and for some to comforte me, but I fynde none.
Psalms 69:21 They gaue me gall to eate, & when I was thurstye, they gaue me vinegar to dryncke.
Psalms 69:22 Let their table be made a snare to take them selues with all, an occasyon to fall and a reward vnto them.
Psalms 69:23 Let their eyes be blinded, that they se not: and euer bow downe their backes.
Psalms 69:24 Power out thyne indignacyon vpon them, and let thy wrathfull dyspleasure take holde of them.
Psalms 69:25 Let theyr habytacyon be voyd, and no man to dwel in ther tentes.
Psalms 69:26 For they persecute hym whom thou hast smytten, and besyde thy woundes they haue geuen him mo.
Psalms 69:27 Let them fall from one wyckednesse to another, and not come into thy ryghtuousnesse.
Psalms 69:28 Let them be wyped out of the boke of the lyuynge, and not be wrytten amonge the ryghtuous.
Psalms 69:29 As for me, I am poore and in heuines, let thy helpe defend me O God.
Psalms 69:30 That I may praise the name of God, with a songe and magnyfye it wyth thanckesgeuynge.
Psalms 69:31 Thys shall please the Lord better then a bullocke, that hath hornes and hoofes.
Psalms 69:32 O consyder this and be glad (ye that be in aduersytye) seke after God, and youre soule shall lyue.
Psalms 69:33 For the Lorde heareth the poore, and despyseth not hys priesoners.
Psalms 69:34 Let heauen and earth praise him, the sea & all that moueth ther in.
Psalms 69:35 For God wyll saue Syon, and buyld the cityes of Iuda, that men may dwel ther, and haue them in possession.
Psalms 69:36 The sede of his seruauntes shall inherette it, and they that loue hys name shall dwell therein.

CHAPTER: 70

Psalms 70:1 The chaunter, of Dauid to bryng to remembraunce. Hast the, O God, to deliuer me, and to helpe me, O Lord.
Psalms 70:2 Let them be shamed and confounded that seke after my soule let them be turned backward and put to confusyon, that wysh my euyl.
Psalms 70:3 Let them sone be broughte to shame, that crye ouer me, there there.
Psalms 70:4 But let all those that seke the, be ioyfull & gladde in the: and let al suche as delyte in thy sauynge health, saye alwaye: the Lorde be praysed.
Psalms 70:5 As for me, I am poore and in misery, hast the God for to helpe me. Thou art my helpe, my redemer and my God: Oh make no long tarying.

CHAPTER: 71

Psalms 71:1 In the, O Lord, is my trust, let me neuer be put to confusyon,
Psalms 71:2 but rydde me, and delyuer me thorow thy ryghtuousnesse: enclyne thyne eare vnto me, and helpe me.
Psalms 71:3 Be thou my strong hold (wher vnto I may all waye fle) thou that hast promised to helpe me: for thou art my house of defence and my castell.
Psalms 71:4 Deliuer me, O my God, out of the hand of the vngodly, oute of the hande of the vnryghtuous and cruell man.
Psalms 71:5 For thou, O Lord God, art the thing that I long for, thou art my hope euen fro my youth.
Psalms 71:6 I haue leaned vpon the euer sence I was borne, thou art he that toke me out of my mothers wombe therfore is my prayse all waye of the.
Psalms 71:7 I am become a wonder vnto the multytude, but my sure trust is in the.
Psalms 71:8 Oh let my mouth be filled with thy praise and honour all the day long.
Psalms 71:9 Cast me not away in myne old age forsake me not when my strength fayleth me.
Psalms 71:10 For myne enemyes speake agaynst me & they that laye wayte for my soule, take their councell together,
Psalms 71:11 sayinge: God hath forsaken hym, persecute hym, take hym, for there is none to helpe hym.
Psalms 71:12 Go not farre fro me, O God: my God, haste the to helpe me.
Psalms 71:13 Let them be confounded and perysh, that are agaynste my soule: let theym be couered with shame and dishonoure, that seke too do me euell.
Psalms 71:14 As for me, I wil paciently abyde alwaye, and will euer encrease thy prayse.
Psalms 71:15 My mouth shall speake of thy righteousnesse and sauyng health all the day longe, for I knowe no ende therof.
Psalms 71:16 Let me go in (O Lorde God) and I wyll make mencion of thy power and righteousnesse onely.
Psalms 71:17 Thou, O God, haste learned me fro my youth vp vntyll now, therfore wyll I tell of thy wonderous workes.
Psalms 71:18 Forsake me not, O GOD, in myne olde age, when I am gray headed: vntyll I haue shewed thyne arme vnto chylders chyldren, and thy power to all them that are yet for to come.
Psalms 71:19 Thy righteousnes, O God, is very hye, thou that doest great thinges: O God, who is lyke vnto the?
Psalms 71:20 O what great troubles and aduersityes hast thou shewed me? and yet dyddest thou turne and refreshe me: yea, & broughtest me from the depe of the earth agayn.
Psalms 71:21 Thou hast brought me to great honoure, and comforted me on euery syde.
Psalms 71:22 Therfore wil I prayse the and thy faythfulnesse, O God, playing vpon the lute, vnto the will I singe vpon the harpe, O thou holy one of Israell.
Psalms 71:23 My lippes wolde fayne singe prayses vnto the: and so wolde my soule, whom thou hast deliuered.
Psalms 71:24 My tongue talketh of thy righteousnesse all the daye longe, for they are confounded and brought vnto shame, that soughte to do me euell.

CHAPTER: 72

Psalms 72:1 Of Salomon. Geue the king thy iudgement, O God, and thy righteousnesse vnto the kynges sonne.
Psalms 72:2 That he maye gouerne thy people accordynge vnto ryght and defende thy poore.
Psalms 72:3 That the mountaynes maye brynge peace, and the litle hylles righteousnesse vnto the people.
Psalms 72:4 He shall kepe the symple folke by theyr ryght, defende the chyldren of the poore, and punish the wronge doer.
Psalms 72:5 Thou shalt be feared as longe as the sunne and moone endureth, from one generacyon to another.
Psalms 72:6 He shall come doune lyke the rayne into a fleise of wolle, & like the droppes that water the earth.
Psalms 72:7 In hys tyme shall righteousnesse florysh, yea, and aboundaunce of peace, so longe as the moone endureth.
Psalms 72:8 Hys dominion shalbe from the one sea to the other, & from the floud vnto the worldes ende.
Psalms 72:9 They that dwell in the wyldernes shall knele before him, & his enemyes shal licke the dust.
Psalms 72:10 The kynges of the sea & of the Iles shall bringe presentes, the kynges of Araby and Saba shall offre gyftes.
Psalms 72:11 All kynges shall worshyppe hym, and all Heathen shall do hym seruyce.
Psalms 72:12 For he shall delyuer the poore when he cryeth, and the neady that hath no helpe.
Psalms 72:13 He shalbe fauorable to the simple & poore, he shall preserue the soules of suche as be in aduersitie.
Psalms 72:14 He shall delyuer their soules from extorcyon and wrong, and deere shall their bloud be in hys sight.
Psalms 72:15 He shall lyue, and vnto hym shalbe geuen of the golde of Arabia: Prayer shalbe made euer vnto hym, and daylye shall he be praysed.
Psalms 72:16 There shalbe an heape of corne in the earth hye vpon the hilles, his frute shal shake like Libanus, and shalbe grene in the cytye, lyke grasse vpon the earth.
Psalms 72:17 Hys name shal endure for euer, his name shall remayne vnder the sunne amonge the posterites, which shalbe blessed thorow him and all the Heathen shall prayse hym.
Psalms 72:18 Blessed be the Lorde God, euen the God of Israell, whiche onely doeth wonderous thinges.
Psalms 72:19 And blessed be the name of his maiesty for euer, and al landes be fulfilled with his glory. Amen, Amen.
Psalms 72:20 Here ende the prayers of Dauid the sonne of Iesse.

CHAPTER: 73

Psalms 73:1 A Psalme of Asaph. O how louyng is God vnto Israel, to suche as are of a cleane hert?
Psalms 73:2 Neuerthelesse my fete were almost gone, my treadynges had well nye slypte.
Psalms 73:3 And why? I was greued at the wicked, to se the vngodly in suche prosperitie.
Psalms 73:4 For they are in no parell of deathe, but stande fast lyke a palace.
Psalms 73:5 They come in no misfortune lyke other folke, neither are they plaged like other men.
Psalms 73:6 And this is the cause that they be so puft vp in pryde, and ouerwhelmed with crueltie & vnrighteousnesse.
Psalms 73:7 Their eyes swell for fatnesse, they do euen what they lyst.
Psalms 73:8 Corrupte are they, and speake blasphemyes maliciouslye, proude and presumpteous are their wordes.
Psalms 73:9 They stretche forth their mouthe vnto the heauen, and their tongue goeth thorow the worlde.
Psalms 73:10 Therfore fall the people vnto them, and thereout sucke they no small auauntage.
Psalms 73:11 Tush (saye they) howe shoulde God perceiue it? is there knowlege in the most hyest?
Psalms 73:12 Lo, these are the vngodly, these prospere in the worlde, these haue ryches in possession.
Psalms 73:13 Shoulde I then clense my herte in vayne (thougt I) and washe my handes in innocency?
Psalms 73:14 Wherefore shoulde I be then punyshed dayly, & be chastened euery mornynge?
Psalms 73:15 Yea, I had almoost also sayd euen as they: but lo, then shoulde I haue condemned the generacion of thy chyldren.
Psalms 73:16 Then thought I, to vnderstande this, but it was to harde for me.
Psalms 73:17 Vntyll I wente into the Sanctuary of God, and considred the ende of these men.
Psalms 73:18 Namely, how thou hast set them in a slippery place, that thou mayst cast them doune headlinges and destroye them.
Psalms 73:19 O how sodenly do they consume, perysh, and come to a fearful ende?
Psalms 73:20 Yea, euen like as a dreame when one awaketh, so makest thou their ymage too vanysh out of the cytye.
Psalms 73:21 Thus my hert was greued, and it wente euen thorow my reynes.
Psalms 73:22 So folysh was I and ignoraunte, and as it were a beast before the.
Psalms 73:23 Neuerthelesse I am al waye by the, thou holdest me by my right hande.
Psalms 73:24 Thou leadest me with thy counsayll, and afterwarde receyuest me vnto glory.
Psalms 73:25 O what is there prepared for me in heauen? there is nothinge vpon earthe, that I desyre in comparyson of the.
Psalms 73:26 My fleash & my hert fayleth, but God is the strength of my herte, and my porcion for euer.
Psalms 73:27 For lo, they that forsake the shall perysh: thou destroyest all them that committe fornicacion agaynst the.
Psalms 73:28 But it is good for me, to holde me fast by God, to put my trust in the Lorde God, and to speake of all thy workes.

CHAPTER: 74

Psalms 74:1 An instruccion of Asaph. O God, wherfore doest thou cast vs so cleane away? why is thy wrath so hoote agaynste the shepe of thy pasture?
Psalms 74:2 O thynke vpon thy congregacion, whome thou hast purchased from the beginnyng: the stafe of thyne enheritaunce, whome thou hast redemed, euen this hyll of Sion wherein thou dwellest.
Psalms 74:3 Treade vpon them with thy fete, and cast them doune to the grounde, for the enemye hath destroyed altogether in the Sanctuary.
Psalms 74:4 Thyne aduersaries roare in thy houses, & set vp their banners for tokens.
Psalms 74:5 Men may se the axes glyster aboue, lyke as those that hewe in the wood.
Psalms 74:6 They cut doune all the syelyng worke of the Sanctuary with bylles and axes.
Psalms 74:7 They haue set fyre vpon the Sanctuary, they haue defyled the dwellyng place of thy name, euen vnto the grounde.
Psalms 74:8 Yea, they say in their hertes: let vs spoyle them altogether, thus haue they brent vp all the houses of God in the lande.
Psalms 74:9 We se oure tokens no more, there is not one Prophet more, no not one that vnderstandeth any more.
Psalms 74:10 O God, how long shall the aduersary do this dishonoure? how longe shall the enemy blaspheme thy name? for euer?
Psalms 74:11 Why withdrawest thou thine hand? why pluckest thou not thy right hande out of thy bosome, to consume thyne enemyes?
Psalms 74:12 But God is my Kynge of olde, the helpe that is done vpon earth, he doth it hym selfe.
Psalms 74:13 Thou deuidest the sea thorow thy power thou breakest the heades of the dragons in the waters.
Psalms 74:14 Thou smitest the heades of Leuiathan in peces, and geuest him to be meate for people in the wyldernes.
Psalms 74:15 Thou diggest vp welles and brokes, thou dryest vp myghty waters.
Psalms 74:16 The daye is thyne, and the nyght is thine thou hast prepared the lightes and the sunne.
Psalms 74:17 Thou hast set all the borders of the earth, thou hast made both sommer and winter.
Psalms 74:18 Remember this, O Lord, how the enemy rebuketh, and howe the folyshe people blaspheme thy name.
Psalms 74:19 O delyuer not the soule of thy turtle doue vnto the beastes, and forget not the congregacyon of the poore for euer.
Psalms 74:20 Loke vpon the couenaunte, for the darcke houses of the earth are full of wyckednesse.
Psalms 74:21 O let not the symple go awaye ashamed: for the poore and nedy geue prayses vnto thy name.
Psalms 74:22 Aryse, O God, and mayntaine thine own cause, remembre howe the folyshe man blasphemeth the daylye.
Psalms 74:23 Forget not the voyce of thyne enemyes, for the presumptyon of them that hate the, increaseth euer more and more

CHAPTER: 75

Psalms 75:1 To the chaunter destroye not, a Psalme and song of Asaph. Vnto the, O God, wil we geue thankes, yea vnto the wyll we geue thanckes, and seynge thy name is so ny, we wil tel of thy wonderous worckes.
Psalms 75:2 When I maye get a conuenyent tyme, I shall iudge accordyng vnto ryght.
Psalms 75:3 The earh is weake and al that is therein, but I beare vp her pyllers.
Psalms 75:4 I sayde vnto the madde people, deale not so madly, and to the vngodly set not vp your hornes.
Psalms 75:5 Set not vp your hornes on hie, and speake not wyth a styfe necke.
Psalms 75:6 For promocyon commeth neyther from the East ner from the weste, ner yet from the wyldernesse
Psalms 75:7 And why? God is the Iudge: he putteth downe one, and setteth vp another.
Psalms 75:8 For in the hand of the Lord ther is a cup full of strong wyne, and he poureth oute of the same: As for the dregges therof, al the vngodly of the earth shall dryncke them, and sucke them oute.
Psalms 75:9 But I wyll talke of the God of Iacob, & prayse him for euer.
Psalms 75:10 Al the hornes of the vngodly wil I breake and the hornes of the ryghtuous shall be exalted.

CHAPTER: 76

Psalms 76:1 To the chaunter, in Neginoth, a Psalm and songe of Asaph. In Iuda is God knowne, hys name is great in Israel.
Psalms 76:2 At Salem is hys tabernacle, and his dwellinge in Sion.
Psalms 76:3 Ther breaketh he the arowes of the bow, the shylde, the swearde, and the whole battaylle, Selah.
Psalms 76:4 Thou art of more honour and might then the hylles of robbers.
Psalms 76:5 The proude shalbe robbed and slepe their slepe, and the myghtye shalbe able to do nothyng with their handes.
Psalms 76:6 When thou rebukest them, O God of Iacob, both the charrettes and horsemen shall fal on slepe.
Psalms 76:7 Thou art fearful, for who maye abyde in thi sight, when thou art angry?
Psalms 76:8 When thou lettest thy iudgment be heard from heauen, the earth trembleth and is stil.
Psalms 76:9 Yea when God aryseth to geue iudgment and to helpe all them that be in aduersyty vpon earth. Selah.
Psalms 76:10 When thou punyshest one man, he muste knowledge that thou arte readye to punyshe other mo.
Psalms 76:11 Loke what ye promise vnto the Lord your God, se that, ye kepe it, all ye that be rounde about him: brynge presentes vnto hym that ought to be feared.
Psalms 76:12 Which taketh awaye the breth of Prynces, and is wonderfull amonge the Kynges of the earth.

CHAPTER: 77

Psalms 77:1 To the chaunter, for Iduthun. a Psalme of Asaph. I cryed vnto God wyth my voyce, yea vnto God cryed I wyth my voyce, and he hearde me.
Psalms 77:2 In the tyme of my trouble I soughte the Lorde, I helde vp myne handes vnto him in the night season, for my soule refused all other comforte.
Psalms 77:3 When I was in heuinesse, I thought vpon God: when my hert was vexed, then dyd I speake Selah.
Psalms 77:4 Thou heldest myne eyes wakyng, I was so feble, that I coulde not speake.
Psalms 77:5 Then remembred I the tymes of old, and the yeares that were past.
Psalms 77:6 I called to remembraunce my song in the night, I communed wyth myne owne herte, and sought out my spirite.
Psalms 77:7 Wyll the Lorde cast out for euer? Wyl he be no more intreated?
Psalms 77:8 Is hys mercye cleane gone? Is hys promyse come vtterlye to an ende for euermore?
Psalms 77:9 Hath the Lord forgotten to be gracyous? Or, hath he shut vp hys louynge kyndnes in dyspleasure? Selah.
Psalms 77:10 At the last, I came to thys poynte, that I thought: O why art thou so folysh? the right hande of the moost hyest can chaunge all.
Psalms 77:11 Therefore wyll I remembre the worckes of the Lorde, and call to mynde thy wonders of olde tyme.
Psalms 77:12 I wyll speake of all thy worckes, and my talkynge shalbe of thy doynges.
Psalms 77:13 Thy waye, O God, is holye: who is so great and myghty as God?
Psalms 77:14 Thou arte the God that doeth wonders, thou hast declared thy power amonge the people
Psalms 77:15 Thou wyth thyne arme hast delyuered thy people, euen the sonnes of Iacob and Ioseph. Selah.
Psalms 77:16 The waters saw the, O God, the waters sawe the, & were afrayed, the deapthes were moued.
Psalms 77:17 The thicke cloudes poured out water, the cloudes thondered, and thyne arowes went abroade.
Psalms 77:18 The thonder was hearde rounde aboute, the lyghtenynges shone vpon the grounde, the earth was moued and shoke wyth al.
Psalms 77:19 Thy waye was in the sea, and thy pathes in the greate waters, yet coulde noman know thy fotesteppes.
Psalms 77:20 Thou leddeste thy people lyke a flocke of shepe, by the hande of Moyses and Aaron.

CHAPTER: 78

Psalms 78:1 An instruccyon of Asaph. Heare my lawe, O my people, enclyne your eares vnto the wordes of my mouth.
Psalms 78:2 I wyll open my mouth in parables, and speake of thynges of olde.
Psalms 78:3 Whych we haue herde and knowne, and such as our fathers haue told vs.
Psalms 78:4 That we shoulde not hyde them from the chyldren of the generations to come: but to shewe the honoure of the Lorde, hys myghte and wonderfull worckes that he hath done.
Psalms 78:5 He made a couenaunte wyth Iacob, and gaue Israel a lawe, whiche he commaunded oure forefathers to teache their chyldren.
Psalms 78:6 That their posterytye myghte knowe it, and the chyldren whych were yet vnborne. To thintent that when they came vp they myghte shewe their chyldren the same.
Psalms 78:7 That they also myghte put their truste in God, & not to forget what he had done, but to kepe his commaundementes,
Psalms 78:8 And not to be as their forefathers, a froward and ouerthwarte generatyon, a generation that set not their herte a ryghte, and whose spirite was not true towarde God.
Psalms 78:9 Lyke as the chyldren of Ephraim, which beyng harnessed and carieng bowes, turned them selues backe in tyme of battayl.
Psalms 78:10 They kept not the couenant of god, and wold not walke in his law.
Psalms 78:11 They forgate what he had done, and the wonderfull workes that he had shewed for them.
Psalms 78:12 Maruelous thynges dyd he in the sighte of our fathers in the lande of Egipt, euen in the felde of Zoan.
Psalms 78:13 He deuided the sea & let them go thorowe it, & made the waters to stande like a wall.
Psalms 78:14 In the daye tyme he ledde them with a cloude, and all the night thorow with a light of fyre.
Psalms 78:15 He cloaue the harde rockes in the wildernesse, & gaue them drynke therof, as it hadde bene out of the great deapth.
Psalms 78:16 He brought waters out of the stony rock, so that they gusshed out lyke the ryuers.
Psalms 78:17 Yet for all this they synned agaynste hym, and prouoked the moost hyest in the wyldernes.
Psalms 78:18 They tempted God in their hertes, and requyred meate for their lust.
Psalms 78:19 For they spoke agaynst God, & sayde: yea yea, God shall prepare a table in the wildernesse, shall he?
Psalms 78:20 Lo, he smote the stony rocke, that the watery streames gusshed out, and the streames flowed with all: but how can he geue bread and prouyde flesh for hys people?
Psalms 78:21 When the Lord hearde this, he was wroth so the fyre was kyndled in Iacob, and heauy displeasure agaynst Israel.
Psalms 78:22 Because they beleued not in God, & putte not their trust in hys helpe.
Psalms 78:23 So he commaunded the cloudes aboue, & opened the dores of heauen.
Psalms 78:24 He rayned doune Manna vpon them for to eate, and gaue them bread from heauen.
Psalms 78:25 Then eate they aungels fode, for he sentte them meate ynough.
Psalms 78:26 He caused the East wynd to blowe vnder the heauen, & thorow hys power he brought in the South wynde.
Psalms 78:27 He made flesh to raine vpon them as thicke as dust, and fethered foules like as the sande of the sea.
Psalms 78:28 He let it fall amonge their tentes rounde about theyr habitacions.
Psalms 78:29 So they eate, and were fylled, for he gaue them their owne desyre.
Psalms 78:30 They were not disapoynted of their lust. But whyle the meate was yet in their mouthes:
Psalms 78:31 the heuy wrath of God came vpon them, slewe the welthiest of them, & smote doune the chosen men of Israel.
Psalms 78:32 But for all this they sinned yet more, and beleued not hys wonderous workes.
Psalms 78:33 Therfore their dayes were consumed in vanyte, and sodenly their yeares were gone.
Psalms 78:34 When he slewe them, they sought hym, & turned them early vnto God.
Psalms 78:35 They thoughte then that God was theyr succour, and that the hye God was their redemer.
Psalms 78:36 Neuerthelesse they dyd but flatter him in their mouthes, and dissembled with hym in their tonges.
Psalms 78:37 For their herte was not whole with him, neither continued they in his couenaunt.
Psalms 78:38 But he was so mercifull, that he forgaue their misdedes, and destroyed them not. Yea, many a tyme turned he hys wrathe awaye, and wolde not suffre hys whole dyspleasure to aryse.
Psalms 78:39 For he considered that they wer but flesh: euen a wynde that passeth awaye, and commeth not agayne.
Psalms 78:40 O how ofte haue they greued hym in the wyldernesse? How many a tyme haue they prouoked hym in the deserte?
Psalms 78:41 They turned backe, and tempted God, & moued the holy one in Israel.
Psalms 78:42 They thought not of hys hand, in the day when he delyuered them from the hande of the enemye.
Psalms 78:43 Howe he had wroughte hys myracles in Egypte, and hys wonders in the lande of Zoan.
Psalms 78:44 How he turned their waters into bloude, so that they myghte not dryncke of the ryuers.
Psalms 78:45 How he sent lyce among them, to eate them vp, and frogges to destroye them.
Psalms 78:46 How he gaue their frutes vnto the catyrpyller, & their labour vnto the greshopper.
Psalms 78:47 How he bete doune theyr vyneyardes wt hayle stones, and their molbery trees wyth the frost.
Psalms 78:48 How he smote theyr cattel with haylestones, & their flockes with hote thonder boltes.
Psalms 78:49 How he sent vppon them the furiousnesse of his wrath, anger & displeasure: with trouble and falling in of euell aungels.
Psalms 78:50 When he made a waye to hys fearful indignacion, and spared not their soules from death, yea, & gaue their cattell ouer to the pestilence.
Psalms 78:51 When he smote al the first born in Egipt, the mooste principall and mightyest in the dwellynges of Ham.
Psalms 78:52 But as for his owne people, he lead them forth lyke shepe, and caried them in the wyldernesse lyke a flocke.
Psalms 78:53 He brought them out safely, that they shoulde not feare, and ouerwhelmed their enemyes with the sea.
Psalms 78:54 He caryed them vnto the borders of his Sanctuary: euen into thys hyl, which he purchased with hys ryghthande.
Psalms 78:55 He dyd cast out the Heathen before them, caused their lande to be deuyded among them for an heritage, and made the trybes of Israel to dwell in their tentes.
Psalms 78:56 For all this they tempted & displeased the most hye God, and kept not hys couenaunt.
Psalms 78:57 But turned their backes, and fell awaye lyke their forefathers, startynge asyde like a broken boowe.
Psalms 78:58 And so they greued hym with theyr hye places, & prouoked him with their ymages.
Psalms 78:59 When God hearde thys, he was wroth, and toke sore dyspleasure at Israell.
Psalms 78:60 So that he forsoke the Tabernacle in Silo, euen his habitacyon wherin he dwelte amonge men.
Psalms 78:61 He delyuered their power into captyuitye and their glory into the enemies hande.
Psalms 78:62 He gaue his people ouer into the swearde for he was wroth wyth hys herytage.
Psalms 78:63 The fyre consumed their yonge men, and their maydens were not geuen to mariage.
Psalms 78:64 Their Prestes were slaine with the swerd and there were no wyddowes to make lamentacyon.
Psalms 78:65 So the Lorde, awaked as one oute of slepe, and lyke a gyaunte refreshed wyth wyne.
Psalms 78:66 He smote hys enemyes in the hynder partes, and put them to perpetuall shame.
Psalms 78:67 He refused the tabernacle of Ioseph, and chose not the trybe of Ephraim.
Psalms 78:68 Neuertheles, he chose the trybe of Iuda, euen the hyll of Syon which he loued.
Psalms 78:69 And there he buylded hys temple on hye, and layd the foundation of it like the ground that it myght perpetually endure.
Psalms 78:70 He chose Dauid also hys seruaunte, and toke hym away from the shepe foldes.
Psalms 78:71 As he was folowynge the yewes greate with yonge, he toke him, that he myghte fede Iacob hys people, & Israel hys enherytance.
Psalms 78:72 So he fedde them wyth a fayethfull and true herte, and ruled them wyth diligence of of his power.

CHAPTER: 79

Psalms 79:1 A Psalme of Asaph. O God, the Heathen are fallen into thyne heritage: the holy temple haue they defiled, and made Ierusalem an heape of stones.
Psalms 79:2 The deade bodye of thy seruauntes haue they geuen vnto the foules of the ayre to be deuoured, and the flesh of thy saintes vnto the beastes of the lande.
Psalms 79:3 Their bloude haue they shed lyke water on euery syde of Ierusalem, and ther was no man to bury them.
Psalms 79:4 We are become an open shame vnto oure enemyes, a verye scorne and derysyon vnto them that are rounde aboute vs.
Psalms 79:5 Lorde, howe longe wylt thou be angrye? shall thy ielousy burne lyke fyre for euer?
Psalms 79:6 Poure oute thyne indignacyon vpon the Heathen that knowe the not, and vpon the Kyngdomes that call not vpon thy name.
Psalms 79:7 For they haue deuoured Iacob, and laied wast his dwellynge place.
Psalms 79:8 O remembre not oure olde synnes, but haue mercye vpon vs, and that soone, for we are come to greate mysery.
Psalms 79:9 Helpe, vs, O God oure sauyoure, for the glory of thy name: O deliuer vs, and forgeue vs oure synnes for thy names sake.
Psalms 79:10 Wherfore shall the Heathen say: wher is now their God? O lette the vengeaunce of thy seruauntes bloude that is shed, be openly shewed vpon the Heathen in our syght.
Psalms 79:11 O Let the sorowfull sighehyng of the presoners come before the, and accordinge vnto the power of thyne arme, preserue those that are appoynted to dye.
Psalms 79:12 And for the blasphemye wherewyth oure neyghboures haue blasphemed the, rewarde them, O Lorde, seenu folde into theyr bosome.
Psalms 79:13 So we that be the people and shepe of thy pasture, shall geue the thanckes for euer, and wyll all waye be shewynge forth thy prayse more and more.

CHAPTER: 80

Psalms 80:1 To the chaunter, vpon Sosanim, a Psalme of Asaph. Heare O thou shepeherde of Israel, thou that leadest Iacob lyke a flocke of shepe: shew thy self, thou that sittest vppon the Cherubyns.
Psalms 80:2 Before Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manasses: stirre vp thy power, & come help vs.
Psalms 80:3 Turne vs agayn, O God, shew the light of thy countenaunce, and we shalbe whole.
Psalms 80:4 O Lord God of hostes, howe longe wilt thou be angry ouer the praier of thy people?
Psalms 80:5 Thou hast fed them with the bread of teares, yea, thou hast geuen them plenteousnes of teares to drynke.
Psalms 80:6 Thou haste made vs a verye stryfe vnto oure neyghbours, and oure enemyes laugh vs to scorne.
Psalms 80:7 Turne vs agayne, thou God of hoostes, shewe the light of thy countenaunce, & we shalbe whole.
Psalms 80:8 Thou hast broughte a vyneyarde oute of Egypte, thou diddest cast out the Heathen, & planted it.
Psalms 80:9 Thou madest rowme for it, and caused it to take rote, so that it fylled the lande.
Psalms 80:10 The hylles were couered with the shadow of it, and so were the stronge Cedre trees wt the bowes therof.
Psalms 80:11 She stretched out her braunches vnto the sea, and her bowes vnto the water.
Psalms 80:12 Why haste thou then broken doune her hedge, that all they whiche go by, plucke of her grapes?
Psalms 80:13 Then wylde bore out of the wood hath roted it vp, and the beastes of the felde haue deuoured it.
Psalms 80:14 Turne the agayne, thou God of hoostes, loke doune from heauen, beholde and vyset this vyneyarde.
Psalms 80:15 Maynteyne it, that thy rightehande hath planted, and the sonne whom thou madest so muche of for thy self.
Psalms 80:16 For why? it is brent with fyre, and lyeth waste: O let them peryshe at the rebuke of thy wrath.
Psalms 80:17 Let thy hande be vpon the man of thy right hande, and vpon the man whome thou madest so much of for thyne owne selfe.
Psalms 80:18 And so will not we go back from the: Oh let vs lyue, & we shall call vpon thy name.
Psalms 80:19 Turne vs agayne, O Lorde God of hoostes, shewe the light of thy countenaunce, & we shalbe whole.

CHAPTER: 81

Psalms 81:1 To the chaunter vpon Githith, of Asaph. Singe merely vnto God which is our strengthe, make a chearfull noyse vnto the god of Iacob.
Psalms 81:2 Take the Psalme, brynge hyther the tabret, the mery harpe & lute.
Psalms 81:3 Blowe vp the trompettes in the new mone, vpon our solempne feast daye.
Psalms 81:4 For this is the vse in Israel, and a lawe of the God of Iacob.
Psalms 81:5 This he ordeined in Ioseph for a testimony, when he came out of Epipt, & had heard a straunge language.
Psalms 81:6 When he eased hys shoulder from the burthen, and when hys handes were deliuered from the pottes.
Psalms 81:7 When thou callest vpon me in trouble, I helped the, and hearde the, what tyme as the storme fell vpon the, I proued the also at the water of stryfe. Selah.
Psalms 81:8 Heare, O my people, for I assure the O Israel, if thou wilt herken vnto me:
Psalms 81:9 There shal no straunge God be in the, neither shalt thou worshippe any other God.
Psalms 81:10 I am the Lord thy God, which broughte the out of the lande of Egipt, open thy mouth wyde, and I shall fyll it.
Psalms 81:11 But my people wolde not heare my voice and Israel wolde not obey me.
Psalms 81:12 So I gaue them vp vnto their owne hertes luste, and let them folowe theyr owne ymaginacions.
Psalms 81:13 O that my people wolde obeye me, for if Israel wolde walke in my wayes:
Psalms 81:14 I should soone put doune their enemyes, and turne myne hande againste their aduersaries.
Psalms 81:15 The haters of the Lord should mysse Israel, but their tyme shoulde endure for euer.
Psalms 81:16 He should feade them with the finest wheat floure, and satisfye them with hony out of the stony rocke.

CHAPTER: 82

Psalms 82:1 A Psalme of Asaph. God standeth in the congregacion of the Goddes, and is a iudge amonge the iudges.
Psalms 82:2 How long will ye geue wrong iudgement, and accept the personnes of the vngodly? Selah.
Psalms 82:3 Defende the poore and fatherlesse, se that suche as be in nede & necessitie haue right.
Psalms 82:4 Deliuer the outcaste & poore, & saue hym from the hande of the vngodly.
Psalms 82:5 Neuerthelesse, they will not be learned & vnderstande, but walke on styll in darkenesse: therfore must all the foundacions of the lande be moued.
Psalms 82:6 I haue sayde: ye are Goddes, ye all are the chyldren of the moost hyest.
Psalms 82:7 But ye shall dye lyke men, and fall lyke one of the tyrauntes.
Psalms 82:8 Aryse, O God, & iudge thou the earth, for all the Heathen are thyne by enheritaunce.

CHAPTER: 83

Psalms 83:1 A songe and Psalme of Asaph. Holde not thy tongue, O God, kepe not styll silence, refrayne not thy self O God.
Psalms 83:2 For lo, thyne enemies make a murmurynge, and they that hate the, lyft vp their heade.
Psalms 83:3 They ymagyn craftely agaynst thy people, and take counsayll agaynste thy secrete ones.
Psalms 83:4 Come (saye they) let vs rote them out from amonge the people, that the name of Israell maye be put out of remembraunce.
Psalms 83:5 For they haue caste their heades together with one consent, & are confederate agaynst the.
Psalms 83:6 The tabernacles of the Edomites and Ismaelytes, the Moabytes and Hagarenes.
Psalms 83:7 Gebal, Ammom, and Amalech: the Philistines with them that dwell at Tyre.
Psalms 83:8 Assur also is ioyned vnto them, and helpe the chyldren of Loth. Selah.
Psalms 83:9 But do thou to them as vnto the Madianites, vnto Sisera, and vnto Iabin by the broke of Kyson.
Psalms 83:10 Whych peryshed at Endor, & became as the donge of the earth.
Psalms 83:11 Make their prynces lyke Oreb & Zeb. Yea, make all their prynces lyke as Zebea & Salmana.
Psalms 83:12 Whiche saye: we will haue the houses of God in possession.
Psalms 83:13 O my God, make them lyke vnto a whele, and as the stubble before the wynde.
Psalms 83:14 Lyke as a fyre that burneth vp the wood, and as the flame that consumeth the mountaynes.
Psalms 83:15 Persecute them euen so with thy tempest, and make them afrayed with thy storme.
Psalms 83:16 Make their faces ashamed, O Lord that they maye seke thy name.
Psalms 83:17 Let them be confounded and vexed euer more and more: let them be put to shame and perishe.
Psalms 83:18 That they may know that thou art alone that thy name is the Lorde, & that thou onely art the moost hyest ouer all the earth.

CHAPTER: 84

Psalms 84:1 Vpon Githith, a Psalm of the sonnes of Corah. O howe amiable are thy dwellinges, thou Lord of hoostes?
Psalms 84:2 My soule hath a desyre & longing for the court of the Lord, my hert and my fleshe reioyse in the lyuyng God.
Psalms 84:3 For the sparow hath founde her an house and the swalow a nest, where she maye laye her yonge: euen thy aulters O Lorde of hostes, my kynge and my God.
Psalms 84:4 O how blessed are they that dwell in thy house, they are all way praysing the. Selah.
Psalms 84:5 Blessed are the men whose strengthe is in the, in whose herte are thy wayes.
Psalms 84:6 Which goinge thorow the vale of misery vse it for a well, and the poles are filled with water.
Psalms 84:7 They go from strength to strength, and so the God of Goddes appeareth vnto them in Sion.
Psalms 84:8 O Lord God of hostes, heare my prayer: herken O God of Iacob.
Psalms 84:9 Beholde O God our defence, loke vpon the face of thyne anoynted.
Psalms 84:10 For one daye in thy courte is better then a thousande. I had rather be a dore keper in the house of my God, then to dwell in the tentes of the vngodly.
Psalms 84:11 For the Lord God is a light and defence, the Lorde wyll geue grace and worshyppe, and no good thynge shall he wytholde from them that lyue a godly lyfe.
Psalms 84:12 O Lorde God of Hostes, blessed is the man that putteth his truste in the.

CHAPTER: 85

Psalms 85:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of the sonnes of Corah. Lorde, thou barest a loue vnto thy land thou dydest brynge agayne the captyuyte of Iacob.
Psalms 85:2 Thou dydest forgeue the offence of thy people, and couerdest al their synnes. Sela.
Psalms 85:3 Thou takest away al thy displeasure, and turnedest thy selfe from thy wrathfull indignacyon.
Psalms 85:4 Turne vs then. O God oure Sauyoure, and let thyne anger ceasse from vs.
Psalms 85:5 Wylt thou be dyspleased at vs for euer? wylt thou stretch out thy wrath from one generacyon to another?
Psalms 85:6 Wylt thou not turne agayne and quycken vs, that thy people maye reioyse in the?
Psalms 85:7 n/a
Psalms 85:8 I wyll herken what the Lorde God wyll saye for he shall speake peace vnto hys people and to hys saynctes, that they turne not them selues vnto folyshnes.
Psalms 85:9 For hys saluacyon is nye them that feare hym so, that glory shall dwell in oure lande.
Psalms 85:10 Mercy and trueth are met together, ryghtuousnesse and peace kysseth eche other.
Psalms 85:11 Trueth shall ryse oute of the earthe, and ryghtuousnesse shal loke downe from heauen
Psalms 85:12 And why? the Lorde shall shewe louynge kyndnesse, and oure lande shal geue her encrease.
Psalms 85:13 Rightuousnes shall go before hym, and prepare the waye for his commynge.

CHAPTER: 86

Psalms 86:1 A prayer of Dauyd. Bow downe thine eare, O Lord and heare me, for I am comfortles and poore.
Psalms 86:2 O kepe my soule, for I am holy my God, helpe thy seruante that putteth his trust in the.
Psalms 86:3 Be merciful vnto me, O Lord, for I cal dayly vpon the.
Psalms 86:4 Comfort the soule of thy seruaunt, for vnto the, O Lord, do I lyft vp my soule.
Psalms 86:5 For thou Lorde arte good and gracyous, and of greate mercye vnto all them that call vpon the.
Psalms 86:6 Geue eare Lord vnto my praier, and ponder my humble desyre.
Psalms 86:7 In the tyme of my trouble I cal vpon the, for thou hearest me.
Psalms 86:8 Amonge the Goddes ther is none like vnto the, O Lorde, there is not one that can do as thou doest.
Psalms 86:9 All nacyons whom thou hast made, shall come and worship before the, O Lorde, and shal gloryfy thy name.
Psalms 86:10 For thou art great, thou dost wonderous thinges, thou art God alone.
Psalms 86:11 Leade me in thy way, O Lord, that I may walke in thy trueth: O let my herte delyte in fearyng thy name.
Psalms 86:12 I thanke the. O Lorde my God, and will prayse thy name for euer.
Psalms 86:13 For great is thy mercy towarde me, thou hast delyuered my soule from the nether most hell.
Psalms 86:14 O God the proude are rysen agaynst me, and the congregacyon of the myghtye seketh after my soule, and sette not the before theyr eyes.
Psalms 86:15 But thou, O Lord God, art ful of compassion, and mercy, long suffring, great in goodnes and truth.
Psalms 86:16 O turne the then vnto me, haue mercy vpon me: geue thy strength vnto thy seruante, and helpe the sonne of thyne handmayde.
Psalms 86:17 Shew some token vpon me for good, that they which hate me, maye se it, and be ashamed: because thou Lord hast helped me, and comforted me.

CHAPTER: 87

Psalms 87:1 A Psalme and songe of the sonnes of Corah Her foundatyons are vpon the holye hylles:
Psalms 87:2 the Lorde loueth the gates of Syon more then all the dwellynges, of Iacob.
Psalms 87:3 Very excellent thynges are spoken of the thou cyty of God. Selah.
Psalms 87:4 I wyll thynke vpon Rahab and Babilon so that they shall know me. Yea the Philistines also, and they of Tire wyth the Morians. Lo ther was he borne.
Psalms 87:5 And of Sion it shalbe reported, that he was borne in her, euen the most hyest whych hath buylded her.
Psalms 87:6 The Lorde shall cause it to be preached & wrytten amonge the people, that he was borne ther. Selah.
Psalms 87:7 Therfore the dwellynge of all syngers & daunsers is in the.

CHAPTER: 88

Psalms 88:1 A Psalme and songe, of the sonnes of Corah, to the chaunter vpon Mahelath, for affliccyon, an instruccyon of Heman the Ezrathyte. O Lord God my sauiour, I cry day and nyghte before the:
Psalms 88:2 Oh let my praier enter into thy presence, incline thyne eare vnto my callynge.
Psalms 88:3 For my soule is full of trouble, and my lyfe draweth nye vnto hell.
Psalms 88:4 I am counted as one of them that go downe vnto the pitte, I am euen as a man that hath no strength.
Psalms 88:5 Fre among the dead, like vnto them that lye in the graue, whyche be out of remembraunce, and are cutte away from thy hand.
Psalms 88:6 Thou hast layed me, in the lowest pytte, in the darcknesse and in the depe.
Psalms 88:7 Thyne indignacion lieth harde vpon me, and thou vexest me wyth all thy floudes Selah.
Psalms 88:8 Thou hast put awaye myn acquaintance farre fro me, and made me to be abhorred of them: I am so faste in pryson, that I can not get forth.
Psalms 88:9 My syght fayleth for very trouble: Lord I call dayly vpon the, and stretch oute myne handes vnto the.
Psalms 88:10 Doest thou shewe wonders amonge the deade? Can the Phisicions raise them vp againe that they maye prayse the?
Psalms 88:11 Maye thy louynge kyndnes be shewed in the graue or thy faythfulnesse in destruccyon:
Psalms 88:12 May thy wonderous workes be knowne in the darcke, or thy ryghtuousnes in the land wher al thinges are forgotten?
Psalms 88:13 Vnto the I crye, O Lorde, and early commeth my prayer before the.
Psalms 88:14 Lorde, why putteste thou awaye my soule? Wherfore hydest thou thy face fro me?
Psalms 88:15 My strength is gone for very sorow & myserye, wyh fearfulnesse do I beare thy burthens.
