Psalms 88:16 Thy wrathfull dyspleasure goeth ouer me the feare of the, oppresseth me.
Psalms 88:17 They come rounde about me dayly lyke water, and compasse me together on euerye side.
Psalms 88:18 My louers, and frendes hast thou put awaye fro me, and turned awaye myne acquayntaunce.

CHAPTER: 89

Psalms 89:1 An instruccyon yf Ethan the Ezrahyte. My songe shalbe alway of the louynge kyndnesse of the Lorde, wyth my mouth wyl I euer be shewynge thy faythfulnes from one generacyon to another.
Psalms 89:2 For I haue sayed, mercy shalbe set vp for euer, thy faythfulnesse shalt thou stablysh in the heauens.
Psalms 89:3 I haue made a couenaunt wyth my chosen, I haue sworne vnto Dauid my seruant.
Psalms 89:4 Thy sede wyll I stablyshe for euer, and set vp thy trone from one generacyon to another Selah.
Psalms 89:5 O Lorde the verye heauens shall prayse thy wonderous, worckes, yea and thy faythfulnes in the congregation of the saynctes.
Psalms 89:6 For who is he amonge the cloudes, that may be compared vnto the Lord. Yea, what is he among the Gods that is like vnto the lord?
Psalms 89:7 God is greatly to be feared in the councel of the saintes and to be had in reuerence of al them that are aboute hym.
Psalms 89:8 O Lorde God of Hostes who is lyke vnto the in power? thy trueth is round about the
Psalms 89:9 Thou rulest the pryde of the sea, thou stillest the waues therof, when they aryse.
Psalms 89:10 Thou breakest the proude, like one that is wounded, thou scatrest thine enemies abroad with thy mightye arme.
Psalms 89:11 The heauens are thine, the earth is thine: thou hast layed the foundation of the rounde world, and al that therin is.
Psalms 89:12 Thou hast made the north and the south, Tabor and Hermon shal reioyse in thy name
Psalms 89:13 Thou hast a myghty arme, stronge is thy hande, and hye is thy righthande.
Psalms 89:14 Righteousnes and equite is the habitacion of thy seate, mercy and truethe go before thy face.
Psalms 89:15 Blessed is the people, O Lorde, that can reioyse in the, & walketh in the lyghte of thy countenauce.
Psalms 89:16 Their delyte is in thy name all the daye longe, and thorowe thy righteousnesse they shalbe exalted.
Psalms 89:17 For thou art the glory of their strength, & thorow thy fauoure shalt thou lyfte vp oure hornes.
Psalms 89:18 The Lorde is our defence, and the holy one of Israel is our kyng.
Psalms 89:19 Thou spakest sometyme in visions vnto thy saynctes, and saydest: I haue layed helpe vpon one that is mighty, I haue exalted one chosen out of the people.
Psalms 89:20 I haue founde Dauid my seruaunt, with my holy oyle haue I anoynted hym.
Psalms 89:21 My hande shal holde him fast, and myne arme shall strengthen hym.
Psalms 89:22 The enemye shall not ouercome hym, & the sonne of wyckednesse shall not hurte hym.
Psalms 89:23 I shall smyte doune hys foes before hys face, and plage them that hate hym.
Psalms 89:24 My trueth also & my mercy shalbe wyth hym, and in my name shall hys horne be exalted.
Psalms 89:25 I will set hys hande in the sea, & his right hande in the floudes.
Psalms 89:26 He shall call me, thou art my father, my God, and the strength of my saluacion.
Psalms 89:27 And I will make hym my fyrste borne, hyer then the kynges of the earth.
Psalms 89:28 My mercy wyll I kepe for hym for euermore, and my couenaunte shall stande faste with hym.
Psalms 89:29 Hys sede wyll I make to endure for euer, yea, and his trone as the dayes of heauen.
Psalms 89:30 But if hys chyldren forsake my law, and walke not in my iudgementes.
Psalms 89:31 If they breake myne ordynaunces, & kepe not my commaundementes.
Psalms 89:32 I will vyset their offences wyth the rodde, and their synnes wit scourges.
Psalms 89:33 Neuerthelesse, my louinge kyndnesse wil I not vtterly take from hym, nor suffre my trueth to fayle.
Psalms 89:34 My couenaunt wyl I not breake, nor disanulle the thynge that is gone out of my lippes.
Psalms 89:35 I haue sworne once by my holinesse, that I will not fayle Dauid.
Psalms 89:36 Hys sede shall endure for euer, and hys seate also lyke as the sunne before me.
Psalms 89:37 He shall stande faste for euermore as the moone, and as the faythfull wytnesse in heauen. Selah.
Psalms 89:38 But now thou forsakest & abhorrest thine anoynted, and art displeased at hym.
Psalms 89:39 Thou hast turned backe the couenaunte of thy seruaunt, and caste hys croune to the grounde.
Psalms 89:40 Thou hast ouerthrowen all his hedges, & broken doune his stronge holdes.
Psalms 89:41 All they that go by, spoyle hym, he is become a rebuke vnto hys neyghbours.
Psalms 89:42 Thou settest vp the righthande of his enemyes, and makest all hys aduersaries to reioyse.
Psalms 89:43 Thou hast taken awaye the strengthe of his swerde, and geuest him not victory in the battayle.
Psalms 89:44 Thou hast put out his glory, and cast his trone doune to the grounde.
Psalms 89:45 The dayes of his youth hast thou shortened, & couered him with dishonoure. Selah.
Psalms 89:46 Lord, how longe wilt thou hyde thy self? For euer? shall thy wrathe burne lyke fyre?
Psalms 89:47 O remembre how shorte my time is, hast thou made all men for nought?
Psalms 89:48 What man is he that lyueth, and shall not se death? Maye a man deliuer his owne soule from the hande of hell? Selah.
Psalms 89:49 Lorde, where are thy olde louing kyndnesses, whyche thou sworest vnto Dauid in thy trueth?
Psalms 89:50 Remembre Lord the rebuke that the multitude of the people do vnto thy seruauntes, and how I haue borne it in my bosome.
Psalms 89:51 Wherwith thyne enemyes blaspheme the, and sclaunder the footesteppes of thyne anoynted.
Psalms 89:52 Thankes be too the Lorde for euermore: Amen: Amen.

CHAPTER: 90

Psalms 90:1 A prayer of Moyses the man of God. Lorde thou art oure refuge from one generacion to another.
Psalms 90:2 Before the mountaines were broughte forthe, or euer the earthe and the worlde were made, thou art God from euerlastynge and worlde without ende.
Psalms 90:3 Thou turnest man to destruccyon, Agayne, thou sayest: come agayne ye chyldren of men
Psalms 90:4 For a thousande yeares in thy sighte are but as yesterdaye that is past, and lyke as it were a nyght watch.
Psalms 90:5 As sone as thou scatrest them, they are euen as a slepe, & fade awaye sodenly like the grasse.
Psalms 90:6 In the mornyng it is grene and groweth vp, but in the euenynge it is cut doune and wythered.
Psalms 90:7 For we consume awaye in thy displeasure, and are afrayed at thy wrathful indignacion.
Psalms 90:8 Thou settest our misdedes before the, and our secrete sinnes in the light of thy countenaunce.
Psalms 90:9 For when thou art angrye, all oure dayes are gone, we brynge our yeares to an ende, as it were a tale that is tolde.
Psalms 90:10 The dayes of oure age are .iij. score yeares and ten: and though men be so strong that they come to foure score yeares, yet is their strength then but laboure, & sorowe: so soone passeth it awaye, and we are gone.
Psalms 90:11 But who regardeth the power of thy wrath thy fearfull and terrible displeasure?
Psalms 90:12 O teach vs to numbre our daies, that we maye apply our hertes vnto wisdome.
Psalms 90:13 Turne the agayn (O Lorde) at the last, & be gracious vnto thy seruauntes.
Psalms 90:14 O satisfie vs with thy mercy, & that sone, so shall we reioyse and be glad all the dayes of our lyfe.
Psalms 90:15 Comforte vs agayne, now after the tyme that thou hast plaged vs, and for the yeares wherin we haue suffred aduersitie.
Psalms 90:16 Shewe thy seruauntes thy worke, & their chyldren thy glory.
Psalms 90:17 And the glorious maiesty of the Lord our God be vpon vs: O prospere thou the worke of our handes vpon vs, O prospere thou our handy worke.

CHAPTER: 91

Psalms 91:1 Who so dwelleth vnder the defence of the most hyest, & abydeth vnder the shadowe of the almightye.
Psalms 91:2 He shal say vnto the Lorde: O my hope, and my strong holde, my God, in whome I will trust.
Psalms 91:3 For he shall delyuer the from the snare of the hunter, and from the noysome pestylence.
Psalms 91:4 He shall couer the vnder hys wynges, that thou mayest be safe vnder his fethers: his faythfulnesse & trueth shalbe thy shylde and buckler.
Psalms 91:5 So that thou shalt not nede to be afrayed for any bugges by night, nor for the arrowe that flyeth by daye.
Psalms 91:6 For the pestilence that crepeth in the darkenesse, nor for the sikenesse that destroyeth in the noone daye.
Psalms 91:7 A thousande shall fall beside the, and ten thousande at thy righthande, but it shall not come nye the.
Psalms 91:8 Yea, with thyne eyes shalt thou beholde, and se the rewarde of the vngodly.
Psalms 91:9 For thou Lorde art my hope, thou hast set thyne house of defence very hye.
Psalms 91:10 There shall no euell happen vnto the, neither shall any plage come nye thy dwelling.
Psalms 91:11 For he shall gyue his aungels charge ouer the, to kepe the in all thy wayes.
Psalms 91:12 They shall beare the in their handes, that thou hurt not thy fote agaynst a stone.
Psalms 91:13 Thou shalt go vpon the Lyon and Adder the yonge lyon and the Dragon shalte thou treade vnder thy fete.
Psalms 91:14 Because he hath set his loue vppon me, I shall deliuer hym: I shal defende him, for he hath knowen my name.
Psalms 91:15 When he calleth vpon me, I shall heare hym: yea, I am with hym in hys trouble, wherout I will deliuer him, and bring hym to honoure.
Psalms 91:16 With longe lyfe will I satisfye him, and shewe hym my saluacion.

CHAPTER: 92

Psalms 92:1 A Psalme of the songe for the Sabboth daye. It is a good thynge too geue thankes vnto the Lord, and to synge prayses vnto thy name, O moost hyest.
Psalms 92:2 To tell of thy louyng kyndnesse early in the mornyng. and of thy trueth in the night season.
Psalms 92:3 Vpon an instrument of ten strynges, vpon the lute and with a songe vpon the harpe.
Psalms 92:4 For thou lord hast made me glad thorow thy workes, and I will reioyse ouer the operacion of thy handes.
Psalms 92:5 O Lorde, how glorious are thy workes, thy thoughtes are very depe.
Psalms 92:6 An vnwyse man will not knowe thys, and a foole will not vnderstande it.
Psalms 92:7 That the vngodly are grene as the grasse and that all the workes of wickednes do florish to be destroyed for euer.
Psalms 92:8 But thou Lorde O mooste hyest, abydest worlde without ende.
Psalms 92:9 For lo, thyne enemyes, O Lord, lo, thyne enemyes shall perishe, and all the workers of wickednes shalbe scatred abroade.
Psalms 92:10 But my horne shalbe exalted like the horne of an Vnicorne, & shalbe anoynted wyth fresh oyle.
Psalms 92:11 Myne eye also shall se hys luste of myne enemyes, and myne eare shall heare his desire of the wicked that ryse vp agaynst me.
Psalms 92:12 The righteous shall florish lyke a palme tree, and growe like a Cedre of Libanus.
Psalms 92:13 Suche as be planted in the house of the Lorde, be frutefull,
Psalms 92:14 plenteous and grene.
Psalms 92:15 That they maye shew, how true the Lorde my strength is, and that there is no vnrighteousnesse in hym.

CHAPTER: 93

Psalms 93:1 The Lorde is kyng, and hath put on glorious apparell, the Lorde hath put on his apparell, & gyrded him selfe with strengthe: he hath made the rounde world so sure, that it can not be moued.
Psalms 93:2 From that tyme forth hath thy seate bene prepared, thou art from euerlastyng.
Psalms 93:3 The floudes aryse (O Lorde) the floudes lyft vp their noyse, the floudes lyfte vp theyr waues.
Psalms 93:4 The waues of the sea are mightye, & rage horribly: but yet the Lorde that dwelled on hye, is mightier.
Psalms 93:5 Thy testimonies, O LORD, are very sure, holynesse becommeth thyne house for euer.

CHAPTER: 94

Psalms 94:1 O Lorde God, to whome vengeaunce belongeth: thou God to whome vengeaunce belongeth shewe thy self.
Psalms 94:2 Aryse thou iudge of the world & rewarde the proude after their deseruyng.
Psalms 94:3 Lorde how longe shall the vngodly, how longe shall the vngodly triumphe?
Psalms 94:4 How longe shall all wicked doers speake so disdaynfully, and make such proude boastynge?
Psalms 94:5 They smyte doune thy people, O Lorde, and trouble thine heritage.
Psalms 94:6 They murthur the wydowe & the straunger, and put the fatherlesse to death.
Psalms 94:7 And yet they saye: Tushe, the Lorde seyth not, the God of Iacob regardeth it not.
Psalms 94:8 Take hede, ye vnwyse among the people: O ye fooles, when will ye vnderstande?
Psalms 94:9 He that planted the eare, shal he not heare? he that made the eye, shal not he se?
Psalms 94:10 He that nurtureth the Heathen, and teacheth a man knowlege, shall not he punish?
Psalms 94:11 The Lord knoweth the thoughtes of men, that they are but vayne.
Psalms 94:12 Blessed is the man, whome thou learnest (O LORDE) and teacheste hym in thy lawe.
Psalms 94:13 That thou mayest geue hym pacience in tyme of aduersitie, vntil the pytte be dygged vp for the vngodly.
Psalms 94:14 For the Lorde will not fayle his people, neither will he forsake his inheritaunce.
Psalms 94:15 And why? iudgement shalbe turned agayn vnto righteousnesse, and all suche as be true of hert shall folow it.
Psalms 94:16 Who ryseth vp with me agaynst the wicked? who taketh my parte agaynste the euell doers?
Psalms 94:17 If the Lord had not helped me, my soule had almost bene put to silence.
Psalms 94:18 When I sayde: my fote hath slypped, thy mercy (O Lord) helde me vp.
Psalms 94:19 In the multitude of the sorowes that I had in my herte, thy comfortes haue refreshed my soule.
Psalms 94:20 Wilt thou haue any thing to do with the stoole of wickednesse, which ymagineth mischief in the lawe?
Psalms 94:21 They gather them together agaynste the soule of the righteous, and condemne the innocent bloude.
Psalms 94:22 But the Lord is my refuge, my God is the strength of my confidence.
Psalms 94:23 He shall recompence them their wickednesse, & destroye them in their owne malyce: yea, the Lorde our God shall destroy them.

CHAPTER: 95

Psalms 95:1 O come let vs prayse the Lord, let vs hertely reioyse in the strength of our saluacion.
Psalms 95:2 Let vs come before his presence with thankesgeuynge, & shewe oure selfe gladde in hym with Psalmes.
Psalms 95:3 For the Lord is a great God, and a great kyng aboue all Goddes.
Psalms 95:4 In his hand are al the corners of the earth, and the strength of the hylles is his also.
Psalms 95:5 The sea is his, for he made it, & his handes prepared the drye lande.
Psalms 95:6 O come, let vs worshippe & bowe doune our selfes: Let vs knele before the Lord our maker.
Psalms 95:7 For he is oure God: & we are the people of his pasture, and the shepe of his handes. To daye if ye wil heare his voyce,
Psalms 95:8 harden not youre hertes, as when ye prouoked in tyme of temptacion in the wildernes.
Psalms 95:9 Where your fathers tempted me, proued me, and sawe my workes.
Psalms 95:10 .xl. yeares long was I greued with the generacion, & sayd: they euer erre in their hertes, they verely haue not knowen my wayes.
Psalms 95:11 Therfore I sayd vnto them in my wrath, that they should not enter into my rest.

CHAPTER: 96

Psalms 96:1 O synge vnto the Lorde a newe songe, singe vnto the Lorde all the whole earth.
Psalms 96:2 Synge vnto the Lord, and prayse his name, be tellyng of his saluacion from daye to daye.
Psalms 96:3 Declare his honour among the Heathen, and his wonders among all people.
Psalms 96:4 For the Lord is great, and can not worthely be praysed: he is more to be feared then all goddes.
Psalms 96:5 As for all the goddes of the Heathen, they be but Idols, but it is the Lorde that made the heauens.
Psalms 96:6 Thankesgeuynge and worshippe are before hym, power & honoure are in hys Sanctuary.
Psalms 96:7 Ascribe vnto the Lord (O ye kynredes of the Heathen) ascribe vnto the Lord worship and strength.
Psalms 96:8 Ascribe vnto the Lord the honoure of his name, brynge presentes, and come into hys courte.
Psalms 96:9 O worship the lorde in the beuty of holynesse, lette the whole earthe stande in awe of hym.
Psalms 96:10 Tell it out amonge the Heathen, that the Lorde is kynge: and that it is he, which hath made the rounde worlde so faste, that it can not be moued, and howe that he shall iudge the people righteously.
Psalms 96:11 Let the heauens reioyse, and let the earth be glad: let the sea make a noyse, yea, and all that therin is.
Psalms 96:12 Let the felde be ioyfull and all that is in it, lette all the trees of the woode leape for ioye.
Psalms 96:13 Before the lorde, for he commeth: for he commeth to iudge the earth: yea, with ryghteousnesse shall he iudge the worlde, and the people with his trueth.

CHAPTER: 97

Psalms 97:1 The Lord is king, the earth may be glad therof: yea, the multitude of the Iles may be glad therof.
Psalms 97:2 Cloudes & darkenesse are round about him, righteousnesse & iudgement are the habitacion of hys seate.
Psalms 97:3 There goeth a fyre before hym, to burne vp hys enemyes on euery syde.
Psalms 97:4 Hys lightenynges geue shyne vnto the worlde, the earth seyth it, and is afrayed.
Psalms 97:5 The hilles melt like waxe at the presence of the lord of the whole earth.
Psalms 97:6 The very heauens declare his righteousnes, and all the people se his glory.
Psalms 97:7 Confounded be all thei that worship ymages, and delyte in their Idols: worship him all ye Goddes.
Psalms 97:8 Sion heareth of it & reioyseth: yea, & all the daughters of Iuda are glad because of thy iudgementes, O lorde.
Psalms 97:9 For thou lorde art the most hyest ouer all the earth, thou arte exalted farre aboue all goddes.
Psalms 97:10 O ye that loue the lorde, se that ye hate that thyng whiche is euell: the lorde preserueth the soules of his saynctes, he shall deliuer them from the hande of the vngodly.
Psalms 97:11 There is sprong vp a lighte for the ryghteous, and a ioyfull gladnesse for suche as be true herted.
Psalms 97:12 Reioyse therfore in the lorde, ye ryghteous: and geue thankes for a remembraunce of hys holinesse.

CHAPTER: 98

Psalms 98:1 A Psalme. O synge vnto the Lorde a new song, for he hath done maruelous thynges. With hys owne ryght hande and with his holy arme hathe he gotten the victory.
Psalms 98:2 The lord hath declared his sauyng health & hys righteousnes hathe he openly shewed in the sight of the Heathen.
Psalms 98:3 He hath remembred his mercy and trueth towarde the house of Israel: so that all the endes of the worlde, se the sauing health of our God.
Psalms 98:4 Shewe youre selfes ioyfull vnto the Lorde all ye landes, synge, reioyse, and geue thanckes.
Psalms 98:5 Prayse the Lordes, vpon the harpe, synge to the harpe wyth a psalme of thanckesgeuynge
Psalms 98:6 With trompettes also and shawmes: O shewe youre selues ioyfull before the Lorde the kynge.
Psalms 98:7 Let the sea make a noyse and all that therin is, yea the whole worlde, and al that dwel therein.
Psalms 98:8 Let the floudes clappe their handes, and let al the hylles be ioyful together.
Psalms 98:9 Before the Lorde, for he is come to iudge the earth. Yea wyth ryghtuousnes shall he iudg the worlde, and the people wyth equyte.

CHAPTER: 99

Psalms 99:1 The Lorde is kynge, be the people neuer so vnpaciente: he sytteth vpon the Cherubyns, be the earth neuer so vnquiete.
Psalms 99:2 The Lord is greate in Sion, & hye aboue all people.
Psalms 99:3 O let men geue thanckes vnto thy greate and wonderfull name, for it is holye.
Psalms 99:4 The kinges power loueth iudgment, thou preparest equite, thou executest iudgment and ryghtuousnes in, Iacob.
Psalms 99:5 O magnyfy the Lorde oure God, fal down before his fote stole, for he is holye.
Psalms 99:6 Moyses ond Aaron amonge hys pryestes and Samuell amonge such as call vpon hys name: these called vpon the Lorde, and he hearde them.
Psalms 99:7 He spake vnto them out of the cloudy piller for he kepte hys testymonyes, and the lawe that gaue them.
Psalms 99:8 Thou heardest them, O Lorde oure God thou forgauest them O God, and punyshedst their owne inueucions.
Psalms 99:9 O magnyfye the Lorde oure God, and worshyppe hym vpon hys holy hyll, for the Lorde oure God is holy.

CHAPTER: 100

Psalms 100:1 A Psalme of praise. O be ioiful in God (al ye landes)
Psalms 100:2 serue the Lorde with gladnes, come before his presence wyth ioye.
Psalms 100:3 Be ye sure, that the Lord he is God: It is he that hath made vs, and not we our selues: we are but his people, and the shepe of his pastoure.
Psalms 100:4 O go youre waye into hys gates then with thanckesgeuynge, and into his courtes with prayse, be thanckefull vnto hym, and speake good of his name.
Psalms 100:5 For the Lorde is gracyous, hys mercie is euerlastynge, and hys trueth endureth from generatyon to generacyon.

CHAPTER: 101

Psalms 101:1 A Psalme of Dauid. My songe shalbe of mercye and iudgment yea vnto the, O Lord wyll I synge.
Psalms 101:2 O let me haue vnderstandynge in the way of Godlynesse vntyll the tyme that thou come vnto me: and so shall I walcke in my house wyth an innocent herte.
Psalms 101:3 I wyl take no wycked thynge in hande, I hate the synne of vnfaythfulnesse, it shal not cleaue vnto me.
Psalms 101:4 A frowarde harte shall departe fro me I wyll not knowe a wicked personne.
Psalms 101:5 Who so preuely sclaundereth hys neyghboure. hym wyl I destroye: Who so hath a prowd loke and an hye stomacke, I may not awaye with him.
Psalms 101:6 Myne eyes shal loke for such as be faythfull in the lande, that they maye dwell wyth me: and who so leadeth a godly liue, shall be my seruaunt.
Psalms 101:7 There shall no disceatfull personne dwell in my house he that telleth lyes shall not tary in my syght.
Psalms 101:8 I shalll soone destroye all the vngodlie of the lande, that all wycked doers maye be roted out of the cytie of the Lord.

CHAPTER: 102

Psalms 102:1 A prayer of the afflycte, when he was in woo, and powered oute hys complaynte before the Lord. Heare my prayer, O Lord, & and lette my crienge come vnto the.
Psalms 102:2 Hyde not thy face fro me in the tyme of my trouble encline thyne eares vnto me when I call, O heare me, and that ryghte sone.
Psalms 102:3 For my dayes are consumed awaye lyke smoke, and my bones are brent vp as it were a fyre brande.
Psalms 102:4 My herte smytten doune and wythered lyke grasse, so that I forgette too eate my bread.
Psalms 102:5 For the voyce of my gronynge, my bone wil scarse cleue to my flesh.
Psalms 102:6 I am be come lyke a Pellicane in the wildernes, and lyke an owle in a broken wal.
Psalms 102:7 I wake, and am euen as it were a sparow sittinge alone vpon the house toppe.
Psalms 102:8 Myne enemyes reuyle me all the daye longe, they laugh me to scorne, & are sworne together agaynst me.
Psalms 102:9 I eate ashes with my bread, and myngle my drynke with wepynge.
Psalms 102:10 And that because of thyne indignacion & wrath, for thou hast taken me vp, and caste me awaye.
Psalms 102:11 My dayes are gone lyke a shadowe, and I am wythered lyke grasse.
Psalms 102:12 But thou O Lord, endurest for euer, and thy remembraunce thorow out all generacyons.
Psalms 102:13 Aryse therfore & haue mercy vpon Sion, for it is time to haue mercy vpon her, yea, the tyme is come.
Psalms 102:14 And why? thy seruauntes haue a loue too her stones, and it pitieth them to se her in the dust.
Psalms 102:15 The Heathen shal feare thy name, O Lord, and all the kynges of the earth thy maiesty.
Psalms 102:16 For the Lorde shall buylde vp Sion, and shall apeare in hys glory.
Psalms 102:17 He turneth him vnto the prayer of the poore destitute, & despiseth not their desyre.
Psalms 102:18 This shalbe wrytten for those that come after, that the people whiche shalbe borne, maye prayse the Lorde.
Psalms 102:19 For he loketh doune from hys Sanctuary, out of the heauen doth the Lorde beholde the earth.
Psalms 102:20 That he maye heare the mournynges of such as be in captiuitie, and deliuer the chyldren of death.
Psalms 102:21 That they maye preache the name of the Lorde in Sion, and his worshippe at Hierusalem.
Psalms 102:22 When the people are gathered together, & the kyngdomes also to serue the Lord.
Psalms 102:23 He hath brought doune my strength in my iourney, and shortened my dayes.
Psalms 102:24 Yet will I saye: O my God, take me not away in the myddest of myne age: as for thy yeares, they endure thorowe out all generacions.
Psalms 102:25 Thou Lorde in the beginnyng hast layed the foundacion of the earth, and the heauens are the workes of thy handes.
Psalms 102:26 They shal perish, but thou shalt endure: they all shall wexe olde as doth a garment, & as a vesture shalt thou chaunge them, & they shalbe chaunged.
Psalms 102:27 But thou art the same, & thy yeares shall not fayle.
Psalms 102:28 The chyldren of thy seruauntes shall continue, and their sede shall prospere in thy sighte.

CHAPTER: 103

Psalms 103:1 Of Dauid. Prayse the Lorde O my soule: & all that is within me prayse hys holy name.
Psalms 103:2 Prayse the Lord O my soule & forget not all his benefites.
Psalms 103:3 Whych forgeueth all thy synnes, & healeth all thyne infirmities.
Psalms 103:4 Which saueth thy lyfe from destruccion, and crouneth the with mercy, and louynge kyndnesse.
Psalms 103:5 Whiche satisfeth thy desyre wyth good thynges, makyng the yonge and lusty as an Aegle.
Psalms 103:6 The Lorde executeth righteousnesse and iudgement, for all theim that suffre wronge.
Psalms 103:7 He shewed his wayes vnto Moses, & his workes vnto the chyldren of Israel.
Psalms 103:8 The Lord is ful of compassion and mercy, long sufferyng, & of great goodnesse.
Psalms 103:9 He will not alwaye be chydynge, neither will he kepe his anger for euer.
Psalms 103:10 He hath not dealt with vs after oure sinnes, nor rewarded vs according to our wickednesse.
Psalms 103:11 For loke how hye the heauen is in comparison of the earth, so greate is his mercy also towarde them that feare hym.
Psalms 103:12 Loke how wyde the East is from the West, so farre hath he set oure sinnes from vs.
Psalms 103:13 Yea, like as a father pitieth his owne children, euen so is the Lord mercifull vnto them that feare hym.
Psalms 103:14 For he knoweth whereof we be made, he remembreth that we are but dust.
Psalms 103:15 That a man in hys time is but as grasse, and florisheth as a floure of the felde.
Psalms 103:16 For as sone, as the wynde goeth ouer it, it is gone, and the place thereof knoweth it no more.
Psalms 103:17 But the mercyfull goodnesse of the Lorde endureth for euer and euer, vpon them that feare him, and his righteousnesse vpon their chyldren.
Psalms 103:18 Suche as kepe hys couenaunte, & thynke vpon hys commaundementes to do them.
Psalms 103:19 The Lorde hath prepared his seate in heauen, and his kingedome ruleth ouer all.
Psalms 103:20 O prayse the Lorde ye aungels of his, ye that be myghty in strength fulfyllynge hys commaundement that men may here the voice of hys wordes.
Psalms 103:21 O prayse the Lorde all ye his Hostes, yea seruauntes of his, that do hys pleasure.
Psalms 103:22 O speake good of the Lorde al ye workes of his, in euery place of his dominion: praise thou the Lorde, O my soule.

CHAPTER: 104

Psalms 104:1 Prayse the Lorde O my soule: O Lord my God, thou art become excedinge glorious, thou arte clothed with maiesty and honoure.
Psalms 104:2 Thou deckest thy self with light, as it were with a garment, thou spredest out the heauen lyke a curtayne.
Psalms 104:3 Thou voltest it aboue with waters, thou makest the cloudes thy charet, & goest vpon the wynges of the wynde.
Psalms 104:4 Thou makest thyne aungels sprites, and thy ministers flammes of fyre.
Psalms 104:5 Thou hast layed the earth vpon her foundacion, that it neuer moueth at any tyme.
Psalms 104:6 Thou couerest it with the depe lyke as wt a garmente, so that the waters stande aboue the hylles.
Psalms 104:7 But at thy rebuke they fle, at the voyce of thy thonder they are afrayed.
Psalms 104:8 (Then are the hylles sene alofte, and the valleis beneth in their place which thou hast appoynted for them.)
Psalms 104:9 Thou hast set them their boundes, which they maye not passe, that they turne not agayne to couer the earth.
Psalms 104:10 Thou causest the welles to sprynge vp amonge the valleys, and the waters to runne amonge the hylles.
Psalms 104:11 That all beastes of the felde maye haue drynke, & that the wilde asses maye quenche their thyrste.
Psalms 104:12 Aboue vpon the hylles haue the foules of the ayre their habitacion, and singe amonge the braunches.
Psalms 104:13 Thou waterest the hilles from aboue, the earth is filled wt the frutes of thy workes.
Psalms 104:14 Thou bringest forth grasse for the cattell, and grene herbes for the seruice of men. Thou bringest fode out of the earth:
Psalms 104:15 wyne to make glad the herte of man, oyle to make hym a chearfull countenaunce and bread to strength mans herte.
Psalms 104:16 The trees of the Lord are ful of sappe, euen the trees of Libamis whiche he hathe planted.
Psalms 104:17 There make the byrdes their nestes, & the fyrre hylles are a dwellyng for the storke.
Psalms 104:18 The hilles are a refuge for the wilde goates, & so are the stony rockes for the conyes.
Psalms 104:19 Thou hast appoynted the moone for certayne seasons, the sunne knoweth hys going doune.
Psalms 104:20 Thou makest darkenesse, that it maye be night, wherin all the beastes of the forest do moue.
Psalms 104:21 Yea, and the yonge lyons which roare after their praye, and seke their meate at God.
Psalms 104:22 But when the sunne aryseth, they get them awaye together, and lye them doune in their dennes.
Psalms 104:23 Then goeth man forth to hys worke, and to tyll hys lande vntyll the euenynge.
Psalms 104:24 O Lord, how manifolde are thy workes, right wisely hast thou made them al: yea, the earth is full of thy ryches.
Psalms 104:25 So is this great & wyde sea also, wherein are thynges creping innumerable, both smal and great beastes.
Psalms 104:26 There go the shippes ouer, and there is the Leuiathan, whom thou hast made, to take hys pastyme therein.
Psalms 104:27 They wayte all vpon the, that thou mayest geue them meate in due season.
Psalms 104:28 When thou geuest it them, they gather it: when thou openest thyne hande, they are filled with good.
Psalms 104:29 But when thou hydest thy face, they are sorowfull: if thou takest awaye their breth, they dye, & are turned agayne to their dust.
Psalms 104:30 Agayne, when thou lettest thy brethe goo forth, they are made, and so thou renuest the face of the earth.
Psalms 104:31 The glorious maiesty of the Lorde endureth for euer, & the Lorde reioyseth in hys workes.
Psalms 104:32 The earth trembleth at the loke of hym, he doethe but touche the hylles and they smoke.
Psalms 104:33 I wyll synge vnto the Lorde as longe as I lyue, I will prayse my God whyle I haue my beyng.
Psalms 104:34 O that my wordes might please hym, for my ioye is in the Lorde.
Psalms 104:35 As for synners, they shalbe consumed out of the earth, and the vngodlye shall come to an ende: but prayse thou the Lorde, O my soule. Prayse the euerlastynge.

CHAPTER: 105

Psalms 105:1 O geue thankes vnto the Lord, and cal vpon his name: tel the people what thynges he hath done.
Psalms 105:2 O let your songes be of him prayse hym, and let your talking be of al hys wonderous workes.
Psalms 105:3 Gyue hys holye name a good report lette their hertes reioyse that seke the Lord.
Psalms 105:4 Seke the Lord, and his strength, seke his face euermore.
Psalms 105:5 Remember the maruelous worckes that he hath done, his wonders and the iudgementes of his mouth.
Psalms 105:6 O ye sede of Abraham hys seruaunte, ye chyldren of Iacob hys chosen.
Psalms 105:7 He is the Lorde oure God, whose punishmentes are thorow oute all the worlde.
Psalms 105:8 He is alwaye myndeful of his couenaunt and promyse that he made to a thousand generations.
Psalms 105:9 Yea the couenant that he made with Abraham, and the oth that, he sware vnto Isaac,
Psalms 105:10 And appoynted the same vnto Iacob for a lawe, and to Israell for an euerlastynge testamente.
Psalms 105:11 Sayenge: vnto the wyl I geue the land of Canaan, the lot of your heritage.
Psalms 105:12 When there was yet but a fewe of them, and the straungers therin.
Psalms 105:13 What tyme as they wente from one nacyon to another, from one kyngedome to another.
Psalms 105:14 He suffered no man to hurt them, but reproued euen kynges for their sakes.
Psalms 105:15 Touch not myne anoynted, do my prophetes no harme.
Psalms 105:16 Moreouer he called for a dearth vpon the lande, and destroyed all the prouysyon of breade.
Psalms 105:17 But he had sente a man before them, euen Ioseph whiche was solde to be a bonde seruaunte.
Psalms 105:18 They hurte hys fete in the stockes the yron pearsed hys hert.
Psalms 105:19 Vntill the tyme that his worde, and tyll the word of the Lorde had tryed hym.
Psalms 105:20 Then sent the kyng & caused him to be deliuered, the prince of the people bad let him go
Psalms 105:21 He made him Lorde of hys house, and ruler of all hys substaunce.
Psalms 105:22 That he might enfourme his princes after hys wyl, & teach his Senatoures wisedom.
Psalms 105:23 Israell also came into Egipte, and Iacob was a straunger in the lande of Ham.
Psalms 105:24 But he increased hys people exceadyngly and made them stronger then their enemyes.
Psalms 105:25 Whose hert turned so that they hated his people: and dealt vntruly wt hys seruauntes.
Psalms 105:26 Then sente he Moses his seruaunte, and Aaron, whome he had chosen.
Psalms 105:27 These dyd his tokens amonge them, and wonders in the lande of Ham.
Psalms 105:28 He sente darcknesse and it was darcke, for they were not obedyent vnto hys worde.
Psalms 105:29 He turned their waters into bloude, and slew theyr fysh.
Psalms 105:30 Their land brought forth frogges, yea euen in their kynges chambers.
Psalms 105:31 He spake the worde, and their came all maner of flyes and lyce in al their quarter
Psalms 105:32 He gaue them hayle stones for rayne, and flammes of fyre in their land.
Psalms 105:33 He smot their vineyeardes & figge trees, & destroyed the trees that were in their coastes.
Psalms 105:34 He spake the worde, and ther were greshoppers and catyrpyllers innumerable.
Psalms 105:35 These eate vp all the grasse in their land, and deuoured their frutes of the grounde.
Psalms 105:36 He smote al the fyrst borne in the lande, euen the chefe of al their substaunce.
Psalms 105:37 He broughte them forth wyth syluer and gold, ther was not one feble person amonge theyr trybes.
Psalms 105:38 Egypte was glad of their departinge, for they were afrayed of them.
Psalms 105:39 He spred out a cloude to be a couerynge, and fyres to geue lyght in the nyght season.
Psalms 105:40 At their desyre, ther came quailes, and he fylled them wyth the breade of heauen.
Psalms 105:41 He opened the rocke of stone, and the waters flowed out: so that ryuers ranne in the wyldernesse.
Psalms 105:42 For why? he remembred his holy promes whyche he had made vnto Abraham his seruaunte.
Psalms 105:43 Thus he broughte forth hys people wyth ioy, and his chosen with gladnesse.
Psalms 105:44 And gaue them the landes of Heathen, where they toke the laboures of the people in possessyon.
Psalms 105:45 That they myghte kepe hys statutes, and obserue his lawes. Prayse the euerlastynge.

CHAPTER: 106

Psalms 106:1 Prayse the euerlastynge. O geue thankes vnto the Lorde, for he is gracyous, and hys mercy endureth for euer.
Psalms 106:2 Who can expresse the noble actes of the Lord, or shewe forth al hys prayse?
Psalms 106:3 Blessed are they that allwaye kepe iudgement, and do ryghtuousnes.
Psalms 106:4 Remember vs, O Lorde, accordynge to the fauour that thou bearest vnto thy people O vyset vs wyth thy sauynge health.
Psalms 106:5 That we myght se the pleasure of thy chosen, that we myght reioyse in the gladnesse of thy people, and geue thanckes with thine enherytaunce.
Psalms 106:6 We haue synned wyth oure fathers, we haue done amysse, we haue dealt wyckedlye.
Psalms 106:7 Oure fathers regarded not thy wonders in Egypte, they kepte not thy great goodnes in remembraunce: but were dysobedyent at the sea, euen at the reed sea.
Psalms 106:8 Neuertheles, he helped them for hys names sake, that he myghte make hys power to be knowne.
Psalms 106:9 He rebuked the read sea, and it was dryed vp: so he led them thorowe the depe as in a wyldernes.
Psalms 106:10 Thus he saued them from the hand of the hater, and delyuered them from the hande of the enemye.
Psalms 106:11 As for those that troubled them the waters ouerwhelmed them, ther was not one of them left.
Psalms 106:12 Then beleued they in his worde, and sang prayse vnto hym.
Psalms 106:13 But within a whyle they forgat his workes, and wold not abyde his councel.
Psalms 106:14 A lust came vpon them in the wildernesse, so that they tempted God in the deserte.
Psalms 106:15 Yet he gaue them their desire, and sent them ynough at their wylles.
Psalms 106:16 They angred Moyses in the tentes, & Aaron the saynct of the Lord.
Psalms 106:17 So the earth opened & swalowed vp Dathan, & couered the congregatyon of Abyram.
Psalms 106:18 The fyre was kyndled in their companie, the flamme brent vp the vngodly.
Psalms 106:19 They made a calfe in Horeb, and worshipped the molten ymage.
Psalms 106:20 Thus they turned their glorye into the similitude of a calfe, that eateth hay.
Psalms 106:21 They forgat God their Sauiour, whyche had done so greate thynges in Egypte.
Psalms 106:22 Wonderous workes in the land of Ham and fearful thynges in the read sea.
Psalms 106:23 So he sayde he wuld haue destroyed them had not Moses hys chosen stand before him in that gappe: to turne awaye his wrathfull indignatyon, lest he should destroy them.
Psalms 106:24 Yea, they thought scorne of that pleasaunt lande, and gaue no credence vnto hys worde
Psalms 106:25 But murmured in their tentes, and herkened not vnto the voyce of the Lord.
Psalms 106:26 Then lyft he vp his hand against them to ouerthrowe them in the wildernes.
Psalms 106:27 To cast out their sede among the nacions. and to scatter them in the landes.
Psalms 106:28 They ioyned them selues vnto Baal Peor and eate the offeringes of the dead.
Psalms 106:29 Thus they prouoked him vnto anger with their owne inuencyons, and the plage was great among them.
Psalms 106:30 Then stode vp Phynehes and executed iustice, and so the plage ceased.
Psalms 106:31 And that was counted vnto him for ryghtuousnesse, amonge all posterityes for euermore.
Psalms 106:32 They angeryd hym also at the waters of strife, so that Moyses was punished for ther sakes.
Psalms 106:33 Because they prouoked his spirite, and he told them plainly with his lippes.
Psalms 106:34 Nether destroied they the Heathen, as the Lorde commaunded them.
Psalms 106:35 But were mingled among the Heathen, and lerned their workes.
Psalms 106:36 In so much that they worshipped their images, which turned to their owne decay.
Psalms 106:37 Yea they offred their sons and their daughters vnto deuels.
Psalms 106:38 And shed the innocent bloud of their sonnes and of their daughters, whom they offered vnto the ymages of Canaan, so that the land was defiled with bloud.
Psalms 106:39 Thus were they stayned with their owne workes, and went a whoring with their owne inuencyons.
Psalms 106:40 Therfore was the wrath of the Lord kindled agaynst hys people, in so much that he abhorred his owne enheritaunce.
Psalms 106:41 And gaue them ouer into the hand of the Heathen, and they that hated them, were lordes ouer them.
Psalms 106:42 Their enemyes oppressed them, and had them in subieccion.
Psalms 106:43 Many a tyme did he delyuer them but they prouoked him wyth theyr owne inuencyons and were broughte downe for theyr wyckednesse.
Psalms 106:44 Neuertheles when he saw their aduersitie he herd their complaynt.
Psalms 106:45 He thought vpon hys couenaunt, and pytyed them, accordyng vnto the multytude of hys mercyes.
Psalms 106:46 Yea he made all those that had led them awaye captyue, to pitiye them.
Psalms 106:47 Delyuer vs, O Lorde oure God, and gather vs from amonge the Heathen: that we maye geue thanckes to thy holye name, and make our boast of thy prayse.
Psalms 106:48 Blessed be the Lorde God of Israel from euerlastyng and world without ende, and let all people saye: Amen, Amen. Prayse the euerlastynge.

CHAPTER: 107

Psalms 107:1 O geue thankes vnto the Lord, for he is gracious, & his mercy endureth for euer.
Psalms 107:2 Let them geue thankes whome the Lord hath redemed, & deliuered from the hande of the enemye.
Psalms 107:3 And gathered them out of the landes, from the East, from the West, from the North and from the South.
Psalms 107:4 They went astraye in the wildernesse in an vntroden waye, and founde no cytye too dwell in.
Psalms 107:5 Hungry & thirsty, and their soule faynted in them.
Psalms 107:6 So they cryed vnto the Lorde in theyr trouble, and he deliuered them from theyr distresse.
Psalms 107:7 He ledde them forth by the ryghte waye, that they myghte go to the cytye where they dwelt.
Psalms 107:8 O that men wolde praise the goodnesse of the Lorde, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
Psalms 107:9 For he satisfied the empty soule, & fylled the hungry soule with good.
Psalms 107:10 Such as sat in darkenesse and in the shadow of death, beyng fast bounde in mysery and yron.
Psalms 107:11 Because they were not obedient to the commaundementes of God, but lightely regarded the counsayll of the moost hyghest.
Psalms 107:12 Their hert was vexed with labour, they fel doune, and there was none to helpe them.
Psalms 107:13 So they cryed vnto the LORD in their trouble, and he deliuered them oute of theyr dystresse.
Psalms 107:14 He brought them out of darkenesse & oute of the shadow of death, & brake their bondes in sonder.
Psalms 107:15 O that men wolde prayse the goodnesse of the Lord, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
Psalms 107:16 For he hath broken the gates of brasse, and smytten the barres of yron in sonder.
Psalms 107:17 Folysh men were plaged for their offence and because of their wickednesse.
Psalms 107:18 Their soule abhorred all maner of meate, they were euen harde at deaths dore.
Psalms 107:19 So they cryed vnto the Lorde in their trouble, and he deliuered them oute of theyr distresse.
Psalms 107:20 He sent hys worde and healed them, and saued them from destruccion.
Psalms 107:21 O that men woulde prayse the goodnesse of the Lord, and the wonders that he doth for the chyldren of men.
Psalms 107:22 That they wolde offre vnto him the sacrifice of thankesgeuyng, & tell out hys workes with gladnes.
Psalms 107:23 They that go doune to the sea in shippes, and occupy their businesse in great waters.
Psalms 107:24 These men se the workes of the Lorde, & his wonders in the deape.
Psalms 107:25 For at his worde, the stormy winde aryseth, and lifteth vp the waues therof.
Psalms 107:26 They are caryed vp to the heauen, & doun agayne too the deape, their soule melteth awaye in the trouble.
Psalms 107:27 They rele to and fro, they stacker lyke a droncken man, and are at their wittes ende.
Psalms 107:28 So they crye vnto the Lorde in their trouble, and he delyuereth them oute of their distresse.
Psalms 107:29 He maketh the storme to ceasse, so that the waues are styll.
Psalms 107:30 Then are they glad because they be at rest & so he bringeth them vnto the hauen, where they wolde be.
Psalms 107:31 O that men wolde prayse the goodnes of the Lorde, and the wondres that he doth for the chyldren of men.
Psalms 107:32 That they wolde exalte him in the congregacion of the people, & loane hym in the seate of the elders.
Psalms 107:33 Which turneth the floudes into drye land, and drieth vp the water sprynges.
Psalms 107:34 A frutefull lande maketh he baren, for the wickednesse of them that dwell therin.
Psalms 107:35 Agayn, he maketh the wildernes a standinge water, and water springes of a drye grounde.
Psalms 107:36 There he setteth the hongrye, that they maye buylde them a cytye to dwell in.
Psalms 107:37 That they may sow their grounde, plante vyneyardes, to yelde them frutes of increase.
Psalms 107:38 He blesseth them, so that they multiplye excedingly, and suffreth not their cattel to decrease.
Psalms 107:39 When they are minished & brought lowe thorowe oppression, thorowe any plage or trouble.
Psalms 107:40 Though he suffre them to be euell intreated thorow tyrauntes, or lette them wandre out of the waye in the wildernesse.
Psalms 107:41 Yet helpeth he the poore out of misery (at the last) and maket hym an housholde lyke a flocke of shepe.
Psalms 107:42 The righteous will considre this & reioyse, the mouth of all wyckednesse shalbe stopped.
Psalms 107:43 Who so is wyse, & pondreth these thynges well, shal vnderstande the louyng kyndnesses of the Lorde.

CHAPTER: 108

Psalms 108:1 A songe of Psalme of Dauid. O God, my herte is ready to synge, and to geue prayse. Awake, O my glorye,
Psalms 108:2 awake lute and harpe, I my selfe wyll awake ryght early.
Psalms 108:3 I wyll geue thanckes vnto the, O Lord, amonge the people. I wil syng prayses vnto the among the Heathen.
Psalms 108:4 For the greatenesse of thy mercy is higher then the heauens, and thy faithfulnesse reacheth vnto the cloudes.
Psalms 108:5 Set vp thy selfe, O God, aboue the heauens, and thy glory aboue al the eartth.
Psalms 108:6 That thy beloued may be delyuered: helpe them with thy right hand and heare me
Psalms 108:7 God hath spoken in his Sanctuary, whych thyng reioyseth me. I wyll deuyde Sichem, and meate out the valley of Suchoth.
Psalms 108:8 Galaad is myne, Manasses is myne, Ephraym is the strength of my head, Iuda is my captaine.
Psalms 108:9 Moab is my washpotte, ouer Edom will I stretch oute my shue, Phylystea shall be glad of me.
Psalms 108:10 Who wyll lead me into the stronge cyty? Who wyll brynge me into Edom?
Psalms 108:11 Shalt not thou do it (O God) which hast cast vs: out thou God, that wentest not forth with our Hostes?
Psalms 108:12 O be thou our helpe in trouble, for vayne is the helpe of man.
Psalms 108:13 Thorow God we shal do great actes, for it is he that shal treade downe our enemyes.

CHAPTER: 109

Psalms 109:1 To the chaunter, a Psalme of Dauyd. Holde not thy tong: O God of my praise.
Psalms 109:2 For the mouth of the vngodlye yea and the mouth of the disceatfull is opened vpon me, and speake agaynste me wyth false tonges.
Psalms 109:3 They compase me aboute with wordes of hatred, and fight against me without a cause
Psalms 109:4 For the loue that I had vnto them, they take now my contrary parte, but I geue my selfe vnto prayer.
Psalms 109:5 Thus they reward me euel for good, and hatred for my god wyll.
Psalms 109:6 Set an vngodly man to be ruler ouer him and let Satan stande at his ryghte hande.
Psalms 109:7 When sentence is geuen vpon him, let him be condempned, and let his prayer be turned into synne.
Psalms 109:8 Let his daies be few, and his bishopricke let another take.
Psalms 109:9 Let hys chyldren be fatherlesse, and hys wyfe a wydowe.
Psalms 109:10 Let his children be vagabaundes, and bege their breade: lette them seke it, as they that be destroyed.
Psalms 109:11 Let the extorcioner consume al that he hath and let straungers spoyle his laboure.
Psalms 109:12 Let ther be no man to pytye, ner to haue compassyon vpon his fatherles chyldren.
Psalms 109:13 Let hys ende be destruccyon, & in the next generacion let his name be cleane put oute.
Psalms 109:14 Let the wickednesse of his fathers be had in remembraunce in the syght of the Lorde & and let not the synne of hys mother be done awaye.
Psalms 109:15 Let them alway be before the Lorde, but as for the memoryall of them selues, let it perysh from out of the earth.
Psalms 109:16 And that because hys mynde was not to do good. but persecuted the poore helplesse, and hym that was vexed at the harte, to slay hym.
Psalms 109:17 Hys delyte was in cursynge, and therfore shall it happen vnto hym: he loued not blessynge and that shall be far from hym.
Psalms 109:18 He clothed hym selfe wyth cursynge lyke as wyth a rayment: yea it wente into hys bowels lyke water, and lyke oile into his bone
Psalms 109:19 Let it be vnto hym as the cloke that he hath vpon hym, and as the gyrdle that he is gyrded with al.
Psalms 109:20 Let it thus happen from the Lorde vnto myne enemyes, and to those that speake euel agaynst my soule.
Psalms 109:21 But deale thou wyth me, O Lorde God, accordynge vnto thy name, for swete is thy mercy. O deliuer me,
Psalms 109:22 for I am helplesse, and pore and my herte is wounded within me.
Psalms 109:23 I go hence lyke the shadowe that departeth, & am driuen away as the greshoppers.
Psalms 109:24 My knees are weake thorow fastynge my flesh is dryed vp for want of fatnesse.
Psalms 109:25 I am become a rebuke vnto them, they loke vpon me and shake their heades.
Psalms 109:26 Helpe me, O Lorde my God, oh saue me for thy mercies sake.
Psalms 109:27 That they maye knowe, how that thys is thy hand, and that thou hast done it.
Psalms 109:28 Though they curse, yet blesse thou: and let them be confounded, that ryse vp agaynst me, but let thy seruaunt reioyse.
Psalms 109:29 Let myne aduersaryes be clothed wyth their owne shame, as with a cloke.
Psalms 109:30 As for me, I wyl geue thanckes vnto the Lord wyth my mouth, and praise hym among the multitude.
Psalms 109:31 For he standeth at the ryght hand of the pore, to saue hym from suche as condempne hys soule.

CHAPTER: 110

Psalms 110:1 A Psalme of Dauyd. The Lorde sayde vnto my Lord: Syt thou on my ryght hande, vntyll I make thyne enemies thy fotestole.
Psalms 110:2 The Lord shal sende the rod of thy power out of Sion; be thou ruler euen in the myddest amonge thyne enemyes.
Psalms 110:3 In the daye of thy power shal thy people offer the frewyll offerynges wyth an holye worshyppe, the dewe of thy byrthe is of the wombe of the mornynge.
Psalms 110:4 The Lorde sware, and wyll not repente: Thou arte a priest for euer after the order of Melchisedec.
Psalms 110:5 The Lorde vpon thy ryghte hande, shall smyte euen kinges in the daye of hys wrath.
Psalms 110:6 He shall be iudge amonge the Heathen, he shall fyl them wyth deade bodyes, and smite in sunder the heades ouer diuerse countres.
Psalms 110:7 He shall dryncke of the broke in the waye, therfore shall he lyft vp his head.

CHAPTER: 111

Psalms 111:1 Prayse the euerlastynge. I wyll geue thanckes vnto the Lorde wyth my whole herte: secretly amonge the faythful and in the congregacyon:
Psalms 111:2 The worckes of the Lorde are greate, sought oute of all them, that haue pleasure therin.
Psalms 111:3 Hys worcke is worthy to be praysed and had in honoure, and his rightuousnes endureth for euer.
Psalms 111:4 The mercyfull and gracyous Lord hath so done his maruelous workes, that they ought to be had in remembraunce.
Psalms 111:5 He geueth meat vnto them, that feare him he is euer myndfull of hys couenaunte.
Psalms 111:6 He sheweth hys people the power of hys worckes, that he may geue them the herytage of the Heathen.
Psalms 111:7 The worckes of his hands are veryte and iudgment, all hys commaundementes are true.
Psalms 111:8 They stand fast for euer and euer, and are done in truth and equyte.
Psalms 111:9 He sent redempcyon vnto hys people, he hath commaunded his couenaunte for euer, holy and reuerente is his name
Psalms 111:10 The feare of the Lorde is the beginning of wysdome, a good vnderstandyng haue al they that do therafter: the prayse of it endureth for euer.

CHAPTER: 112

Psalms 112:1 Prayse the euerlastynge. Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, and hath great delite in hys commaundementes.
Psalms 112:2 Hys sede shal be mighty vpon earth the generacyon of the faythfull shalbe blessed.
Psalms 112:3 Ryches and, plenteousnesse shalbe in hys house, and hys ryghtuousnesse endureth for euer.
Psalms 112:4 Vnto the godly there aryseth vp lyghte in the darcknesse: he is mercyfull, louynge and ryghtuous.
Psalms 112:5 Well is he that is mercyfull, and lendeth gladly, and pondereth his wordes wyth discrecyon,
Psalms 112:6 For he shall neuer be moued, the ryghtuous shall be had in an euerlastynge remembraunce.
Psalms 112:7 He wyll not be afrayed for anye euyll tydynges, his herte standeth fast, and beleueth in the Lord.
Psalms 112:8 Hys hert is stablished, he wyl not shrynke, vntyl he se hys desyre vpon hys enemyes.
Psalms 112:9 He hath sparsed abrode, and geuen to the poore, hys ryghtuousnes remayneth for euer his horne shalbe exealted with honoure
Psalms 112:10 The vngodly shall se it, and it shall greue them: he shall gnash with his teeth, and consume awaye. and the desyre of the vngodlye shall perysh.

CHAPTER: 113

Psalms 113:1 Prayse the euerlastynge. Prayse the Lord (O ye seruauntes) O prayse the name of the Lorde.
Psalms 113:2 Blessed be the name of the lord, from this time forth euermore
Psalms 113:3 The Lords name is worthy to be praysed from the risynge vp of the Sun vnto the going downe of the same.
Psalms 113:4 The Lorde is hye aboue all Heathen, and his glory aboue the heauens.
Psalms 113:5 Who is lyke vnto the Lorde oure God, that hath his dwellynge so hye,
Psalms 113:6 whyche humbleth him selfe, to beholde that is in heauen and earth.
Psalms 113:7 Which taketh vp the simple out of the dust and lyfteth the poore out of the myre.
Psalms 113:8 That he may sette him amonge the prynces, euen amonge the prynces of hys people.
Psalms 113:9 Whyche maketh the baren woman to kepe house, and to be a ioyfull mothere of chyldren. Prayse the euerlastyng.

CHAPTER: 114

Psalms 114:1 When Israel came out of Egypt and the house of Iacob from among that straunge people.
Psalms 114:2 Iuda was his Sanctuary, Israell his domynyon.
Psalms 114:3 The sea saw that & fled, Iordan turned backe.
Psalms 114:4 The mountaynes skipped like rammes, and the lytle hylles like yong shepe.
Psalms 114:5 What ayled the, O thou sea, that thou fleddest so thou Iordan, that thou turnedest backe?
Psalms 114:6 Ye mountaynes that ye skypped lyke rammes: and ye litle hilles, like yong shepe?
Psalms 114:7 The earth trembled at the presence of the Lorde, at the presence of the God of Iacob.
Psalms 114:8 Whyche turned the harde rocke into a staudynge water, and the flynte stone into a spryngyng well.

CHAPTER: 115

Psalms 115:1 Not vnto vs, O Lorde not vnto vs. but vnto thy name geue the praise for thy louing mercye & faythfulnesse.
Psalms 115:2 Wherfore shal the Heathen say wher is now their God?
Psalms 115:3 As for oure God, he is in heauen, he doeth whatsoeuer it pleaseth him.
Psalms 115:4 Their ymages are but syluer and gold, euen the worke of mens handes.
Psalms 115:5 They haue mouthes, and speake not: eies haue they, but they se not.
Psalms 115:6 Thei haue eares, and heare not: noses haue they, but they smell not.
Psalms 115:7 They haue handes, and handle not, fete haue they, but they cannot goo, neyther can they speake thorow their throte.
Psalms 115:8 They that made them, are lyke vnto them and so are all suche as put theyr truste in them.
Psalms 115:9 But let Israell trust in the Lorde, for he is their succoure and defence.
Psalms 115:10 Let the house of Aaron put their truste in the Lorde for he is their succoure and defence
Psalms 115:11 They that feare the Lorde, lette them put their trust in the Lord, for he is their succour and defence.
Psalms 115:12 The Lorde is myndfull of vs, and blesseth vs: he blesseth the house of Israel, he blesseth the house of Aaron.
Psalms 115:13 Yea he blesseth al them that feare the Lord both smale and great.
Psalms 115:14 The Lorde encrease you more and more: you, and your children.
Psalms 115:15 For ye are the blessed of the Lord, whych made heauen and earth.
Psalms 115:16 Al the whole heauens are the Lordes, but the earth hath he geuen vnto the chyldren of men.
Psalms 115:17 The dead prayse not the (O Lorde) nether all they that go downe into sylence.
Psalms 115:18 But we wil prayse the Lord, from this time forth for euermore. Prayse the euerlastynge.

CHAPTER: 116

Psalms 116:1 I am wel pleased, that the Lord hath hearde the voyce of my prayer.
Psalms 116:2 That he hath enclyned his eare vnto me, therfore wil I cal vpon him as long as I lyue.
Psalms 116:3 The snares of death compased me round aboute, the paynes of hell gat hold vpon me I founde trouble and heauynesse.
Psalms 116:4 Then called I vpon the name of the Lord O Lorde: delyuer my soule.
Psalms 116:5 Gracious is the Lord, and rightuous, yea oure God is mercyfull.
Psalms 116:6 The Lorde preserueth the symple, I was brought downe, and he helped me.
Psalms 116:7 Turne agayne then vnto thy rest, O my soule, for the Lord hath geuen the thy desire.
Psalms 116:8 And why thou haste delyuered my soule from death, myne eyes from teares, and my fete from fawlyng.
Psalms 116:9 I wyll walcke before the Lorde, in the land of the lyuyng.
Psalms 116:10 I beleued, and therfore haue I spoken, but I was sore troubled.
Psalms 116:11 I sayde in my hast: Al men are liers.
Psalms 116:12 What rewarde shall I geue vnto the Lorde, for all the benyfytes that he hath done vnto me?
Psalms 116:13 I wyl receyue the, cuppe of saluacion, and call vpon the name of the Lord.
Psalms 116:14 I wyll paye my vowes in the presence of al his people,
Psalms 116:15 right deare in the syghte of the Lorde is the death of his saynctes.
Psalms 116:16 O Lorde, I am thy seruaunt, I am thy seruant, and the son of thy handmaide, thou hast broken my bondes in sonder.
Psalms 116:17 I wyl offre to the sacrifyce of thanckesgegeuynge, and wyll call vpon the name of the Lord.
Psalms 116:18 I wyll paye my vowes vnto the Lord in the syght of al his people,
Psalms 116:19 in the courtes of the Lordes house, euen in the middest of the, O Ierusalem. Prayse the euerlasting.

CHAPTER: 117

Psalms 117:1 O prayse the Lorde all ye Gentyles, laude him al ye people.
Psalms 117:2 For his mercyfull kyndnes is euer more and more toward vs, and the truth of the Lorde eudureth for euer. Prayse the euerlasting.

CHAPTER: 118

Psalms 118:1 O geue thankes vnto the Lord, for he is gracyous, & hys mercy endureth for euer.
Psalms 118:2 Let Israel now confesse, that his mercy eudureth for euer.
Psalms 118:3 Let the house of Aaron now confesse, that his mercy endureth for euer.
Psalms 118:4 Yea let them now that feare the Lorde confesse, that his mercy endureth for euer.
Psalms 118:5 I called vpon the lord in trouble, and the lord heard me at large.
Psalms 118:6 The lord is my helper, I wyll not feare what man doeth vnto me.
Psalms 118:7 The lord is my helper, and I shall se my desyre vpon myne enemyes.
Psalms 118:8 It is better to trust in the lord, then to put any cofydence in man.
Psalms 118:9 It is better to trust in the lord then to put any confydence in prynces.
Psalms 118:10 All Heathen compassed me round about but in the name of the lorde wyll I destroye them.
Psalms 118:11 They kepe me in on euery side, but in the name of the lord, I wyll destroy them.
Psalms 118:12 They came aboute me lyke bees, and wer as hote as the fyre in the thornes, but in the name of the Lorde I wyll destroye them.
Psalms 118:13 They thrust at me, that I myght fall, but the lorde was my helpe.
Psalms 118:14 The lorde is my strength, and my songe and is become my saluation.
Psalms 118:15 The voice of ioy and meyth is in the dwellynges of the rightuous, for the ryght hand of the Lord hath gotten the victory.
Psalms 118:16 The ryght hande of the Lord hath the preemynence, the ryght hande of the Lorde hath gotten the victory.
Psalms 118:17 I wyll not dye, but lyue, and declare the workes of the lord.
Psalms 118:18 The Lorde hath chastened and correcte me, but he hath not geuen me ouer vnto deathe.
Psalms 118:19 Open me the gates of ryghtuousnes, that I maye go in there thorowe, and geue thanckes vnto the Lord.
Psalms 118:20 This is the dore of the Lorde, the rightuous shall enter in thorow it.
Psalms 118:21 I thancke, the that thou hast herd me, and are become my saluatyon.
Psalms 118:22 The same stone whych the builders refused, is become the heade stone in the corner
Psalms 118:23 Thys was the Lordes doynge, and it is maruelous in our eyes.
Psalms 118:24 This is the, daye whych the Lorde hath made, let vs reioyse and be glad in it.
Psalms 118:25 Helpe now O lord O, lord sende vs now prosperity.
Psalms 118:26 Blessed be he that commeth in the name of the Lorde, we wysh you good lucke, ye that be of the house of the Lord.
Psalms 118:27 God is the lord, and hath shewed vs light O garnysh the solempne feaste wyth grene braunches, euen vnto the hornes of the aulter.
Psalms 118:28 Thou art my God, and I wil thancke the: thou art my God, and I wyll prayse the.
Psalms 118:29 O geue thanckes vnto the lorde, for he is gracyous, and his mercy endureth for euer.

CHAPTER: 119

Psalms 119:1 Aleph. Blessed are those that be vndefyled in the way: which walcke in the law of the Lord.
Psalms 119:2 Blessed are they that kepe hys testimonies, and seke him with their whole herte.
Psalms 119:3 Which walcke in hys wayes, and do no wickednes.
Psalms 119:4 Thou haste geuen strayte charge to kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:5 O that my wayes were stablished to kepe thy statutes.
Psalms 119:6 So shoulde I not be confounded while I haue respecte vnto all thy commaundemente
Psalms 119:7 I wyll thancke the wyth an vnfayned herte, because I am learned in the iudgmentes of thy ryghtuousnesse.
Psalms 119:8 I wyll kepe thy statutes, O forsake me not vtterly.
Psalms 119:9 Beth. Where withall shall a yonge man clense his waye? Euen by rulynge hym selfe after thy worde.
Psalms 119:10 Wyth my whole herte do I seke the, O let me not go wronge out of thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:11 Thy wordes haue I hyd wythin my hert that I should not synne against the.
Psalms 119:12 Praysed be thou O Lorde, O teache me thy statutes.
Psalms 119:13 With my lippes wil I be tellyng out all the iudgmentes of thy mouth.
Psalms 119:14 I haue as greate delyte in the way of thy the testimonies, as in al maner of ryches.
Psalms 119:15 I wyl exercise my selfe in thy commaundementes, and haue respect vnto thy fotepathe
Psalms 119:16 My delite shalbe in thy statutes, I wyll not forget thy wordes.
Psalms 119:17 Gimel. O do well vnto thy seruant, that I maye lyue and kepe thy wordes.
Psalms 119:18 Open thou myne eyes, and so shall I spy out wonderous thynges in thy lawe.
Psalms 119:19 I am a straunger vpon earth, O hide not thy commaundementes fro me.
Psalms 119:20 My soule breaketh out, for the very feruent desire that I haue alwaie vnto the iudgementes.
Psalms 119:21 Thou rebukest the proud, cursed are they that departe from thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:22 O turne fro me shame and rebuke, for I kepe thy testimonies.
Psalms 119:23 Princes also syt and speake against me but thy seruaunt is occupied in thy statutes.
Psalms 119:24 In thy testomonyes is my delite, they are my councelers.
Psalms 119:25 Deleth. My soule cleaueth to the dust, O quicken thou me accordyng to thy word.
Psalms 119:26 I knowledged my waies, and thou herdest me, O teach me then thy statutes.
Psalms 119:27 Make me to vnderstand the waye of thy commaundementes, and so shall I talcke of thy wonderous workes.
Psalms 119:28 My soule melteth awaye for verye heuynesse, O set me vp accordyng vnto thy word
Psalms 119:29 Take fro me the waye of lyeng, and graunte me thy lawe.
Psalms 119:30 I haue chosen the way of truth, thy iudgementes haue I layed before me.
Psalms 119:31 I stycke vnto thy testimonies, O Lorde confound me not.
Psalms 119:32 I wyll runne the waye of thy commaundementes, when thou haste comforted my herte.
Psalms 119:33 He. Teach me O lord the way of thy statutes and I shall kepe it vnto the ende.
Psalms 119:34 O geue me vnderstandyng, & I shall kepe thy lawe, yea I shal kepe it wyth my whole herte.
Psalms 119:35 Leade me in the pathe of thy commaundmentes, for that is my desyre,
Psalms 119:36 Enclyne myne herte vnto thy testymonies, and not to couetousnes.
Psalms 119:37 O turne awaye myne eyes, leste they behold vanite, and quycken me in thy way.
Psalms 119:38 O stablish thy word in thy seruaunt, that I may feare the.
Psalms 119:39 Take awaie the rebuke that I am afraied of, for thy iudgmentes are amyable.
Psalms 119:40 Beholde, my delyte is in thy commaundementes, O quicken me in thy ryghtuousnesse.
Psalms 119:41 Vau. Let thy louynge mercy come vnto me, O Lorde, and thy sauynge health accordynge vnto thy worde.
Psalms 119:42 That I may geue answere vnto my blasphemers, for my trust is thy word.
Psalms 119:43 O take not the worde of treuth vtterly out of my my mouthe, for my hope is in thy iudgementes.
Psalms 119:44 So shall I alwaye kepe thy lawe, yea for euer and euer.
Psalms 119:45 And I wyll walcke at lybertye, for I seke thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:46 I wyll speake of thy testimonyes euen before kynges, and wyll not be ashamed.
Psalms 119:47 My delyte shalbe in thy commaundementes whych I loue.
Psalms 119:48 My handes also wyll I lyft vp vnto thy commaundementes which I loue, and my talkinge shalbe of thy statutes.
Psalms 119:49 Zain. O thyncke vpon thy seruaunt as concernynge thy worde, wherin thou haste caused me to put my trust.
Psalms 119:50 For it is my comfort in my trouble, yea thy word quyckeneth me.
Psalms 119:51 The proude haue me greatly in derysyon yet shryncke not I from thy law.
Psalms 119:52 I remember thyne euerlasting iudgementes O Lorde, and am comforted.
Psalms 119:53 I am horrible afraied for the vngodly, that forsake thy law.
Psalms 119:54 Thy statutes are my songes in the house of my pylgremage.
Psalms 119:55 I thyncke vpon thy name, O Lorde, in the nyghte esason, and kepe thy lawe.
Psalms 119:56 It is mine owne, for I kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:57 Heth Thou art my porcion, O lord, I am purposed to kepe thy law.
Psalms 119:58 I make myne humble petycyon in thy presence wyth my whole herte, O be mercyfull vnto me accordynge vnto thy word.
Psalms 119:59 I cal myne owne wayes to remembrance, and turne my fete into thy testimonies.
Psalms 119:60 I make haste, and prolonge not the time, to kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:61 The congregacyons of the vngodly haue robbed me, but I forget not thy law.
Psalms 119:62 At midnight stand I vp, to geue thanckes vnto the, for the iudgmentes of thy ryghtuousnesse.
Psalms 119:63 I am a companyon of all them that feare the, and kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:64 The earth, O Lord, is ful of thy mercy. O teach me thy statutes.
Psalms 119:65 Teh. O Lord, thou hast dealt frendly wyth thy seruaunt, according vnto thy word.
Psalms 119:66 O learne me thy kyndnesse, nourtoure and knowlege, for I beleue thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:67 Before I was troubled, I wente wronge but now I kepe thy word.
Psalms 119:68 Thou art good & frendly, O teach me the statutes.
Psalms 119:69 The proud ymagyn lyes vpon me, but I kepe thy commaundementes with my whole herte.
Psalms 119:70 Their herte is as fat as brawne, but my delyte is in thy law.
Psalms 119:71 It is good for me that I haue bene in trouble, that I may learne thy statutes.
Psalms 119:72 The law of thy mouth is dearer vnto me, then thousandes of golde and siluer.
Psalms 119:73 Iod. Thy hands haue made me and fashyoned me, O geue me vnderstandyng, that I may learne thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:74 They that feare the, wyll be glad when they se me, because I put my truste in thy worde.
Psalms 119:75 I knowe, O Lorde, that thy iudgmentes are right, and that thou of very faithfulnes hast caused me to be troubled.
Psalms 119:76 O let thy mercyful kyndnesse be my comforte, accordynge to the promes that thou hast made vnto thy seruaunt.
Psalms 119:77 O let thy louyng mercies come vnto me, that I may lyue, for thy law is my delite.
Psalms 119:78 Let the proud be confounded, which handle me so falslye.
Psalms 119:79 But let such as feare the, and knowe the testimonies, be turned vnto me.
Psalms 119:80 O let myne herte be vndefyled in thy statutes that I be not ashamed.
Psalms 119:81 Caph. My soule longeth for thy sauynge health, for my trust is in thy word,
Psalms 119:82 Myne eyes long sore for thy word, saing: O when wylt thou comforte me?
Psalms 119:83 For I am become like a botel in the smoke, yet do not I forget thy statutes.
Psalms 119:84 How many are the dayes of thy seruaunt? When wilt thou be auenged of myne aduersaryes?
Psalms 119:85 The proude haue dygged pyttes for me, which are not after thy lawe.
Psalms 119:86 All thy commaundementes are true, they persecute me falsely, O be thou my helpe.
Psalms 119:87 They haue almooste made an ende of me vpon earth, but I forsake not thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:88 O quycken me after thy louynge kyndenes, and so shall I kepe the testimonyes of thy mouth.
Psalms 119:89 Lamed. O Lorde, thy worde endureth for euer in heauen.
Psalms 119:90 Thy trueth also remayneth from one generacion to another: thou hast layed the foundacion of the earth, and it abydeth.
Psalms 119:91 They contynue this daye accordinge too thyne ordinaunce, for all thinges serue the.
Psalms 119:92 If my delyte were not in thy lawe, I should perysh in my trouble.
Psalms 119:93 I will neuer forget thy commaundementes, for with them thou quickenest me.
Psalms 119:94 I am thyne, Oh helpe me, for I seke thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:95 The vngodly laye wayte for me too destroye me, but I considre thy testimonyes.
Psalms 119:96 I se that all thynges come to an ende, but thy commaundement is exeeadyng broade.
Psalms 119:97 Mem. O what loue haue I vnto thy law? all the daye longe is my talkyng of it.
Psalms 119:98 Thou thorow thy commaundement hast made me wyser then myne enemyes, for it is euer by me.
Psalms 119:99 I haue more vnderstandyng then all my teachers, for thy testimonies are my studye.
Psalms 119:100 Yea, I am wyser then the aged, for I kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:101 I refrayne my fete from euery euell waye, that I maye kepe thy woordes.
Psalms 119:102 I shrynke not from thy iudgementes, for thou teachest me.
Psalms 119:103 O howe swete are thy woordes vnto my throte? Yea, more then hony vnto my mouth.
Psalms 119:104 Thorow thy commaundementes I gette vnderstandynge, therefore I hate all false wayes.
Psalms 119:105 Nun. Thy woorde is a lanterne vnto my fete and a light vnto my pathes.
Psalms 119:106 I haue sworne and am stedfastly purposed, to kepe the iudgementes of thy righteousnesse.
Psalms 119:107 I am troubled aboue measure, quycken me, O Lord, according vnto thy worde.
Psalms 119:108 Let the frewill offeringes of my mouthe please the, O Lorde, and teache me thy iudgementes.
Psalms 119:109 My soule is alwaye in my hande, yet do not I forget thy lawe.
Psalms 119:110 The vngodly haue layed a snare for me, but yet swarue not I from thy commaundmentes.
Psalms 119:111 Thy testimonyes haue I claymed as myne heritage for euer: and why? thei are the very ioye of my herte.
Psalms 119:112 I applye myne herte to fulfil thy statutes alwaye, euen vnto the ende.
Psalms 119:113 Samech. I hate the vngodly, but thy law do I loue.
Psalms 119:114 Thou art my defence & shylde, my truste is in thy woorde.
Psalms 119:115 Away fro me ye wycked, I will kepe the commaundementes of my God.
Psalms 119:116 O stablish me according vnto thy worde, that I maye lyue, & let me not be disapoynted of my hope.
Psalms 119:117 Holde thou me vp, and I shall be safe: yea I shall euer be talkyng of thy statutes.
Psalms 119:118 Thou treadest doune all them that departe from thy statutes, for they ymagin but disceate.
Psalms 119:119 Thou puttest awaye all the vngodly of the earth lyke drosse, therfore I loue thy testymonies,
Psalms 119:120 My flesh trembleth for feare of the, and I am afrayed of thy iudgementes.
Psalms 119:121 Ain. I deale wt the thinge that is lawfull & ryght, O geue me not ouer vnto mine oppressours.
Psalms 119:122 Be thou suertye for thy seruaunte too do hym good, that the proude do me no wronge.
Psalms 119:123 Myne eyes are waysted awaye with lokyng for thy health, and for the worde of thy righteousnesse.
Psalms 119:124 O deale with thy seruaunt according vnto thy louing mercy, & teach me thy statutes.
Psalms 119:125 I am thy seruaunt, O graunte me vnderstanding, that I may know thy testimonies.
Psalms 119:126 It is tyme for the (O Lord) to lay to thine hande, for they haue destroyed thy lawe.
Psalms 119:127 For I loue thy commaundementes aboue golde and precious stone.
Psalms 119:128 Therfore holde I streyght all thy commaundementes, and all false wayes I vtterly abhorre.
Psalms 119:129 Phe. Thy testimonyes are wonderfull, therefore doth my soule kepe them.
Psalms 119:130 When thy woorde goeth forthe, it geueth light & vnderstandyng, euen vnto babes.
Psalms 119:131 I open my mouth and draw in my breath, for I desyre thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:132 O loke thou vpon me, & be mercifull, as thou vsest to do vnto those that loue thy name.
Psalms 119:133 Ordre my goinges after thy woorde that no wickednesse raygne in me.
Psalms 119:134 O delyuer me from the wrongeous dealinges of men, and so shall I kepe thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:135 Shewe the light of thy countenaunce vnto thy seruaunt, and learne me thy statutes.
Psalms 119:136 Myne eyes gusshe out with water, because men kepe not thy lawe.
Psalms 119:137 Zade. Ryghteous art thou, O Lorde, and true is thy judgement.
Psalms 119:138 Thy testimonyes that thou hast commaunded are exceadyng, righteous and true.
Psalms 119:139 My zeale hath euen consumed me, because myne enemyes haue forgotten thy wordes.
Psalms 119:140 Thy worde is tryed to the vttermost, and thy seruaunt loueth it.
Psalms 119:141 I am small and of no reputacion, yet do not I forget thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:142 Thy righteousnesse is an euerlastyng righteousnes, and thy lawe is true.
Psalms 119:143 Trouble and heuynesse haue taken holde vpon me, yet is my delite in thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:144 The righteousnes of thy testimonyes is euerlastyng, O graunt me vnderstandinge, and I shall lyue.
Psalms 119:145 Koph. I call with my whole herte, heare me, O Lorde, I will kepe thy statutes.
Psalms 119:146 Yea, euen vpon the do I call, helpe me, & I shall kepe thy testimonies.
Psalms 119:147 Early in the mornyng do I crye vnto the, for in thy worde is my trust.
Psalms 119:148 Myne eyes preuente the night watches, that I might be occupyed in thy wordes.
Psalms 119:149 Heare my voyce, O Lorde, accordynge vnto thy louyng kyndnesse, quycken me accordyng as thou art wont.
Psalms 119:150 They drawe nye that of malyce persecute me, and are farre from thy lawe.
Psalms 119:151 Be thou nye at hande also, O Lorde, for thy promyses are faythfull.
Psalms 119:152 As concernynge thy testimonies, I haue knowen euer sens the beginnuing, that thou hast grounded them for euer.
Psalms 119:153 Res. O considre myne aduersite, & deliuer me, for I do not forget thy lawe.
Psalms 119:154 Manteyn thou my cause and defende me, quycken me according vnto thy worde.
Psalms 119:155 Health is farre from the vngodly, for thei regarde not thy statutes.
Psalms 119:156 Great is thy mercy, O Lorde, quicken me as thou art wont.
Psalms 119:157 Many there are that trouble me, & persecute me, yet do not I swarue from thy testimonies.
Psalms 119:158 It greueth me, when I se, that the transgressours kepe not thy law.
Psalms 119:159 Considre, O Lorde, how I loue thy commaundementes, O quycken me with thy louyng kyndnesse.
Psalms 119:160 Thy worde is true from euerlastyng, all the iudgementes of thy righteousnesse endure for euer more.
Psalms 119:161 Sin. The princes persecute me withoute cause, but my herte standeth in awe of thy woordes.
Psalms 119:162 I am as gladde of thy worde, as one that fyndeth great spoyles.
Psalms 119:163 As for lyes, I hate and abhorre them, but thy law do I loue.
Psalms 119:164 Seuen times a daye do I prayse the, because of thy righteous iudgementes.
Psalms 119:165 Great is the peace that they haue whych loue thy law, and they are not offended at it.
Psalms 119:166 Lord, I loke for thy sauynge healthe, and do after thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:167 My soule kepeth thy testimonies, and loueth them exceadingly.
Psalms 119:168 I kepe thy commaundementes and testimonies, for all my wayes are before the.
Psalms 119:169 Thau. Let my complaynte come before the, O Lorde, geue me vnderstanding, accordynge vnto thy worde.
Psalms 119:170 Oh let my supplicacion come before the, deliuer me according to thy promes.
Psalms 119:171 My lyppes shall speake of thy prayse, seyng thou hast taught me thy statutes.
Psalms 119:172 Yea, my tonge shall synge of thy worde, for all thy commaundementes are right.
Psalms 119:173 Let thine hande helpe me, for I haue chosen thy commaundementes.
Psalms 119:174 I longe for thy sauyng health, O Lorde, and in thy law is my delyte.
Psalms 119:175 Oh let my soule lyue and prayse the, that thy iudgementes maye helpe me.
Psalms 119:176 I go astraye, lyke a shepe that is lost: Oh seke thy seruaunt, for I do not forget thy commaundementes.

CHAPTER: 120

Psalms 120:1 The song of the steares When I am in trouble, I cal vpon the Lorde, and he answereth me.
Psalms 120:2 Delyuer my soule, O Lord from liyng lippes, and from a disceatful tonge.
Psalms 120:3 What rewarde shalbe geuen or done vnto the, thou false tonge.
Psalms 120:4 Euen myghty and sharpe arowes, wyth hote burnynge coales.
Psalms 120:5 Who is me that my banyshmente endureth so longe: I dwel in the tabernacles of the sorowfull.
Psalms 120:6 My soule hath long dwelt amonge them that be enemies vnto peace,
Psalms 120:7 I laboured for peace, but when I spake therof, they made them to battayle.

CHAPTER: 121

Psalms 121:1 The song of the steares. I lyft vp myne eyes vnto the hylles, from whence commeth my helpe.
Psalms 121:2 My helpe commeth euen from the Lord which hath made heauen and earth.
Psalms 121:3 He wyll not suffer thy fote to be moued, and he that kepeth the slepeth not.
Psalms 121:4 Beholde, he that kepeth Israell, doth nether slomber nor slepe.
Psalms 121:5 The Lorde him selfe is thy keper, the Lorde is thy defence vpon thy ryght hande.
Psalms 121:6 So that the sunne shall not burne the by daye, nether the mone by nyght.
Psalms 121:7 The Lorde preserueth the from all euyll, yea it is the Lorde that kepeth thy soule.
Psalms 121:8 The Lorde preserueth thy goyng out and thy commynge in, from thys tyme forth for euer more.

CHAPTER: 122

Psalms 122:1 The songe of the steares. I was glad, when they sayed vnto me: we wyll go into the house of the Lorde.
Psalms 122:2 Oure fete shall stande in thy gates O Ierusalem.
Psalms 122:3 Ierusalem is buylded as a cytye, that is at vnyte in it selfe.
Psalms 122:4 For ther the tribes go vp, euen the tribes of the Lorde: to testyfye vnto Israel, to geue thanckes vnto the name of the Lorde.
Psalms 122:5 For there is the seate of iudgmente, euen the seate of the house of Dauyd.
Psalms 122:6 O praye for the peace of Ierusalem, they shall prospere that loue the.
Psalms 122:7 Peace be wyth thy walles, and plenteousnes within thy palaces.
Psalms 122:8 For my brethren and companions sakes, I wyll wysh the prosperite.
Psalms 122:9 Yea because of the house of the Lord oure God, I wyll seke to do the good.

CHAPTER: 123

Psalms 123:1 The songe of the steares. Vnto the lyft I vp mine eies, thou that dwelleste in the heauens.
Psalms 123:2 Beholde euen, as the eyes of seruauntes loke vnto the handes of their maysters: and as the eyes of a maiden vnto the handes of her mastresse, euen so oure eyes wayte vpon the Lorde our God vntylll he haue mercy vpon vs.
Psalms 123:3 Haue mercy vpon vs, O Lord, haue mercy vpon vs, for we are vtterly despysed.
Psalms 123:4 Our soule is filled with the scornefull reprofe of the welthy, and wyth the despitefulnes of the proude.

CHAPTER: 124

Psalms 124:1 The songe of the steares. If the Lord had not bene of oure side (now may Israel say)
Psalms 124:2 If the Lord had not bene of oure syde when men rose vp against vs.
Psalms 124:3 They had swalowed vs vp quicke when thei were so wrathfully displeased at vs.
Psalms 124:4 Yea the waters had drowned vs, the streame had gone ouer oure soule.
Psalms 124:5 The depe waters of the proud had gon euen vnto our soule.
Psalms 124:6 But praysed be the Lord, which hath not geuen vs ouer for a praie vnto their teeth.
Psalms 124:7 Oure soule is escaped, euen as a byrde out of the snare of the fouler: the snare is broken and we are delyuered.
