Matthew 14:19 And he commaunded the people to sit doune on the grasse: and toke the .v. loues and the .ij. fishes, and loked vp to heauen, and blessed, and brake and gaue the loues to his disciples, & the disciples gaue them to the people.
Matthew 14:20 And they did all eate, & were suffised. And they gathered vp the gobbets that remayned .xij. basketsful.
Matthew 14:21 And they that eate, were in numbre about .v.M. men beside women and chyldren.
Matthew 14:22 And strayght way Iesus made hys disciples into a ship, & to go ouer before him while he sent the people away.
Matthew 14:23 And assone as he had sent the people away, he went vp into a mountayn alone to pray, & when night was come, he was there him self alone.
Matthew 14:24 And the ship was now in the middest of the sea, & was toste wt waues, for it was a contrary wynde.
Matthew 14:25 In the .iiij. watch of the night. Iesus came vnto them walking on the sea.
Matthew 14:26 And when his disciples sawe him walkinge on the sea, they were troubled, saying: it is some spirite, & cried out for feare.
Matthew 14:27 And straight way Iesus spake vnto them saing be of good cheare, it is I, be not afrayed.
Matthew 14:28 Peter aunswered him & saied: master: if thou be he, bid me come vnto the on the water.
Matthew 14:29 And he saide come. And when Peter was come doun out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Iesus.
Matthew 14:30 But when he saw a mighty wynd, he was afrayed. And as he began to synke, he cried saying: master, saue me.
Matthew 14:31 And immediatly Iesus stretched forth his hande & caught him, & sayed to him. O thou litle fayth wherfore diddest thou doubt?
Matthew 14:32 And assone as they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.
Matthew 14:33 Then they that were in the ship came & worshipped him sayng: of a truth thou art the sonne of God.
Matthew 14:34 And when thei were come ouer, they went into the land of Genesareth.
Matthew 14:35 And when the men of the place had knowlege of him, they sent out into all the country rounde about, & brought vnto him al that were sicke,
Matthew 14:36 & besoughte him, that thei migh touche the hemme of his vesture only, & as many as touched it were made safe.

CHAPTER: 15

Matthew 15:1 Then came to Iesus Scribes and Phariseis from Hierusalem, sayinge:
Matthew 15:2 why do thy disciples transgresse the tradicions of the elders? for thei washe not their handes when they eate bread.
Matthew 15:3 He aunswered sayd vnto them: why do ye also transgresse the commaundement of God thorow your tradicions?
Matthew 15:4 For God commaunded saying: honoure thy father and mother, and he that curseth father or mother shall suffre death.
Matthew 15:5 But ye saye, euery man shal say to hys father or mother: that which thou desirest of me to helpe the with: is geuen to God,
Matthew 15:6 and so shall he not honour hys father or mother. And thus haue ye made, that the commaundement of God is without effecte, thorow your tradicions.
Matthew 15:7 Hypocrites, well prophecied of you Esaias sayinge:
Matthew 15:8 Thys people draweth nye vnto me with their mouthes, & honoureth me with their lippes, howe be it their hertes are farre from me:
Matthew 15:9 but in vayne they worshippe me teaching doctrines, which are nothyng but mens preceptes.
Matthew 15:10 And he called the people vnto hym, & sayd to them, heare and vnderstande.
Matthew 15:11 That whych goeth into the mouth, defileth not the man: but that whych commeth out of the mouthe, defileth the man.
Matthew 15:12 Then came hys disciples, and sayde vnto hym: Perceyuest thou not, how that the Phariseis are offended in hearing thys saying?
Matthew 15:13 He aunswered and sayd: al plantes whiche my heauenly father hath not planted, shalbe plucked vp by the rootes.
Matthew 15:14 Let them alone, thei be the blynde leaders of the blynd. If the blynd leede the blynde, both shall fall into the dytche.
Matthew 15:15 Then aunswered Peter and sayd to hym: declare vnto vs thys parable.
Matthew 15:16 Then sayde Iesus are ye yet without vnderstandyng?
Matthew 15:17 Perceyue ye not that whatsoeuer goeth in at the mouth, descendeth doune into the bealy, and is cast out into the draught?
Matthew 15:18 But those thynges, whiche procede out of the mouthe, come from the hert and they defyle the man.
Matthew 15:19 For out of the hert come euil thoughtes, murther, breakyng of wedlocke, whoredom, thefte, false, witnes bearing, blasphemye.
Matthew 15:20 These are the thynges which defyle a man. But to eate wt vnwashen handes, defileth not a man.
Matthew 15:21 And Iesus went thence, and departed into the costes of Tyre and Sidon
Matthew 15:22 And beholde a woman whych was a Cananite came out of the same costes, and cryed vnto hym sayinge: haue mercy on me Lord the sonne of Dauid, my doughter is piteously vexed with a deuel.
Matthew 15:23 And he gaue her neuer a woorde to aunswer. Then came to hym hys disciples, & besoughte hym saying: sende her away, for she foloweth vs criyng.
Matthew 15:24 He aunswered, and saide: I am not sent, but vnto the lost shepe of the house of Israel.
Matthew 15:25 Then she came and worshipped him saiyng master helpe me.
Matthew 15:26 He aunswered & sayde: It is not good, to take thy chyldrens bread, & to cast it to dogges.
Matthew 15:27 She aunswered & said: truth Lord, neuerthelesse the whelpes eate of the crommes, whiche fall from their masters table.
Matthew 15:28 Then Iesus aunswered and sayd vnto her: O woman, great is thy fayth, be it to the euen as thou desirest. And her doughter was made whole, euen at that same houre.
Matthew 15:29 Then Iesus went awaye from thence, and came vnto the sea of Galile, and went vp into a mountaine, and sate doune there.
Matthew 15:30 And much people came vnto him, hauynge with them, halt, blynd, domme, maymed, and other many: and cast them doune at Iesus fete. And he healed them,
Matthew 15:31 in so muche that the people wondred to se the domme speake, the maymed whole, the halt to go, and the blynde to se, And they glorified the God of Israel.
Matthew 15:32 Then Iesus called hys disciples to hym & sayd I haue compassion on the people, because they haue continued with me now .iij. dayes & haue nought to eate, and I wil not let them departe fasting, lest they perish in the waie.
Matthew 15:33 And his disciples sayd vnto hym, whence shoulde we get so muche breadde in the wildernes, as should suffice so great a multitude?
Matthew 15:34 And Iesus sayde vnto them: How many loues haue ye? And they sayde: seuen, and a fewe litle fishes.
Matthew 15:35 And he commaunded the people to sit doune on the grounde:
Matthew 15:36 and toke the seuen loues and the fishes, and gaue thankes, and brake them and gaue to hys disciples, & the disciples gaue them to the people.
Matthew 15:37 And they dyd all eate and were suffised. And they toke vp of the broken meate that was lefte .vij. baskettes full.
Matthew 15:38 And yet thei that eate were .iiij.M. men, beside women and chyldren.
Matthew 15:39 And he sent away the people & toke ship & came into the parties of Magdala.

CHAPTER: 16

Matthew 16:1 Then came the Phariseis and Saduceis, and dyd tempte hym, desiring hym to shew them some signe from heauen.
Matthew 16:2 He aunswered and saide vnto them. At euen ye saye, we shall haue fayre wedder, and that because the skye is reed:
Matthew 16:3 and in the mornynge ye saye: to daye shalbe foule wedder, & that because the skie is cloudy and redde. O ye hypocrites ye can discerne the fashion of the skie and can ye not discerne the signes of the times
Matthew 16:4 The froward nacion and aduouterous seketh a signe: and there shal no nother signe be geuen vnto them, but the signe of the prophet Ionas So lefte he them, and departed.
Matthew 16:5 And when his disciples were come to the otherside of the water, they had forgotten too take bread with them.
Matthew 16:6 Then Iesus sayd vnto them: Take hede and beware of the leuen of the Phariseis and of the Saduces.
Matthew 16:7 And thei thoughte in theim selues sayinge: because we haue brought no breade wyth vs.
Matthew 16:8 When Iesus vnderstode that, he sayd vnto them? O ye of litle fayth, why are your myndes cumbred because ye haue brought no bread?
Matthew 16:9 Do ye not yet perceyue, neither remember those fyue loues when there were .v.M. men, & how many baskettes toke ye vp:
Matthew 16:10 Neyther the seuen loues when there were .iiij. thousand, and how many baskettes toke ye vp?
Matthew 16:11 Why perceyue ye not then, that I spake not vnto you of bread, when I sayde: beware of the leuen of the Pharises and of the Saduces.
Matthew 16:12 Then vnderstode they, howe that he had not them beware of the leuen of breade: but of the doctrine of the Phariseis and of the Saduces.
Matthew 16:13 When Iesus came into the costes of the citie whych is called Cesarea Philippi, he axed his disciples sayinge: whome do men saye that I the sonne of man am?
Matthew 16:14 They sayde: some saye that thou arte Ihon Baptist, some Helyas, som Ieremias, or one of the Prophetes.
Matthew 16:15 He sayde vnto them: but whome saye ye that I am?
Matthew 16:16 Simon Peter aunswered and sayde: Thou arte Christ the sonne of the liuynge God.
Matthew 16:17 And Iesus aunswered and sayde to hym: happy arte thou Symon the sonne of Ionas, for fleshe & bloude hath not opened vnto the that, but my father which is in heauen.
Matthew 16:18 And I saye also vnto the that thou arte Peeter: and vpon thys rocke I wil buylde my congregacion. And the gates of hell shall not preuayle against it.
Matthew 16:19 And I wil geue vnto the, the keyes of the kyngdome of heauen, and whatsoeuer thou bindest vpon earth shalbe bounde in heauen, and whatsoeuer thon lowsest on earth shalbe lowsed in heauen.
Matthew 16:20 Then he charged hys disciples, that they should tell no man, that he was Iesus Christ.
Matthew 16:21 From that time forth Iesus beganne to shew vnto hys disciples, how that he must go vnto Ierusalem, and suffer many thinges of the elders, and of the hygh priestes, and of the scribes, and must be kylled: and ryse agayne the thyrde daye.
Matthew 16:22 But Peter toke hym asyde, and beganne to rebuke hym saying: master fauer thy selfe: thys shall not come vnto the.
Matthew 16:23 Then tourned he about and sayd vnto Peeter: come after me Sathan, thou offendest me, because thou sauorest not godly thynges, but worldly thynges.
Matthew 16:24 Iesus then sayde to hys disciples. If anye man will folow me, let hym forsake hym selfe, and take vp hys crosse and folowe me.
Matthew 16:25 For whosoeuer will saue hys lyfe, shall loose it. And whosoeuer shall loose hys lyfe for my sake shall finde it.
Matthew 16:26 What shall it proffet a man though he shoulde wynne al the whole world if he loose hys awne soule? Or els what shall a man geue to redeme his soule agayne withall?
Matthew 16:27 For the sonne of man shall come in the glorye of hys father, wyth hys aungels: & then shall he rewarde euery man accordyng to his dedes.
Matthew 16:28 Verely I saye vnto you, some there be among them that here stande, whiche shall not taste of death, till they shall haue sene the sonne of man come in hys kyngdom.

CHAPTER: 17

Matthew 17:1 And after .vi. dayes Iesus toke Peter and Iames and Ihon his brother, and broughte them vp into an hygh mountayne oute of the waye,
Matthew 17:2 and was transfigured before them, and his face did shyne as the sunne and hys clothes were as whyte as the light:
Matthew 17:3 & behold there appeared vnto theim Moyses & Helyas, talkyng with hym.
Matthew 17:4 Then aunswered Peter and sayd to Iesus: master here is good beyng for vs. If thou wilt, let vs make here thre tabernacles, one for the, & one for Moses, and one for Helyas.
Matthew 17:5 Whyle he yet speake, beholde a bryght cloude shadowed theim. And beholde there came a voyce out of the cloude, sayinge: this is my deare sonne, in whome I delite heare hym.
Matthew 17:6 And when the disciples hearde that, they fell on theyr faces and were soore afrayed.
Matthew 17:7 And Iesus came and touched them, and saide: arise and be not afrayed.
Matthew 17:8 And when they loked vp, they sawe no man saue Iesus onely.
Matthew 17:9 And as they came doune from the mountayne, Iesus charged them sayinge: se that ye shewe the vision to noman, vntyll the sonne of man be rysen agayne from death.
Matthew 17:10 And hys disciples axed of hym saying: Why then say the Scribes, that Helyas must first come?
Matthew 17:11 Iesus aunswered and sayde vnto them Helias shall first come and restore all thynges.
Matthew 17:12 And I say vnto you that Helyas is come already, and they knewe hym not: but haue done vnto hym whatsoeuer they lusted. In lykewise shal also the sonne of man suffer of them.
Matthew 17:13 Then the disciples perceiued that he spake vnto them of Ihon Baptist.
Matthew 17:14 And when they were come to the people, there came to hym a certayne man, and kneled doune to hym, and sayde:
Matthew 17:15 Master haue mercy on my sonne for he is francticke, and is sore vexed. For ofte tymes he falleth into the fire: and ofte into the water.
Matthew 17:16 And I broughte hym to thy disciples, and thei could not heale him.
Matthew 17:17 Iesus aunswered and sayde: O generation faythles and croked: howe longe shall I be wt you? how longe shal I suffre you? bryng him hydder to me.
Matthew 17:18 And Iesus rebuked the deuel, & he came out of hym. And the chylde was healed euen that same houre.
Matthew 17:19 Then came the disciples to Iesus secretly and sayd: Why coulde not we cast hym out?
Matthew 17:20 Iesus sayd vnto them: Because of your vnbelefe. For I saye verely vnto you: if ye hadde faith as a grayn of a mustard seede, ye should say vnto thys mountayne, remoue hence too yonder place, and it shoulde remoue, neyther shoulde any thyng be impossible for you too do.
Matthew 17:21 Howe be it this kynde goeth not out, but by prayer and fastynge.
Matthew 17:22 As they passed the tyme in Galile, Iesus sayde vnto them: the sonne of man shalbe betrayed into the handes of men,
Matthew 17:23 and they shall kyll hym, and the thyrde daye he shall ryse agayne. And they sorowed greatly.
Matthew 17:24 And when they were come to Capernaum they that were wont to gadre poll money, came to Peter and sayde: Doeth your master paye tribute?
Matthew 17:25 He sayd: yea. And when he was come into the house. Iesus spake fyrst to him, sayinge: What thinkest thou Simon? of whom do the kynges of the earth take tribute or pol money? of their chyldren, or of straungers?
Matthew 17:26 Peter sayde vnto hym: of straungers. Then sayde Iesus vnto hym agayne: Then are the chyldren fre.
Matthew 17:27 Neuerthelesse, lest we should offende them: go to the sea and caste in thyne angel, and take the fish that first cometh vp: & when thou hast opened hys mouth, thou shalt fynde a pece of twenty pence: that take and paye for me and the.

CHAPTER: 18

Matthew 18:1 The same tyme the disciples came vnto Iesus sayinge: who is the greatest in the kyngdom of heauen
Matthew 18:2 Iesus called a chylde vnto hym, and set hym in the middes of them:
Matthew 18:3 and sayde. Verely I saye vnto you: excepte ye tourne, and become as chyldren, ye cannot enter into the kyngedome of heauen.
Matthew 18:4 Who soeuer therfore humble hym selfe as thys chylde, the same is the greatest in the kyngedom of heauen.
Matthew 18:5 And whosoeuer receyueth suche a chylde in my name, receyueth me.
Matthew 18:6 But whosoeuer offende one of these litelone, whych beleue in me: it were better for hym, that a milstone were hanged about his necke, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
Matthew 18:7 Wo be vnto the worlde because of offences. Howe be it, it cannot be auoyded but that offences shall be geuen. Neuerthelesse woo be to the man, by whome the offence cometh.
Matthew 18:8 Wherfore if thy hande or thy fote offende the, cut hym of and cast hym from the. It is better for the to enter into lyfe halte or maymed, rather then thou shouldest hauinge two handes or two fete, be cast into euerlastynge fyre.
Matthew 18:9 And if also thyne eye offende the, plucke hym out and cast hym from the. It is better for the to entre into lyfe with one eye, then hauyng two eyes to be cast into hell fyre.
Matthew 18:10 Se that ye not dispise not one of these litelones. For I saye vnto you, that in heauen their aungels alwaies behold the face of my father which is in heauen.
Matthew 18:11 Yea, and the sonne of man is come to saue that whych is lost.
Matthew 18:12 Howe thynke ye? If a man haue an hundred shepe, & one of them be gone astray, doth he not leaue nynty and nyne in the mountaynes, and go & seke that one whych is gone astraye.
Matthew 18:13 If it happen that he fynde him, verely I say vnto you: he reioyseth more of that shepe, then of the nyntye and nyne, which went not astray.
Matthew 18:14 Euen so it is not the wil of your father in heauen, that one of these litelons shoulde perish.
Matthew 18:15 Moreouer, if thy brother trespase agaynst the, Go and tell hym hys fault betwene hym and the alone. If he heare the, thou hast wonne thy brother.
Matthew 18:16 But if he heare the not, then take yet with the one or two, that in the mouthe of two or thre witnesses, all thynges may be stablished.
Matthew 18:17 If he heare not them, tell it vnto the congregacion. If he heare not the congregacion, take hym as a Heathen man, & as a publican.
Matthew 18:18 Verely I saye vnto you, whatsoeuer ye bynde on earth, shalbe bounde in heauen. And whatsoeuer ye lowse on erth, shalbe lowsed in heauen.
Matthew 18:19 Agayne I say vnto you, that if two of you shall agre in earth vpon any maner thyng whatsoeuer they shall desire: it shalbe geuen them of my father whyche is in heauen.
Matthew 18:20 For where two or thre are gathered together in my name, there am I in the middes of them.
Matthew 18:21 Then came Peter to hym, & sayde: master howe ofte shall I forgeue my brother, if he synne agaynst me, seuen tymes?
Matthew 18:22 Iesus sayde vnto hym: I say not vnto the seuen times: but seuenty times seuen tymes.
Matthew 18:23 Therefore is the kyngedom of heauen lykened vnto a certayne kyng, whithe woulde take a countes of hys seruauntes.
Matthew 18:24 And when he had begon to recken: one was broughte vnto hym: which ought hym ten thousand talentes,
Matthew 18:25 whome because he had noughte to paye, hys master commaunded him to be solde, and his wyfe, and hys chyldren, and all that he had, & payment to be made.
Matthew 18:26 The seruaunt fel doune and besought hym sayinge: Syr geue me respyte, and I will paye it euery whyt.
Matthew 18:27 Then had the Lord pitye on that seruaunt, & lowsed him and forgaue hym the dette.
Matthew 18:28 And the sayd seruaunt went out & found one of hys felowes, which ought him an hundred pence, & layed handes on him, & toke hym by the throote sayinge: paye me that thou owest.
Matthew 18:29 And hys felowe fell doune & besoughte hym, saying: haue pacience with me, and I wil pay the all.
Matthew 18:30 But he woulde not, but wente and cast hym into pryson till he shoulde pay the det.
Matthew 18:31 When hys other felowes sawe what was done, they were very sory, and came and told vnto theyr Lord all that had happened.
Matthew 18:32 Then his Lorde called hym, and sayde vnto hym. O euill seruaunt I forgaue the al that det, because thou praiest me:
Matthew 18:33 was it not mete also that thou shouldest haue had compassion on thy felow, euen as I had pitie on the?
Matthew 18:34 And his lord was wroth and deliuered him to the iaylers, til he should paye all that was due to hym.
Matthew 18:35 So likewyse shal my heauenly father do vnto you except ye forgeue with your hertes, eache one to hys brother theyr trespasses.

CHAPTER: 19

Matthew 19:1 And it came to passe when Iesus had finished those sayinges, he gat him from Galile, and came into the coostes of Iury beyonde Iordan,
Matthew 19:2 and much people folowed hym, and he healed them there.
Matthew 19:3 Then came vnto him the Pharises, tempting him, & saying to hym: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wyfe for all maner of causes?
Matthew 19:4 He aunswered and sayde vnto them: Haue ye not reade, howe that he whiche made man at the beginnyng, made them man and woman
Matthew 19:5 and sayd: for this thynge, shall a man leaue father and mother & cleaue vnto his wyfe, & thei twayne but one flesh.
Matthew 19:6 Wherefore now are they not twaine, but one fleshe. Let not man therefore put a sunder, that whiche God hath couppled together.
Matthew 19:7 Then sayd they to him: why did Moyses commaund to geue a testimoniall of diuorcement, & to put her awaye?
Matthew 19:8 He sayde vnto them: Moyses because of the hardnes of youre hertes suffred you to put away your wyfes: But from the beginning it was not so.
Matthew 19:9 I say therfore vnto you, whosoeuer putteth awaye hys wyfe, (except it he for fornicacion) & marieth another, breaketh wedloke. And whosoeuer maryeth her, which is diuorced, doth commit aduoutry.
Matthew 19:10 Then sayde his disciples to him: if the matter be so betwene man and wyfe, then is it not good to marye.
Matthew 19:11 He sayde vnto them: all men can not awaye with that sayinge, saue they to whome it is geuen.
Matthew 19:12 There are chaste whiche were so borne out of theyr mothers bealy. And there are chaste whiche be made of men. And there be chast which haue made them selues chaste for the kyngdom of heauens sake. He that can take it let hym take it.
Matthew 19:13 Then were brought to him iong chyldren, that he should put his handes on them & praye. And the disciples rebuked them.
Matthew 19:14 But Iesus sayd suffer the chyldren and forbid them not to come to me: for of suche is the kyngdome of heauen.
Matthew 19:15 And when he had put his handes on them he departed thence.
Matthew 19:16 And beholde one came and saide to him: good master, what good thinge shall I do, that I maye haue eternall lyfe?
Matthew 19:17 He sayde to him: why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, & that is God. But if thou wilt enter into lyfe, kepe the commaundementes,
Matthew 19:18 The other sayd to him: Which And Iesus sayde: Breake no wedloke, kyll not, steale not: beare not false witues,
Matthew 19:19 honoure father and mother, and loue thy neyghboure as thy selfe.
Matthew 19:20 And the iong man sayd vnto him: I haue obserued all these thynges from my youth, what lacke I yet?
Matthew 19:21 And Iesus sayde vnto him, if thou wilt be perfecte go and sell that thou haste, and geue it to the poore, and thou shalt haue treasure in heauen, and come and folowe me.
Matthew 19:22 When the ionge man hearde that saying: he went away mournynge. For he had great possessions.
Matthew 19:23 Then Iesus sayd vnto his disciples: Verely I saye vnto you: it is harde for a riche man to enter into the kyngdom of heauen.
Matthew 19:24 And moreouer I saye vnto you, it is easier for a Camel to go thorow the eye of a nedle, then for a ryche man to entre into the kyngdom of God
Matthew 19:25 When his disciples hearde that, thei were exceadingly amased saying: who then can be saued?
Matthew 19:26 Iesus beheld them and sayde vnto them: with men this is impossible, but with God al thynges are possible.
Matthew 19:27 Then aunswered Peeter and sayde vnto hym: Beholde we haue forsaken all and folowed the, what shall we haue?
Matthew 19:28 Iesus sayde vnto them: Verely I saye vnto you: when the sonne of man shall sit in the seate of hys maiestie, yea, which folow me in the second geueracion, shall sitte also vpon .xij. seates, and iudge the .xij. tribes of Israel.
Matthew 19:29 And whosoeuer forsaketh houses, or brethren, or systers, other father or mother, or wyfe or chyldren, or landes, for my names sake, the same shal receyue an .C. folde, & shal enherite euerlasting life.
Matthew 19:30 Many that are firste shall be last, and the last shalbe the first.

CHAPTER: 20

Matthew 20:1 For the kyngedom of heauen is lyke vnto an housholder, which went out early in the mornynge to hyre labourers into hys vyneyarde.
Matthew 20:2 And he agreed with the labourers for a peny a daye, and sent them into hys vyneyarde.
Matthew 20:3 And he went out about the .iij. houre, and saw other standing ydel in the market place,
Matthew 20:4 and sayd vnto them, go ye also into my vineyard: and whatsoeuer is right, I wil geue you. And they went theyr waye.
Matthew 20:5 Agayn he went out about the sixt and nynth houre and did likewise.
Matthew 20:6 And he went out about the eleuenth houre, and founde other standynge ydel, and sayde vnto theim: Why stande ye here all the day ydell?
Matthew 20:7 They sayde vnto hym: because no man hath hyred vs. He sayde to them go ye also into my vyneyarde, & whatsoeuer is right, that shall ye receyue.
Matthew 20:8 When euen was come, the Lorde of the vineyarde sayde vnto hys Stewarde: call the labourers, and geue them their hyer, beginning at the laste, tyll thou come to the first.
Matthew 20:9 And they whiche were hyred about the eleuenth houre, came and receyued euery man a peny.
Matthew 20:10 Then came the first, supposing that they should receyue more, and they lykewise receyued euery man a peny.
Matthew 20:11 And when they had receyued it, they murmured agaynst the good man of the house
Matthew 20:12 saying: These laste haue wrought but one houre, and thou haste made theym equall vnto vs whiche haue borne the burthen, and heat of the daye.
Matthew 20:13 He aunswered to one of them, saying: frende I do the no wrong: diddest thou not agre with me for a peny?
Matthew 20:14 Take that which is thy duety, and go thy waye, I will geue vnto thys laste as muche as to the.
Matthew 20:15 Is it not lawful for me to do as me lusteth with myne owne? Is thyne eye euel because I am good?
Matthew 20:16 So the laste shalbe firste, and the first shalbe laste. For many are called, and few be chosen.
Matthew 20:17 And Iesus ascended to Ierusalem and toke the .xij. disciples a parte in the way, and sayde to them:
Matthew 20:18 Beholde we go vp to Ierusalem, and the sonne of man shalbe betrayed vnto the chief priestes and vnto the scribes: and they shal condemne hym to death,
Matthew 20:19 and shall deliuer hym to the gentels, to be mocked, to be scourged, & to be crucified, and the thirde daye he shall rise agayne.
Matthew 20:20 Then came to him the mother of Zebedes chyldren with her sonnes, worshippyng hym and desiring a certayn thinge of hym.
Matthew 20:21 And he saide vnto her: what wilt thou haue? She said vnto hym: Graunt that these my two sonnes maye sitte, the one on thy right hande, and the other on the lift hande in thy kyngdome
Matthew 20:22 Iesus aunswered and sayde: Ye wotte not what ye are. Are ye able to drinke of the cup that I shall drynke of: and to be baptised with the baptisme that I shalbe baptised wt?
Matthew 20:23 They aunswered to hym: that we are. And he sayde vnto them: Ye shall drynke of my cup, & shal be baptised with the baptisme that I shalbe baptised with. But to sit on my right hande and on my lifte hande, is not myne to geue: but to them for whome it is prepared of my father.
Matthew 20:24 And when the ten hearde this, they disdayned at the two brethren.
Matthew 20:25 But Iesus called them vnto hym and sayd: Ye know that the Lordes of the gentils haue domination ouer them. And they that are great, exercyse power ouer them.
Matthew 20:26 It shall not be so amonge you. But whosoeuer wil be great amonge you, let hym be your minister,
Matthew 20:27 and whosoeuer wil be chief, let hym be your seruaunt,
Matthew 20:28 euen as the sonne of man came not to be minnistred vnto, but to minister, and to geue his life for the redempcion of many.
Matthew 20:29 And as they departed from Hiericho, much people folowed hym.
Matthew 20:30 And beholde two blynd men sitting by the way syde, when thei heard Iesus passe by, cryed saying: Thou Lord the sonne of Dauid haue mercy on vs.
Matthew 20:31 And the people rebuked theym: because they shoulde holde their peace. But they cried the more sayinge: Haue mercy on vs thou Lord which art the sonne of Dauid.
Matthew 20:32 Then Iesus stode styll, & called them, and sayde: What will ye that I shoulde do to you?
Matthew 20:33 Thei sayde to him: Lorde, that our eyes maye be opened.
Matthew 20:34 Iesus had compassion on them, and touched their eyes. And immediatly their eyes receiued sight. And thei folowed him.

CHAPTER: 21

Matthew 21:1 When they drewe nygh vnto Ierusalem, and were come too Bethphage, to mount Oliuete: then sent Iesus two of his disciples,
Matthew 21:2 sayinge to them. Go into the towne that lyeth ouer agaynste you, and anone ye shal fynde an Asse bound, & her colte with her: lose them, and bringe them vnto me.
Matthew 21:3 And if any man saye ought vnto you, saye ye that the Lord hath nede of them: and streyght waye he will let them go.
Matthew 21:4 All this was done, to fulfill that whiche was spoken by the Prophet saying:
Matthew 21:5 Tel ye the doughter of Sion: beholde thyne kyng cometh vnto the meke, and sitting vpon an Asse and a colte, the fote of an Asse vsed to the yooke.
Matthew 21:6 The disciples went and did as Iesus commaunded them,
Matthew 21:7 & brought the Asse and the colte, and put on theym theyr clothes, and set him thereon.
Matthew 21:8 And many of the people spred their garmentes in the way. Other cut doune braunches from the trees, and strawed them in the waye.
Matthew 21:9 Moreouer the people that went before, and they also that came after, cryed sayinge: Hosanna to the sonne of Dauid. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lorde Hosanna in the hyest.
Matthew 21:10 And when he was come into Ierusalem all the cytye was moued sayinge: who is thys?
Matthew 21:11 And the people sayd: this is Iesus the prophet of Nazareth a citie of Galile.
Matthew 21:12 And Iesus wente into the temple of God, and caste out all them that soulde and bought in the temple, & ouerthrewe the tables of the money chaungers, & the seates of them that solde doues,
Matthew 21:13 and sayde to them: It is writen, my house shalbe called the house of prayer. But ye haue made it a denne of theues.
Matthew 21:14 And the blind and the halt came to hym in the temple and he healed them.
Matthew 21:15 When the chiefe priestes sawe the marueylles that he dyd, and the chyldren criynge in the temple and saying: Hosanna to the sonne of Dauid, they disdayned,
Matthew 21:16 and sayde vnto hym: hearest thou what these saye? Iesus sayde to them, yea. Haue ye neuer reade, of the mouth of babes and suckelynges thou hast ordeyned prayse?
Matthew 21:17 And he lefte them, and wente out of the cytye vnto Bethanye, and had hys abydynge there.
Matthew 21:18 In the mornynge as he retourned into the cytie agayn, he hungred,
Matthew 21:19 and spyed a fygge tree in the waye, and came to it, and found nothynge thereon, but leaues onely, and sayed to it, neuer frute growe on the hence forwardes. And anone the figge tre wyddered away
Matthew 21:20 And when hys disciples sawe that, they marueyled sayinge: How sone is the fygge tree wyddered awaye?
Matthew 21:21 Iesus answered, and sayd vnto them: Verelye I say vnto you: if ye shal haue fayth, and shall not dout ye shall not onely do that which I haue done to the fygge tree but also yf ye shall saye vnto thys mountayne, take thy selfe awaye and cast thy selfe into the sea it shall be done.
Matthew 21:22 And whatsoeuer ye shall axe in prayer (yf ye beleue) ye shall receyue it.
Matthew 21:23 And when he was come into the temple, the chiefe Priestes and the elders of that people came vnto hym as he was teachynge, and sayde. By what auctoritie doest thou these thynges and who gaue the thys power?
Matthew 21:24 Iesus answered, and sayed vnto them: I also wil axe of you a certayne questyon, whiche yf ye assoyle me, I in lyke wyse wyll tell you by what authoritie I do these thynges.
Matthew 21:25 The baptisme of Iohn whence was it: from heauen or of men? Then they reasoned amonge themselues, sayinge: yf we shall saye from heauen, he wyll laye vnto vs: why dyd ye not then beleue hym?
Matthew 21:26 But and yf we shall saye of men, then feare we the people. For all men helde Iohn as a Prophete.
Matthew 21:27 And they answered Iesus and sayed: we cannot tell. And he lykewyse sayd vnto them: neyther tell I you by what authoritie I do these thynges.
Matthew 21:28 What saye ye to thys? A certayne man had two sonnes, and came to the elder and sayde: sonne go and worke to daye in my vyneyarde.
Matthew 21:29 He answered and sayde, I wyll not: but after warde repented and wente.
Matthew 21:30 Then came he to the seconde, and sayed lykewyse. And he answered and sayed: I wyll syr: yet wente not.
Matthew 21:31 Whether of them twayne dyd the wyll of the father? And they sayde vnto hym: the fyrst. Iesus sayde vnto them: verelye I saye vnto you, that the Publycans and the harlotes shall come into the kyngedome of God before you.
Matthew 21:32 For Iohn came vnto you in the waye of ryghtuousnes, and ye beleued hym not. But the Publicans and the harlotes beleued hym. And yet ye (thoughe ye sawe it) were not yet moued wyth repentaunce, that ye myght afterwarde haue beleued hym.
Matthew 21:33 Herken another similitude. There was a certayne housholder, which planted a vyneyard, and hedged it rounde aboute and made a wynepresse in it, and buylt a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a straunge countrey.
Matthew 21:34 And when the tyme of the frute drewe neare, he sente hys seruauntes to the husbandmen to receyue the fruytes of it.
Matthew 21:35 And the husbandmen caughte hys seruauntes and bet one, kylled another, and stoned another.
Matthew 21:36 Agayne he sent other seruauntes, mo then the fyrste, and they serued them lykewyse.
Matthew 21:37 But last of all, he sent vnto them hys owne sonne, sayinge: they wyll feare my sonne.
Matthew 21:38 But when the husbandmen sawe the sonne, they sayde amonge them selues. Thys is the heyre: come let vs kyll hym, and let vs take hys enheritaunce to oure selues.
Matthew 21:39 And they caughte hym and thruste him out of the vyneyard, and slewe hym.
Matthew 21:40 When the Lorde of the vyneyard cometh, what wyll he do with those husbandmen?
Matthew 21:41 They sayed vnto hym: he wyll cruellye destroye those euyll persons, and wyll let out hys vyneyarde vnto other husbandmen, which shall delyuer hym the frute at tymes conuenient.
Matthew 21:42 Iesus sayde vnto them: dyd ye neuer reade in the scriptures. The stone which the buylders refused, the same is set in the principall parte of the corner: thys was the Lordes doynge, and it is meruelous in oure eyes.
Matthew 21:43 Therfore saye I vnto you the kyngdome of God shalbe taken from you, and shalbe gyuen to the gentyles, whiche shall brynge forth the frutes of it.
Matthew 21:44 And whosoeuer shall fall ou thys stone, he shalbe broken, but on whosoeuer it shall fall vpon, it wyll grynde hym to powder.
Matthew 21:45 And when the chiefe priestes and pharyses hearde these similitudes, they perceyued that he spake of them.
Matthew 21:46 And they wente aboute to laye handes on hym, but they feared the people, because they toke hym as a Prophete.

CHAPTER: 22

Matthew 22:1 And Iesus answered, and spake vnto them agayne in symylytudes sayinge.
Matthew 22:2 The kyngdome of heauen is like vnto a certayne kynge, whiche maryed hys sonne,
Matthew 22:3 and sent forth hys seruauntes to call them that were byd to the wedding, & they woulde not come.
Matthew 22:4 Agayne he sent forth other seruauntes saynge. Tell them which are bydden: beholde I haue prepared my dyner, myne oxen and my fatlynges are kylled, and all thinges are redy, come vnto the mariage.
Matthew 22:5 But they made lyght of it, and went theyr wayes: one to hys ferme place, an other about hys marchaundyse,
Matthew 22:6 the remnaunt toke hys seruauntes and intreated them vngodly and slewe them.
Matthew 22:7 When the kynge hearde that, he was wrothe and sente forthe hys warryers and destroyed those murtherers and brent vp theyr citie.
Matthew 22:8 Then sayde he to hys seruauntes: the wedding was prepared. But they which were bidden: were not worthye.
Matthew 22:9 Go ye therfore out into the hye waies, & as many as ye finde byd them to the mariage.
Matthew 22:10 The seruauntes went out into the hye wayes, and gaddered together as many as they could fynde. Both good & bad, and the weddynge was furnyshed with gestes.
Matthew 22:11 Then the kynge came in, to viset the gestes, and spyed there a man which had not on a weddynge garment,
Matthew 22:12 and sayd vnto hym, frend howe fortuned it that thou camest in hyther, and hast not on a weddinge garmente? And he was euen speachlesse.
Matthew 22:13 Then sayed the kynge to hys mynisters: take and bynde hym hande and fote, and caste hym into vtter darcknes, there shal be weping and gnashing of teeth.
Matthew 22:14 For manye are called and fewe be chosen.
Matthew 22:15 Then went the pharises and toke counsell how they myght tangle hym in hys wordes.
Matthew 22:16 And they sent vnto hym theyr discyples with Herodes seruauntes sayinge: Mayster, we knowe that thou art true, & teachest the waye of God truely: neither carest for any man, for thou considerest not mennes estate.
Matthew 22:17 Tel vs therfor how thinkest thou. Is it lawful to giue tribute vnto Cesar or not?
Matthew 22:18 Iesus perceyued theyr wickednes, & sayd: Why tempt ye me ye hypocrites?
Matthew 22:19 Let me se the tribute money. And they toke him a peny.
Matthew 22:20 And he sayd vnto them: whose is thys ymage & superscripcion?
Matthew 22:21 They sayed vnto him: Cesars. Then sayed he vnto them: Gyue therfore to Cesar, that which is Cesars: And gyue vnto God, that which is Goddes.
Matthew 22:22 When they hearde that they maruayled, and left hym, and went theyr waye.
Matthew 22:23 The same day the Saduces came to hym (which say that there is no resurreccion) axed him
Matthew 22:24 saying: Mayster, Moyses bad, yf a man dye hauyng no chyldren, that the brother marye hys wyfe, and reyse vp seed vnto hys brother.
Matthew 22:25 There were with vs seuen brethren, and the fyrst maryed and dyseased without yssue and left hys wyfe vnto his brother.
Matthew 22:26 Like wyse the second and the thyrde vnto the seuenth.
Matthew 22:27 Last of all the woman dyed also.
Matthew 22:28 Nowe in the resurreccyon whose wyfe shall she be of these seuen? For all had her.
Matthew 22:29 Iesus answered & sayd vnto them: ye are deceyued and vnderstande not the scriptures, nor yet the power of God.
Matthew 22:30 For in the resurrection they nether marye nor are maryed: but are as the angels in heauen.
Matthew 22:31 As touchyng the resurreccion of the dead: haue ye not reade what is sayd vnto you of God which sayth:
Matthew 22:32 I am Abrahams God, and Isaacks God. & the God of Iacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the liuynge.
Matthew 22:33 And when the people hearde that, they were astonyed at hys doctrine.
Matthew 22:34 When the Pharises had hearde, how that he had put the Saduces to silence, they drewe together,
Matthew 22:35 and one of them whiche was a doctoure of lawe, axed a question temptyng hym and sayinge:
Matthew 22:36 Mayster which is the chief commaundement in the lawe?
Matthew 22:37 Iesus sayd to him: Loue the Lord thy God with all thyne herte, and with all thy soule, and with al thy mynd.
Matthew 22:38 This is the fyrst and the chiefe commaundement.
Matthew 22:39 And there is another lyke vnto thys. Loue thy neyghboure as thy selfe.
Matthew 22:40 In these two commaundementes hange all the lawe & the Prophetes.
Matthew 22:41 Whyle the pharyses were gaddered together. Iesus axed them
Matthew 22:42 saying: what thynke ye of Christ? Whose sonne is he? They sayed vnto him: the sonne of Dauid.
Matthew 22:43 He sayed vnto them: how then doeth Dauid in sprite, call him Lorde, sayenge:
Matthew 22:44 The Lorde sayed to my Lord sit on my righthande: tyl I make thyne enemyes thy fotestole.
Matthew 22:45 If Dauid call hym Lorde, how is he than hys sonne?
Matthew 22:46 And none coulde aunswere hym agayne one worde, neyther durste any from that daye forth axe him any more question.

CHAPTER: 23

Matthew 23:1 Then spake Iesus to the people, & to hys disciples
Matthew 23:2 sayinge: The Scribes and the Phariseis sit in Moyses seate.
Matthew 23:3 All therfore whatsoeuer they bid you obserue, that obserue and do, but after their workes do not,
Matthew 23:4 for they say and do not. Yea, and they bynd heauy burthens and greuous to be borne and lay them on mens shoulders: but they them selfs will not heaue at them with one of theyr fyngers.
Matthew 23:5 All their workes thei do for to be sene of men. They set abroade theyr philateries, & make large borders on theyr garmentes,
Matthew 23:6 and loue to sit vppermoste at feastes, and to haue the chiefe seates in the Synagoges,
Matthew 23:7 and gretynges in the markettes, and too be called of men Rabbi.
Matthew 23:8 But ye shall not suffer youre selues to be called Rabbi. For one is your master, that is to witte Christ, and all ye are brethreu.
Matthew 23:9 And call no man your father vpon the earth, for there is but one your father, & he is in heauen.
Matthew 23:10 Be not called masters: for there is but one your master: and he is Christ.
Matthew 23:11 He that is greatest amonge you: shalbe your seruaunt.
Matthew 23:12 But whosoeuer exalteth hym selfe: shalbe brought lowe, and he that humbleth hym selfe, shalbe exalted.
Matthew 23:13 Wo be vnto you Scribes and Phariseis, hypocrites, for ye shut vp the kyngdome of heauen before men: ye youre selues go not in, neyther suffer ye them that come to enter in.
Matthew 23:14 Wo be vnto you Scribes and Phariseis, hypocrites, ye deuoure wyddowes houses, & that vnder a coloure of praieng long prayers wherfore ye shall receyue great damnacion.
Matthew 23:15 Wo be vnto you Scribes and Phariseis hypocrites: which compasse sea and lande, to brynge one into youre belefe: and when he is brought ye make hym two folde more the chyld of hell: then ye your selues are.
Matthew 23:16 Wo be vnto you blynde guydes, whyche say whosoeuer sweare by the temple, it is nothing, but whosoeuer sweared by the golde of the temple: he offendeth.
Matthew 23:17 Ye fooles and blind, whither is greater, the golde, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?
Matthew 23:18 And whosoeuer sweareth by the aultare, it is nothynge: but whosoeuer sweareth by the offeryng that lyeth on the aulter, offendeth.
Matthew 23:19 Ye fooles and blynde, whither is greater the offerynge, or the aulter whiche sanctifieth the offeryng?
Matthew 23:20 Whosoeuer therfore sweareth by the aultare, sweareth by it and by all that thereon is.
Matthew 23:21 And whosoeuer sweareth by the temple, sweareth by it and by hym that dwelleth therin.
Matthew 23:22 And he that sweareth by heauen sweareth by the seate of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.
Matthew 23:23 Wo be to you Scribes and Phariseis, hypocrites, which tythe mynte, anyse and commen, and leaue the wayghtyer matters of the lawe vndone: iudgement, mercy, and faythe. These ought ye to haue done, and not to haue lefte the other vndone.
Matthew 23:24 Ye blynde guydes whiche strayne out a gnat, and swallowe a cammell.
Matthew 23:25 Wo be to you Scribes and Pharises hypocrites, which make cleane the vtter side of the cuppe, & of the platter: but within they are ful of bribery and excesse.
Matthew 23:26 Thou blynd Pharisei, clense first the ynneside of the cup & platter, that the outside of them may be clene also.
Matthew 23:27 Wo be to you Scribes and Phariseis hypocrytes, for ye are lyke vnto paynted tombes, whiche appeare beautifull outwarde, but are within full of dead bones and of all filthines.
Matthew 23:28 So are ye, for outwarde ye apeare righteouse vnto men, when within, ye are full of hypocresie and iniquitie.
Matthew 23:29 Wo be vnto you Scribes and Phariseis hypocrites, ye buylde the tombes of the Prophetes and garnysh the sepulchres of the righteouse,
Matthew 23:30 and saye: if we had bene in the dayes of our fathers, we woulde not haue bene parteners with them in the bloude of the Prophetes.
Matthew 23:31 So then ye be witnesses to your selues, that ye are the chyldren of them whyche kylled the Prophetes.
Matthew 23:32 Fulfil ye likewyse the measure of your fathers.
Matthew 23:33 Ye serpentes and generacion of vppers howe shoulde ye scape the damnacion of hell?
Matthew 23:34 Wherfore, behold I send vnto you Prophetes, wise men, & Scribes. Of them ye shal kyl and crucifye: and of them ye shall scourge in your synagoges, and persecute from citye to citye
Matthew 23:35 that vpon you may come all the ryghtuous bloude that was shede vpon the earth, from the bloude of ryghtuous Abel, vnto the bloude of Zacharias the sonne of Barachias, whom ye slewe betwene the tempel and the aulter.
Matthew 23:36 Verely I say vnto you, al these things shall lyght vpon this generation.
Matthew 23:37 Ierusalem, Ierusalem which killest prophetes, and stone them which are sent to the: howe often would I haue gathered thy children together: as the henne gathered her chikens vnder her winges, but ye would not.
Matthew 23:38 Beholde your habitation shalbe left vnto you desolate.
Matthew 23:39 For I saye to you, ye shall not se me hence forth tyll that ye saye blessed is he that commeth in the name of the Lorde.

CHAPTER: 24

Matthew 24:1 And Iesus went out and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to hym for to shew him the building of the temple.
Matthew 24:2 Iesus sayde vnto them: Se ye not all these thinges? Verely I say vnto you there shal not be here left one stone vpon another that shall not be cast doune.
Matthew 24:3 And as he sate vpon the mounte Oliuet: his disciples came vnto him secretlye saying. Tell vs when these thinges shalbe: and what sygne shalbe of thy comminge and of the ende of the worlde?
Matthew 24:4 And Iesus aunswered and sayd vnto them: take hede that no man deceyue you.
Matthew 24:5 For many shal come in my name sayng: I am Christe: and shall deceyue many.
Matthew 24:6 Ye shall heare of warres? and of the fame of warres: but se that ye be not troubled. For all these thinges muste come to passe, but the ende is not yet.
Matthew 24:7 For nacion shall ryse against nacion and realme against realme: and ther shalbe pestylence, honger and earth quakes in certayne places?
Matthew 24:8 All these are the begynnynge of sorowes.
Matthew 24:9 Then shall they put you to trouble, and shall kyll you: and ye shalbe hated of all nacions for my names sake.
Matthew 24:10 And then shall manye be offended, and shal betray one another, and shall hate one the other.
Matthew 24:11 And manye false prophetes shall aryse, and shall deceyue manye.
Matthew 24:12 And because iniquite shall haue the vpper hande the loue of manye shall abate.
Matthew 24:13 But he that endureth to the ende, the same shall be safe.
Matthew 24:14 And this glad tydinges of the kingdome shalbe preached in all the worlde, for a wytnes vnto all nacions: & then shal the ende come.
Matthew 24:15 When ye therfore shall se the abhomination that betokeneth desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophete, stande in the holye place (let hym that readeth it, vnderstande it)
Matthew 24:16 then let theim which be in Iurye, flye into the mountaines.
Matthew 24:17 And let him which is on the house toppe not come doune to fetche anye thinge out of his house.
Matthew 24:18 Neither let him which in is the fielde returne backe to fetche his clothes.
Matthew 24:19 Wo in those daies to theim that are with childe, and to them that geue sucke.
Matthew 24:20 But praye that youre flyghte be not in the Winter, neyther on the saboth daye.
Matthew 24:21 For then shalbe great trybulacion such as was not from the beginninge of the worlde to this tyme, nor shalbe:
Matthew 24:22 yea, and except those dayes should be shortened, there shoulde no fleshe be saued: but for the chosens sake, those daies shalbe shortened.
Matthew 24:23 Then if anye man shall saye vnto you: lo here is Christe, or there is christ: beleue it not.
Matthew 24:24 For there shall aryse false Christes, and false prophetes, and shall do great myracles and wonders. In so much that if it were possyble the very electe should be deceiued.
Matthew 24:25 Take hede, I haue tolde you before.
Matthew 24:26 Wherfor if they shal saye vnto you: beholde he is in the deserte, in the secrete places beleue not.
Matthew 24:27 For as the lyghteninge cometh out of the east, and shyneth into the west, so shal the comminge of the sonne of man be.
Matthew 24:28 For whersoeuer a dead carkes is, euen thither wyl egles resort.
Matthew 24:29 Immediatly after the trybulations of those dayes, shall the sonne be darkened: and the mone shall not gyue hyr lyght, and the starre shal fall from heauen, & the powers of heauen shal moue.
Matthew 24:30 And then shal apeare the sygne of the sonne of man in heauen. And then shall all the kynredes of the earth morne, and they shall se the sonne of man come in the cloudes of heauen with power and great glorye.
Matthew 24:31 And he shall sende his aungels with the greate voyce of a trompe, and they shall gader together his chosen from the foure windes, and from the one ende of the worlde to the other.
Matthew 24:32 Learne a symylytude of the fygge tre: when his braunches are yet tendre, and his leaues spronge, ye knowe that sommer is nye,
Matthew 24:33 so lykewyse ye, when ye se all these thynges, be ye sure that it is neare euen at the dores.
Matthew 24:34 Verely I say vnto you, that this generation shal not passe tyll all these be fulfylled.
Matthew 24:35 Heauen & earth shal perishe, but my wordes shal abide.
Matthew 24:36 But of that daye and houre knoweth no man, no not the aungels of heauen, but my father onelye.
Matthew 24:37 As the tyme of Noe was, so lykewyse shal the commynge of the sonne of man be.
Matthew 24:38 For as in the dayes before the floude, they did eate & drinke, mary and were maried, euen vnto the daye that Noe entred into the shippe,
Matthew 24:39 & knew of nothinge, tyll the floude came and toke them all awaye. So shal also the comminge of the sonne of man be.
Matthew 24:40 Then two shall be in the fielde, the one shalbe receyued, and the other shalbe refused,
Matthew 24:41 two shalbe grindinge at the myll, the one shalbe receyued, and the other shalbe refused.
Matthew 24:42 Wake therfor, because ye knowe not what houre your maister wyl come.
Matthew 24:43 Of this be sure, that if the good man of the house knewe what houre the these woulde come, he would suerlye watche, and not suffer his house to be broken vp.
Matthew 24:44 Therfore be ye also redye, for in the houre ye thinke he woulde not, wyll the sonne of man come.
Matthew 24:45 Yf there be anye faythful seruaunt and wyse, whome his maister hath made rueler ouer his housholde to geue them meate in season conuenient:
Matthew 24:46 happy is that seruaunt whom his maister (when he cometh) shall fynde so doyinge.
Matthew 24:47 Verelye I saye vnto you, he shall make hym ruler ouer all hys goodes.
Matthew 24:48 But and if that euyll seruaunt shall saye in his herte, my maister wyll defer hys commynge,
Matthew 24:49 and begynne to smyte his felowes, yea, and to eate and to drinke with the dronken:
Matthew 24:50 that seruauntes maister wyll come in a daye when he loketh not for him, and in an houre that he is not ware of,
Matthew 24:51 and wyll deuide hym, and geue him his rewarde with hipocrites. There shalbe weping and gnashing of tethe.

CHAPTER: 25

Matthew 25:1 Then the kingdome of heauen shalbe lykened vnto ten virgins, which toke their lampes and went to mete the bridegrom,
Matthew 25:2 Fyue of them were folyshe, & fyue were wise.
Matthew 25:3 The folyshe toke theyr lampes, but toke none oyle with them.
Matthew 25:4 But the wise toke oyle with them in their vessels with their lampes also.
Matthew 25:5 Whyle the brydegrome taried, al slombred and slepte.
Matthew 25:6 And euen at midnight there was a crye made: beholde, the brydegrome cometh, goo out againste hym.
Matthew 25:7 Then all those virgins arose, and prepared their lampes.
Matthew 25:8 And the folishe sayed to the wise: gyue vs of your oyle for oure lampes go out.
Matthew 25:9 But the wyse aunswered sayinge not so, least there be not ynough for vs and you: but go rather to them that sell & by for your selues.
Matthew 25:10 And whyle they went to bye the brydegrome came: and they that were redie, went in wyth hym to the weddinge, and the gate was shut vp.
Matthew 25:11 Afterwardes cam also the other virgins sayinge: maister maister, open to vs.
Matthew 25:12 But he aunswered and sayd: verely I say vnto you: I knowe not you
Matthew 25:13 watche therfore: for ye knowe neither the daye nor yet the houre when the sonne of man shall come.
Matthew 25:14 Lykewyse as a certayne man, redye to take iorney to a straunge countre, called hys seruauntes and delyuered to them his goodes.
Matthew 25:15 And vnto one he gaue fyue talentes, to another .ij. and to another one: to euery man after his abylite, and straight waye departed.
Matthew 25:16 Then he that had receyued the .v. talentes, went and bestowed them and wan other fyue talentes.
Matthew 25:17 Likewise he that receiued two, gained other two.
Matthew 25:18 But he that receiued the one, wente and digged a pit in the earth and hid his maisters money.
Matthew 25:19 After a longe season the Lorde of those seruauntes came and rekened with them.
Matthew 25:20 Then came he that had receyued .v. talentes, and brought other .v. talentes, sayinge: maister thou delyuerest vnto me fyue talentes beholde I haue gained with them fyue talentes mo.
Matthew 25:21 Then his maister sayde vnto him: Well good seruaunt and faithfull. Thou hast bene faythfull in litle, I wyll make the rueler ouer muche enter in into thy maisters ioye.
Matthew 25:22 Also he that receiued .ij. talentes, came and sayed mayster thou deliuerest vnto me twoo talentes, beholde I haue won two other talentes with them.
Matthew 25:23 And his maister sayde vnto hym, well good seruaunt and faithfull. Thou hast bene faithfull in litle, I wyll make the ruler ouer much: go in into thy maisters ioye.
Matthew 25:24 Then he which had receiued the one talent, came & sayde, maister, I consydered that thou waste an harde man, which repest were thou sowest not, & gadderest where thou strawest not,
Matthew 25:25 and was therfore afraide, and went and hid thy talente in the earth: beholde, thou hast thyne owne.
Matthew 25:26 His maister aunswered and said vnto hym: thou euyll seruaunte and slouthful, thou knewest that I repe wher I sowed not, and gadder wher I strawed not:
Matthew 25:27 thou oughtest therfore to haue had my money to the chaungers, then at my commynge shoulde I haue receyued myne owne with vauntage.
Matthew 25:28 Take therfore the talent from him, and giue it vnto him which hath ten talentes.
Matthew 25:29 For vnto euerye man that hathe shalbe geuen, and he shall haue aboundaunce, and from hym that hath not, shall be taken awaye, euen that he hath.
Matthew 25:30 And caste that vnprofytable seruaunt into vtter darcknes: there shalbe wepinge & gnashinge of tethe.
Matthew 25:31 When the sonne of man cometh in hys glorye, and all the holye aungels with him, then shall he sytte vpon the seate of his glory,
Matthew 25:32 and before him shall be gathered all nations, and he shall separate them one from another, as a shephearde deuideth the shepe from the gootes.
Matthew 25:33 And he shall set the shepe on his right haude, and the gootes on his lyfte.
Matthew 25:34 Then shal the kinge saye to them on his right hand. Come ye blessed chyldren of my father, enheryte ye the kingdome prepared for you from the begynninge of the worlde.
Matthew 25:35 For I was an hungred & ye gaue me meate. I thirsted and ye gaue me drinke. I was herbourles and ye lodged me. I was naked and ye clothed me.
Matthew 25:36 I was sycke and ye visyted me. I was in pryson and ye came vnto me.
Matthew 25:37 Then shal the rightuous aunswere him sayinge, maister, when sawe we the an houngred, & fede the, or a thyrst, & gaue the drinke
Matthew 25:38 when sawe we the herborles, and lodged the? or naked and clothed the?
Matthew 25:39 or when sawe we the syke or in pryson and came vnto the?
Matthew 25:40 And the kinge shall aunswere and saye vnto theym: verelye I saye vnto you: in as much as ye haue done it to one of the least of these my brethren, ye haue done it vnto me.
Matthew 25:41 Then shall the kinge saye vnto them that shalbe on the lyfte hande. Departe from me ye cursed, into euerlastinge fyre, which is prepared for the deuyll and hys angels.
Matthew 25:42 For I was an hungred and ye gaue me no meate, I thyrsted and ye gaue me no drynke,
Matthew 25:43 I was herbourles, and ye lodged me not, I was naked and ye clothed me not, I was sicke and in pryson, and ye vysited me not.
Matthew 25:44 Then shal they answere him, sayinge: mayster when sawe we the an hungred, or a thyrst or herbourles, or naked, or sicke, or in pryson, and dyd not minister vnto the.
Matthew 25:45 Then shall he answere them, and saye: Verelye I saye vnto you, in as much as ye dyd it not to one of these little ones: ye dyd it not vnto me.
Matthew 25:46 And these shall go into euerlasting payne. And the righteouse into lyfe eternall.

CHAPTER: 26

Matthew 26:1 And it came to passe, when Iesus had finyshed all these sayinges, he sayed vnto hys disciples.
Matthew 26:2 Ye know that after two dayes shalbe easter, and the sonne of man shalbe delyuered to be crucifyed.
Matthew 26:3 Then assembled together the chiefe priestes and the scrybes and the elders of the people to the palaice of the hye priest, called Cayphas,
Matthew 26:4 and helde a counsell, howe they myghte take Iesus by sutteltie, and kyl hym.
Matthew 26:5 But they sayed, not on the holy daye, lest any vproure aryse amonge the people.
Matthew 26:6 When Iesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
Matthew 26:7 there came to him a woman, which had an alabaster boxe of precious oyntment, and poured it on hys heade, as he sate at the bourde.
Matthew 26:8 When hys discyples sawe that, they had indignacyon, sayinge: what neded thys waste?
Matthew 26:9 Thys oyntment myght haue bene wel solde, and geuen to the poore.
Matthew 26:10 When Iesus vnderstode that, he sayed vnto them: why trouble ye the woman? she hath wrought a good worke vpon me.
Matthew 26:11 For ye shall haue poore folke alwaies with you, but me shall ye not haue alwayes.
Matthew 26:12 And in that she casted thys oyntmente on my bodye, she dyd it to burye me with al.
Matthew 26:13 Verelye I saye vnto you, wheresoeuer thys gospell shalbe preached throughout al the world, there shal also thys that she hath done, be told for a memorial of her.
Matthew 26:14 Then one of the twelue called Iudas Iscaryoth went vnto the chiefe priestes,
Matthew 26:15 and sayd: What wyll ye geue me, and I wyll delyuer him vnto you? And they appoynted vnto him thyrtye peces of syluer.
Matthew 26:16 And from that tyme he sought oportunite to betraye hym.
Matthew 26:17 The fyrst day of swete bread the disciples came to Iesus sayinge vnto hym: where wylt thou that we prepare for the to eate the paschall lambe?
Matthew 26:18 And he sayde: go into the cytye vnto suche a man, & saye to hym: the mayster sayth my tyme is at hande, I wyll kepe myne easter at thy house wyth my disciples.
Matthew 26:19 And the discyples dyd as Iesus had appoynted them, and made redy the easter lambe.
Matthew 26:20 When the euen was come, he sate doune with the .xij.
Matthew 26:21 And as they dyd eate, he sayed: Verelye I saye vnto you, that one of you shal betraye me.
Matthew 26:22 And they were excedynge sorowfull, and beganne euery one of them to saye vnto hym: is it I mayster?
Matthew 26:23 He answered & sayed: he that deppeth hys hand wyth me in the dish the same shall betraye me.
Matthew 26:24 The sonne of man goeth as it is written of hym: but wo be to that man, by whome the sonne of man shalbe betrayed. It had ben good for that man, yf he had neuer bene borne.
Matthew 26:25 Then Iudas whiche betrayed him, answered and sayde: is it I mayster? He sayed vnto hym: thou hast sayed.
Matthew 26:26 As they dyd eate, Iesus toke bread and gyue thankes, brake it and gaue it to the discyples and sayed: Take, eate, thys is my body.
Matthew 26:27 And he toke the cup, & thanked, and gaue it them, saying: drynke of it euery one:
Matthew 26:28 For thys is my bloude of the newe testament, that shalbe shedde for many, for the remissyon of synnes.
Matthew 26:29 I saye vnto you: I wyll not drinke henceforth of this frute of the vyne tree, vntyll that daye, when I shall drinke it newe wyth you in my fathers kyngdome.
Matthew 26:30 And when they had sayde grace, they went oute into mounte oliuete.
Matthew 26:31 Then sayd Iesus vnto them: all ye shall be offended by me thys nyght. For it is written. I wyll smyte the shepehearde, and the shepe of the flocke shall be scattered abroade.
Matthew 26:32 But after I am rysen agayne, I wyll goo before you into Galile.
Matthew 26:33 Peter answered and sayd vnto hym, thoughe all men should be offended by the yet would I neuer be offended.
Matthew 26:34 Iesus sayde vnto hym: Verelye I saye vnto the that thys same nyghte before the cocke crowe thou shalte denye me thryse.
Matthew 26:35 Peter sayed vnto him: Yf I should dye with the, yet would I not denye the, lykewyse also sayed all the discyples.
Matthew 26:36 Then went Iesus with them into a place whiche is called Gethsemane, and sayde vnto the disciples: sit ye here whyle I go and praye yonder.
Matthew 26:37 And he toke with hym Peter and the two sonnes of Zebede, and began to waxe sorowful, and to be in an agonye.
Matthew 26:38 Then said Iesus vnto them: my soule is heauy euen to the death. Tary ye here & watche with me.
Matthew 26:39 And he went a lytell aparte, and fell flat on hys face and prayed sayinge: O my father, yf it be possible, let thys cup passe from me: neuerthelesse not as I wyll, but as thou wilte.
Matthew 26:40 And he came vnto the discyples, and founde them a slepe, & sayd to Peter: what, could ye not watche with me one houre:
Matthew 26:41 watche and praye, that ye fall not into temptacion. The spirite is ready, & the fleshe is weake.
Matthew 26:42 He wente awaye once more, & prayed, sayinge: O my father, yf thys cup can not passe awaye from me, but that I drinke of it, thy wyl be fulfylled.
Matthew 26:43 And he came and founde them a slepe agayne. For theyr eyes were heauye.
Matthew 26:44 And he lefte them, and went agayne and prayed the thyrde tyme, sayinge the same wordes.
Matthew 26:45 Then came he to hys discyples and sayde vnto them: Slepe hence forth and take youre reste. For lo the houre is at hande, and the sonne of man shalbe delyuered into the handes of synners.
Matthew 26:46 Ryse, let vs be goynge: beholde, he is at hand that shall betraye me.
Matthew 26:47 Whyle he yet spake: lo Iudas one of the twelue came, and with hym a great multitude with sweardes and staues, sent from the chiefe priestes and elders of the people.
Matthew 26:48 And he that betrayed hym, had geuen them a token, saying: whosoeuer I kysse, that same is he, laye handes on hym.
Matthew 26:49 And forthe wt al he came to Iesus, and sayed: hayle mayster and kyssed hym.
Matthew 26:50 And Iesus sayde vnto hym: frende, wherfore arte thou come? Then came they, and layed handes on Iesus, & toke him.
Matthew 26:51 And behold, one of them which were with Iesus, stretched out hys hande, and drue hys swerde, and stroke a seruaunt of the hye priest and smote of hys eare.
Matthew 26:52 Then sayed Iesus vnto hym: put vp thy swearde into hys place. For all that laye hand on the swearde, shal perysh with the swerd.
Matthew 26:53 Eyther thynkest thou that I can not nowe praye to my father, and he shal geue me more then .xij. legyons of Angelles?
Matthew 26:54 But how then shoulde the scriptures be fulfylled: for so must it be.
Matthew 26:55 The same tyme sayde Iesus to the multitude: ye be come out as it were vnto a thief with sweardes and staues, for to take me. I sat daylye teachynge in the temple amonge you, and ye toke me not.
Matthew 26:56 Al this was done that the scriptures of the Prophetes myght be fulfylled.
Matthew 26:57 Then all the disciples forsoke hym and fled. And they toke Iesus, and ledde hym to Cayphas the hye Priest, where the Scribes & the Elders were assembled.
Matthew 26:58 And Peter folowed him a farre of vnto the hye priestes palayce: and went in and sat with the seruauntes, to se the ende.
Matthew 26:59 The chiefe priestes and the elders, and all the counsell, sought false wytnes agaynst Iesus, for to put hym to death,
Matthew 26:60 but founde none in so muche that when manye false wytnesses came yet founde they none. At the laste came two false wytnesses,
Matthew 26:61 and sayed: Thys fellowe sayed: I can destroye the temple of God and buylde it agayne in thre dayes.
Matthew 26:62 And the chief priest arose, and sayd to hym: answerest thou nothynge? How is it that these beare wytnes agaynst the?
Matthew 26:63 But Iesus held hys peace: And the chief Priest answered and sayed to hym: I charge the in the name of the liuynge God, that thou tell vs whyther thou be Christ the sonne of God.
Matthew 26:64 Iesus sayd to him thou hast sayed. Neuertheles I say vnto you, hereafter shall ye se the sonne of men sittynge on the ryght hand of power, and come in the cloudes of the skye.
Matthew 26:65 Then the hye Priest rent hys clothes sayinge: He hath blasphemed: what nede we of anye more wytnesses? Beholde nowe ye haue heard hys blasphemy
Matthew 26:66 what thynke ye? They answered and said: he is worthy to dye.
Matthew 26:67 Then spat they in hys face and boffeted hym wyth fistes. And other smot hym with the palme of theyr handes
Matthew 26:68 on the face, sayinge tell vs thou Christ who is he that smote the?
Matthew 26:69 Peter sate without in the palayce. And a damsell came to him saying: Thou also wast with Iesus of Galile:
Matthew 26:70 but he denyed before them al sayinge: I wote not what thou sayst.
Matthew 26:71 When he was gone oute into the poorche, another wenche sawe hym, and sayde vnto them that were there. Thys felowe was also with Iesus of Nazareth,
Matthew 26:72 and agayne he denyed with an oth that he knew not the man.
Matthew 26:73 And after a whyle came vnto hym they that stode by & sayde vnto Peter: surely thou art euen one of them, for thy speache bewrayeth the.
Matthew 26:74 Then beganne he to corse and to sweare that he knew not the man. And immediatly the cocke crewe.
Matthew 26:75 And Peter remembred the wordes of Iesu whiche sayed vnto hym: before the cocke crowe, thou shalt deny me thryse. And went out at the dores and wept bitterlye.

CHAPTER: 27

Matthew 27:1 When the morning was come, al the chief priestes & the elders of the people held a counsell agaynste Iesus, to put hym to death,
Matthew 27:2 & broughte hym bounde and delyuered hym vnto Poncius Pilate the debitie.
Matthew 27:3 Then when Iudas whiche betrayed him, saw that he was condemned, he repented him selfe, and brought agayne the .xxx. plates of syluer to the chiefe priestes and elders
Matthew 27:4 saying: I haue synned betrayinge the innocent bloud. And they sayde: what is that to vs? Se thou to that.
Matthew 27:5 And he caste doune the syluer plates in the temple, and departed, and wente, and honge hym selfe.
Matthew 27:6 And the chief priestes toke the syluer plates, & sayed: it is not lawfull for to putte them into the treasury, because it is the pryce of bloude.
Matthew 27:7 And they toke counsell, and bought wyth them a potters fylde to bury straungers in.
Matthew 27:8 Wherfore that fylde is called the fylde of bloude vntyll thys day.
Matthew 27:9 Then was fulfylled that which was spoken by Ieremy the Prophete saying: and they toke thyrty syluer plates the pryce of hym that was valewed, whom they bought of the chyldren of Israell.
Matthew 27:10 and they gaue them for the potters fylde: as the Lorde appoynted me.
Matthew 27:11 Iesus stode before the debitie: and the debytie axed hym saying: Art thou the Kynge of the Iewes? Iesus sayed vnto hym: Thou sayest,
Matthew 27:12 and when he was accused of the chief priestes & elders he answered nothynge.
Matthew 27:13 Then sayed Pylate vnto him: hearest thou not how many thynges they laye agaynst the?
Matthew 27:14 And he answered hym to neuer a word: in so muche that the debitie marueyled greatly.
Matthew 27:15 At that feast, the debitye was wont to delyuer to the people a prysoner, whom they would desyre.
Matthew 27:16 He had then a notable prysonner called Barrabas.
Matthew 27:17 And when they were gathered together. Pylate sayde to them whether wyl ye that I let lose vnto you Barrabas or Iesu, whiche is called Christe?
Matthew 27:18 For he knewe well that for enuye they had delyuered hym.
Matthew 27:19 When he was set doune to geue iudgement hys wyfe sent to hym saying: haue thou nothing to do with that iust man. For I haue suffered manye thynges thys daye in a dreame about hym.
Matthew 27:20 But the chief priestes and the elders had perswaded the people, that they shulde axe Barrabas and destroye Iesus.
Matthew 27:21 Then the debitye answered and sayd vnto them: whether of the twayne wyll ye that I let lose vnto you? And they sayed: Barrabas
Matthew 27:22 Pylate sayed vnto them: what shall I do then with Iesus whiche is called Christ? They all sayed vnto hym: let hym be crucifyed.
Matthew 27:23 Then sayed the debitie: what euyll hath he done? And they cried the more sayinge: let hym be crucifyed.
Matthew 27:24 When Pilate sawe that he preuayled nothyng but the more busynes was made, he toke water and washed his handes before the people sayinge I am innocent of the bloude of this iust persone, or on your perille be it.
Matthew 27:25 Then aunswered al the people & sayed, his bloude be on vs and on oure children.
Matthew 27:26 Then let he Barrabas louse vnto them, and schourged Iesus, and deliuered hym to be crucyfyed.
Matthew 27:27 Then the souldiers of the debytye toke Iesus to the common hall, and gathered to hym all the companye.
Matthew 27:28 And they strypped him, and put on him a purpyll roobe,
Matthew 27:29 and platted a croune of thornes & put vpon his head, and a reed in his ryght hande, & bowed their knees before him and mocked hym, sayinge: hayle kinge of the Iewes,
Matthew 27:30 and spitted vpon hym & toke the reed and smote him on the head.
Matthew 27:31 And when they had mocked hym: they toke the robe of hym agayn, and put his owne rayment on hym, and lead him awaye to crucyfye hym.
Matthew 27:32 And as they came out, they found a man of Cyren named Symon: him they compelled to beare his crosse.
Matthew 27:33 And when they came vnto the place, called Golgotha (that is to saye: a place of dead mens sculles)
Matthew 27:34 they gaue hym veneger to drynke mengled with gall. And when he had tasted therof: he woulde not drinke.
Matthew 27:35 When they had crucifyed hym: they parted his garmentes, and did cast lottes, to fulfyll that was spoken by the prophete. They deuided my garmentes amonge them, and vpon my vesture dyd cast lottes.
Matthew 27:36 And they sate and watched him there.
Matthew 27:37 And they set vp ouer his head the cause of his death written. This is Iesus the kinge of the Iewes.
Matthew 27:38 And ther were two theues crucifyed with him one on the right hande, and another on the lyfte.
Matthew 27:39 They that passed by, reuyled hym wagginge their heades
Matthew 27:40 & sayinge: Thou that destroyest the temple of God and buyldest it in thre dayes: saue thy selfe. If thou be the sonne of God: come doune from the crosse.
Matthew 27:41 Lykewise also the hye priestes mockynge hym with the scrybes and elders sayde.
Matthew 27:42 He saued other, him selfe he can not saue. If he be the kinge of Israel let him now come doune from the crosse, and we wyll beleue him.
Matthew 27:43 He trusted in God, let hym deliuer hym now, if he wyl haue him: for he sayde I am the sonne of God.
Matthew 27:44 That same also the theues which were crucified with him cast in his teth.
Matthew 27:45 From the syxte houre was there darcknes ouer all the lande vnto the ninthe houre.
Matthew 27:46 And aboute the ninthe houre Iesus cryed with a loude voice sayinge: Eli Eli lama sabathani. That is to saye, my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Matthew 27:47 Some of them that stode ther, when they hearde that, saied. This man called for Helias.
Matthew 27:48 And straight waye one of them ranne & toke a sponge and fylled it full of veneger, and put it on a rede, and gaue him to drinke.
Matthew 27:49 Other sayed, let be: let vs se whither Helias wyll come and delyuer hym.
Matthew 27:50 Iesus cryed agayne with a loude voyce and yeldeth vp the ghost.
Matthew 27:51 And beholde the vayle of the tempell dyd rent in twayne from the toppe to the bottome and the earth dyd quake, and the rockes did rent,
Matthew 27:52 and graues did open, and the bodies of manye saynctes which slept arose
Matthew 27:53 & came out of the graues after his resurreccion: and came into the holy citie and appered vnto manye.
Matthew 27:54 When the Centurion and they that were with hym watchinge Iesus, sawe the earth quake and those thinges whiche happened they feared greatly sayinge: Of a surtye this was the sonne of God.
Matthew 27:55 And many women were there, beholding him a farre of, which folowed Iesus from Galile, ministring vnto him.
Matthew 27:56 Among which was Marye Magdalena and Marye the mother of Iames & Ioses, and the mother of Zebedes children.
Matthew 27:57 When the euen was come, there came a riche man of Aramathia named Ioseph, which same also was Iesus disciple.
Matthew 27:58 He wente to Pilate and begged the bodye of Iesus, Then Pilate commaunded the body to be deliuered.
Matthew 27:59 And Ioseph toke the body, & wrapped it in a cleane linnen cloth,
Matthew 27:60 & put it in his newe tombe: which he had hewen out, euen in the rocke and rolled a great stone to the dore of the sepulchre and departed.
Matthew 27:61 And ther was Marye Magdalene and the other Mary syttynge ouer agaynste the sepulchre.
Matthew 27:62 The nexte daye that foloweth good fryday the hye pryestes and phariseis gothe them selues to Pilate
Matthew 27:63 and sayd: Syr, we remembre that this deceyuer sayed whyle he was yet alyue. After thre daies I will aryse agayne.
Matthew 27:64 Commaunde therfore that the sepulchre be made sure vntyll the thirde daye lest peraduenture his disciples come, and steale him away, and saye vnto the people, he is rysen from death, & the last errourre be worste then the fyrste.
Matthew 27:65 Pylate sayde vnto them: Take watche men: Go, and make it as sure as ye can.
Matthew 27:66 And they went and made the sepulchre sure with watche men, and sealed the stone.

CHAPTER: 28

Matthew 28:1 The Saboth daye at euen which dauneth the morowe after the saboth. Mary Magdalene, & the other Marye came to se the sepulchre.
Matthew 28:2 And beholde there was a great earthquake. For the aungell of the Lorde descended from heauen: & came & rowled backe the stone from the dore, and sat vpon it.
Matthew 28:3 His countenaunce was lyke lyghtnyng, & his raymente whyte as snowe.
Matthew 28:4 And for feare of him the kepers were astonnied and became as dead men.
Matthew 28:5 The aungel aunswered & sayd to the women: feare ye not. I knowe that ye seke Iesus, whiche was crucifyed:
Matthew 28:6 he is not here: he is rysen as he sayd. Come & se the place where the Lord was put,
Matthew 28:7 & go quickly & tel hys discyples that he is rysen from death. And behold, he wil go before you into Galile, there ye shall se hym. Lo, I haue tolde you.
Matthew 28:8 And thei departed quickly from the sepulchre with feare & greate ioye: & dyd runne to bring hys disciples word.
Matthew 28:9 And as they went to tell hys disciples: beholde, Iesus met them saying al hayle. And they came & helde him by the fete and worshypped him.
Matthew 28:10 Then sayde Iesus vnto them: be not afrayd. Go and tel my brethren that they go into Galile, & there shal they se me.
Matthew 28:11 When they were gone: beholde, some of the kepers came into the citye, & shewed vnto the hye Priestes all the thynges that were happened.
Matthew 28:12 And they gathered them together with the elders, and toke counsel, & gaue large money vnto the souldiers,
Matthew 28:13 sayinge: Saye that his discyples came by night, & stole hym away whyle ye slept:
Matthew 28:14 and yf thys come to the rulers eares, we wyll pease him, & saue you harmles.
Matthew 28:15 And they toke the money & did as thei were taughte. And this saiynge is noysed amonge the Iewes vnto thys daye.
Matthew 28:16 Then the .xi. disciples wente away into Galile, into a mountayne wher Iesus had appointed them.
Matthew 28:17 And when they sawe hym they worshipped hym. But some of them doubted.
Matthew 28:18 And Iesus came and spake vnto them saiynge: all power is geuen vnto me in heauen and in earth.
Matthew 28:19 Go therfore & teache all nacyons, baptisyng them in the name of the father, and the sonne, & the holye ghoste.
Matthew 28:20 Teachyng then to obserue all thynges whatsoeuer I commaunded you, And lo I am with you alwaye, euen vntyll the ende of the worlde.

BOOK: Mark

CHAPTER: 1

Mark 1:1 The begynning of the gospell of Iesu Christ, the sonne of God,
Mark 1:2 as it is written in the prophetes. Beholde, I send my messenger before thy face which shal prepare thy waye before the
Mark 1:3 The voyce of a cryer in the wildernes prepare the waye of the Lord: make hys pathes strayghte.
Mark 1:4 Iohn dyd baptyse in the wyldernes, and preache the baptisme of repentaunce: for the remissyon of synnes.
Mark 1:5 And all the lande of Iury and they of Ierusalem wente out vnto him, & were all baptysed of hym in the riuer Iordan: confessyng theyr synnes.
Mark 1:6 Iohn was clothed with camylles heare, & with a gerdyll of a skyn about hys loynes. And he dyd eate locustes, and wilde honey,
Mark 1:7 & preached saiynge: a stronger then I commeth after me, whose shoe latchet I am not worthy to stoupe doune, and vnlose.
Mark 1:8 I haue baptysed you with water: but he shal baptyse you with the holye ghost.
Mark 1:9 And it came to passe in those dayes, that Iesus came from Nazareth, a citye of Galile: and was baptysed of Iohn in Iordan.
Mark 1:10 And assone as he was come out of the water Iohn saw heauen open, and the holy ghost descendynge vpon him lyke a doue.
Mark 1:11 And there came a voyce from heauen: Thou arte my dere sonne in whom I delyte.
Mark 1:12 And immediatly the spirite draue hym into wyldernes,
Mark 1:13 & he was there in the wyldernes .xl. dayes, and was tempted of Sathan, & was with wylde beastes. And the Aungels minystred vnto hym.
Mark 1:14 After Iohn was taken, Iesus came into Galyle, preachynge the gospell of the kyngedom of God,
Mark 1:15 and sayinge: the tyme is come, & the kyngdome of God is at hande, repente & beleue the Gospell.
Mark 1:16 And as he walked by the sea of Galile, he saw Simon & Andrew hys brother, castyng nettes into the sea, for they were fishers.
Mark 1:17 And Iesus sayde vnto them: folowe me, and I wyll make you fishers of men:
Mark 1:18 And strayghtwaye they forsoke theyr nettes, and folowed hym.
Mark 1:19 And when he had gone a lyttell further thence, he sawe Iames the sonne of Zebede, & Iohn hys brother, euen as they were in the shyppe mendynge theyr nettes.
Mark 1:20 And anone he called them. And they left theyr father Zebede in the shyppe with hys hyred seruauntes, & went theyr waye after hym.
Mark 1:21 And they entred into Capernaum: & straight waye on the Saboth dayes, he entred into the synagoge & taught.
Mark 1:22 And they merueyled at hys learning. For he taught them as one that had power with hym, and not as the scrybes.
Mark 1:23 And there was in theyr Synagoge a man vexed with an vncleane spirite, that cryed
Mark 1:24 saiyng: let be: what haue we to do with the thou Iesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroy vs, I knowe the what thou arte, euen the holye of God.
Mark 1:25 And Iesus rebuked him, saying: hold thy peace, and come out of hym.
