Mark 15:36 And one ran and fylled a sponge full of vyneger and put it on a rede, and gaue him to drinke, saying let him alone, let vs se whither Helyas wyll come and take him doune.
Mark 15:37 But Iesus cryeth with a loude voice, and gaue vp the ghost.
Mark 15:38 And the vayle of the temple dyd rent in two peces from the toppe to the bottome.
Mark 15:39 And when the Centurion which stode before him, sawe that he so cried and gaue vp the ghost he sayde: truly this man was the sonne of God.
Mark 15:40 Ther were also women a good waye of beholdyng hym: among whom was Mary Magdalen, and Marye the mother of Iames the lytle, and of Ioses, & Mary Salome:
Mark 15:41 whiche also when he was in Galile, folowed hym, and mynistred vnto hym: and manye other women, whiche came vp with hym vnto Ierusalem:
Mark 15:42 And now when night was come (because it was the euen that goeth before the Saboth)
Mark 15:43 Ioseph of Arimathia a noble Councelloure which also loked for the kyngdome of God, came and went in boldly vnto Pylate, & begged the bodye of Iesu.
Mark 15:44 And Pylate merueyled that he was already deade, and called vnto hym the Centurion, and axed of hym, whether he had bene anye whyle deade.
Mark 15:45 And when he knewe the truth of the Centuryon, he gaue the body to Ioseph.
Mark 15:46 And he bought a lynnen clothe, and toke him doune, and wrapped him in the lynnen clothe, and layde hym in a tombe that was hewen out of the rocke, and rolled a stone vnto the dore of the sepulchre.
Mark 15:47 And Mary Magdalen & Marye Ioses behelde where he was layed.

CHAPTER: 16

Mark 16:1 And when the Saboth was past. Mary Magdalen, and Mary Iacobi, and Salome, boughte odours, that they myghte come & anoynt hym.
Mark 16:2 And very early in the morninge the next daye after the Saboth daye they came to the sepulchre, when the sunne was rysen.
Mark 16:3 And they sayed one to another: who shal rolle vs awaye the stone from the dore of the sepulchre?
Mark 16:4 And when they loked, they sawe howe the stone was rolled awaye: for it was a verye great one.
Mark 16:5 And they wente into the sepulchre, and sawe a yonge man syttyng on the ryght syde, clothed in a long white garment, & they were abashed.
Mark 16:6 And he sayed vnto them, be not afrayed: ye seke Iesus of Nazareth whiche was crucifyed. He is rysen, he is not here. Beholde the place where they put hym.
Mark 16:7 But go your waye, and tell hys discyples and namelye Peter: He wil go before you into Galile, there shal ye se him as he sayde vnto you.
Mark 16:8 And they wente oute quickly, and fled from the sepulchre. For they trembled and were amased. Neyther sayed they anye thynge to anye man, for they were afrayed.
Mark 16:9 When Iesus was rysen the morowe after the Saboth daye, he appeared fyrst to Marye Magdalen, out of whome he cast seuen deuils.
Mark 16:10 And she went and tolde them that were wyth hym as they mourned & wepte.
Mark 16:11 And when they heard that he was alyue, and he had appeared to her, they beleued it not.
Mark 16:12 After that he appered to two of them in a straunge fygure, as they walked and went into the countre.
Mark 16:13 And they wente and tolde it to the remnaunt. And they beleued them neyther.
Mark 16:14 After that he appeared vnto the eleuen, as they sate at meat, and caste in theyr tethe theyr vnbelese and hardnes of hert: because they beleued not them which had sene hym after hys resurreccyon.
Mark 16:15 And he sayed to them: Go ye into all the worlde, and preache the glad tydynges to all creatures,
Mark 16:16 he that beleueth & is baptised, shall be saued. But he that beleueth not, shalbe damned.
Mark 16:17 And these sygnes shall folowe them that beleue. In my name they shall caste oute deuils, & shall speake with newe tonges,
Mark 16:18 & shall kyll serpentes, and yf they drinke any deadly thynge, it shall not hurte them. They shal lay theyr handes on the sycke, and they shal recouer.
Mark 16:19 So then when the Lorde had spoken vnto them: he was receyued into heauen, and is set doune on the ryght hande of God.
Mark 16:20 And they wente forth and preached euerye where. And the Lorde wrought with them, and confyrmed the word wt miracles that folowed.

BOOK: Luke

CHAPTER: 1

Luke 1:1 For asmuche as manye haue taken in hande to compyle a treatyse of those thynges which are surelye knowen amonge vs,
Luke 1:2 euen as they declared them vnto vs, which from the begynnynge sawe theim their selues, and were ministers at the doyinge,
Luke 1:3 I determined also, assone as I had searched out dylygentlye all thinges from the beginning, that then I would write vnto the, good Theophilus:
Luke 1:4 that thou mightest knowe the certaintye of those thynges wherof thou art enfourmed.
Luke 1:5 Ther was in the dayes of Herode kynge of Iurye, a certaine prieste named Zacharias, of the course of Abaia. And his wyfe was of the doughters of Aaron and her name was Elizabeth.
Luke 1:6 Both were perfect before God, and walked in al the lawes and ordinaunces of the Lorde, that no man coulde fynde faute with them.
Luke 1:7 And they had no childe: because that Elyzabeth was barren, and both were well striken in age.
Luke 1:8 And it came to passe, as he executed the priestes office before God, as his course came
Luke 1:9 (accordinge to the custome of the pryestes offyce) his lot was to bourne incense.
Luke 1:10 And wente into the tempell of the Lorde and the whole multytude of the people were without in prayer while incense was a burninge.
Luke 1:11 And ther appeared vnto hym an Aungell of the Lorde standynge on the ryght syde of the altare of incense.
Luke 1:12 And when Zacharias sawe him, he was abashed, and feare came on him.
Luke 1:13 And the aungel sayde vnto him: feare not Zacharye, for thy prayer is heard: And thy wyfe Elysabeth shall beare the a sonne, & thou shalt call his name Iohn,
Luke 1:14 and thou shalt haue ioye and gladnes, and manye shall reioyce at his birth.
Luke 1:15 For he shalbe greate in the syght of the Lorde, and shall neyther drinke wyne nor stronge drinke. And he shalbe fylled with the holy ghost, euen in his mothers wombe:
Luke 1:16 and manye of the children of Israel shal he turne to their Lorde God.
Luke 1:17 And he shall go before hym in the spryte of power of Helyas, to turne the hertes of the fathers to the chyldren and the vnbeleuers to the wisdome of the iust men, to make the people redy for the Lord.
Luke 1:18 And Zacharias sayde vnto the aungel: wherby shal I knowe this? seyinge that I am olde and my wyfe well stricken in yeares.
Luke 1:19 And the aungell aunswered and sayed vnto hym. I am Gabryel that stande in the presence of God, and am sente to speake to the: & shewe the these glad tidinges.
Luke 1:20 And behold thou shalt be dombe, and not able to speake vnto the tyme that these thinges be performed, because thou beleuest not my wordes whiche shalbe fulfylled in their ceason.
Luke 1:21 And the people wayted for Zacharias, and maruayled that he taryed in the temple.
Luke 1:22 And when he came out he coulde not speake to them. Wherby they perceyued that he had sene some vysyon in the temple. And he beckened vnto them, and remayned speacheles.
Luke 1:23 And it fortuned assone as the time of his offyce was out, he departed home into his owne house.
Luke 1:24 And after those dayes his wyfe Elyzabeth conceyued and hid hir selfe .v. monethes, sayinge.
Luke 1:25 This wyfe hath God dealt with me in the dayes when he loked on me, to take from me the rebuke that I suffred amonge men.
Luke 1:26 And in the .vi. moneth the aungell Gabriel was sent from God, vnto a citye of Galile, named Nazareth,
Luke 1:27 to a vyrgin spoused to a man whose name was Ioseph, of the house of Dauid, and the virgins name was Mary.
Luke 1:28 And the aungel wente in vnto her, & sayde Hayle full of grace, the Lorde is with the: blessed art thou amonge women.
Luke 1:29 When she sawe hym, she was abashed at his sayinge: and caste in her mynde what maner of salutacion that shoulde be.
Luke 1:30 And the aungell sayed vnto her: feare not Mary: for thou haste founde grace wyth God.
Luke 1:31 Lo: thou shalt conceyue in thy wombe & shalt beare a sonne, and shalt call his name Iesus.
Luke 1:32 He shalbe greate, and shalbe called the sonne of the hiest. And the Lorde God shal geue to hym the seat of his father Dauid,
Luke 1:33 and he shall raigne ouer the house of Iacob for euer, & of his kingdome shall be no ende.
Luke 1:34 Then sayde Mary to the aungell. How shall this be, seyinge I knowe not a man?
Luke 1:35 And the aungell aunswered and sayd vnto her: The holye ghoste shall come vnto the, and the power of the hyest shall ouer shadowe the. Therfore also that holye thynge whiche shall be borne shalbe called the sonne of God.
Luke 1:36 And beholde thy cosyn Elyzabeth hath also conceyued a sonne in her age: & thys is her syxt moneth though she be called barren:
Luke 1:37 for with God can nothing be vnpossyble.
Luke 1:38 And Marye sayde: beholde the hande mayden of the Lord, be it vnto me euen as thou haste said. And the aungel departed from her.
Luke 1:39 And Mary arose in those dayes, & went into the mountaines with hast, into a cytye of Iurye,
Luke 1:40 and entred into the house of Zachary, and saluted Elisabeth.
Luke 1:41 And it fortuned as Elysabeth hearde the salutacion of Marye, the babe spronge in her belly. And Elizabeth was fylled with the holye ghost,
Luke 1:42 and cryed wyth a loude voice, and sayde: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the frute of thy wombe.
Luke 1:43 And whence happeneth this to me that the mother of my Lorde shoulde come to me?
Luke 1:44 For lo, assone as the voice of thy salutacion sounded in myne eares, the babe sprange in my bellye for ioye.
Luke 1:45 And blessed art thou that beleuedest: for those thinges shall be performed, whiche were tolde the from the Lorde.
Luke 1:46 And Marye sayde: My soule magnifyed the Lorde.
Luke 1:47 And my sprete reioyceth in God my sauiour.
Luke 1:48 For he hath loked on the poore degre of his hande maiden. Beholde now from henceforth shall all generacions cal me blessed.
Luke 1:49 For he that is mightye hath done to me great thinges, and holy is his name.
Luke 1:50 And his mercy is on them that feare hym thorowe out all generacions.
Luke 1:51 He sheweth strength with his arme, he scattereth them that are proude in the ymagynacion of their hertes.
Luke 1:52 He putteth doune the mightye from their seates, and exalteth them of low degre.
Luke 1:53 He fylleth the hongry with good thinges, & sendeth away the ryche empty.
Luke 1:54 He remembreth mercye, and helpeth his sernaunte Israell.
Luke 1:55 Euen as he promysed to our fathers Abraham and to his sede for euer.
Luke 1:56 And Marye abode with her aboute a .iij. moneths, and retourned againe to her owne house.
Luke 1:57 Elyzabeths time was come that she should be delyuered, and she brought forth a sonne.
Luke 1:58 And her neighbours and her cosyne harde tell howe the Lorde had shewed great mercye vpon her, And they reioyceth with her.
Luke 1:59 And it fortuned the .viij. daye, they came to circuncyse the childe, and called his name Zacharias, after the name of his father.
Luke 1:60 How be it his mother aunswered, and sayde: not so, but he shalbe called Ihon.
Luke 1:61 And they saide vnto her: There is none of thy kinne that is named with this name.
Luke 1:62 And they made sygnes to his father: howe he woulde haue him called.
Luke 1:63 And he axeth for writtyng tables, and wrote sayinge: his name is Ihon. And they maruayled al.
Luke 1:64 And his mouthe was opened immediatlye, and his tonge also, and he spake laudinge God.
Luke 1:65 And feare came on all them that dwelt nye vnto them. And all these sayinges were noysed abrode throughout al the hyll country of Iury,
Luke 1:66 and all that hearde them laide them vp in their hartes sayinge: What maner chylde shall this be? And the hande of the Lorde was with him.
Luke 1:67 And his father Zacharias was fylled with the holye ghost, and prophecied sayinge:
Luke 1:68 Blessed be the Lorde God of Israel, for he hath visyted and redemed his people.
Luke 1:69 And hath reysed vp an horne of saluacion vnto vs in the house of his seruaunt Dauid.
Luke 1:70 Euen as he promised by the mouthe of his holye prophetes which were sence the worlde began.
Luke 1:71 That we shoulde be saued from oure enemyes, & from the power of all that hath vs.
Luke 1:72 To fulfyll the mercy promysed to oure fathers, and to remember his holye couenaunt.
Luke 1:73 And to performe the othe which he sware to oure father Abraham,
Luke 1:74 for to geue vs. That we delyuered out of the power of oure enemyes, might serue him without feare
Luke 1:75 all the dayes of our lyfe, in such holynes and ryghtuousnes as are accept before hym.
Luke 1:76 And thou chylde shalt be called the prophete of the hiest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lorde to prepare his wayes.
Luke 1:77 And to geue knowledge of saluacion vnto his people for the remissyon of synnes.
Luke 1:78 Through the tender mercye of our God, wherby the daye sprynge from on hye hath vysyted vs.
Luke 1:79 To geue lyght to them that sate in darcknes & in shadowe of death, and to guyde oure fete into the waye of peace.
Luke 1:80 And the chylde grewe and wexed stronge in spirite and was in wyldernes tyll the daye came when he shoulde shewe him selfe vnto the Israelytes.

CHAPTER: 2

Luke 2:1 And it chaunced in those dayes: that there wente out a commaundemente from Auguste the Emperour, that al the worlde should be taxed.
Luke 2:2 And this taxynge was the fyrste, and executed when Syrenius was lieftenaunt in Siria.
Luke 2:3 And euerye man wente into his owne citye to be taxed.
Luke 2:4 And Ioseph also ascended from Galyle: out of a cytye called Nazareth, into Iury: vnto the citye of Dauid which is called Bethleem, because he was of the house and lynage of Dauid,
Luke 2:5 to be taxed with Marye his spoused wyfe whiche was with childe.
Luke 2:6 And it fortuned whyle they were there, her tyme was come that she shoulde be deliuered.
Luke 2:7 And she brought forth her first begotten sonne, and wrapped him in swadlynge clothes, and layed him in a maunger, because ther was no roume for them within the ynne.
Luke 2:8 And there were in the same region shepherdes abydinge in the fyelde, and watchinge theyr flocke by night.
Luke 2:9 And lo: the aungel of the Lord stode harde by them, and the brightnes of the Lord shone round about them, and they were sore afrayed.
Luke 2:10 But the aungel sayde vnto them: Be not afrayed. For beholde, I bringe you tydinges of greate ioye that shall come to al the people:
Luke 2:11 for vnto you is borne this day in the citye of Dauid, a sauioure whiche is Christe the Lorde.
Luke 2:12 And take this for a sygne: ye shall fynde the chylde swadled and layed in a maunger.
Luke 2:13 And strayght waye there was with the aungel a multitude of heauenly souldiours, laudinge God and sayinge:
Luke 2:14 Glory to God on hye, and peace on the earth: and vnto men reioysynge.
Luke 2:15 And it fortuned, assone as the aungels were gone awaye from them into heauen, the shepherdes sayed one to another: let vs go euen vnto Bethleem & se this thing that is happened which the Lorde hath shewed vnto vs.
Luke 2:16 And they came with haste: and founde Mary and Ioseph and the babe layed in a maunger.
Luke 2:17 And when they had sene it, they published abroade the sayinge which was tolde them of that chylde.
Luke 2:18 And all that heard it, wondered at those thinges whiche were tolde them of the shepherdes.
Luke 2:19 But Mary kept all those sayinges, and pondered them in her herte.
Luke 2:20 And the shepherdes retourned, praisynge and lauding God for all that they had hearde and sene, euen as it was tolde vnto them.
Luke 2:21 And when the eyght daye was come, that the chylde shoulde be circuncysed, his name was called Iesus, which was named of the aungell before he was conceyued in the wombe.
Luke 2:22 And when the tyme of their puryfycacion (after the lawe of Moyses) was come, they brought him to Ierusalem, to presente hym to the Lorde
Luke 2:23 (as it is wryttem in the lawe of the Lorde: euerye male that fyrst openeth the mattrix, shall be called holye to the Lord)
Luke 2:24 and to offer (as it is sayde in the lawe of the Lorde) a payre of turtel doues or two yonge pygyons.
Luke 2:25 And beholde ther was a man in Hierusalem whose name was Symeon. And the same man was iuste and feared God, and longed for the consolacion of Israel and the holye ghost was in him.
Luke 2:26 And an aunswere was geuen him of the holye ghost, that he shoulde not se death, before he had sene the Lordes Christe.
Luke 2:27 And he came by inspiration into the tempell. And when the father and mother broughte in the childe Iesus, to do for him after the custome of the lawe,
Luke 2:28 then toke he him vp in hys armes and sayed.
Luke 2:29 Lorde. Nowe lettest thou thy seruaunt departe in peace, accordinge to thy promes.
Luke 2:30 For mine eyes haue sene the sauiour sent from the.
Luke 2:31 Which thou hast prepare before the face of all people.
Luke 2:32 A lyght to lighten the gentils and the glorye of thy people Israel.
Luke 2:33 And his father and mother meruayled at those thinges which were spoken of him.
Luke 2:34 And Symon blessed them, & sayd vnto Mary his mother: beholde, this chylde shalbe the fal and resurrection of manye in Israel, & sygne which shalbe spoken againste.
Luke 2:35 And moreouer the swearde shall pearce thy soule, that the thoughtes of manye hertes maye be opened.
Luke 2:36 And ther was a prophetesse, one Anna the doughter of Phanuell of the trybe of Aser which was of a great age, and had liued with her housbande .vij. yeares from her virginitie.
Luke 2:37 And she had bene a weddowe aboute .iiij. score and .iiij. yeares, which went neuer out of the temple, but serued God with fastinge and prayer night & daye.
Luke 2:38 And the same came forth that same houre and praysed the Lorde and spake of him to all that loked for redempcion in Ierusalem.
Luke 2:39 And assone as they had perfourmed al thynges accordynge to the lawe of the Lorde they retourned into Galyle to their owne cytye Nazareth.
Luke 2:40 And the chylde grewe & waxed stronge in spyryte, and was fylled wyth wisdome, & the grace of God was with him.
Luke 2:41 And his father and mother went to Hierusalem euerye yeare at the feaste of easter.
Luke 2:42 And when he was .xij. yeare olde, they went vp to Ierusalem after the custome of the feaste.
Luke 2:43 And when they had fulfilled the dayes, as they returned home, the chylde Iesus bode styll in Ierusalem vnknowinge to his father and mother.
Luke 2:44 For they supposed he had bene in the company, and therfore came a dayes iorneye and sought him amonge their kinsfolke and acquaintaunce.
Luke 2:45 And when thei founde him not, they went backe againe to Ierusalem, & sought hym.
Luke 2:46 And it fortuned after thre dayes that they founde him in the tempell, syttynge in the middes of the doctours, both hearynge them and posynge them.
Luke 2:47 And all that hearde him, meruaylled at his wit and aunswers.
Luke 2:48 And when they sawe him, they were astonyed. And his mother sayde vnto him: sonne, why hast thou thus dealt with vs? Beholde thy father and I haue sought the, sorowing.
Luke 2:49 And he sayed vnto them: howe is it that ye sought me? Wyst ye not that I must go about my fathers busynes?
Luke 2:50 And they vnderstode not the sayinge that he spake to them.
Luke 2:51 And he went with them, and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them: But his mother kepte al these sayinges in her herte.
Luke 2:52 And Iesus increased in wisdome and age, and in fauoure with God and man.

CHAPTER: 3

Luke 3:1 And in the .xv. yeare of the raygne of Tiberius the Emperoure, Pontius Pilate beiynge lieftenaunte of Iury, and Herode beyinge Tethrarch of Galyle, and hys brother Philippe Tethrarchin Iturea & in the region of Traconytes, and Lysanyas the Tetrarche of Abilene,
Luke 3:2 when Anna and Cayphas were the hye pryestes: the word of God came vuto Iohn the sonne of Zacharias in the wildernes.
Luke 3:3 And he came into all the costes about Iordan, preaching the baptisme of repentaunce for the remissyon of synnes,
Luke 3:4 as it is written in the boke of the sayinges of Esaias the prophete which sayeth. The voyce of a cryer in wildernes, prepare the waye of the Lorde, make hys pathes strayght.
Luke 3:5 Euerye valley shall be fylled, and euerye mountayne and hyll shall be brought lowe. And croked thinges shalbe made straight: and the rough wayes shalbe made smoth:
Luke 3:6 and all fleshe shall se the sauioure sent of God.
Luke 3:7 Then sayde he to the people that were come to be baptysed of him. O generacion of vipers, who hath taught you to flye from the wrath to come?
Luke 3:8 Bringe forth due frutes of repentaunce, and begin not to saye in your selues, we haue Abraham to our father: For I say vnto you God is able of these stones to rayse vp chyldren vnto Abraham.
Luke 3:9 Now also is the axe lyed vnto the rote of the trees, so that euery tree which bringeth not forth good frute shall be hewen doune, and cast into the fyre.
Luke 3:10 And the people axed him sayinge: What shall we do then?
Luke 3:11 He aunswered and sayd vnto theim: He that hath two cotes, let him parte with him that hath none, & he that hath meate let him do lykewyse.
Luke 3:12 Then came there publicans to be baptysed, and sayde vnto hym: Maister, what shall we do?
Luke 3:13 And he sayde vnto them: require nomore then that which is appointed vnto you.
Luke 3:14 The souldioures lykewyse demaunded of him saiynge: and what shall we do? And he sayde to them: Do violence to no man: neither trouble any man wrongfullye: but be content with your wages.
Luke 3:15 As the people were in a doubte, and all men disputed in their hertes of Iohn, whither he were very Christ,
Luke 3:16 Iohn aunswered and sayde to them all: I baptyse you with water, but a stronger then I cometh after me, whose shoe latchet I am not worthy to vnlouse: he wyll baptyse you with the holye ghost, and with fyre.
Luke 3:17 Which hath his fanne in his hande, and wyll purge his floore, and wyll gather the corne into his barne, but the chaffe wil he burne with fyre that neuer shalbe quenched.
Luke 3:18 And many other thinges in his exhortacion preached he vnto the people.
Luke 3:19 Then Herode the Tetrarche (when he was rebuked of him for Herodias his brothers wyfe and for al the euyls, which Herode had done)
Luke 3:20 added this aboue al, and laied Ihon in prison.
Luke 3:21 And it fortuned as all the people receyued baptisme (And when Iesus was baptised and did praye) that heauen was opened,
Luke 3:22 and the holye ghost came doune in a bodelye shape lyke a done vpon him, and a voyce came from heauen saiynge: thou art my deare sonne, in the do I delyte.
Luke 3:23 And Iesus him selfe was entring the thirthy yeare of his age as men supposed hym to be the sonne of Ioseph. which was the sonne of Hely,
Luke 3:24 which was the sonne of Mathat, which was the sonne of Leui, which was the sonne of Melchi. which was the sonne of Ianna, which was the sonne of Ioseph,
Luke 3:25 which was the sonne of Mattathias, which was the sonne of Amos, which was the sonne of Nasum, which was the sonne of Esli, which was the sonne of Nagge,
Luke 3:26 which was the sonne of Maath, which was the sonne of Matathias, which was the sonne of Semei, which was the sonne of Iosech, which was the sonne of Iuda,
Luke 3:27 which was the sonne of Ioanna, which was the sonne of Rhesia, which was the sonne of Zorobabel, which was the sonne of Salathiel, which was the sonne of Neri,
Luke 3:28 which was the sonne of Melchi, which was the sonne of Addi, which was the sonne of Cosan, which was the sonne of Helmadam, which was the sonne of Hir,
Luke 3:29 which was the sonne of Ieso, which was the sonne of Heliasar, which was the sonne of Ioram, which was the sonne of Mattha, which was the sonne of Leuy,
Luke 3:30 which was the sonne of Simeon, which was the sonne of Iuda, which was the sonne of Ioseph, which was the sonne of Ionam, which was the sonne of Heliachim,
Luke 3:31 which was the sonne of Melca, which was the sonne of Menam, which was the sonne of Mathathan, which was the sonne of Nathan, which was the sonne of Dauid,
Luke 3:32 which was the sonne of Iesse, which was the sonne of Obed, which was the sonne of Boos, which was the sonne of Salmon, which was the sonne of Naason,
Luke 3:33 which was the sonne of Aminadab, which was the sonne of Aram, which was the sonne of Esrom, which was the sonne of Phares, which was the sonne of Iuda,
Luke 3:34 which was the sonne of Iacob, which was the sonne of Isaac, which was the sonne of Abraham, which was the sonne of Tharra, which was the sonne of Nachor,
Luke 3:35 which was the sonne of Saruch, which was the sonne of Ragan, which was the sonne of Phalec, which was the sonne of Heber, which was the sonne of Sala,
Luke 3:36 which was the sonne of Cainan, which was the sonne of Arphaxat, which was the sonne of Sem, which was the sonne of Noe, which was the sonne of Lameth,
Luke 3:37 which was the sonne of Mathusalem, which was the sonne of Enoch, which was the sonne of Iareth, which was the sonne of Malalehel, which was the sonne of Cainan,
Luke 3:38 which was the sonne of Enos, which was the sonne of Seth, which was the sonne of Adam, which was the sonne of God,

CHAPTER: 4

Luke 4:1 Iesus then full of the holye ghost returned from Iordan & was caried of the spyrite into wildernes,
Luke 4:2 and was .xl. dayes tempted of the deuil. And in those dayes eate he nothinge. And when they were ended he afterwarde hungred.
Luke 4:3 And the deuyll sayde vnto him: If thou be the sonne of God, commaunde this stone that it be bread.
Luke 4:4 And Iesus aunswered hym saiynge: It is written, man shall not lyue by bread onlye, but of euerye worde of God.
Luke 4:5 And the deuyl toke him vp into an hye mountayne, and shewed him all the kyngdomes of the worlde euen in the twincklinge of an eye.
Luke 4:6 And the deuyl sayde vnto hym: al this power wyll I geue the euerye whit and the glorye of them for that is delyuered to me & to whomsoeuer I wyl, I geue it:
Luke 4:7 If thou therfore wilt worship me, they shalbe al thine.
Luke 4:8 Iesus aunswered him and sayde. Hence from me Sathan. For it is written: Thou shall honoure the Lord thy God and him onlye serue.
Luke 4:9 And he caryed hym to Ierusalem, and set him on a pynacle of the tempel, and sayde vnto him. If thou be the sonne of God caste thy selfe doune from hence:
Luke 4:10 For it is wrytten. He shall geue his aungels charge ouer the to kepe the
Luke 4:11 and wyth their handes they shal sley the vp that thou dashe not thy fote agaynst a stone.
Luke 4:12 Iesus aunswered and sayde to hym, it is sayde: Thou shalt not tempt the Lorde thy God.
Luke 4:13 Assone as the deuyll had ended all his temptacion, he departed from him for a season.
Luke 4:14 And Iesus retourned by the power of the spyryte into Galile, and there went a fame of hym throughout all the regyon rounde about.
Luke 4:15 And he taught in their synagoges, and was commended of all men.
Luke 4:16 And he came to Nazareth wher he was nourished: and as his custome was, went into the synagoge on the. Sabboth dayes, & stode vp to reade.
Luke 4:17 And there was delyuered vnto hym the boke of the prophete Esayas. And when he had opened the boke, he founde the place wher it was written:
Luke 4:18 The spyryte of the Lorde vpon me, because he hath anointed me: to preache the gospell to the poore he hath sent me, and to heale the broken herted, to preache deliueraunce to the captiue, and syght to the blynde, and frely to set at lyberte them that are brused,
Luke 4:19 and to preache the acceptable yeare of the Lorde.
Luke 4:20 And he closed the boke, and gaue it againe to the mynister, and sate doune. And the eyes of all that were in the synagoge were fastened on him.
Luke 4:21 And he began to saye vnto them. This daye is this scripture fulfylled in youre eares.
Luke 4:22 And all bare him witnes, and wondred at the gracious wordes which proceded out of his mouthe, and saide: Is not this Iosephs sonne?
Luke 4:23 And he sayde vnto them: Ye maye very wel saye vnto me these prouerbe: Phisicon, heale thy selfe. Whatsoeuer we haue hearde done in Capernaum, do the same here lykewyse in thine owne countrye.
Luke 4:24 And he sayed: verely I saye vnto you. No prophete is accepted in his owne countrye.
Luke 4:25 But I tell you of a truthe, manye wydowes were in Israel in the dayes of Helias, when heauen was shut thre yeares & syxe moneths when great fanishment was through out all the lande,
Luke 4:26 and vnto none of them was Helias sent, saue vnto Sarepta besydes Sydon vnto a woman that was a wydowe.
Luke 4:27 And manye lepers were in Israel in the tyme of Helyseus the prophet, and yet none of them was healed, sauinge Naman of Siria.
Luke 4:28 And as many as were in the synagoge when they hearde that, were fylled with wrath:
Luke 4:29 and rose vp, and thrust him out of the citye, & ledde him euen vnto the edge of the hyll, where on their cytye was bult, to cast hym doune hedlynge.
Luke 4:30 But he wente his way euen through the myddes of them.
Luke 4:31 And came into Capernaum a cytye of Galyle, and there taught them on the saboth dayes.
Luke 4:32 And they were astonyed at his doctryne, for his preachinge was wyth power.
Luke 4:33 And in the synagoge ther was a man which had a spyryte of an vncleane deuyll, and cried with a loude voyce
Luke 4:34 saiyng: let me alone, what hast thou to do with vs, thou Iesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroye? I knowe the what thou arte, euen the holye of God.
Luke 4:35 And Iesus rebuked him saiynge: holde thy peace & come out of hym. And the deuyll throwe hym in the myddes of them and came out of hym and hurte hym not.
Luke 4:36 And feare come on them all and they spake amonge them selues saiynge what maner of thinge is this? For with authoryte and power he commaundeth the foule spirites, and they come out.
Luke 4:37 And the fame of him spread abroade through out all places of the country rounde aboute.
Luke 4:38 And he arose vp & came out of the synagoge, and entred into Simons house. And Simons mother in lawe was taken with a great feuer and they made intercessyon to hym for her.
Luke 4:39 And he stode ouer her, and rebuked the feuer, and it left her. And immediatly she arose and mynystred vnto them.
Luke 4:40 When the sunne was doune, all they that had sicke, taken with diuerse dyseases, brought them vnto hym, and he layde hys handes on euery one of them, and healed them.
Luke 4:41 And deuyls also came oute of many of them cryinge and saiyng: thou arte Christ the sonne of God. And he rebuked them, and suffered them not to speake: for they knewe that he was Christe.
Luke 4:42 Assone as it was daye, he departed & went awaye into a desert place, & the people sought hym and came to hym, and kept hym that he shoulde not departe from them.
Luke 4:43 And he sayed vnto them: I muste to other cityes also preache the kyngdome of God: For therfore am I sent.
Luke 4:44 And he preached in the synagoges of Galyle,

CHAPTER: 5

Luke 5:1 It came to passe as the people preased vpon him to heare the worde of God, that he stode by the lake of Genezareth:
Luke 5:2 and sawe two shyppes stande by the lake syde, but the fisher men were gone out of them, and were washynge their nettes.
Luke 5:3 And he entred into one of the shyppes, which pertayned to Symon, and prayed him, that he woulde thruste out a lytle from the lande. And he sat doune and taught the people out of the shyppe.
Luke 5:4 When he had left speakynge, he sayed vnto Simon: launce out into the depe, and let slip your nettes to make a draught.
Luke 5:5 And Simon aunswered and sayed vnto hym: Mayster, we haue laboured all nyght, and haue taken nothynge. Neuerthelater at thy worde I wyll lose forth the net.
Luke 5:6 And when they had so done, they enclosed a greate multytude of fyshes. And their net brake:
Luke 5:7 but they made sygnes to their fellowes which were in the other shyp that they shoulde come and helpe them. And they came and fylled both the shyppes that they sonke againe.
Luke 5:8 When Simon Peter sawe that, he fell doune at Iesus knees saiynge: Lorde go
Luke 5:9 from me for I am a synfull man. For he was vtterlye astonyed and all that were with hym at the draughte of fyshe, which they toke:
Luke 5:10 and so was Iames and Iohn the sonnes of Zebede, which were parteners with Symon. And Iesus sayed vnto Simon: feare not, from hence forth thou shalt catche men.
Luke 5:11 And they brought the shyppes to lande, and forsoke all and folowed hym.
Luke 5:12 And it fortuned as he was in a certayne citye: beholde, there was a man full of leprosye: and when he had spyed Iesus, he fell on his face, and besought him saiynge: Lorde, if thou wylt thou canst make me cleane.
Luke 5:13 And he stretthed forth the hande and touched him saiynge: I wyl, be thou cleane. And immediatlye the leprosye departed from him.
Luke 5:14 And he warned hym that he shoulde tell no man but that he should go and shewe him selfe to the pryeste and offer for his clensyng, accordinge as Moyses commaundement was, for a witnes vnto them.
Luke 5:15 But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him, & much people came together to heare and to be healed of him, of their infirmyties.
Luke 5:16 And he kepte him selfe aparte in the wyldernesse, and gaue him selfe to prayer.
Luke 5:17 And it happened on a certayne daye, that he taught, and there sate the phariseis and the doctours of lawe, which were come out of all the tounes of Galyle, Iurye, and Hierusalem. And the power of the Lorde was to heale them.
Luke 5:18 And beholde men brought a man liynge in his bedde which was taken with a palsey: & sought meanes to brynge him in, and to laye him before him.
Luke 5:19 And when they could not finde by what way they might bring him in, because of the prease, they went vp on the toppe of the house, and let him doune thorowe the tyling, bedde & all in the middest before Iesus.
Luke 5:20 When he sawe their faith, he sayed to him: man, thy sinnes are forgeuen the.
Luke 5:21 And the scribes and pharyseis began to thinke saiynge: What felowe is this which speaketh blasphemy? who can forgeue synnes but God onlye?
Luke 5:22 When Iesus perceiued their thoughtes, he aunswered and sayd vnto them: What thinke ye in your hertes?
Luke 5:23 Whether is it easyer to say, thy synnes are forgeuen the, or to saye: ryse & walke?
Luke 5:24 But that ye may knowe that the sonne of man hath power to forgeue sinnes on earth, he said to the sycke of the paulsye, I say to the, aryse, take vp thy bed & go home to thy house.
Luke 5:25 And immediatlye he rose vp before them, and toke vp his bed wheron he laye, and departed to his owne house praysyng God.
Luke 5:26 And they were all amased, and they lauded God & were filled with fear saiyng: We haue sene straung thinges to daye.
Luke 5:27 And after that he wente forth and sawe a Publican named Leui, sittinge at the receite of custome and saide vnto him: folowe me.
Luke 5:28 And he left al, rose vp and folowed him.
Luke 5:29 And the same Leui made him a great feaste at home in his owne house. And ther was a great companye of publicans and of other that sate at meat with him.
Luke 5:30 And the scribes and pharyseis murmured againste his disciples saiynge: Why eate ye, and drinke ye with publicans and sinners?
Luke 5:31 Iesus aunswered and sayde vnto them: They that are whole nede not of the phisician: but thei that are sicke.
Luke 5:32 I am not come to cal the rightuous, but synners to repentaunce.
Luke 5:33 Then they sayed vnto him: Why do the disciples of Ihon faste often and praye, and the disciples of the phariseis also: and thyne eate and drinke?
Luke 5:34 And he sayed vnto them: Can ye make the children of the weddinge faste, as longe as the bridgrome is present with them?
Luke 5:35 The dayes will come, when the bridgrome shall be taken awaye from them: Then shall they faste in those dayes.
Luke 5:36 Then spake he vnto them in a symylytude. No man putteth a pece of a newe garmente, into an olde vesture: for if he do, then breaketh he the newe and the pece that was taken out of the newe agreeth not with the olde.
Luke 5:37 Also no man poureth newe wine into olde vessels. For if he do, the newe wyne breaketh the vessels, and runneth out it selfe, and the vessels perishe:
Luke 5:38 But newe wyne muste be poured into newe vessels, and both are preserued.
Luke 5:39 Also no man that drinketh olde wyne, strayght waye can awaye with newe, for he sayeth the olde is pleasaunter.

CHAPTER: 6

Luke 6:1 It happened on an after saboth, that he wente through the corne fyelde, and that his disciples plucked the eares of corne and eate, and rubbed them in their handes.
Luke 6:2 And certayne of the pharyseis sayde vnto them: Why do ye that whiche is not lawfull to do on the saboth dayes?
Luke 6:3 And Iesus aunswered them and sayde: Haue ye not read what Dauid did when he him selfe was an hongred, and they which were with hym:
Luke 6:4 how he wente into the house of God and toke and eate the loues of halowed breade, & gaue also to them which were with him, which was not lawfull to eate, but for the priestes onlye.
Luke 6:5 And he sayed vnto them: The sonne of man is Lorde of the saboth daye.
Luke 6:6 And it fortuned in another saboth also, that he entred into the synagoge and taught. And there was a man whose righthande was dried vp.
Luke 6:7 And the scrybes and pharyseis watched him, to see whether he would heale on the saboth daye, that they myght fynde an accusacion against him.
Luke 6:8 But he knewe their thoughtes, and sayde to the man which had the withered hande: Rise vp and stande forth in the middes. And he arose and stepped forth.
Luke 6:9 Then sayde Iesus vnto them: I wyll axe you a question: Whither is it lawfull on the saboth dayes to do good or to do euyl? to saue lyfe, or for to destroye it?
Luke 6:10 And he behelde them al in compasse, and sayde vnto the manye: Stretche forth thy hande. And he dyd so: & his hande was restored, and made as whole as the other.
Luke 6:11 And thei were fylled full of madnes, and communed one with another, what they might do to Iesus.
Luke 6:12 And it furtuned in those dayes that he went out into a mountaine for to praye, and contynued all night in prayer to God.
Luke 6:13 And assone as it was daye, he called his disciples, and of them he chose .xij. whiche also he called Apostles:
Luke 6:14 Symon whom he named Peter, & Andrewe his brother, Iames and Ihon, Philippe and Bartelmewe,
Luke 6:15 Mathewe and Thomas, Iames the sonne of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelotes,
Luke 6:16 and Iudas Iames sonne, and Iudas Iscarioth which same was the traytour.
Luke 6:17 And he came doune with them & stode in the playne fyelde with the companye of hys discyples, and a great multytude of people out of all partyes of Iurye and Ierusalem & from the sea coste of Tyre and Sydon, which came to heare hym, and to be healed of their disceases,
Luke 6:18 and they also that were vexed with foule spyrytes, and they were healed.
Luke 6:19 And all the people preased to touche hym, for there wente vertue out of hym, and healed them all.
Luke 6:20 And he lyfte vp his eye vpon the disciples, and sayde: Blessed be ye pore: for yours is the kyngdome of God.
Luke 6:21 Blessed are ye that honger nowe: for ye shalbe satisfyed. Blessed are ye that wepe nowe for ye shall laughe.
Luke 6:22 Blessed are ye when men hate you, and thruste you out of their companye, and rayle, & abhorre youre name as an euill thinge, for the sonne of mans sake.
Luke 6:23 Reioyse then, and be glad: for behold your reward is great in heauen. After this maner their father entreated the prophetes.
Luke 6:24 But wo be to you that are riche: for ye haue therin your consolacion.
Luke 6:25 Wo be to you that are full: for ye shal honger. Wo be to you that nowe laugh: for ye shall wayle and wepe.
Luke 6:26 Wo be to you when all men prayse you: for so dyd their fathers to the false prophetes.
Luke 6:27 But I say vnto you which heare: loue your enemyes. Do good to them which hate you.
Luke 6:28 Blesse them that coursse you. And praye for them which wrongfully trouble you.
Luke 6:29 And vnto hym that smiteth the on the one cheke, offer also the other. And him that taketh awaye thy gonne, forbyd not to take thy cote also.
Luke 6:30 Giue euerye man that axeth of the. And of hym that taketh awaye thy goodes, axe them not again.
Luke 6:31 And as ye woulde that men should do to you: so do ye to them likewyse.
Luke 6:32 Yf ye loue them which loue you, what thanke are ye worthy of? For the verye synners loue their louers.
Luke 6:33 And if ye do for them which do for you, what thanke are ye worthye of? For the verye synners do euen the same.
Luke 6:34 If ye lende to them of whom ye hope to receiue, what thanke shall ye haue: for the very synners lende to synners to receiue much againe.
Luke 6:35 Wherfore, loue ye your enemyes, do good and lende, lokinge for nothynge againe, and your rewarde shall be greate, and ye shalbe the children of the hyest for he is kinde vnto the vnkinde and to the euyll.
Luke 6:36 Be ye therfore mercifull, as your father is mercyfull.
Luke 6:37 Iudge not and ye shall not be iudged. Condemne not, and ye shall not be condemned. Forgeue you, ye shalbe forgeuen.
Luke 6:38 Geue, and it shalbe geuen vnto you: good measure, pressed doune, shaken together and runninge ouer, shal men geue vnto your bosomes. For with what measure ye mete with the same shall men mete to you agayne.
Luke 6:39 And he putteth forth a symylytude vnto them: Can the blinde leade the blinde? Do they not both then fall into the dyche?
Luke 6:40 The discyple is not aboue his maister. Euery man shalbe perfecte if he be as his mayster is.
Luke 6:41 Why seist thou a moote in thy brothers eye, and consyderest not the beame that is in thyne owne eye?
Luke 6:42 Either howe canst thou saye to thy brother? Brother, let me pul out the moote that is thine eye: When thou perceyuest not the beame that is in thine owne eye? Ypocryte, cast out the beame that is in thine owne eye fyrst, and then shalt thou se perfectlye to pul out the mote out of thy brothers eye.
Luke 6:43 It is not a good tre that bryngeth forth euyll frute: neither is that au euil tre that bringeth forth good frute.
Luke 6:44 For euery tre is knowen by his fruite. Neyther of thornes gather men fygges, nor of bushes gather they grapes.
Luke 6:45 A good man out of the good treasure of his hert bringeth forth that which is good. And an euil man out of the euyll treasure of his herte bringeth forth that which is euyl. For of the aboundaunce of the herte, his mouth speaketh.
Luke 6:46 Why call ye me Maister Maister, and do not as I byd you?
Luke 6:47 whosoeuer commeth to me, and heareth my saiynges, and doth the same, I wyll shewe you to whom he is lyke.
Luke 6:48 He is lyke a man which builde an house and digged depe and layde the foundacion on a rocke. When the waters arose, the floud bet vpon that house, and coulde not moue it for it was grounded vpon a rocke.
Luke 6:49 But he that heareth and doeth not, is lyke a man that without foundacion bylt an house vpon the earth, against which the floude dyd beate and it fell by and by, and the fall of that house was greate.

CHAPTER: 7

Luke 7:1 When he had ended al his saynges in the audience of the people, he entred into Capernaum.
Luke 7:2 And a certayne Centuryons seruaunt was sycke and redye to dye, whom he made much of.
Luke 7:3 And when he heard of Iesu, he sent vnto hym the elders of the Iewes, besechinge hym that he woulde come & heale his seruaunte.
Luke 7:4 And they came to Iesus and besought hym instauntlye saiynge: He is worthye that thou shouldest do this for hym.
Luke 7:5 For he loueth oure nacion, and hath bylt vs a synagoge.
Luke 7:6 And Iesus went with them. And when he was not farre from the house the Centurion sent frendes to him saiynge vnto him: Lorde trouble not thy selfe, for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter vnder my roffe.
Luke 7:7 Wherfore I thought not my selfe worthy to come vnto the: but saye the worde and my seruaunte shalbe whole.
Luke 7:8 For I lykewise am a man vnder power, and haue vnder me souldiers, and I saye vnto one, go: and he goeth. And to an other, come: and he cometh. And to my seruaunte, do this: and he doeth it.
Luke 7:9 When Iesus harde this, he maruailed at him, & tourned him about & saide to the people that folowed hym: I say vnto you, I haue not founde so greate fayth, no, not in Israel.
Luke 7:10 And they that were sent, turned backe home againe, and founde the seruaunte that was sycke, whole.
Luke 7:11 And it fortnned after that, that he wente into a cytye called Naim, and manye of hys disciples went with him and much people.
Luke 7:12 When he came nye to the gate of the cytye, beholde there was a dead man caryed out which was the onlye sonne of his mother and she was a wydowe, and much people of the cytye was with her.
Luke 7:13 And when the Lorde sawe her, he had compassyon on her and saide vnto her, wepe not.
Luke 7:14 And he went and touched the coffin, and they that bare hym, stode styll. And he sayde: Yonge man, I say vnto the, aryse.
Luke 7:15 And the dead sate vp, and began to speake. And he delyuered him to his mother.
Luke 7:16 And there came a feare on them all. And they glorifyed God saiynge: a greate Prophete is rysen among vs, and God hath visyted his people.
Luke 7:17 And this rumore of hym wente forth throughout all Iurye, and thoroweout all the regions which lye rounde about.
Luke 7:18 And the discyples of Ihon shewed hym of all these thinges.
Luke 7:19 And Ihon called vnto him two of his discyples, and sente them to Iesus saiynge: Arte thou he that shall come? or shall we loke for another?
Luke 7:20 When the men were come vnto him they sayde: Ihon Baptiste sent vs vnto the saiynge. Art thou he that shall come, or shall we wayte for an other?
Luke 7:21 And at that same tyme he cured manye of their infyrmytyes and plages and of euyll spirites, and vnto manye that were blinde he gaue syght.
Luke 7:22 And Iesus aunswered and saide vnto them: Go your wayes and shewe Ihon what thinges ye haue seane and hearde: howe that the blynd se, the halt go, the lepers are clensed, the deafe heare, the dead aryse, to the poore is glad tydinges preached,
Luke 7:23 and happye is he that is not offended by me.
Luke 7:24 When the messengers of Ihon were departed, he began to speake vnto the people of Ihon. What went ye out into the wildernes for to se? Went ye to se a rede shaken with the winde?
Luke 7:25 But what went ye out for to se? a man clothed in softe raiment? Beholde they which are gorgeouslye apparilled, and lyue delicatly are in kinges courtes.
Luke 7:26 But what went ye forth to se? a Prophete, yea I saye vnto you, and more then a prophete.
Luke 7:27 This is he of whom it is written: Behold I sende my messenger before thy face, to prepare thy waye before the
Luke 7:28 For I saye vnto you: a greater Prophete then Ihon, amonge womens children is ther none. Neuerthelesse one that is lesse in the kingdome of God, is greater then he.
Luke 7:29 And all the people that hearde and the publicans iustifyed God, and were baptysed with the baptime of Ihon.
Luke 7:30 But the Phariseis and scribes despised the counsel of God againste them selues, and were not baptysed of him.
Luke 7:31 And the Lorde sayed: Wherunto shall I lyken the men of this generacion, and what thinge are they?
Luke 7:32 They are lyke vnto chyldrin syttyng in the marcked place, & cryenge one to an other, and saiynge: We haue pyped vnto you and ye haue not daunsed: we mourned to you, & ye haue not wept.
Luke 7:33 For Ihon Baptyste came, neyther eatinge breade nor drincking wyne, and ye saye: he hath the deuyll.
Luke 7:34 The sonne of man is come and eateth and drincked, and ye saye: beholde a man which is a glotten, and a drincker of wine, a frende of publicans and synners.
Luke 7:35 Yet is wysdome iustyfyed of all her chyldren.
Luke 7:36 And one of the pharyseis desyred hym that he wolde eate with him. And he wente into the pharyseis house and sate doune to meate.
Luke 7:37 And beholde a woman in that citye which was a synner, assone as she knewe that Iesus sate at mete in the phariseis house, she brought an alabaster boxe of ointment,
Luke 7:38 and she stode at his fete behinde him wepinge, and began to washe his fete with teares, and dyd wype them wyth the heares of her head, and kyshed his fete, and annoynted them with oyntment.
Luke 7:39 When the pharysey which bade him, sawe that he speake within him selfe saiyng. If this man were a Prophete, he woulde surely haue knowen who and what maner woman this is which toucheth him, for she is a synner.
Luke 7:40 And Iesus aunswered and sayde vnto him: Simon I haue some what to saye vnto the. And he sayed: Maister saye on.
Luke 7:41 There was a certayne lender, which had two detters, the one ought fyue hundred pence: and the other fyfty.
Luke 7:42 When they had nothinge to paye, he forgaue them both. Which of them tell me, wyll loue him most.
Luke 7:43 Simon aunswered and saide: I suppose, that he to whom he forgaue moste. And he sayde vnto hym: Thou haste truly iudged.
Luke 7:44 And he turned to the woman, and sayde vnto Symon: Seist thou this woman? I entred into thy house, and thou gauest me no water to my fete, but she hath washed my fete with teares and wyped them wyth the heyres of her head.
Luke 7:45 Thou gauest me no kisse: but she, sence the tyme I came in, hath not ceased to kisse my fete.
Luke 7:46 Myne head with oyle thou dyddest not anoynte, but she hath annointed my fete with oyntmente.
Luke 7:47 Wherfore I saye vnto the manye synnes are forgeuen her, for she loued much. To whom lesse is forgeuen, the same doth lesse loue.
Luke 7:48 And he sayde vnto her, thy synnes are forgeuen the.
Luke 7:49 And they that sate at meate with him, began to saye with in them selues: Who is this which forgeueth synnes also?
Luke 7:50 And he sayde to the woman. Thy fayth hath saued the. Go in peace.

CHAPTER: 8

Luke 8:1 And it fortuned after that, that he him selfe went thorowe out cyties and tounes preachinge and shewinge the kingdome of God, and the .xij. with hym.
Luke 8:2 And also certaine women, which were healed of euyll spretes and infyrmytyes: Marye called Magdalene, out of whom went seuen deuyls,
Luke 8:3 and Ioanna the wyfe of Chusa Herodes stewarde, and Susanna, and manye other: which ministred to them of their substaunce.
Luke 8:4 When much people were gathered together, and were come to hym out of all cytyes, he spake by a symilitude.
Luke 8:5 A sower went out to sowe his sede: and as he sowed, some fel by the waye syde: and it was troden vnder fete, and the foules of the ayre deuoured it vp.
Luke 8:6 And some fell on the stone, and assone as it was spronge vp, it withered awaye because it lacked moistnes.
Luke 8:7 And some fell amonge thornes, and the thornes spronge vp with it, and choked it.
Luke 8:8 And some fell on good grounde and spronge vp and bare fruite an hundred folde. And as he sayed these thinges he cryed: He that hath eares to heare, let hym heare.
Luke 8:9 And his discyples axed him saiynge: what maner of symylytude is this?
Luke 8:10 And he sayed vnto you is it geuen to knowe the secretes of the kingdome of God: but to other in symylytudes, that when they se, they shoulde not vnderstande.
Luke 8:11 The symylytude is this. The sede is the worde of God.
Luke 8:12 Those that are besyde the waye, are they that heare, and afterwarde commeth the deuyll and taketh awaye the worde out of their hertes leste they should beleue & be saued.
Luke 8:13 Thei on the stones, are thei which when they heare, receiue the worde with ioye. But these haue no rotes, whiche for a whyle beleue, & in tyme of temptacion go awaye.
Luke 8:14 And that whiche fell amonge thornes, are thei which heare, and go forth, and are choked with cares and with ryches, and voluptuouse liuinge, and bringe forth no fruite.
Luke 8:15 That in the good grounde, are they whyche with a good and pure herte, heare the worde and kepe it, and brynge forth fruyte wyth pacience.
Luke 8:16 No man lighteth a candell, and couereth it vnder a vessell, neither putteth it vnder a table, but setteth it on a candelstike, that thei that enter in, maye se the lyghte.
Luke 8:17 Nothinge in secrete, that shall not come abrode: Neyther any thynge hyd that shall not be knowen, and come to light.
Luke 8:18 Take hede therfore how ye heare. For who soeuer hath, to hym shall be geuen: And whosoeuer hath not, from hym shal be taken, euen that same which he supposeth that he hath.
Luke 8:19 Then came to hym his mother and his brethren and coulde not come at hym for preace.
Luke 8:20 And they tolde him sayinge: Thy mother and thy brethren stande without, and woulde se the.
Luke 8:21 He aunswered and sayde vnto them: my mother and my brethren are these which heare the worde of God and do it.
Luke 8:22 And it chaunsed on a certaine daye that he went into a shippe, and his disciples also, and he sayed vnto them: Let vs go ouer to the other syde of the lake. And they lanched forth.
Luke 8:23 And as they sayled he fell on slepe, and there arose a storme of winde in the lake, and they were fylled with water, and were in ieopardy.
Luke 8:24 And they went to him and awoke him saiyng: Maister Maister we are loste. Then he rose & rebuked the winde & the tempeste of the water, & they ceased, & it wexed calme.
Luke 8:25 And he sayed vnto them: Wher is your faythe? They feared and woundered saiynge one to another, what felowe is this: for he commaundeth both the windes & water, & they obey him?
Luke 8:26 And they sayled vnto the region of the Gaderenites, which is ouer against Galile.
Luke 8:27 And as he went out to lande, there mete him a certaine man out of the citie, which had a deuil long time, & ware no clothes, neither abode in anye house: but amonge graues.
Luke 8:28 When he sawe Iesus he cried and fel doune before him, and with a loud voice saied: What haue I to do with the Iesus the sonne of the God moste hiest? I besech the tormente me not.
Luke 8:29 Then he commaunded the foule sprete to come out of the man. For oft times he caughte him, and he was bounde with chaines, and kept with fetters, and he brake the bondes, and was caried of and the fende, into wildernes.
Luke 8:30 And Iesus axed him saiynge: what is thy name? And he saied Legion, because many deuils were entred into him.
Luke 8:31 And they besought him, that he woulde not commaunde them to go out into the depe.
Luke 8:32 And there was therby an hearde of manie swine, feadinge on an hyl: and they besought him, that he woulde suffer them to enter into them. And he suffred.
Luke 8:33 Then wente the deuyls out of the man, and entred into the swine: and the hearde toke their course, and ranne headlinge into the lake, and were choked.
Luke 8:34 When the heardmen sawe what had chaunsed, they fled and tolde it in the cytye, and in the villages.
Luke 8:35 And they came out to se what was done: and came to Iesus, and founde the man out of whom the deuyls were departed syttynge at the fete of Iesus, clothed and in his ryghte mynde, and they were afrayed.
Luke 8:36 They also which sawe it tolde them by what meanes he that was possessed of the deuyll, was healed.
Luke 8:37 And all the whole multitude of the Gaderenites, besought hym that he woulde departe from them: for they were taken with greate feare. And he gate him into the shyppe, and retourned backe againe.
Luke 8:38 Then the man out of whom the deuils were departed, besought him that he myght be with him. But Iesus sent hym awaye saiynge.
Luke 8:39 Go home againe into thine owne house, and shewe what greate thinges God hath done to the. And he wente his waye, and preached thorow out all the cytye what great thinges Iesus hath done vnto him.
Luke 8:40 And it fortuned when Iesus was come againe that the people receiued him. For they all wayted for hym.
Luke 8:41 And beholde there came a man named Iairus (and he was a ruler of the synagoge) and he fell doune at Iesus fete, and besought hym that he woulde come into his house,
Luke 8:42 for he had but a doughter only vpon a twelwe yere of age, and she lay a diynge. As he wente the people thronged hym.
Luke 8:43 And a woman hauinge an yssue of bloude twelue yeares (whiche hath spent all her substaunce amonge phisycions, neyther coulde be holpen of anye)
Luke 8:44 came behinde him, and touched the heme of his garment and immediatlye her yssue of bloude staunched.
Luke 8:45 And Iesus sayde: Who is it that touched me? When euerye man denyed, Peter and they that were with him, saide: Mayster, the people thruste the and vexe the, and sayest thou who touched me?
Luke 8:46 And Iesus saide: Some bodye touched me. For I perceyue that vertue is gone out of me.
Luke 8:47 When the woman sawe that she was not hyd, she came trimblynge, and fell at his fete, and tolde hym before all the people for what cause she had touched him, and howe she was healed immediatlye.
Luke 8:48 And he sayde vnto her: Doughter be of good comfort. Thy faith hath made the whole, go in peace.
Luke 8:49 Whyle he yet spake, there came on from the rulers of the synagoges house, which said to hym thy doughter is dead, dysease not the maister.
Luke 8:50 When Iesus hearde that. He aunswered the father saiynge: Feare not beleue onelye, and she shalbe made whole.
Luke 8:51 And when he came to the house he suffered no man to go in with him, saue Peter, Iames, and Iohn, and the father and mother of the mayden.
Luke 8:52 Euerye bodye wepe and sorowed for her. And he sayd: Wepe not: for she is not dead but slepeth.
Luke 8:53 And they laughte hym to scorne. For they knewe that she was dead.
Luke 8:54 And he thruste them all out, and caught her by the hand, and cried saiynge: Mayde aryse.
Luke 8:55 And her spiryte came againe, and she arose straight waye. And he commaundeth to geue her meate.
Luke 8:56 And the father and the mother of her were astonied. But he warned theim that they shoulde tell no man, what was done.

CHAPTER: 9

Luke 9:1 Then called he the .xij. together, and gaue them power, and authoryte ouer all Deuyls, and that they myght heale diseases.
Luke 9:2 And he sent them to preache the kyngdome of God, and to cure the sycke.
Luke 9:3 And he sayed to them: Take nothinge to sucker you by the waye neither staffe, nor scrype, neyther bread neyther money, neither haue .ij. cotes.
Luke 9:4 And whatsoeuer house ye enter into, there abyde and thence departe:
Luke 9:5 And whosoeuer wyll not receyue you, when ye go out of that cytye shake of the verye dust from your fete, for a testimonye against them.
Luke 9:6 And they went out, and went through the tounes, preachyng the gospell: and healynge euerye wher.
Luke 9:7 And Herode the Tetrarch hearde of al that was done by hym, and doubted, because that it was sayde of some, that Iohn was rysen agayne from death,
Luke 9:8 and of some that Helyas had appeared: and of other that one of the olde prophetes was rysen agayne.
Luke 9:9 And Herode sayde: Ihon haue I beheaded: who then is this of whom I hearde such thinges? And he desyred to se hym.
Luke 9:10 And the Apollels retourned, and told him what great thinges thei had done. And he toke them and wente a syde into a solitary place nye to a cytye called Bethsayda.
Luke 9:11 And the people knew of it, & folowed him. And he receiued them and spake vnto them of the kingdome of God, and healed them that had nede to be healed.
Luke 9:12 And when the daye began to weare away then came the twelue and sayde vnto hym, sende the people awaye, that they maye go into the tounes and villages rounde aboute and lodge, and get meate, for we are here in a solytarye place or wyldernes.
Luke 9:13 But he sayed vnto them: Geue ye them to eate. And they sayde: We haue nomore but fyue loues and two fyshes, excepte we should goo & by meate, for al this people.
Luke 9:14 And they were about a fyue thousande men. And he sayd to his discyples: Cause them to syt doune by fyftyes in a company.
Luke 9:15 And they dyd so, and made them all syt doune.
Luke 9:16 And he toke the fiue loues and the two fishes, and loked vp to heauen: and blessed them, and brake, and gaue to the discyples, to set before the people.
Luke 9:17 And they eate, and were all satisfyed. And there was taken vp of that remained of them, twelue baskettes full of broken meate.
Luke 9:18 And it fortuned as he was alone praiynge: his disciples were with him, and he axed them saiyng: Who saye the people that I am?
Luke 9:19 They aunswered and sayd: Iohn Baptiste. Some saye, Helyas. And some saye, one of the olde prophetes is risen agayne.
Luke 9:20 He sayde vnto them: who saye ye that I am? Peter aunswered and sayde: thou arte the Christe of God.
Luke 9:21 And he warned and commaunded them that they shoulde tell no man that thynge
Luke 9:22 saiynge: that the sonne of man muste suffer manye thinges, and be reproued of the elders, and of the hye pryestes and scrybes and be slayne, & the thirde daye ryse agayne.
Luke 9:23 And he sayed to them all, if anye man wyll come after me, let him denye hym selfe, & take vp his crosse dayly, and folowe me.
Luke 9:24 Whosoeuer wyll saue his lyfe, shall lose it. And whosoeuer shall lose his lyfe for my sake, the same shall saue it.
Luke 9:25 For what auauntageth it a man to winne the whole worlde if he lose him selfe, or runne in damage of him selfe.
Luke 9:26 For whosoeuer is ashamed of me, and of my saiynges: of hym shall the sonne of man be ashamed, when he cometh in his owne glory, & the glory of his father, and of the holye aungels.
Luke 9:27 And I tell you of a surtye. Ther be some of them that stande here, which shall not taste of death, tyll they se the kingdome of God.
Luke 9:28 And it folowed about an .viij. dayes after those saiynge: that he toke Peter, Iames, and Iohn, and went vp into a mountaine to pray.
Luke 9:29 And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenaunce was chaunged, and his garment was white and shone.
Luke 9:30 And beholde, two men talked with him, and they were Moyses & Helias,
Luke 9:31 which appeared gloriouslye, and spake of his departinge, which he shoulde ende at Ierusalem,
Luke 9:32 Peter & they that were with him were heauy with slepe. And when they awoke, they sawe his glory, and two men standinge wyth hym.
Luke 9:33 And it chaunsed as they departed from him, Peter sayd vnto him: Maister, it is good beynge here for vs. Let vs make thre tabernacles, one for the, and one for Moyses, & one for Helyas, & wist not what the sayde.
Luke 9:34 Whyle he thus spake, ther came a cloude & shadowed them, and they feared when they were come vnder the cloude.
Luke 9:35 And ther came a voice out of the cloude saiynge. This is my deare sonne, heare hym.
Luke 9:36 And assone as the voyce was paste Iesus was founde alone. And they kept it close and tolde no man in those dayes anye of those thinges which they had sene.
Luke 9:37 And it chaunched on the nexte dayes as they came doune from the hill, much peopel mete hym.
Luke 9:38 And beholde a man of the company cried out saiyng: Maister, I beseche the beholde my sonne, for he is all that I haue:
Luke 9:39 and se, a sprete taketh him, and sodenlye he cryeth, and he teareth him that he fometh agayne, and wyth much payne departeth from hym, when he hath rent hym,
Luke 9:40 and I besought thy dyscyples to cast him out, and they coulde not.
Luke 9:41 Iesus aunswered and sayde: O generacyon without fayth, and croked, howe longe shall I be wyth you? & shall suffer you? Bringe thy sonne hyther.
Luke 9:42 As he yet was a commyng, the fende rent hym, and tare hym. And Iesus rebuked the vncleane spirite and healed the chyld, and delyuered hym to hys father.
Luke 9:43 And they were all amased at the myghtye power of God. Whyle they wondred euerye one at al thinges, whiche he dyd, he sayde vnto hys discyples:
Luke 9:44 Let these sayinges sinke doune into your eares. The tyme wil come, when the sonne of man shalbe delyuered into the handes of men.
Luke 9:45 But they wiste not what the worde meante, & it was hyd from them, that they vnderstode it not. And they feared to axe him of that sayinge.
Luke 9:46 Then there arose disputacyon amonge them: who should be the greatest.
Luke 9:47 When Iesus perceyued the thoughtes of theyr hertes, he toke a chylde, and set hym harde by hym,
Luke 9:48 & sayde vnto them. Whosoeuer receyueth thys chylde in my name receyueth me. And whosoeuer receyueth me, receyueth hym that sent me. For he that is least among you all the same shalbe great.
Luke 9:49 And Iohn aunswered and sayeth: Mayster we sawe one castyng out deuils in thy name, and we forbad hym, because he foloweth not with vs.
Luke 9:50 And Iesus sayed vnto hym: forbyd ye hym not. For he that is not agaynste vs: is with vs.
Luke 9:51 And it folowed when the tyme was come, that he shoulde be receyued vp, then he set his face to go to Ierusalem,
Luke 9:52 and sent messengers before hym. And they went and entred into a citye of the Samaritans: to make readye for hym.
Luke 9:53 But they woulde not receyue hym, because hys face was as thoughe he woulde go to Ierusalem.
Luke 9:54 When his disciples Iames and Iohn sawe that, they sayde: Lorde, wilte thou that we commaunde that fyre come doune from heauen and consume them, euen as Helyas dyd?
Luke 9:55 Iesus turned aboute, and rebuked them sayinge: ye wote not what maner spirite ye are of.
Luke 9:56 The sonne of man is not come to destroye mennes lyues, but to saue them. And they wente to another toune.
Luke 9:57 And it chaunsed as he went in the waye a certayne man sayde vnto hym: I wyl folowe the, whyther soeuer thou go.
Luke 9:58 Iesus sayd vnto him: foxes haue holes, and byrddes of the ayre haue nestes, but the sonne of man hathe not wheron to laye hys heade.
Luke 9:59 And he sayed vnto another: folow me. And the same sayde: Lorde suffer me fyrste to go & burye my father,
Luke 9:60 Iesus sayde vnto him. Let the dead burye her dead: but go thou & preach the kyngedome of God.
Luke 9:61 And another sayed: I wyll folowe the Lord but let me fyrste go byd them fare wel, which are at home at my house.
Luke 9:62 Iesus sayed vnto hym. No man that putteth hys hande to the plough, and loketh backe, is apte to the kyngdome of God.

CHAPTER: 10

Luke 10:1 After these thynges, the Lord appoynted other seuentye also: and sent them, two & two before him into euery citie and place, whyther he hym selfe woulde come.
Luke 10:2 And he sayed vnto them, the haruest is great, but the laborers are fewe. Praye therfore the Lorde of the harueste, to sende forth laborers into hys haruest.
Luke 10:3 Go youre wayes: beholde, I sende you forth as lambes among wolues.
Luke 10:4 Beare no wallet neyther scryppe, nor shues, and salute no man by the way.
Luke 10:5 Into whatsoeuer house ye enter, fyrste saye: Peace be to thys house.
Luke 10:6 And yf the sonne of peace be there your peace shal reste vpon hym: yf not, it shal returne to you agayne.
Luke 10:7 And in the same house tary styll, eatynge and drinckynge suche as they haue. For the labourer is worthy of thys rewarde. Go not from house to house,
Luke 10:8 & into whatsoeuer citie ye enter, yf they receyue you, eate suche thynges as are set before you,
Luke 10:9 and heale the sycke that are there, and say vnto them: the kyngedome of God is come nye vnto you.
Luke 10:10 But into whatsoeuer citie ye shall enter, yf they receyue you not, go youre wayes out into the streates of the same and saye:
Luke 10:11 euen the very duste, whiche cleaueth on vs of your citie, we wype of agaynste you. Notwithstandynge marke this that the kyngdome of God was come nye vpon you.
Luke 10:12 Yea, and I saye to you, that it shalbe easier in that daye for Zodome then for that citie.
Luke 10:13 Wo be to the Chorazim, wo be to the Bethsaida. For yf the myracles had bene done in Tyre and Sidon, whiche haue bene done in you, they had a great whyle a gone repented, sittynge in hayre and ashes.
Luke 10:14 Neuerthelesse, it shalbe easyer for Tyre and Sidon at the iudgement, then for you.
Luke 10:15 And thou Capernaum, which arte exalted to heauen, shalt be thruste doune to hell.
Luke 10:16 He that heareth you, heareth me, and he that dispyseth you, despyseth me: & he that despyseth me, despiseth hym that sente me.
Luke 10:17 And the seuenty returned againe with ioye saiynge. Lorde euen the very deuyls are subdued to vs throughe thy name.
Luke 10:18 And he sayde vnto them: I sawe Sathan, as it had bene lyghtenynge, fall doune from heauen.
Luke 10:19 Beholde, I geue vnto you power to treade on serpentes & scorpions, & ouer all maner power of the enemye, and nothynge shall hurte you.
Luke 10:20 Neuerthelesse, in thys reioyse not that the spirites are vnder youre power: but reioyse because your names are written in heauen.
Luke 10:21 That same time reioysed Iesus in the spirite, and sayde: I confesse vnto the father, Lorde of heauen and earth, that thou haste hyd these thynges from the wyse and prudente, and hast opened them to the babes. Euen so father for so pleased it the.
Luke 10:22 All thynges are geuen me of my father. And no man knoweth who the sonne is, but the father: neyther who the father is, saue the sonne, and he to whom the sonne wyll shewe hym.
Luke 10:23 And he turned to hys discyples, and sayed secretely: Happy are the eyes, which se that ye se.
Luke 10:24 For I tell you that many prophetes and kinges haue desyred to se those thinges which ye se, and haue not sene them, and to heare those thynges whiche ye heare and haue not hearde them.
Luke 10:25 And beholde a certaine lawyer stode vp, & tempted hym, saiynge: Mayster what shall I do to enherite eternall lyfe?
Luke 10:26 He sayed vnto him: What is writen in the law? how redest thou?
Luke 10:27 And he aunswered and sayde: Loue thy Lorde God with all thy hert, and with al thy soule, and with all thy mynde, and thy neyghboure as thy selfe.
Luke 10:28 And he sayed to hym: Thou haste aunswered ryght. Thys do and thou shalte lyue.
Luke 10:29 He wyllinge to iustifye hym self, sayde vnto Iesus. Who is then my neyghboure?
Luke 10:30 Iesus aunswered, and sayde: A certayne man descended from Ierusalem into Hierico, and fell into the handes of theues, which robbed hym of hys rayment, and wounded him, and departed leuynge him halfe dead.
Luke 10:31 And by chance there came a certayne priest that same waye, and when he sawe hym, he passed by.
Luke 10:32 And lykewyse a Leuite, when he was come nye to the place, went and loked on hym, and passed by.
Luke 10:33 Then a certayne Samaritayne, as he iournyed, came nye vnto hym, and when he sawe hym, he had compassion on hym,
Luke 10:34 and went to, and bounde vp hys woundes, & poureth in oyle and wyne, and put hym on hys owne beaste, and broughte him to a common ynne, and made prouysion for him.
Luke 10:35 And on the morowe when he departed, he toke oute two pence, and gaue them to the hoste, and sayde vnto hym: Take cure of him, and whatsoeuer thou spendest more, when I come agayne, I wyll recompence the.
Luke 10:36 Whiche nowe of these thre thinkest thou, was neyghboure vnto him that fell into the theues handes?
Luke 10:37 And he sayd: he that shewed mercy on hym. Then sayd Iesus vnto hym: Go, & do thou lykewyse.
Luke 10:38 It fortuned as they went, that he entred into a certayne toune. And a certayne woman named Martha, receyued hym into her house.
Luke 10:39 And this woman had a syster called Marye whiche sate at Iesus fete, and hearde his preachynge.
Luke 10:40 And Martha was combred aboute muche seruynge, and stode and sayed: Mayster doest thou not care, that my syster hath lefte me to mynister alone? Byd her therfore, that she helpe me.
Luke 10:41 And Iesu aunswered & said vnto her: Martha, Martha, thou carest, and arte troubled aboute manye thinges,
Luke 10:42 verelye one is nedefull. Marye hath chosen her that good part whiche shall not be taken away from her.

CHAPTER: 11

Luke 11:1 And it fortuned as he was praiynge in a certayne place: when he ceased, one of hys discyples said vnto hym: Mayster, teache vs to praye, as Iohn taught his disciples.
Luke 11:2 And he sayde vnto them: When ye pray saye: O oure father whiche arte in heauen, halowed be thy name. Thy kyngedome come. They will be fulfylled euen in earthe as it is in heauen.
Luke 11:3 Geue vs oure daylye breade euermore.
Luke 11:4 And forgeue vs oure synnes: For euen we forgeue euery man that trespasseth vs: And ledde vs not into temptacyon. But deliuer vs from euyll.
Luke 11:5 And he sayde vnto them: Yf any of you shoulde haue a frende, and shoulde go to hym at midnight, and saye vnto hym: frende lende me thre loues,
Luke 11:6 for a frende of myne is come out of the waye to me, and I haue nothinge to set before him:
Luke 11:7 and he within shoulde aunswere & saye: trouble me not, the dore is now shut, and my seruauntes are with me in the chamber, I cannot ryse, and geue them to the.
Luke 11:8 I saye vnto you, thoughe he woulde not arise and geue him, because he is hys frende: yet because of hys importunitie he wold ryse, and geue him as many as he neded.
Luke 11:9 And I saye vnto you: axe and it shalbe geuen you. Seke, and ye shal finde. Knocke, and it shalbe opened vnto you.
Luke 11:10 For euery one that axeth, receyueth: and he that seketh, findeth: & to hym that knocketh shall it be opened
Luke 11:11 Yf the sonne shall axe bread of any of you that is a father, will he geue him a stone? Or yf he axe fishe, will he for a fishe geue hym a serpente?
Luke 11:12 Or yf he axe an egge, wyl he offer hym a scorpion?
Luke 11:13 Yf ye then which are euill, can geue good gyftes vnto youre chyldren, howe much more shall the father of heauen geue an holy spirite to them that desyre it of hym?
Luke 11:14 And he was castynge oute a deuyll, which was domme. And it folowed when the deuyl was gone out, the domme spake, & the people wondred.
Luke 11:15 But some of them sayed: he casteth out deuyls by the power of Belzebub the chief of the deuyls.
Luke 11:16 And other tempted hym, seking of him a signe from heauen.
Luke 11:17 But he knew their thoughtes, and sayd vnto them: Euery kingdome deuyded within it selfe, shalbe desolate: and one house shall fall vpon another:
Luke 11:18 So yf Satan be deuyded with in him selfe: how shal hys kyngdome endure? Because ye saye that I caste oute deuils by the power of Belzebub
Luke 11:19 If I by the power of Belzebub caste oute deuyls: by whom do youre chyldren caste them oute? Therefore shall they be youre iudges.
Luke 11:20 But yf I with the finger of God caste oute deuyls, no doubte the kyngedome of God is come.
Luke 11:21 When a strong man armed, watched hys house, that he possesseth is in peace.
Luke 11:22 But when a stronger then he cometh vpon hym & ouercommeth hym: he taketh from hym his harnes, wherin he trusted and deuydeth hys goodes.
Luke 11:23 He that is not with me, is agaynste me. And he that gadereth not with me, scatereth.
Luke 11:24 When the vncleane spirite is gone oute of a man, he walketh through waterles places, sekynge reste. And when he fyndeth none, he sayeth, I wyll returne agayne vnto my house whence I came out.
Luke 11:25 And when he cometh, he findeth it swepte and garnyshed.
Luke 11:26 Then goeth he and taketh to him seuen other spirites worse then hym selfe: and they enter in, and dwell there. And the ende of that man, is worsse then the begynnynge.
Luke 11:27 And it fortuned as he spake those thinges, a certayne woman of the companye lyft vp her voyce, and sayde vnto hym: Happy is the wombe that bare the, and the pappes whiche gaue the sucke.
Luke 11:28 But he sayde: Yea, happye are they that heare the worde of God, and kepe it.
Luke 11:29 When the people were gathered thycke together: he began to saye: Thys is an euyll nacyon: they seke a signe, and there shal no signe be geuen them, but the signe of Ionas the prophet.
Luke 11:30 For as Ionas was a signe to the Niniuites, so shall the sonne of man be to thys nacion.
Luke 11:31 The quene of the south shall ryse at iudgement with the men of thys generation: & condempne them: for she came from the ende of the world to heare the wysdome of Salomon. And beholde a greater then Salomon is here.
Luke 11:32 The men of Niniue shall ryse at the iudgement wt thys generacyon, and condempne them: for they repented at the preaching of Ionas. And beholde a greater then Ionas is here.
Luke 11:33 No man lyghteth a candell, & putteth in a pryuy place, neyther vnder a bushell: but on a candelsticke, that they that come in, maye se the lyght.
Luke 11:34 The lyght of thy body is the eye Therfor when thyne eye is single: then is al thy body full of lyghte. But yf thyne eye be euyll: then shall thy bodye also be ful of darknes.
Luke 11:35 Take hede therfore that the lyght whiche is in the, be not darcknes.
Luke 11:36 For yf all thy body shalbe lyght, hauyng no parte darke, then shal all be full of lyght, euen as when a candell doth lyght the with hys brightnes.
Luke 11:37 And as he spake, a certayne Pharisey besought hym to done with hym, and he wente in, & sat doune.
Luke 11:38 When the Pharisei sawe that he marueyled that he had not fyrste weshed before dyner.
Luke 11:39 And the Lorde sayde to hym: Now do ye pharyses make cleane the outsyde of the cup, and of the platter: but your inward parties are full of rauenyng and wickednes.
Luke 11:40 Ye foles, dyd not he that made that which is without: make that whiche is within also?
Luke 11:41 Neuerthelesse geue almose of that ye haue, and beholde all is cleane to you.
Luke 11:42 But wo be to you Pharyses: for the tyth the mint and rew, and al maner herbes, and passe ouer iudgement and the loue of God. These ought ye to haue lefte the other vndone.
Luke 11:43 Wo be to you Pharises, for ye loue the vppermost seates in the synagoges, and gretynges in the markettes.
Luke 11:44 Wo be to you scribes and pharyses, hypocrites, for ye are as graues which appere not, and the men that walke ouer them, are not ware of them.
Luke 11:45 Then aunswered one of the lawyers, and sayed vnto hym: Mayster, thus saiyng, thou puttest vs to rebuke also.
Luke 11:46 Then he sayde: Wo be to you also ye lawyars, for ye lade men wt burthens greuous to be borne, and ye youre selues touche not the packes with one of your fyngers.
Luke 11:47 Wo be to you: ye buylde the sepulchres of of the Prophetes, and youre fathers kylled them,
Luke 11:48 truelye ye beare witnes, that ye alowe the deedes of youre fathers: for they kylled them, and ye buylde theyr sepulchres.
Luke 11:49 Therfore sayde the wysdome of God: I wyll send them Prophetes and Apostles, and of them they shall slea and persecute,
Luke 11:50 that the bloude of all Prophetes which was shede from the beginnynge of the worlde, maye be requyred of thys generacion
Luke 11:51 from the bloude of Abell vnto the bloude of Zacharye, whiche peryshed betwene the aulter and the temple. Verelye I saye vnto you, it shalbe requyred of thys nacyon.
Luke 11:52 Wo be to you lawyers: for ye haue taken away the keye of knoweledge, ye entred not in your selues, and them that came in, ye forbade.
Luke 11:53 When he thus spake vnto them, the lawyers, and the Pharyses began to wexe busye aboute hym, and to stop hys mouthe with manye questyons,
Luke 11:54 layinge wayte for hym, and sekynge to catche some thynge of hys mouthe, whereby they myghte accuse hym.

CHAPTER: 12

Luke 12:1 As there gathered together an innumerable multitude of people (in so muche that they trode one another) he began to saye vnto hys discyples: Fyrste of all beware of the leuen of the Phariseis, which is hypocrisye.
Luke 12:2 For there is nothynge couered the shall not be vncouered: neyther hydde, that shall not be knowen.
Luke 12:3 For whatsoeuer ye haue spoken in darknes: that same shall be hearde in lyghte. And that whiche ye haue spoken in the eare, euen in secrete places, shall be preached euen on the toppe of the housses.
