1 Corinthians 7:12 To the remnaunte speake I and not the Lord. Yf anye brother haue a wyfe that beleued not, if she be contente to dwel with hym, let him not put her awaye.
1 Corinthians 7:13 And the woman, which hath to her husband an infidele, if he consente to dwell with her, let her not put him awaie.
1 Corinthians 7:14 For the vnbeleuinge husbande, is sainctified by the wyfe: and the vnbeleuinge wife, is sainctified by the husbande. Or els were youre chyldren vnclene: but nowe are they pure.
1 Corinthians 7:15 But and if the vnbeleuinge departe, let him departe. A brother or a syster is not in subieccion to suche. God hath called vs in peace.
1 Corinthians 7:16 For howe knowest thou O woman, whether thou shalt saue that man or no? Other howe knoweste thou O man, whether thou shalt saue that woman or no?
1 Corinthians 7:17 but euen as God hath distributed to euery man. As the Lorde hath called euery person so let him walke: and so ordeine I in all congregations.
1 Corinthians 7:18 If any man be called beynge circumcised, let him adde nothing thereto. If any be called vncircumcised: let him not be circumcised.
1 Corinthians 7:19 Circumcison is nothinge, vncircumcision is nothinge, but the kepinge of the commaundementes of God is altogether.
1 Corinthians 7:20 Let euery man abyde in the same state, wherin he is called.
1 Corinthians 7:21 Art thou called a seruauntes, care not for it. Neuertheles if thou maiest be fre, vse it rather.
1 Corinthians 7:22 For he that is called in the Lord beynge a seruaunte, is the Lordes freman. Lykewyse he that is called beynge fre, is Christes seruaunte.
1 Corinthians 7:23 Ye are dearlye bought, be not mennes seruauntes.
1 Corinthians 7:24 Brethren let euery man wherin he is called, therin abide with God.
1 Corinthians 7:25 As concerninge virgins, I haue no commaundemente of the Lorde: yet geue I counsel, as one that hath obteyned mercy of the Lord to be faithfull.
1 Corinthians 7:26 I suppose that it is good for the presente necessitie. For it is good for a man so to be.
1 Corinthians 7:27 Arte thou bounde vnto a wife? seke not to be loused. Arte thou loused from a wife? seke not a wife.
1 Corinthians 7:28 But and if thou take a wyfe, thou sinnest not. Lykewise if a virgine mary: she sinneth not. Neuerthelesse such shal haue trouble in theyr fleshe: but I fauoure you.
1 Corinthians 7:29 This saye I brethren the tyme is short. It remaineth that they which haue wiues, be as though they had none,
1 Corinthians 7:30 and they that wepe be as though they wept not, and they that reioyse be as though they reioysed not: & they that bye, be as though they possessed not:
1 Corinthians 7:31 and they that vse this worlde, be as though they vsed it not. For the fashion of this world goeth away.
1 Corinthians 7:32 I would haue you without care. The single man careth for the thinges of the Lorde howe he maye please the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 7:33 But he that hath maried, careth for the thinges of the worlde howe he may please his wyfe.
1 Corinthians 7:34 There is difference betwene a virgine and a wyfe. The single woman careth for the thinges of the Lorde, that she maye be pure both in bodye and also in spyryte. But she that is maried, careth for the thinges of the worlde, howe she maye please her husbande.
1 Corinthians 7:35 This speake I for youre profite, not to tangel you in a snare, but for that whiche is honeste and comely vnto you, and that ye maye quietly cleaue vnto the Lorde without separacion.
1 Corinthians 7:36 If anye man thinke that it is vncomelye for his virgine if we passe the tyme of mariage, and yf so nede require, let hym do what he listeth, he sinneth not: let them be coupled in mariage.
1 Corinthians 7:37 Neuerthelesse, he that purposeth surely in his herte, hauing none nede, but hath power ouer his owne wyll, and hath so decreed in his herte that he wyl kepe his virgin, doeth well. So then he that ioyneth his virgine in mariage doeth well.
1 Corinthians 7:38 But he that ioyneth not his virgine in mariage doeth better.
1 Corinthians 7:39 The wife is bounde to the lawe as longe as her husband liueth. If her husbande slepe, she is at libertye to mary with whome she wyll, onely in the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 7:40 But she is happyer if she so abyde, in my iudgemente. And I thinke verely that I haue the spirite of God.

CHAPTER: 8

1 Corinthians 8:1 To speake of thinges dedicate vnto Idols, we are sure that we all haue knowledge, knowledge maketh a man swel, but loue edyfyeth.
1 Corinthians 8:2 If anye man thinke that he knoweth anie thinge, he knoweth nothinge yet as he ought to knowe.
1 Corinthians 8:3 But yf anye man loue God, the same is knowen of hym.
1 Corinthians 8:4 To speake of meate dedicate vnto Idols, we are sure that there is none Idol in the world and that there is none other God but one.
1 Corinthians 8:5 And though there be that are called Goddes, whether in heauen other in earthe (as there be Goddes manye and Lordes manye)
1 Corinthians 8:6 yet vnto vs is there but one God, whiche is the father, of whom are al thinges, and we in him: and one Lorde Iesus Christ, by whom are all thinges, and we by hym.
1 Corinthians 8:7 But euery man hath not knowledge. For some suppose that there is an Idole, vntyll this houre, and eate as of a thinge offered vnto the Idole, and so their consciences beynge yet weake are defyled.
1 Corinthians 8:8 Meate maketh vs not acceptable to God. Neither yf we eate are we the better. Neither, yf we eate not, are we the worsse.
1 Corinthians 8:9 But take hede that your libertye cause not the weake to faule.
1 Corinthians 8:10 For yf some man se the, whiche hast knowledge, syt at meate in the Idoles temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weake, be boldened to eate those thinges, whiche are offered vnto the Idole?
1 Corinthians 8:11 And so thorowe thy knowledge shal the weake brother perishe for whom Christ dyed.
1 Corinthians 8:12 When ye synne so againste the brethren, and wound theyr weake consciences, ye synne agaynste Christe.
1 Corinthians 8:13 Wherfore yf meate hurte my brother, I wyll eate no fleshe, whyle the worlde standeth, because I wyll not hurte my brother.

CHAPTER: 9

1 Corinthians 9:1 Am I not an Apostle? am I not free? haue I not sene Iesus Christ our Lorde?
1 Corinthians 9:2 Are not ye my worke in the Lorde? Yf I be not an Apostle vnto other, yet am I vnto you. For the seale of myne Apostleshyppe are ye in the Lord.
1 Corinthians 9:3 Mine aunswere to them that axe me, is this.
1 Corinthians 9:4 Haue we not power to eate, and to drinke?
1 Corinthians 9:5 Either haue we not power to leade aboute a syster to wyfe as well as other Apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
1 Corinthians 9:6 Either onely I and Barnabas haue not power this to do?
1 Corinthians 9:7 who goeth a warfare anye time at hys owne cost? Who planteth a vineiarde, and eateth not of the fruite? Who fedeth a flocke and eateth not of the mylke?
1 Corinthians 9:8 Saye I these thinges after the maner of men? Or sayeth not the lawe the same also?
1 Corinthians 9:9 For it is written in the lawe of Moyses. Thou shalt not mosell the mouth of the oxe that treadeth out the corne. Doeth God take thought for oxen?
1 Corinthians 9:10 Either saith he it not altogether for our sakes? For our sakes no doubte this is written: that he whiche eareth, shoulde eare in hope: & that he whych thresheth in hope, should be partaker of hys hope.
1 Corinthians 9:11 Yf we sowe vnto you spyrytuall thinges: is it a great thinge yf we reape youre carnall thinges.
1 Corinthians 9:12 Yf other be partakers of this power ouer you: wherfore are not we rather? Neuerthelesse we haue not vsed thys power but suffer all thinges leste we shoulde hinder the Gospell of Christe
1 Corinthians 9:13 Do ye not vnderstande howe that they whiche minister in the temple, haue their fyndynge of the temple? And they whych wayte at the aulter, are partakers of the aulter?
1 Corinthians 9:14 Euen so also dyd the Lord ordaine, that they which preach the Gospel, shoulde lyue of the Gospell.
1 Corinthians 9:15 But I haue vsed none of these thinges. Neither wrote I these thinges, that it should be so done vnto me. For it were better for me to dye, then that anye shoulde take this reioysinge from me.
1 Corinthians 9:16 In that I preache the Gospel, I haue nothinge to reioyce of. For necessytye is put vnto me. Wo is it vnto me yf I preach not the Gospel.
1 Corinthians 9:17 Yf I do it wyth a good wil, I haue a rewarde. But yf I do it against my wyl, an offyce is committed vnto me.
1 Corinthians 9:18 What is my reward then? Verelye, that when I preache the Gospell, I make the Gospell of Christ fre, that I misuse not myne authoryte in the Gospell.
1 Corinthians 9:19 For though I be fre from all men, yet haue I made my selfe seruaunte vnto all men, that I myght winne the mo.
1 Corinthians 9:20 Vnto the Iewes, I became as a Iewe, to winne the Iewes. To them that were vnder the lawe, was I made as though I had ben vnder the lawe, to winne them that were vnder the lawe.
1 Corinthians 9:21 To them that were without lawe, became I as though I had ben without the lawe (when I was not without lawe as perteyninge to God, but vnder a lawe as concerninge Christe) to wynne them that were without lawe.
1 Corinthians 9:22 To the weake became I as weake, to wynne the weake. In all thinge I fashioned my selfe to all men, to saue at the lest waye some.
1 Corinthians 9:23 And thys I do for the Gospel sake, that I might haue my parte thereof.
1 Corinthians 9:24 Perceyue ye not howe that they whyche runne in a course, runne all, yet but one receiueth the reward. So runne that ye maye obtayne.
1 Corinthians 9:25 Euery man that proueth maysters abstaineth from all thinges. And they do it to obtaine a corruptible croune: but we to obtaine an vncorruptible croune.
1 Corinthians 9:26 I therfore so runne, not as an uncertaine thinge. So fight I not as one that beateth the ayer:
1 Corinthians 9:27 but I tame my bodye and bringe it into subieccion, leste after that I haue preached to other, I my selfe should be a cast away.

CHAPTER: 10

1 Corinthians 10:1 Brethren I would not that ye should be ignoraunte of this, howe that oure fathers were all vnder a cloude, and al passed thorowe the sea,
1 Corinthians 10:2 and were all baptysed vnder Moyses, in the cloude, and in the sea:
1 Corinthians 10:3 and dyd al eate of one spyrytual meate,
1 Corinthians 10:4 and dyd al drincke of one maner of spyrytual drincke. And they drancke of that spyrytuall rocke that folowed them, which rocke was Christe.
1 Corinthians 10:5 But in manie of them had God no delite. For they were ouerthrowen in the wyldernes.
1 Corinthians 10:6 These are ensamples to vs that we should not luste after euyll thinges, as they lusted.
1 Corinthians 10:7 Neyther be ye worshippers of Images as were some of them accordynge at it is written: The people sate doune to eate and drynke, and rose vp agayne to playe.
1 Corinthians 10:8 Neyther let vs committe fornicacion as some of them committed fornycacyon, and were destroied in one day .xxiij. thousand.
1 Corinthians 10:9 Neither let vs tempte Christe as some of them tempted, and were destroyed of serpentes.
1 Corinthians 10:10 Neyther murmure ye as some of them murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.
1 Corinthians 10:11 Al these thinges happened vnto them for ensamples, and were written to put vs in remembraunce, whom the endes of the world are come vpon.
1 Corinthians 10:12 Wherfore let him that thynketh he standeth, take hede leste he fall.
1 Corinthians 10:13 There hath none other temptacion taken you, but suche as foloweth the nature of man. But God is faythful whiche shall not suffre you to be tempted aboue your strength: but shall in the middest of the temptacion make a waye to escape out.
1 Corinthians 10:14 Wherfore my deare beloued, fle from worshipping of Idols.
1 Corinthians 10:15 I speake as vnto them, whiche haue dyscrecion, iudge ye what I saye.
1 Corinthians 10:16 Is not the cuppe of blessinge whiche we blesse, partaking of that bloude of Christe?
1 Corinthians 10:17 is not the breade which we breake, partakinge of the bodye of Christ? because that we (thoughe we be manye) yet are one bodye in as muche as we all are partakers of one breade.
1 Corinthians 10:18 Beholde Israell whiche walketh carnally. Are not they which eate of the sacrifyce, partakers of the aultre?
1 Corinthians 10:19 What saye I then? that the Image is any thinge? or that it whiche is offered to Images is anye thinge?
1 Corinthians 10:20 Naye, but I saye, that these thinges, whiche the Gentyles offer, they offer to deuyls, and not to God. And I woulde not that ye should haue felloushippe wt the deuyls.
1 Corinthians 10:21 Ye can not drinke of the cuppe of the Lorde: and of the cuppe of the deuils. Ye can not be partakers of the Lordes table, and of the table of the deuils.
1 Corinthians 10:22 Either shall we prouoke the Lorde? Or are we stronger then he? All thinges are laufull vnto me, but all thinges are not expedient.
1 Corinthians 10:23 All thinges are lauful to me, but all thinges edifye not.
1 Corinthians 10:24 Let no man seke his owne profyte: but let euerye man seke anothers wealth.
1 Corinthians 10:25 Whatsoeuer is solde in the market, that eate and axe no questions for consciens sake.
1 Corinthians 10:26 For the earth is the Lordes, and all that therin is.
1 Corinthians 10:27 Yf anye of them whiche beleue not, byd you to a feste, & yf ye be disposed to go, whatsoeuer is set before you, eate, axing no question for conscience sake.
1 Corinthians 10:28 But and yf anye man saye vnto you: this is dedicate vnto Idols, eate not of it for his sake that sheweth it, and for hurtyng of conscience (The earth is the Lordes, & al that therin is)
1 Corinthians 10:29 Conscience I saye, not thine but the conscience of that other. For why should my libertie be iudged of another mannes conscience?
1 Corinthians 10:30 For yf I take my parte wyth thankes: why am I euil spoken of for the thinge, wherfore I geue thankes.
1 Corinthians 10:31 Whether therfore ye eate or drynke, or whatsoeuer ye do, do al to the praise of God.
1 Corinthians 10:32 See that ye geue occasion of euil, neither to the Iewes, nor yet to the Gentiles, neither to the congregation of God:
1 Corinthians 10:33 euen as I please al men in al thinges, not sekinge myne owne profite, but the profit of manye, that they myghte be saued.

CHAPTER: 11

1 Corinthians 11:1 Folowe me, as I do Christe.
1 Corinthians 11:2 I commende you brethren that ye remembre me in al thinges, & kepe the ordinaunces euen as I deliuered them to you.
1 Corinthians 11:3 I woulde you knewe that Christ is the heade of euery man. And the man is the womans heade. And God is Christes heade.
1 Corinthians 11:4 Euery man praiynge or prophesiynge hauing any thinge on his heade, shameth his head.
1 Corinthians 11:5 Euery woman that prayeth or prophesyeth bare headed, dishonesteth her heade. For it is euen all one, and the very same thinge, euen as though she were shauen.
1 Corinthians 11:6 If the woman be not couered, let her also be shoren. If it be shame for a woman to be shorne or shauen let her couer her head.
1 Corinthians 11:7 A man oughte not to couer his heade, for as muche as he is the ymage and glorye of God. The woman is the glorye of the man.
1 Corinthians 11:8 For the man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man.
1 Corinthians 11:9 Neither was the man created for the womans sake: but the woman for the mannes sake.
1 Corinthians 11:10 For thys cause ought the woman to haue power on her heade, for the aungels sakes.
1 Corinthians 11:11 Neuerthelesse, neyther is the man wythout the woman neyther the woman wythout the man in the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 11:12 For as the woman is of the man, euen so is the man by the woman: but al is of God.
1 Corinthians 11:13 Iudge in your selfes whether it be comelye, that a woman praye vnto God beare headed.
1 Corinthians 11:14 Or els doeth not nature teache you that it is a shame for a man,
1 Corinthians 11:15 yf he haue longe heyr, & prayse to a woman, yf she haue longe heyre? For her heyre is geuen her to couer her wythall.
1 Corinthians 11:16 If there be anye man amonge you, that lusteth to striue let hym knowe that we haue no suche custome, neither the congregations of God.
1 Corinthians 11:17 This I warne you of, and commende not that ye come together: not after a better maner but after a worsse.
1 Corinthians 11:18 Fyrste of all when ye come together in the congregacion, I heare that there is dyssencyon amonge you, and I partely, beleue it.
1 Corinthians 11:19 For there muste be sectes amonge you, that they whyche are perfecte amonge you, myghte be knowen.
1 Corinthians 11:20 When ye come together a man can not eate the Lordes supper. For euery man beginneth afore to eate hys owne supper.
1 Corinthians 11:21 And one is houngerye, and another is drounken. Haue ye not houses to eate and to drinke in?
1 Corinthians 11:22 Or els despise ye the congregacion of God and shame them that haue not? What shall I saye vnto you? shall I prayse you: In thys prayse I you not.
1 Corinthians 11:23 That whiche I delyuered you, I receiued of the Lorde. For the Lorde Iesus the same nyght, in whyche he was betrayed, toke breade,
1 Corinthians 11:24 and thanked and brake, and sayde. Take ye, eate ye thys is my bodye whiche is broken for you. Thys do ye in the remembraunce of me.
1 Corinthians 11:25 After the same maner he toke the cuppe, when supper was done, saying. Thys cuppe is the newe testamente in my bloude. Thys do as ofte as ye drynke it, in the remembraunce of me.
1 Corinthians 11:26 For as often as ye shal eate thys breade, and drincke this cuppe, ye shall shewe the Lordes death tyll he come.
1 Corinthians 11:27 Wherfore whosoeuer shall eate of this bread, or drinke of the cuppe vnworthely, shall be gyltie of the bodye and bloude of the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 11:28 Let a man therfore examen hym selfe, and so let hym eate of the breade and drynke of the cuppe.
1 Corinthians 11:29 For he that eateth or drinketh vnworthelye, eateth and drynketh his owne dampnation, because he maketh no difference of the Lordes bodye.
1 Corinthians 11:30 For this cause manye are weake and sycke amonge you, and manye slepe.
1 Corinthians 11:31 Yf we had truely iudged our selues, we should not haue ben iudged.
1 Corinthians 11:32 But when we are iudged of the Lorde, we are chastened, because we shoulde not be dampued wyth the worlde.
1 Corinthians 11:33 Wherfore my brethren, when ye come together to eate, tary one for another.
1 Corinthians 11:34 If any man hunger, let hym eate at home, that ye come not together vnto condempnation. Other thynges wil I set in order when I come.

CHAPTER: 12

1 Corinthians 12:1 In spiritual thinges brethren I would not haue you ignoraunt.
1 Corinthians 12:2 Ye knowe that ye were Gentyles, and wente your wayes vnto domme Idols, euen as you were led.
1 Corinthians 12:3 Wherfore I declare vnto you, that no man speakinge in the spirite of God, defieth Iesus. Also no man saye that Iesus is the Lorde: but by the holye ghoste.
1 Corinthians 12:4 There are diuersities of gyftes verelye, yet but one spirite.
1 Corinthians 12:5 And there are differences of administracions, & yet but one Lorde.
1 Corinthians 12:6 And there are diuerse maners of operations, and yet but one God, which worketh all thinges that are wrought, in all creatures.
1 Corinthians 12:7 The giftes of the spirite are geuen to euerie man to profite the congregation.
1 Corinthians 12:8 To one is geuen thorowe the spirite the vtteraunce of wysdome. To another is geuen the vtteraunce of knowledge by the same spirite.
1 Corinthians 12:9 To another is geuen fayth by the same spirite. To another the giftes of healinge, by the same spirite.
1 Corinthians 12:10 To another power to do miracles. To another prophecie. To another iudgement of spirites. To an other diuerse tounges. To another the interpretation of tounges.
1 Corinthians 12:11 And these all worketh euen the selfe same spyryte, deuydynge to euerye man seuerall gyftes, euen as he wyll.
1 Corinthians 12:12 For as the bodye is one, and hath manye membres, and all the membres of one bodye though they be many, yet are they but one bodye: euen so is Christ.
1 Corinthians 12:13 For in one spyryte are we al baptysed to make one body, whether we be Iewes or Gentiles, whether we be bounde or fre: and haue al drounke of one spirite.
1 Corinthians 12:14 For the body is not one member, but manye.
1 Corinthians 12:15 Yf the fote saye: I am not the hand, therfore I am not of the bodye: is he therfore not of the bodye?
1 Corinthians 12:16 And yf the eare saye, I am not the eye: therfore I am not of the bodye: is he therfore not of the bodie?
1 Corinthians 12:17 If al the bodye were an eye, where were then the eare? If all were hearinge? wher were the smellynge?
1 Corinthians 12:18 But nowe hath God disposed the membres euerye one of them in the bodye, at hys owne pleasure,
1 Corinthians 12:19 If they were al one member: where were the bodye?
1 Corinthians 12:20 Nowe are there manye membres, yet but one bodye.
1 Corinthians 12:21 And the eye can not saye vnto the hand: I haue no nede of the: nor the heade also to the fete. I haue no nede of you.
1 Corinthians 12:22 Yea rather a greate deale those members of the bodye, whyche seme to be moste feble, are moste necessarye.
1 Corinthians 12:23 And vpon those membres of the bodie, which we thinke leste honest, put we moste honestye on. And oure vngodlye parties haue most beauty on.
1 Corinthians 12:24 For our honeste members nede it not. But God hath so disposed the bodye, and hath geuen moste honoure to that parte whyche lacked,
1 Corinthians 12:25 lest there should be anye stryfe in the bodye: but that the membres shoulde indifferentlye care one for another.
1 Corinthians 12:26 And yf one member be had in honoure, all the membres be glad also.
1 Corinthians 12:27 Ye are the bodye of Christe, and membres one of another.
1 Corinthians 12:28 And God hath also ordeined in the congregation, fyrst the Apostles, secondarely prophetes, thyrdely teachers then them that do miracles: after that the giftes of healinge, helpers, gouernes, diuersitie of tounges.
1 Corinthians 12:29 Are all Apostles? Are all Prophetes? Are all teachers? Are all doers of miracles:
1 Corinthians 12:30 Haue al the gyftes of healinge? Do all speake with tounges? Do al interprete?
1 Corinthians 12:31 Couet after the beste gyftes. And yet shewe I vnto you a more excellente waye.

CHAPTER: 13

1 Corinthians 13:1 Thought I speake with tounges of men and angels, and yet had no loue, I were euen as soundinge brasse, or as a tynklinge Cimbal.
1 Corinthians 13:2 And though I could prophecye, and vnderstande all secretes, and all knowledge: yea, yf I had all fayth so that I coulde moue mountaines out of theyr places, and yet had no loue, I were nothing.
1 Corinthians 13:3 And thought I bestowed all my goodes to fede the pore, and though I gaue my bodye euen that I burned, and yet had no loue, it profeteth me nothinge.
1 Corinthians 13:4 Loue suffreth longe, and is curteous. Loue enuieth not. Loue doth not frowardelye, swelleth not, dealeth not dishonestlye,
1 Corinthians 13:5 seketh not her owne, is not prouoketh to anger, thinketh not euil,
1 Corinthians 13:6 reioiceth not in iniquitie: but reioiseth in the trueth,
1 Corinthians 13:7 suffreth all thinge, beleueth all thinges, hopeth al thinges, endureth in all thinges.
1 Corinthians 13:8 Though that propheciynge fayle, other tounges shall cease, or knowledge vanishe awaye, yet loue falleth neuer awaye.
1 Corinthians 13:9 For oure knowledge is vnperfect, & oure prophesiynge is vnperfecte.
1 Corinthians 13:10 But when that which is perfect, is come: then that which is vnperfect, shal be done awaye:
1 Corinthians 13:11 When I was a child, I spake as a chylde, I vnderstode as a child, I Imagined as a chylde. But assone as I was a man, I put away childishnes.
1 Corinthians 13:12 Nowe we se in a glasse euen in a darke speakinge, but then shall we se face to face. Nowe I knowe vnperfectlye, but then shall I knowe euen as I am knowen.
1 Corinthians 13:13 Nowe abideth fayth, hope, and loue, euen these thre: but the chiefe of these is loue.

CHAPTER: 14

1 Corinthians 14:1 Laboure for loue, and couete spyrytuall gyftes: and moste chiefely for to prophecye.
1 Corinthians 14:2 For he that speaketh wyth tounges speaketh not vnto men, but vnto God, for no man heareth hym, howe be it in the spyryte he speaketh mysteryes.
1 Corinthians 14:3 But he that prophecyeth, speaketh vnto men, to edifiynge, to exhortation and to comforte.
1 Corinthians 14:4 He that speaketh wyth tounges profyteth hym selfe: he that prophecieth edifyeth the congregation.
1 Corinthians 14:5 I woulde that ye all spake with tounges: but rather that ye prophecyed. For greater is he that prophecieth, then he that speaketh with tounges, excepte he expounde it also, that the congregacion maye haue edifiyng.
1 Corinthians 14:6 Nowe brethren yf I come vnto you speakinge with tounges, what shall I profite you, excepte I speake vnto you, other by reuelation or knowledge, or propheciynge, or doctryne.
1 Corinthians 14:7 Moreouer when thynges wythout lyfe, geue sounde: whether it be a pipe or an harpe excepte they make a distinction in the soundes, howe shal it be knowen what is piped or harped?
1 Corinthians 14:8 And also yf the trompe geue an vncertaine voice, who shall prepare him selfe to fyght?
1 Corinthians 14:9 Euen so likewyse when ye speake with tounges, excepte ye speake wordes that haue signifycacion, howe shall it be vnderstande what is spoken? For ye shall but speake in the ayer.
1 Corinthians 14:10 Manye kindes of voices are in the worlde and none of them are wythout significacion.
1 Corinthians 14:11 If I knowe not what the voice meaneth, I shalbe vnto hym that speaketh, an alient: and he that speaketh shall be alient vnto me
1 Corinthians 14:12 Euen so ye (for as much as ye couete spiritual gyftes) seke that ye maye haue plentye vnto the edifiyng of the congregation.
1 Corinthians 14:13 Wherfore let him that speaketh with tounges praye, that he maye interprete also.
1 Corinthians 14:14 If I praye wyth tounges, my spyryte prayeth: but my mynde is wythout fruite.
1 Corinthians 14:15 What is it then? I wyl praye with the spirite, and wyll praye with mynde also. I wil singe with the spyrite, and wil singe with the minde also.
1 Corinthians 14:16 For els when thou blessest with the spirite howe shal he that occupieth the roume of the vnlearned saye amen at thy geuynge of thankes, saynge: he vnderstandeth not what thou sayeste?
1 Corinthians 14:17 Thou verelye geueste thankes wel, but the other is not edifyed.
1 Corinthians 14:18 I thanke my God, I speake with tounges more then ye all.
1 Corinthians 14:19 Yet had I leuer in the congregation, to speake fyue wordes with my mynd to the information of other, rather then .x. thousand wordes with the tounge.
1 Corinthians 14:20 Brethren be not chyldren in wyt howebeit as concerninge maliciousnes be children: but in wyt be perfect.
1 Corinthians 14:21 In the lawe it is written, wyth other tounges, and with other lippes wyl I speake vnto thys people, and yet for al that wil they not heare me, sayeth the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 14:22 Wherfore, tounges are for a signe, not to them that beleue, but to them that beleue not. Contrarywyse propheciyng serueth not, for them that beleue not: but for them whiche beleue.
1 Corinthians 14:23 Yf therfore when all the congregation is come together, and all speake wyth tounges, there come in they that are vnlearned, or they whyche beleue not: wyll they not saye that ye are out of your wyttes?
1 Corinthians 14:24 But and yf all prophecye, and there come in one that beleueth not, or one vnlearned, he is rebuked of al men, and is iudged of euerye man:
1 Corinthians 14:25 and so are the secretes of hys herte opened, and so falleth he doune on hys face, and worshyppeth God, & sayeth that God is wyth you in dede.
1 Corinthians 14:26 Howe is it then brethren? When ye come together, euerye man hath his songe, hath his doctryne, hath his tounge, hath hys reuelation, hath hys interpretation. Let al thynges be done vnto edifiynge.
1 Corinthians 14:27 If anye man speake wyth tounges, let it be two at ones, or at the moste thre at ones, and that by course: and let another interprete it.
1 Corinthians 14:28 But yf there be no interpreter, let him kepe silence in the congregation, and let him speake to him selfe and to God.
1 Corinthians 14:29 Let the Prophetes speake two at ones, or thre at ones, and let other iudge.
1 Corinthians 14:30 And yf anye reuelation be made to another that sitteth by, let the fyrste holde hys peace.
1 Corinthians 14:31 For ye maye all prophecye, one by one that all maye learne, and all maye haue comforte.
1 Corinthians 14:32 For the spirites of the Prophetes are in the power of the Prophetes.
1 Corinthians 14:33 For God is not causer of strife, but of peace, as he is in all other congregations of the sainctes.
1 Corinthians 14:34 Let your wyues kepe silence in the congregations. For it is not permitted vnto them to speake: but let them be vnder obedience, as sayeth the lawe.
1 Corinthians 14:35 If they wil learne anye thynge, let them axe theyr husbandes at home. For it is shame for women to speake in the congregation.
1 Corinthians 14:36 Spronge the worde of God from you? Eyther came it vnto you onelye.
1 Corinthians 14:37 Yf anye man thinke hym selfe a Prophet, either spyrytuall. let him vnderstand, what thinges I write vnto you. For they are the commaundementes of the Lorde.
1 Corinthians 14:38 But and yf anye man be ignoraunte, let him be ignoraunt.
1 Corinthians 14:39 Wherfore brethren couete to prophecye, and forbyd not to speake wyth tounges.
1 Corinthians 14:40 And let al thynges be done honestlye and iu ordre.

CHAPTER: 15

1 Corinthians 15:1 Brethren as pertaininge to the Gospel, whiche I preached vnto you, whiche ye haue also accepted, and in the whiche ye continue,
1 Corinthians 15:2 by whiche also ye are saued: I do you to wit, after what maner I preached vnto you yf ye kepe it, except ye haue beleued in vaine.
1 Corinthians 15:3 For fyrste of al I deliuered vnto you that which I receiued how that Christe dyd for oure synnes, agreinge to the scriptures:
1 Corinthians 15:4 and that he was buried, and that he rose agayne the thyrde daye accordinge to the scriptures
1 Corinthians 15:5 and that he was sene of Cephas, then of the twelue.
1 Corinthians 15:6 After that he was sene of more then fyue hundred brethren at ones of whiche manie remaine vnto this daie, and many are fallen a slepe.
1 Corinthians 15:7 After that appeared he to Iames, then to al the Apostles.
1 Corinthians 15:8 And last of al, he was sene of me, as of one that was borne out of due time.
1 Corinthians 15:9 For I am the leste of al the Apostles, whiche am not worthy to be called an Apostle, because I persecuted the congregation of God.
1 Corinthians 15:10 But by the grace of God I am that I am. And his grace which is in me, was not in vaine, but I laboured more aboundantly then they al, not I but the grace of God which is with me.
1 Corinthians 15:11 Whether it were I or they, so we preache, and so haue ye beleued.
1 Corinthians 15:12 If Christe be preached howe that he rose from death: howe saye some? that are amonge you, that there is no resurreccion from death?
1 Corinthians 15:13 If ther be no rysinge agayne from death, then is Christe not rysen.
1 Corinthians 15:14 If Christ be not rysen, then is our preachinge vayne, and your faith is also in vaine.
1 Corinthians 15:15 Ye and we are founde false witnesses of God. For we haue testifyed of God, howe that he raysed vp Christe, whom he raysed not vp yf it be so that the deade ryse not vp againe.
1 Corinthians 15:16 For yf the dead rise not againe then is Christ not rysen againe.
1 Corinthians 15:17 Yf it be so that Christe rose not, then is youre faith in vayne, and yet are ye in youre synnes.
1 Corinthians 15:18 And ther to they which are fallen a slepe in Christ, are peryshed.
1 Corinthians 15:19 If in thys lyfe onelye we beleue on Christ, then are we of all men the miserablest.
1 Corinthians 15:20 But now in Christ rysen from the dead, and is become the fyrste fruytes of them that slepte.
1 Corinthians 15:21 For by a man came death, and by a man came the resurceccion of the dead.
1 Corinthians 15:22 For as by Adam all dye: euen so by Christe, shall all be made aliue,
1 Corinthians 15:23 and euery man in his owne order. The fyrste is Christe, then they that are Christes at his comminge.
1 Corinthians 15:24 Then commeth the ende when he hath delyuered vp the kyngedome to God the father, when he hath put doune all rule, authoritie, and power.
1 Corinthians 15:25 For he muste reigne tyll he haue put all hys enemies vnder his fete.
1 Corinthians 15:26 The laste enemy that shalbe destroied is death.
1 Corinthians 15:27 For he hath put all thinges vnder hys fete. But when he sayeth, all thinges are put vnder hym it is manifest that he is excepted, whyche dyd put all thinges vnder him.
1 Corinthians 15:28 When all thinges are subdued vnto hym: then shall the sonne also him selfe be subiecte to him that put al thinges, vnder him that God maye be all in all thinges.
1 Corinthians 15:29 Eyther els what do they, which are baptysed ouer the dead, yf the dead ryse not at all? Why are they then baptysed ouer the dead?
1 Corinthians 15:30 yea and why stande we in ieoperdy euerye houre?
1 Corinthians 15:31 By our reioysinge, whyche I haue in Christe Iesu our Lorde, I dye dayly.
1 Corinthians 15:32 That I haue fought wyth beastes at Ephesus, after the maner of men what auauntageth it me, yf the dead rise not againe? Let vs eate and drincke, to morowe we shall dye.
1 Corinthians 15:33 Be not deceiued: malicious speakinges corrupte good maners.
1 Corinthians 15:34 Awake truelye out of slepe and synne not. For some haue not the knowledge of God. I speake this vnto you: rebuke.
1 Corinthians 15:35 But some man wyl saye: howe aryse the dead? wyth what bodyes come they in?
1 Corinthians 15:36 Thou fole, that whiche thou sowest is not quickened except it dye.
1 Corinthians 15:37 And what sowest thou? Thou sowest not that bodye that shall be, but are corne (I meane either of what, or of some other)
1 Corinthians 15:38 and God geueth it a body at his pleasure, to euery seede a seuerall body.
1 Corinthians 15:39 Al fleshe is not one maner of fleshe: but there is one maner fleshe of men, another maner fleshe of beastes, another maner fleshe of fyshes, and another of byrdes.
1 Corinthians 15:40 There are celestiall bodyes, and there are bodyes terrestriall. But the glorye of the celestiall is one, and the glorye of the terrestriall another.
1 Corinthians 15:41 There is one maner glory of the sunne and another glorye of the mone, and another glory of the starres. For one starre dyffereth from another in glorye.
1 Corinthians 15:42 So is the resurreccion of the dead. It is sowen in corruption, and ryseth in incorruption.
1 Corinthians 15:43 It is sowen in dishonoure, and ryseth in honoure. It is sowen in weakenes, and ryseth in power. It is sowen a naturall bodye, and ryseth a spyrytuall bodye.
1 Corinthians 15:44 There is a naturall bodye, and there is a spiritual bodye,
1 Corinthians 15:45 as it is written: the fyrste man Adam was made a lyuinge soule, and the last Adam was made a quickeninge spirite.
1 Corinthians 15:46 Howbeit that is not fyrste whiche is spyrytual: but that which is naturall, and then that which is spyrytual.
1 Corinthians 15:47 The fyrste man is of the earth, earthlye: the seconde man is the Lorde from heauen.
1 Corinthians 15:48 As is the earthlye, such are they that are earthlye. And as is the heauenlye, suche are they that are heauenlye.
1 Corinthians 15:49 And as we haue borne the ymage of the earthly so shal we beare the Image of the heauenlye.
1 Corinthians 15:50 This saye I brethren, that fleshe and bloude can not inheryte the kyngedome of God. Neyther corruption inheryte: vncorruption.
1 Corinthians 15:51 Beholde I shewe you a mysterye. We shal not al slepe: but we shal al be chaunged,
1 Corinthians 15:52 and that in a momente & in the twinkling of an eye, at the sound of the last trompe. For the trompe shall blowe, and the dead shal rise incorruptible and we shal be chaunged.
1 Corinthians 15:53 For this corruptible must put on incorruptibilitie; and this mortal muste put on immortalytye.
1 Corinthians 15:54 When this corruptible, hath put on incorruptibilitie, and this mortal hath put on immortalite, then shalbe brought to passe the saiyng that is written.
1 Corinthians 15:55 Death is consumed into victory. Death wher is thy stynge? Hel wher is thy victory?
1 Corinthians 15:56 The stinge of death is sinne: & the strength of sinne is the lawe.
1 Corinthians 15:57 But thankes be vnto God, which hath geuen vs victory, thorowe our Lorde Iesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 15:58 Therfore my deare brethren, be ye stedfast and vnmouable alwayes ryche in the workes of the Lorde, for as much as ye knowe, howe that your labour is not in vaine in the Lorde.

CHAPTER: 16

1 Corinthians 16:1 Of the gatheringe for the sainctes, as I haue ordeined in the congregations of Galatia, euen, so do ye.
1 Corinthians 16:2 Vpon some sonday let euerye one of you put a syde at home, and laye vp whatsoeuer he thinketh meate that there be no gatheringes when I come.
1 Corinthians 16:3 When I am come, whomsoeuer ye shall alowe by youre letters, them will I sende to bringe your liberalitie vnto Ierusalem.
1 Corinthians 16:4 And yf it be mete that I go, they shal go with me.
1 Corinthians 16:5 I wyl come vnto you after I haue gone ouer Macedonia. For I wyl go throughout Macedonia.
1 Corinthians 16:6 With you peraduenture I wil abide a while, or els winter, that ye maye bringe me on my waye whethersoeuer I go.
1 Corinthians 16:7 I wil not se you nowe in my passage: but I truste to abyde a while wyth you, yf God shal suffer me.
1 Corinthians 16:8 I wyll tary at Ephesus vntyl whitsontyde.
1 Corinthians 16:9 For a greate dore, and a frutefull is opened to me, and there are manye aduersaryes.
1 Corinthians 16:10 If Timotheus come, se that he be with you. For he worketh the worke of the Lorde as I do.
1 Corinthians 16:11 Let no man despyse hym: but conuaye hym forthe in peace, that he maye come vnto me. For I loke for hym wyth the brethren.
1 Corinthians 16:12 To speake of brother Apollo: I greatlye desyred hym to come vnto you wyth the brethren but hys mynd was not at all to come at this tyme. Howbeit he wil come when he shal haue conueniente tyme.
1 Corinthians 16:13 Watche ye, stande faste in the fayth, quyte you lyke men and be stronge,
1 Corinthians 16:14 & let youre busynes be done in loue.
1 Corinthians 16:15 Brethren (ye know the house of Stephana, howe that they are the fyrste fruites of Achaia, and that they haue appoynted them selues to minister vnto the sainctes)
1 Corinthians 16:16 I beseche you that ye be obedient vnto suche, and to all that helpe and laboure.
1 Corinthians 16:17 I am glad of the comminge of Stephana. Fortunatus and Achaichus: for that which was lackinge on youre parte, they haue supplied.
1 Corinthians 16:18 They haue comforted my spyrite and youres. Loke therfore that ye knowe them that are suche.
1 Corinthians 16:19 The congregations of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscylla salute you muche in the Lorde, and so doth the congregation that is in theyr house.
1 Corinthians 16:20 Al the brethren grete you. Grete ye one another wyth an holy kysse.
1 Corinthians 16:21 The salutation of me Paule with myne owne hande.
1 Corinthians 16:22 Yf anye man loue not the Lorde Iesus Christ the same be anathema maranatha.
1 Corinthians 16:23 The grace of the Lorde Iesus Christe be wyth you all,
1 Corinthians 16:24 My loue be wyth you all in Christe Iesus. Amen.

BOOK: 2 Corinthians

CHAPTER: 1

2 Corinthians 1:1 Paule an Apostle of Iesu Christ by the wyll of God, and brother Timotheus. Vnto the congregation of God, whithe is at Corinthum, with all the sainctes, which are in all Achaia.
2 Corinthians 1:2 Grace be wyth you, and peace from God oure father, and from the Lorde Iesus Christ.
2 Corinthians 1:3 Blessed be God the father of oure Lorde Iesus Christ, the father of mercy, and the God of all comforte,
2 Corinthians 1:4 whiche comforteth vs in all oure tribulacion, in so muche that we are able to comforte them, which are troubled in whatsoeuer tribulation it be, with the same comforte wherwith we our selues are comforted of God.
2 Corinthians 1:5 For as the affliccions of Christ are plenteous in vs: euen so is our consolacion plenteous by Christe.
2 Corinthians 1:6 Whether we be troubled for youre consolacion & saluacion, whiche saluacion, sheweth her power in that ye suffer the same afflictions which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted for your consolacion, and saluation,
2 Corinthians 1:7 yet oure hope is stedfast for you, in as muche as we knowe howe that as ye haue youre parte in affliccions, so shall ye be partakers of consolacion.
2 Corinthians 1:8 Brethren I woulde not haue you ignoraunt of oure trouble, whiche happened vnto vs in Asia. For we were greued out of measure passinge strength, so greatlye that we despeared euen of lyfe.
2 Corinthians 1:9 Also we receiued and aunswere of death in our selues, and that because we woulde not put oure truste in oure selues: but in God, whiche rayseth the dead to lyfe again,
2 Corinthians 1:10 & which delyuered vs from so greate a death, and doth delyuer. On whom we truste that yet here after he will delyuer,
2 Corinthians 1:11 by the helpe of your prayer for vs: that by the meanes of manye occasions, thankes maye be geuen of manye on our behalfe, for the grace geuen vnto vs.
2 Corinthians 1:12 Oure reioysinge is this, the testimony of oure conscience, that in synglenes and Godly purenes, and not in fleshely wysdome, but by the grace of God, we haue had oure conuersation in the worlde, and moste of all to youwardes.
2 Corinthians 1:13 We write no nother thinges vnto you, then that ye read and also knowe, yea & I truste ye shall fynde vs vnto the ende euen as ye haue founde vs partelye,
2 Corinthians 1:14 for we are your reioysinge, euen as ye are oures in the day of the Lorde Iesus.
2 Corinthians 1:15 And in this confidence was I minded the other tyme to haue come vnto you, that ye myghte haue had yet one pleasure more,
2 Corinthians 1:16 and to haue passed by you into Macedonia, and to haue come againe out of Macedonia vnto you, & to haue bene led forth to Iewryward of you.
2 Corinthians 1:17 When I thus wyse was mynded: dyd I vse lyghtnes? Or thynke I carnallye those thinges, which I thinke? that with me should be yea yea, and nay nay?
2 Corinthians 1:18 God is faithfull. For oure preaching vnto you, was not yea & nay.
2 Corinthians 1:19 For Gods sonne Iesus Christe, whiche was preached amonge you by vs (that is to saye, by me and Siluanus and Timotheus) was not yea and naye, but in him it was yea:
2 Corinthians 1:20 For all the promyses of God, in him are yea, and are in him Amen, vnto the lande of God thorow vs.
2 Corinthians 1:21 For it is God, whiche stablisheth you and vs in Christ, and hath annointed vs,
2 Corinthians 1:22 which hath also sealed vs, and hath geuen the earnest of the spyryte into oure hertes.
2 Corinthians 1:23 I call God for a recorde vnto my soule that for to fauer you withall I came not anye more to Corinthum.
2 Corinthians 1:24 Not that we be lordes ouer youre fayth but helpers of youce ioye. For by fayth ye stand.

CHAPTER: 2

2 Corinthians 2:1 But I determyned thys in my selfe, that I wold not come agayne to you in heauynes.
2 Corinthians 2:2 For yf I make you sorye, who is it that shoulde make me glad, but the same which is made sorye by me?
2 Corinthians 2:3 And I wrote thys same Epistle vnto you, leste yf I came, I shoulde take heauines of them, of whome I ought to reioyce. Certaynely thys confidence haue I in you al, that my ioye is the ioye of you al.
2 Corinthians 2:4 For in great affliction and anguyshe of herte I wrote vnto you with many teares: not to make you sory, but that ye myght perceyue the loue which I haue most specially vnto you.
2 Corinthians 2:5 Yf anye man haue caused sorowe the same hath not made me sory, but partelye: leaste I shoulde greue you all.
2 Corinthians 2:6 It is suffycyente vnto the same man, that he was rebuked of many.
2 Corinthians 2:7 So that nowe contrarywyse ye ought to forgeue hym, and comforte hym: leaste that same persone shoulde be swalowed vp, with ouer muche heauynes.
2 Corinthians 2:8 Wherfore I exhorte you, that loue maye haue strengthe ouer hym.
2 Corinthians 2:9 For this cause verely dyd I wryte, that I might know the profe of you, whether ye shoulde be obedyent in all thynges.
2 Corinthians 2:10 To whom ye forgeue any thynge, I forgeue also. And verelye yf I forgeue anye thynge, to whome I forgaue it, for your sakes forgaue I it in the roume of Christe,
2 Corinthians 2:11 leaste Sathan shoulde preuente vs. For thys thoughtes are not vnknowen vnto vs.
2 Corinthians 2:12 When I was come to Troada for Christes gospels sake (and a greate dore was opened vnto me of the Lorde)
2 Corinthians 2:13 I had no rest in my spyryte, because I founde not Titus my brother: but toke my leaue of them, and wente awaye vnto Macedonia.
2 Corinthians 2:14 Thankes be vnto God whiche alwayes geueth vs the victorye in Christ, and openeth the sauour of hys knowledge by vs in euerye place.
2 Corinthians 2:15 For we are vnto God the swete sauoure of Christe, bothe amonge them that are saued, and also among them whiche peryshe.
2 Corinthians 2:16 To the one part are we the sauoure of death vnto death. And vnto the other parte are we the lauoure of lyfe vnto lyfe. And who is mete vnto these thynges?
2 Corinthians 2:17 For we are not as many are which choppe & chaunge with the worde of god: but euen out of purenes, and by the power of God, and in the syghte of God, so speake we in Christe.

CHAPTER: 3

2 Corinthians 3:1 We begynne to prayse oure selues agayne. Nede we as some other, of Epistles, of recommendacion vnto you? or letters of recommendacyon from you?
2 Corinthians 3:2 Ye are oure Epistle wrytten in oure hertes, which is vnderstande and read of, all men,
2 Corinthians 3:3 in that ye are knowen, howe that ye are the Epistle of Christe, ministred by vs and writen, not wyth ynke, but wyth the spirite of the lyuyng God, not in tables of stone, but in fleshly tables of the herte.
2 Corinthians 3:4 Suche truste haue we throughe Christe to Godwarde
2 Corinthians 3:5 not that we are suffyciente of our selues to thynke any thynge as it were of our selues, but our ablenes cometh of God,
2 Corinthians 3:6 which hath made vs able to minister the new testament, not of the letter, but of the spirite. For the letter killeth, but the spirite geueth lyfe.
2 Corinthians 3:7 Yf the mynystracyon of death throughe the letters fygured in stones was gloryous, so that the chyldren of Israell coulde not behold the face of Moyses for the glory of hys countenaunce (whiche glory neuerthelesse is done awaye)
2 Corinthians 3:8 why shall not the ministracion of the spiryte be muche more gloryous?
2 Corinthians 3:9 For yf the ministrynge of condempnacyon be glorious, muche more doeth the ministracyon of ryghtuousnes excede in glorye.
2 Corinthians 3:10 For no doubte that which was there glorifyed is not once gloryfyed in respecte of thys excedynge glorye.
2 Corinthians 3:11 Then yf that whih is destroyed was gloryous muche more shall that whiche remayneth, be gloryous.
2 Corinthians 3:12 Seynge then that we haue suche trust, we vse great boldnes,
2 Corinthians 3:13 and do not as Moyses, whiche put a vayle ouer hys face that the children of Israell shoulde not se, for what purpose that serued whiche is put awaye.
2 Corinthians 3:14 But theyr myndes were blynded. For vntil thys daye remayneth the same couerynge vntaken awaye in the olde testament when they reade it, whiche in Christe is put awaye.
2 Corinthians 3:15 But euen vnto thys daye when Moyses is reade, the vayle hangeth before theyr hertes.
2 Corinthians 3:16 Neuerthelesse when they turne to the Lorde, the vayle shalbe taken awaye.
2 Corinthians 3:17 The Lorde no doubte is a spiryte. And where the spiryte of the Lorde is, there is libertye.
2 Corinthians 3:18 But we all beholde the glorye of the Lorde with hys face open, and chaunged vnto the same similitude, from glorye to glory, euen of the spirite of the Lorde.

CHAPTER: 4

2 Corinthians 4:1 Therfore seynge that we haue suche an offyce, euen as mercye is come on vs, we faynte not:
2 Corinthians 4:2 but haue caste from vs the clokes of vnhonestye, and walke not in craftynes, neyther corrupte we the word of God: but walke in open trueth, & reporte our selues to euerye mans conscience in the syght of God.
2 Corinthians 4:3 Yf oure Gospell be yet hyd, it is hyd among them that are loste,
2 Corinthians 4:4 in whome the God of thys worlde hath blynded the myndes of them which beleue not, leste the lyght of the gloryous gospell of Christe which is the ymage of God shoulde shyne vnto them.
2 Corinthians 4:5 For we preache not oure selues, but Christ Iesus to be the Lorde, and oure selues youre seuauntes for Iesus sake.
2 Corinthians 4:6 For it is God that commaunded the lighte to shyne out of darknes, whiche hath shyned in oure hertes, for to geue the lyghte of the knoweledge of the glorye of God, in the face of Iesus Christe.
2 Corinthians 4:7 But we haue thys treasure in earthen vessels that the excellent power of it myght appeare to be of God, and not of vs.
2 Corinthians 4:8 We are troubled on euerye syde, yet are we not withoute shyfte. We are in pouerte, but not vtterlye withoute some what.
2 Corinthians 4:9 We are persecuted, but are not forsaken. We are caste doune, neuerthelesse we peryshe not.
2 Corinthians 4:10 And we alwayes beare in oure bodyes the dyinge of the Lorde Iesus, that the lyfe of Iesus myght appeare in oure bodyes.
2 Corinthians 4:11 For we whiche lyue are alwayes delyuered vnto deathe for Iesus sake, that the lyfe also of Iesu myghte appeare in oure mortall fleshe.
2 Corinthians 4:12 So then death worketh in vs, and lyfe in you.
2 Corinthians 4:13 Seynge then we haue the same spirite of fayth, accordynge as it is writen: I beleued, & therfor haue I spoken. We also beleue, & therfore speake.
2 Corinthians 4:14 For we knowe that he which raysed vp the Lord Iesus, shal rayse vp vs also by the meanes of Iesus, & shall set vs wt you.
2 Corinthians 4:15 For all thynges do I for youre sakes, that the plentuous grace by thankes geuen of manye, maye redounde to the prayse of God.
2 Corinthians 4:16 Wherfor we are not weryed, but though oure outwarde man perysh: yet the inwarde man is renewed daye by daye.
2 Corinthians 4:17 For oure excedynge trybulation whiche is momentanye and lyghte, prepareth an excedynge and eternall wayghte of glory vnto vs,
2 Corinthians 4:18 whyle we loke not on the thinges whiche are sene, but on the thinges which are not sene. For thynges whiche are sene, are temporall, but thynges whiche are not sene, are eternall.

CHAPTER: 5

2 Corinthians 5:1 We knowe surelye yf oure earthy mansyon wherin we nowe dwell were destroyed, that we haue a buyldynge ordeyned of God an habitacyon not made with handes, but eternall in heauen.
2 Corinthians 5:2 And therfore syghe we, desyrynge to be clothed wyth oure mansyon which is from heauen
2 Corinthians 5:3 so yet yf that we be founde clothed, and not naked.
2 Corinthians 5:4 For as longe as we are in thys tabernacle, we syghe and are greued, for we woulde not be vnclothed, but woulde be clothed vpon, that mortalitye myghte be swalowed vp of lyfe.
2 Corinthians 5:5 He that ordeyned vs for thys thynge, is God whiche very same hath geuen vnto vs the earnest of the spiryte.
2 Corinthians 5:6 Therfore we are alwaye of good chere, & knowe well that as longe as we are at home in the bodye, we are absente from God.
2 Corinthians 5:7 For we walke in fayth, and se not.
2 Corinthians 5:8 Neuerthelesse we are of good comforte, and had leuer be absente from the bodye, and to be presente with the Lorde.
2 Corinthians 5:9 Wherfore whether we be at home or from home, we endeuoure oure selues to please hym.
2 Corinthians 5:10 For we muste all appeare before the iudgement seate of Christ, that euery man maye receyue the workes of hys bodye accordyng to that he hath done, whether it be good or badde?
2 Corinthians 5:11 Seynge then that we know, how the Lorde is to be feared, we fare fayre with men. For we are knowen well ynoughe vnto God. I truste also that we are knowen in your consciences.
2 Corinthians 5:12 We prayse not oure selues agayne vnto you, but geue you an occasyon to reioyce of vs that ye maye haue somewhat agaynst them whiche reioyce in the face, and not in the hert,
2 Corinthians 5:13 For yf we be to feruente, to God we are to feruente. Yf we kepe measure, for youre cause kepe we measure.
2 Corinthians 5:14 For the loue of Christ constrayneth vs, because we thus iudge, yf one be dead, for all that then are all dead,
2 Corinthians 5:15 and that he dyed for all, that they which lyue, shoulde not hence forth lyue vnto them selues, but vnto hym, whiche dyed for them, and rose agayne.
2 Corinthians 5:16 Wherfore hence forthe knowe we no man after the fleshe. In so muche though we haue knowen Christe after the fleshe, nowe hence forth knowe we hym so no more.
2 Corinthians 5:17 Therfore yf anye man be in Christe, he is a newe creature. Olde thynges are passed awaye, beholde all thynges are become newe.
2 Corinthians 5:18 Neuerthelesse all thynges are of God, whiche hath reconcyled vs vnto hym selfe by Iesus Christe, and hath geuen vnto vs the offyce to preache the attonement.
2 Corinthians 5:19 For God was in Christe, and made agrement betwene the worlde and hym selfe, and imputed not theyr synnes vnto them, & hathe committed to vs the preachynge of the atonnement.
2 Corinthians 5:20 Nowe then are we messengers in the roume of Christ: euen as thoughe God dyd beseche you thorowe vs: So praye we you in Christes stede, that ye be atone with God,
2 Corinthians 5:21 for he hath made hym to be synne for vs, whiche knewe no synne, that we by hys meanes should be that ryghtuousnes whiche before God is allowed.

CHAPTER: 6

2 Corinthians 6:1 We as healpers therfore exhorte you, that ye receyue not the grace of God in vayne.
2 Corinthians 6:2 For he sayeth: I haue hearde the in a tyme accepted: and in the day of saluacyon. haue I succoured the. Beholde nowe is that well accepted tyme: behold now is that daye of saluacyon.
2 Corinthians 6:3 Let vs geue no man occasyon of euyll, that in our offyce be founde no faulte,
2 Corinthians 6:4 but in al thynges let vs behaue our selues as the ministers of God. In muche pacience, in afflictions, in necessitie, in anguishe,
2 Corinthians 6:5 in strypes, in prysonnement in stryfe, in laboure, in watchynge, in fasting
2 Corinthians 6:6 in purenes, in knoweledge, in longe suffering in kyndnes, in the holye ghoste, in loue vnfayned,
2 Corinthians 6:7 in the wordes of trueth, in the power of God, in the armour of ryghtuousnes on the ryght hande, and on the lyfte,
2 Corinthians 6:8 in honoure and dishonour, in euyll reporte, & good reporte: as disceyuers & yet true:
2 Corinthians 6:9 as vnknowen, & yet knowen: as dying, & beholde we yet liue: as chastened and not kylled:
2 Corinthians 6:10 as sorowyng, & yet alway mery: as poore, and yet make many ryche: as hauynge nothynge, and yet possessynge all thynges.
2 Corinthians 6:11 O ye Corinthyans, oure mouth is open vnto you. Oure hertes made large:
2 Corinthians 6:12 ye are in no strayte in vs, but are in a strayte in youre owne bowelles:
2 Corinthians 6:13 I promyse you lyke rewarde with me, as to my chyldren.
2 Corinthians 6:14 Sette your selues therfore at large, and beare not a straungers yoke with the vnbeleuers. For what feloweshyppe hath ryghtuousnes with vnryghtuousnes? What companye hath lyght with darkenes?
2 Corinthians 6:15 What concorde hath Christe with Belyall? Eyther what parte hath he that beleueth with an infydele?
2 Corinthians 6:16 Howe agreeth the temple of God with Images. And ye are the temple of that lyuynge God, as sayed God. I wyll dwell amonge them, and walke among them, and wyll be theyr God, and they shall be my people.
2 Corinthians 6:17 Wherfore come out from among them, and separate youre selues (sayeth the Lorde) and touche none vncleane thynge: so wyll I receyue you,
2 Corinthians 6:18 and wyll be a father vnto you, and ye shall be vnto me sonnes and doughters, sayth the Lorde almyghtye.

CHAPTER: 7

2 Corinthians 7:1 Seynge that we haue such promyses dearely beloued, let vs cleanse oure selues from al fylthynesse of the fleshe & spyrite, and grow vp to full holynesse in the feare of God.
2 Corinthians 7:2 Vnderstande vs. We haue hurte no man: we haue corrupt no man: we haue defrauded no man.
2 Corinthians 7:3 I speake not thys to condempne you: for I haue shewed you before, that ye are in oure hertes to dye, and lyue wyth you.
2 Corinthians 7:4 I am very bolde ouer you, and reioyce gentelye in you. I am fylled with comforte, and am excedynge ioyouse in all oure trybulatyons.
2 Corinthians 7:5 For when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on euerye syde. Outwarde was fyghtynge, inwarde was feare.
2 Corinthians 7:6 Neuerthelesse GOD that comforteth the abiect, comforteth vs at the comming of Tytus.
2 Corinthians 7:7 And not with hys commynge onelye: but also wyth the consolacyon wherewith he was comforted of you. For he tolde vs youre desyre, youre mournyng, youre feruent mynde to me warde, so that I now reioyce the more.
2 Corinthians 7:8 Wherfore thoughe I made you sory with a letter, I repent not, though I dyd repent. For I perceyue that, that same Epistle made you sory, thoughe it were but for a season.
2 Corinthians 7:9 But I nowe reioyce, not that ye were sory, but that ye so sorowed, that ye repented. For ye sorowed Godlye, so that in nothyng ye were hurt by vs.
2 Corinthians 7:10 For Godly sorowe causeth repentaunce vnto saluacyon, not to be repented of: when worldlye sorowe causeth death.
2 Corinthians 7:11 Beholde, what diligence thys Godlye sorowe that ye toke, hath wroughte in you: yea it caused you to cleare your selues. It caused indignacyon, it caused feare, it caused desyre, it caused a feruent mynde, it caused punyshement. For in all thynges ye haue shewed your selues that ye are cleare in that matter.
2 Corinthians 7:12 Wherfore thoughe I wrote vnto you: I dyd it not for hys cause that dyd hurte, neyther for hys cause that was hurt: but that our good mynd whiche we haue towarde you in the syght of God, myght appeare vnto you.
2 Corinthians 7:13 Therfore we are comforted, because ye are comforted: yea and excedynglye the more ioyed we, for the ioye that Titus had, because his spyryte was refreshed of you all.
2 Corinthians 7:14 I am therfore, not nowe ashamed, though I bosted my selfe to hym of you. For as all thynges which I preached vnto you are true, euen so is oure bostyng, that I bosted my selfe to Titus with all, founde true.
2 Corinthians 7:15 And nowe is his inwarde affection more aboundante towarde you, when he remembreth the obedience of euerye one of you, howe with feare and tremblynge ye receyued hym,
2 Corinthians 7:16 I reioyce that. I maye be bolde ouer you in all thynges.

CHAPTER: 8

2 Corinthians 8:1 I do you to wyt brethren, of the grace of God, which is geuen in the congregacyons of Macedonia,
2 Corinthians 8:2 howe that the aboundaunce of theyr reioysynge is, that they are tryed with muche trybulacyon. And therto thoughe they were excedynge poore, yet haue they geuen excedynge richelye, and that in synglenesse.
2 Corinthians 8:3 For to theyr powers (I beare recorde) ye and beyonde theyr power, they were wyllynge of theyr owne accorde,
2 Corinthians 8:4 & prayed vs with great instaunce that we would receyue theyr benefyte, and suffer them to be partakers with other in mynystrynge to the saynctes.
2 Corinthians 8:5 And thys they dyd, not as we loked for: but gaue theyr owne selues fyrste to the Lorde, and after vnto vs by the wyl of God:
2 Corinthians 8:6 so that we coulde not but desyre Titus to accomplyshe the same beneuolence amonge you also, euen as he had begonne.
2 Corinthians 8:7 Nowe therfore, as ye are ryche in al partties in fayth, in worde, in knoweledge, in all feruentnes, and in loue, which ye haue to vs: euen so se that ye be plenteous in thys beneuolence.
2 Corinthians 8:8 Thys saye I not as commaundyng: but because other are so feruente, therfore proue I youre loue, whether it be perfecte or no.
2 Corinthians 8:9 Ye knowe the lyberalytie of oure Lorde Iesus Christe, whiche though he were ryche, yet for youre sakes became pore that ye thorowe hys pouertye myght be made ryche.
2 Corinthians 8:10 And I geue counsell hereto. For thys is expediente for you, whiche beganne, not to do onelye, but also to wyll, a yeare a go.
2 Corinthians 8:11 Nowe therfore performe the dede: that as there was in you a redynes to wyll, euen so ye may performe the dede of that whiche ye haue.
2 Corinthians 8:12 For yf there be fyrste a wyllynge mynde, it is accepted accordyng to that a man hath, and not accordynge to that he hath not.
2 Corinthians 8:13 It is not my mynde that other be set at ease, and ye broughte into combraunce:
2 Corinthians 8:14 but that there be equalnes nowe at thys tyme, that youre aboundaunce succoure theyr lacke: that theyr aboundaunce maye supplye youre lacke:
2 Corinthians 8:15 that there may be equalitie, agreyng to that which is wryten. He that gathered muche, had neuer the more aboundaunce, and he that gathered lyttell had neuerthelesse.
2 Corinthians 8:16 Thankes be vnto God, which put in the hert of Titus the same good mynde towarde you.
2 Corinthians 8:17 For he accepted the requeste, yea rather he was so well willyng that of hys owne accorde he came vnto you.
2 Corinthians 8:18 We haue sente with him that brother whose lande is the Gospell thorowe out all the congregacyons,
2 Corinthians 8:19 and not so onely, but is also chosen of the congregacyons to be a felowe with vs in oure iorneye concernynge thys beneuolence that is ministred by vs vnto the prayse of the Lorde, and to stere vp youre prompte mynde.
2 Corinthians 8:20 For this we eschue, that anye man shoulde rebuke vs in thys plentuous distribucyon, that is ministred by vs,
2 Corinthians 8:21 and therfore make prouision for honest thynges, not in the syghte of God onelye, but also in the syght of men.
2 Corinthians 8:22 We haue sent with them a brother of ours whome we haue oftentimes proued diligente in many thinges, but now much more diligent.
2 Corinthians 8:23 The greate confydence whiche I haue in you hath caused me thus to do, partely for Tytus sake, whiche is my felowe and helper as concernynge you, partely because of other which are oure brethren, and the messengers of the congregacyons, and the glorye of Christe.
2 Corinthians 8:24 Wherfore shewe vnto them the profe of your loue, and of the reioysynge that we haue of you, that the congregacyons maye se it.

CHAPTER: 9

2 Corinthians 9:1 Of the ministrynge to the saynctes, it is but superfluous for me to wryte vnto you:
2 Corinthians 9:2 for I knowe your redynes of mynde whereof I boste my selfe vnto them of Macedonia, and saye that Achaia was prepared a yeare a go, and youre feruentnes hath prouoked manye.
2 Corinthians 9:3 Neuerthelesse yet haue I sent these brethren, lest oure reioysynge ouer you shoulde be in vayne in thys behalfe, and that ye (as I haue sayed) prepare your selues,
2 Corinthians 9:4 lest parauenture yf they of Macedonia come with me, and fynde you vnprepared, the bost that I made in thys matter, shoulde be a shame to vs. I saye not vnto you.
2 Corinthians 9:5 Wherfore I thought it necessarye to exhorte the brethren, to come before hande vnto you, for to prepare your good blessyng promysed afore, that it myght be redye, so that it be a blessynge, and not a defraudynge.
2 Corinthians 9:6 Thys yet remember, howe that he whiche soweth lyttell, shal reape lyttell, & he that soweth plentuously, shall reape plentuously.
2 Corinthians 9:7 And let euery man do accordyng as he hath purposed in hys hert, not groundgingly, or of necessitie. For God loueth a chearefull geuer.
2 Corinthians 9:8 God is able to make you ryche in al grace that ye in al thynges hauyng suffycyent vnto the vttermoste, maye be ryche vnto all maner good workes,
2 Corinthians 9:9 as it is wrytten. He that sparsed abroade, and hath geuen to the pore, hys ryghtuousnes, remayneth for euer.
2 Corinthians 9:10 He that fyndeth the sower seed, shall minister breade for fode, and shall multyplye your seede and increace the frutes of youre ryghtuousnes that on all partyes,
2 Corinthians 9:11 ye maye be made riche in all synglenes, whiche causeth thorowe vs, thankes geuynge vnto God.
2 Corinthians 9:12 For the offyce of thys ministracyon, not onelye supplyeth the neede of the saynctes: but also is aboundaunte herein, that for thys laudable mynystrynge, thankes myghte be geuen to God of many,
2 Corinthians 9:13 whiche prayse God for the obedience of youre professyng the Gospell of Christe, and for youre synglenes in distrybutynge to them and to all men,
2 Corinthians 9:14 and in theyr prayers to God for you, long after you, for the aboundaunce grace of God geuen vnto you.
2 Corinthians 9:15 Thankes be vnto God for hys vnspakeable gyfte.

CHAPTER: 10

2 Corinthians 10:1 I Paule my selfe beseche you by the mekenesse and softenes of Christe, whiche when I am present amonge you, am of no reputacion, but am bolde toward you beynge absent,
2 Corinthians 10:2 I beseche you, that I nede not to be bolde, when I am present (with that same confydence, wherewith I am supposed to be bolde) agaynste some whiche repute vs as though we walked carnally.
2 Corinthians 10:3 Neuerthelesse thoughe we walke compassed wt the fleshe, yet we ware not fleshly.
2 Corinthians 10:4 For the weapens of oure warre are not carnal thynges, but thynges myghtye in God to caste doune stronge holdes,
2 Corinthians 10:5 wherewith we ouerthrowe Imaginations and euerye hye thynge that exalteth it selfe agaynste the knoweledge of God, and brynge into captiuite all vnderstandynge to the obedience of Christe,
2 Corinthians 10:6 and are redye to take vengeaunce on all disobedience, when youre obedience is fulfylled.
2 Corinthians 10:7 Loke ye on thynges after the vtter apparence? Yf any man truste in hym selfe that he is Christes, let the same also consydre of him self that as he is Christes, euen so are we Christes
2 Corinthians 10:8 and thoughe I shoulde boste my selfe some what more of oure authoritie which the Lord hath geuen vs to edifye, and not to destroye you, it shoulde not be to my shame.
2 Corinthians 10:9 This say I, leste I shoulde seme, as thoughe I went about to make you afrayde with letters.
2 Corinthians 10:10 For the Epystles (sayeth he) are sore and stronge, but hys bodely presence is weake, and hys speach rude.
2 Corinthians 10:11 Let hym that is suche, thynke on thys wyse, that as we are in wordes by letters when we are absent, such are we in dedes when we are present.
2 Corinthians 10:12 For we can not fynde in oure hertes to make oure selues of the numbre of them, or to compare oure selues to them, whiche laud them selues, neuerthelesse while they measure them selues wyth them selues, and compare them selues with them selues, they vnderstande nought.
2 Corinthians 10:13 But we wyll not reioyce aboue measure: but accordynge to the quantitye of the measure, whiche God hath distrybuted vnto vs, a measure that reacheth euen vnto you.
2 Corinthians 10:14 For we stretche not oure selues beyonde measure, as thoughe we had not reacheth vnto you. For euen vnto you haue we come with the Gospell of Christe,
2 Corinthians 10:15 and we boste not oure selues out of measure in other mens labours. Yea, and we hope, when your fayth is increased amonge you, to be magnifyed accordynge to oure measure more largelye,
2 Corinthians 10:16 and to preache the Gospell in those regyons, whiche are beyonde you: and not to reioyce of that whiche is by another mans measure prepared already.
2 Corinthians 10:17 Let hym that reioyceth, reioyce in the Lord.
2 Corinthians 10:18 For he that prayseth hym self, is not allowed: but he whom the Lorde prayseth.

CHAPTER: 11

2 Corinthians 11:1 Wolde to God ye coulde suffre me a lytell in my folyshenes: yea, and I praye you, forbeare me.
2 Corinthians 11:2 For I am gelous ouer you with godly gelousye. For I coupled you to one man, to make you a chaste virgyn to Christe.
2 Corinthians 11:3 But I feare leste as the serpente begyled Eue thorowe hys suttelty, euen so youre wyttes shoulde be corrupte from the synglenes that is in Christe.
2 Corinthians 11:4 For yf he that commeth, preache another Iesus then hym whom we preached: or yf ye receyue another spiryte then that whiche ye haue receyued: other another Gospell then that ye haue receyued, ye myght ryghte well haue bene content.
2 Corinthians 11:5 I impose that I was not behynde the chief Apostles.
2 Corinthians 11:6 Though I be rude in speakynge, yet I am not so in knoweledge. Howe be it amonge you: we are knowen to the vttermoste what we are in all thynges.
2 Corinthians 11:7 Dyd I therein synne, because I submytted my selfe, that ye myght be exalted, and because I preached to you the Gospell of God fre?
2 Corinthians 11:8 I robbed other congregacyons, and toke wages of them, to do you seruyce with al.
2 Corinthians 11:9 And when I was present with you, and had nede, I was greuous to no man, for that whiche was lackynge vnto me, the brethren whiche came from Macedonia, supplyed: and in all thynge I kept my selfe that I shoulde not be greuous to you, & so wyl I kepe my selfe.
2 Corinthians 11:10 Yf the trueth of Christe be in me, thys reioysynge shall not be taken from me in the regyons of Achaia.
2 Corinthians 11:11 Wherfore? Because I loue you not? God knoweth.
2 Corinthians 11:12 Neuerthelesse what I do, that wyll I do, to cut awaye occasyon from them which desyre occasyon, that they myght be founde lyke vnto vs in that wherein they reioyce.
2 Corinthians 11:13 For these false Apostles are disceytfull workers, and fashyon them selues lyke vnto the Apostles of Christe.
2 Corinthians 11:14 And no maruail for Satan hym selfe is chaunged into the fashyon of an angell of lyghte.
2 Corinthians 11:15 Therfore it is no greate thynge, thoughe hys mynysters fashyon them selues as thoughe they were the mynisters of rightuousnes, whose end shalbe accordynge to theyr dedes.
2 Corinthians 11:16 I saye agayne, lest anye man thynke that I am folyshe, or els euen nowe take me as a fole, that I maye boaste my selfe a lyttell.
2 Corinthians 11:17 That I speake, I speake it not after the wayes of the Lorde, but as it were folishly, while we are nowe come to bostynge.
2 Corinthians 11:18 Seyng that manye reioyce after the fleshe, I will reioyse also.
2 Corinthians 11:19 For ye suffer foles gladly, because that ye youre selues are wyse.
2 Corinthians 11:20 For ye suffre euen yf a man brynge you into bondage: yf a man deuoure, yf a man take yf a man exalte hym selfe, yf a man smite you on the face.
2 Corinthians 11:21 I speake as concernynge rebuke, as thoughe we had bene weake. Howe be it, wherein soeuer any man dare be bolde (I speake folyshly) I dare be bolde also.
2 Corinthians 11:22 They are Hebrues, so am I: They are Israelytes, euen so am I. They are the seede of Abraham, euen so am I.
2 Corinthians 11:23 They are the ministers of CHRISTE (I speake as a fole) I am more: In labours more aboundaunte: In strypes aboue measure: In pryson more plentuouslye: In death ofte.
2 Corinthians 11:24 Of the Iewes .v. tymes receyued I euerye tyme .xl. strypes saue one.
2 Corinthians 11:25 Thryse was I beaten with roddes. I was once stoned. I suffered thryse shipwracke. Nyght and daye haue I bene in the depe of the sea.
2 Corinthians 11:26 In iorneyeyng often: in parils of waters: in parylles of robbers: in ieoperdyes amonge the heathen. I haue bene in peryls in cytyes, in peryls in wyldernes, in peryls in the sea, in peryls among false brethren,
2 Corinthians 11:27 in laboure and trauayle, in watchyng often, in hunger, in thyrste, in fastynges often, in colde, and in nakednes.
2 Corinthians 11:28 And besyde the thynges whiche outwardelye happen vnto me, I am combered dayelye, and do care for all congregations.
2 Corinthians 11:29 Who is weake, and I am not weake? Who is hurte in the faythe, and my herte burneth not?
2 Corinthians 11:30 Yf I muste nedes reioyce, I wyll reioyce of myne infirmities.
2 Corinthians 11:31 The God and father of oure Lorde Iesus Christ, whiche is blessed for euermore, knoweth that I lye not
2 Corinthians 11:32 In the citie of Damascon the gouerner of the people vnder king Aretas, layd watche in the citie of the Damascens, and woulde haue caught me,
2 Corinthians 11:33 and at a wyndowe was I let doune in a basket thorow the wall, and so scaped hys handes.

CHAPTER: 12

2 Corinthians 12:1 It is not expedyent for me (no doubte) to reioyce. Neuerthelesse I wyll come to visions and reuelations of the Lorde.
2 Corinthians 12:2 I knowe a man in Christe aboue .xiiij. yeares agone (whether he were in the bodye I cannot tell, or whether he were oute of the bodye I cannot tell, God knoweth) whiche was taken vp into the third heauen.
2 Corinthians 12:3 And I knowe the same man (whether in the bodye, or oute of the bodye, I cannot tell, God knoweth)
2 Corinthians 12:4 howe that he was taken vp into paradyse, and hearde wordes not to be spoken, whiche no man can vtter.
2 Corinthians 12:5 Of thys man wyll I reioyce, of my selfe wyll I not reioyce, excepte it be of myne infyrmytyes.
2 Corinthians 12:6 And yet thoughe I woulde reioyce, I shoulde not be a fole: for I shoulde saye the trueth: Neuerthelesse I spare, lest anye man shoulde thynke of me aboue that he seeth me to be, or heareth of me.
2 Corinthians 12:7 And lest I shoulde be exalted out of measure thorowe the aboundaunce of reuelacions there was geuen vnto me vnquyetnes of the fleshe, the messenger of Satan to buffete me: because I shoulde no be exalted oute of measure.
2 Corinthians 12:8 For thys thynge besought I the Lorde thryse, that it myght departe from me.
2 Corinthians 12:9 And he sayde vnto me: my grace is suffycyent for the. For my strengthe is made perfecte thorowe weakenes. Very gladly therfor wil I reioyce of my weakenes, that the strength of Christe maye dwell in me
2 Corinthians 12:10 Therfore haue I delectacyon in infyrmities, in rebukes, in nede, in persecutions, in anguyshe, for Christes sake. For when I am weake, then am I stronge.
2 Corinthians 12:11 I am made a fole in bostynge my selfe. Ye haue compelled me: I ought to haue bene commended of you. For in nothynge was I inferyor vnto the chiefe Apostles. Thoughe I be nothynge
2 Corinthians 12:12 yet the tokens of an Apostle were wroughte amonge you with al pacience: with signes, and wonders and myghty dedes.
2 Corinthians 12:13 For what is it wherein ye were inferyours vnto other congregacyons except it be therein that I was not greuous vnto you. Forgeue me thys wrong done vnto you.
2 Corinthians 12:14 Behold the now thyrde time I am redy to come vnto you, and yet wyll I not be greuouse vnto you. For I seke not yours, but you. Also the chyldren ought not to lay vp for the fathers & mothers but the fathers a mothers for the chyldren.
2 Corinthians 12:15 I wyll very gladly bestowe, and wyll be bestowed for youre soules: thoughe the more I loue you, the lesse I am loued agayne.
2 Corinthians 12:16 But be it that I greued you not: neuerthelesse I was crafty and toke you with gyle.
2 Corinthians 12:17 Dyd I pyl you by any of them which I sent vnto you?
2 Corinthians 12:18 I desyred Titus, and with hym I sent a brother. Did Tytus defraude you of any thing? walked we not in one spyryte? walked we not in lyke steppes?
2 Corinthians 12:19 Agayne, thynke ye that we excuse oure selues. We speake in Christe in the syght of God. But we do all thynges dearelye beloued for youre edifiynge.
2 Corinthians 12:20 For I feare least it come to passe, that when I come, I shall not fynde you suche as I woulde, and I shalbe founde amonge you debate, enuiynge, wrath, stryfe, backbytynges, whisperynges, swellynges & discorde.
2 Corinthians 12:21 I feare leste when I come agayne, God brynge me lowe amonge you, and I be constrayned to bewayle many of them which haue synned already, and haue not repented of the vncleanes, fornicacyon, and wantonnes, whiche they haue commytted.

CHAPTER: 13

2 Corinthians 13:1 Nowe come I the thyrde time vnto you. In the mouthe of two or three wytnesses shall euery thing stande.
2 Corinthians 13:2 I tolde you before, & tell you before, and as I sayd when I was presente with you the seconde tyme, so wayte I now beynge absent to them which in tyme paste haue synned, and to all other, that yf I come agayne, I wyll not spare,
2 Corinthians 13:3 seyng that ye seke experience of Christe, whiche speaketh in me, which amonge you is not weake, but is myghty in you.
2 Corinthians 13:4 And verely thoughe it came of weakenes that he was crucyfyed, yet liueth he thorowe the power of GOD. And we no doubte are weake in hym: but we shall lyue with hym by the myght of God among you.
2 Corinthians 13:5 Proue youre selues whether you be in the fayth or not. Examen your owne selues: know ye not your owne selues, howe that Iesha Christe is in you, except ye be casteawayes?
2 Corinthians 13:6 I truste that ye shall knowe that we be not cast awayes.
2 Corinthians 13:7 I desyre before God that ye do none euyll, not that we shoulde seme commendale, but that ye shoulde do that which is honest: and let vs be counted as leude persons.
2 Corinthians 13:8 We can do nothynge agaynste the truth. But for the trueth,
2 Corinthians 13:9 we are glad when we are weake, & ye strong. Thys also we wyshe for, euen that ye were perfecte.
2 Corinthians 13:10 Therfore wryte I these thinges beynge absente, leste when I am presente I shoulde vse sharpenesse accordynge to the power whiche the Lorde hath geuen me, to edifye, and not to destroye.
2 Corinthians 13:11 Finally brethren fare ye well, be perfeccte, be of good comforte, be of one mynde, lyue in peace, and the God of loue, and peace, shal be with you.
2 Corinthians 13:12 Grete one another in an holy kysse.
2 Corinthians 13:13 All the saynctes salute you.
2 Corinthians 13:14 The grace of oure Lorde Iesus Christ, and the loue of God, and the feloweshyppe of the holye ghoste be with you all. Amen.

BOOK: Galatians

CHAPTER: 1

Galatians 1:1 Paul an Apostle, not of men, neyther by man, but by Iesus christ and by God the father, which raysed hym from death:
Galatians 1:2 and all the brethren whiche are with me. Vnto the congregacyons of Galacia.
Galatians 1:3 Grace be with you and peace from God the father, and from our Lorde Iesus Christ,
Galatians 1:4 whiche gaue hym selfe for oure synnes, to delyuer vs from thys present euyll worlde, thorow the wyll of God our father,
Galatians 1:5 to whom be prayse for euer and euer. Amen.
Galatians 1:6 I maruayle that ye are so sone turned from hym that called you in the grace of Christ, vnto an other Gospell:
Galatians 1:7 whiche is nothynge els, but that there be some which trouble you, and entende to peruert the Gospell of Christe.
Galatians 1:8 Neuerthelesse thoughe we oure selues, or an Angell from heauen, preache any other Gospell vnto you then that whiche we haue preached vnto you, holde hym as accurssed.
Galatians 1:9 As I haue sayed before, so saye I nowe agayne, yf anye man preache any other thynge vnto you, then that you haue receyued, holde hym accursed.
