Galatians 1:10 Preache I mans doctryne or Goddes? Eyther go I aboute to please men? Yf I studyed to please men, I were not the seruauat of Christe.
Galatians 1:11 I certifye you brethren, that the Gospell which was preached of me, was, not after the maner of men,
Galatians 1:12 neyther receyued I it of man, neyther was I taughte it, but receyued it by the reuelacyon of Iesus Christ.
Galatians 1:13 For ye haue hearde of my conuersacyon in tyme paste, in the Iewes wayes, howe that beyonde measure I persecuted the congregacyon of God, & spoyled it,
Galatians 1:14 and preuayled in the Iewes lawe, aboue many of my companyons, which were of myne own nacyon, & was a much more feruent mayntayner of the tradicions of the elders.
Galatians 1:15 But when it pleased God (whiche separated me from my mothers wombe, and called me by hys grace,
Galatians 1:16 for to declare hys sonne by me) that I shoulde preache hym amonge the heathen immediatly I communed not of the matter with fleshe and bloude,
Galatians 1:17 neyther returned to Hierusalem to them whiche were Apostles before me, but went my wayes into Arabia, and came agayne to Damasco.
Galatians 1:18 Then after .iij. yere I returned to Ierusalem to se Peter and abode with hym .xv. dayes,
Galatians 1:19 no nother of the Apostles sawe I, saue Iames the Lordes brother.
Galatians 1:20 The thynges which I wryte beholde God knoweth I lye not.
Galatians 1:21 After that I went into the costes of Syria, and Cilicia,
Galatians 1:22 and was knowen as touchynge my person vnto the congregacyons of Iewry, whiche were in Christe,
Galatians 1:23 But they hearde onlye that he which persecuted vs in tyme past nowe preacheth the fayth which before he destroyed.
Galatians 1:24 And they gloryfyed God on my be halfe.

CHAPTER: 2

Galatians 2:1 Then .xiiij. yeares after that, I went vp agayne to Hierusalem with Barnabas, and toke with me Titus also.
Galatians 2:2 Yea and I wente vp by reuelacion, and communed with them of the Gospell which I preache amonge the gentyls: but a part with them which were counted chiefe, lest it shoulde haue bene thought, that I should runne or had runne in vayne.
Galatians 2:3 Also Tytus which was wt me, though he were a Greke, yet was not compelled to be circumcysed,
Galatians 2:4 and that because of incommers beynge false brethren which came in amonge other to spye out our lybertye which we haue in Christe Iesus, that they myghte brynge vs into bondage.
Galatians 2:5 To whom we gaue no roume, no not for the space of an houre, as concernynge to be brought into subieccion, & that because that the truth of the Gospel might contynue with you.
Galatians 2:6 Of them whiche seme to be great (what they were in time passed, it maketh no matter to me: God loketh on no mans person) neuerthelesse they which seme great, added nothing to me.
Galatians 2:7 But contrary wyse, when they sawe that the Gospel ouer that vncircumcysyon was committed vnto me, as the gospell ouer the circumcisyon was vnto Peter:
Galatians 2:8 for he that was mighty in Peter in the Apostleshyppe ouer the circumcisyon the same was myghty in me amonge the Gentyls,
Galatians 2:9 and therfore when they perceyued the grace that was geuen vnto me, then Iames, Cephas, and Iohn, whiche semed to be pyllars, gaue to me & Barnabas the ryght handes, & agreed with vs, that we should preach amonge the Heathen, and they amonge the Iewes,
Galatians 2:10 warnyng onely, that we should remembre the pore. Whiche thyng also I was dylygently to do.
Galatians 2:11 And when Peter was come to Antioche, I withstode hym in the face, for he was worthy to be blamed.
Galatians 2:12 For yer that certayne came from Iames, he eate with the Gentyls. But when they were come, he withdrue and separated hym selfe, fearyng them which were of the circumcysyon.
Galatians 2:13 And the other Iewes dissembled lykewyse, in so muche that Barnabas was brought into theyr simulacyon also.
Galatians 2:14 But when I sawe, that they went not the ryghte waye after the truth of the Gospell, I sayde vnto Peter before all men, yf thou beynge a Iew, lyuest after the maner of the Gentyls, and not as do the Iewes: why causeste thou the Gentyls to lyue as do the Iewes?
Galatians 2:15 We whiche are Iewes by nature, and not sinners of the Gentyls,
Galatians 2:16 knowe that a man is not iustifyed by the dedes of the lawe, but by the fayth of Iesus Christe. And therfore we haue beleued on Iesus Christe that we myghte be iustifyed by the fayth of Christe, and not by the dedes of the lawe, because that by the dedes of the lawe no fleshe can be iustifyed.
Galatians 2:17 Yf then whyle we seke to be made ryghtuousnes by Christe, we our selues are founde synners, is not then Christe the mynister of synne? God forbyd,
Galatians 2:18 For yf I buylde agayne that whiche I destroyed, then make I myself a treaspaser.
Galatians 2:19 But I thorowe the lawe, am dead to the law: that I myght lyue vnto God
Galatians 2:20 I am crucyfyed with Christ. I lyue verelye: yet now not I, but Christe lyueth in me. For the lyfe which I now lyue in the, flesh I lyue by the faythe of the sonne of God whiche loued me, and gaue hym selfe for me.
Galatians 2:21 I despyse not the grace of God. For yf ryghteousnes come of the lawe, then Christ dyed in vayne

CHAPTER: 3

Galatians 3:1 O folyshe Galathyans: who hath wytched you, that ye should not beleue the truthe? To whom Iesus Christ was descrybed before the eyes, and among you crucyfyed.
Galatians 3:2 Thys onelye woulde I learne of you, receyued ye the spyryte by the dedes of the law, or els by preachynge of the faith?
Galatians 3:3 Are ye so vnwyse that after ye haue begonne in the spyryte, ye woulde nowe ende in the fleshe?
Galatians 3:4 So many thinges then ye haue suffered in vaine, yf that be vayne.
Galatians 3:5 Which mynistred to you the spyryte, and worketh myracles among you, doth he it thorowe the dedes of that lawe or by preachynge of the fayth?
Galatians 3:6 Euer as Abraham beleued God, and it was ascrybed to hym for ryghtuousnes.
Galatians 3:7 Vnderstande therfore, that they whiche are of fayth, the same are the chyldren of Abraham.
Galatians 3:8 For the scripture sawe afore hand, that God woulde iustifye the heathen thorow fayth, & therfore shewed before hand glad tydynges vnto Abraham. In the shall all nacyons be blessed.
Galatians 3:9 So then they whiche be of faythe are blessed with faythful Abraham.
Galatians 3:10 For as many as are vnder the dedes of the lawe, are vnder malediccyon. For it is wrytten: cursed is euery man that contynueth not in all thynges, whiche are wrytten in the boke of the law, to fulfyll them.
Galatians 3:11 That no man is iustifyed by the lawe in the syght of God, is euydente. For the iuste shall lyue by fayth.
Galatians 3:12 The lawe is not of fayth: but the man that fulfylleth the thinges contayned in the lawe, shall lyue in them.
Galatians 3:13 But Christ hath delyuered vs from the curse of the lawe, and was made accursed for vs. For it is wrytten: cursed is euery one that hangeth on tre,
Galatians 3:14 that the blessyng of Abraham myghte come on the Gentyles thorowe Iesus Christ and that we myght receyue the promes of the spyryte thorow fayth.
Galatians 3:15 Brethren I wyll speake after the maner of men. Thoughe it be but a mans testamente, yet no man despyseth it, or addeth any thyng there to when it is once alowed.
Galatians 3:16 To Abraham and hys seede were the promyses made. He sayth not in the sedes as in manye: but in thy sede as in one, whiche is Christe.
Galatians 3:17 Thys I saye, that the lawe which beganne afterward beyonde: .iiij.C. and .xxx. yeares doth not disanull the testament, that was confyrmed afore of God vnto Christe warde, to make the promes of none effecte.
Galatians 3:18 For yf the inherytaunce come of the lawe, it commeth not of promes. But God gaue it vnto Abraham by promes
Galatians 3:19 Wherfore then serueth the lawe? The law was added because of transgressyon (tyll the sede came to whiche the promes was made) & it was ordeyned by angels in the hande of a mediator,
Galatians 3:20 he is not a mediator of one. But God is one.
Galatians 3:21 Is the lawe then agaynst the promes of God? God forbyd. Howbeit yf there had bene a lawe geuen whiche could haue geuen lyfe: then no doubt ryghteousnes should haue come by the lawe.
Galatians 3:22 But the scrypture concluded all thynges vnder synne that the promes by the fayth of Iesus Christe shoulde be geuen vnto them that beleue.
Galatians 3:23 Before that fayth came, we were kept and shut vp vnder the lawe, to the fayth which shuld afterward be declared.
Galatians 3:24 Wherfore the lawe was our scholemaster to the tyme of Christ, that we might be made ryghtuouse by fayth.
Galatians 3:25 But after that fayth is come, nowe are we no lenger vnder a scholemayster.
Galatians 3:26 For ye are al the sonnes of God, by the fayth whiche is in Christe Iesus.
Galatians 3:27 For al ye that are baptysed, haue put on Christ.
Galatians 3:28 Nowe is there no Iewe neyther gentyle, ther is neyther bonde nor free: there is neyther man nor woman, but ye are all one thyng in christ Iesu.
Galatians 3:29 Yf ye be Christes, then are ye Abrahams seede and heyres by promes.

CHAPTER: 4

Galatians 4:1 And I say that the heyre as longe as he is a chylde, differeth not from a seruaunt thoughe he be Lorde of all,
Galatians 4:2 but is vnder tutours and gouernours, vntyll the tyme appoynted of the father.
Galatians 4:3 Euen so we as longe as we were chyldren, were in bondage vnder the ordinaunces of the world.
Galatians 4:4 But when the tyme was full come, God sente hys sonne made of a woman, and made bonde vnto the lawe,
Galatians 4:5 to redeme them which were vnder the lawe: that we thorowe eleccyon myght receyue the enheritaunce that belongeth vnto the naturall sonnes.
Galatians 4:6 Because ye are sonnes, God hath sent the spyryte of hys sonne into our hertes, whiche cryeth Abba father.
Galatians 4:7 Wherfore now thou art not a seruaunt but a sonne. Yf thou be the sonne, thou arte also the heyre of God thorowe Christe.
Galatians 4:8 Notwithstandynge when ye knewe not God ye dyd seruyce vnto them, which by nature were no Goddes.
Galatians 4:9 But nowe seynge, ye knowe God (yea rather are knowen of God) how is it that ye turne agayne to the weake & beggerly ceremonies, wherevnto agayne ye desyre a freshe to be in bondage?
Galatians 4:10 Ye obserue dayes, and monethes, and tymes, and yeares.
Galatians 4:11 I am in feare of you lest I haue bestowed on you laboure in vayne.
Galatians 4:12 Brethren I beseche you, be ye as I am, for I am as ye are. Ye haue not hurte me at all.
Galatians 4:13 Ye knowe howe thorowe infyrmytye of the fleshe, I preached the Gospell vnto you at the fyrste.
Galatians 4:14 And my temptacion whiche I suffered by reason of my flesh, ye dispysed not, neyther abhorred, but receyued me as an Angell of God: yea as Christe Iesu.
Galatians 4:15 How happye were ye then? for I beare you recorde that yf it had bene possyble, ye woulde haue plucked oute youre owne eyes, and haue geuen them to me.
Galatians 4:16 Am I therfore become your enemye, because I tell you the truth?
Galatians 4:17 They are gelous ouer you amysse. Yea, they intende to exclude you, that ye should be feruent to them ward.
Galatians 4:18 It is good alwayes to be feruent, so it be in a good thinge, and not onelye when I am presente with you.
Galatians 4:19 My lytle chyldren (of whome I trauayle in byrth agayne vntyll Christe be fashyoned in you)
Galatians 4:20 I woulde I were with you now, and coulde chaunge my voyce, for I stande in a doubte of you.
Galatians 4:21 Tell me ye that desyre to be vnder the law haue ye not heard of the law?
Galatians 4:22 For it is writen, that Abraham had two sonnes, the one by a bonde mayd the other by a fre woman.
Galatians 4:23 Yea and he whiche was of the bond woman, was borne after the fleshe: but he whiche was of the fre woman, was borne by promes.
Galatians 4:24 Whiche thynges betoken misterye. For these women are two testamentes the one from the mounte Syna, whiche gendreth to bondage whiche is Agar.
Galatians 4:25 For mounte Syna is called Agar in Arabia, and bordreth vpon the citie, which is nowe Hierusalem, and is in bondage with her chyldren.
Galatians 4:26 But Hierusalem, whiche is aboue, is fre, whiche is the mother of vs all.
Galatians 4:27 For it is written: Reioyce thou baren, that bearest no chyldren: breake forth and crye, thou that trauaylest not. For the desolate hath many more children then she whiche hath an husband.
Galatians 4:28 Brethren we are after the maner of Isaac children of promes.
Galatians 4:29 But as then he that was borne carnally, persecuted him that was borne spirytuallye. Euen so is it nowe.
Galatians 4:30 Neuerthelesse what sayth the scripture: put awaye the bond woman and her sonne. For the sonne of the bond woman shall not be heyre with the sonne of the fre woman.
Galatians 4:31 So then brethren we are not chyldren of the bonde woman, but of the fre woman.

CHAPTER: 5

Galatians 5:1 Stande fast therfore in the lybertye wherewith Christ hath made vs free and wrappe not your selues againe in the yoke of bondage.
Galatians 5:2 Beholde I Paule saye vnto you, that yf ye be circumcysed Christe shall profyte you nothynge at all.
Galatians 5:3 I testifye agayne to euery man whiche is circumcysed that he is bounde to kepe the whole lawe.
Galatians 5:4 Ye are gone quyte from Christe as manye as are iustifyed by the law, and are fallen from grace.
Galatians 5:5 We loke for, and hope in the spiryte, to be iustifyed thorow fayth.
Galatians 5:6 For in Iesu Christ nether is circumcysion any thing worth, neyther yet vncircumcysyon, but fayth which by loue is myghtye in operacyon.
Galatians 5:7 Ye dyd runne wel: who was a let to you, that ye shoulde not obeye the trueth?
Galatians 5:8 Euen that counsell that is not of hym that called you.
Galatians 5:9 A lytell leuen doeth leuen the whole lumpe of dowe.
Galatians 5:10 I haue trust towarde you in the Lorde, that ye wyll be none otherwyse mynded. He that troubleth you, shall beare hys iudgemente, whatsoeuer he be.
Galatians 5:11 Brethren, yf I yet preache circumcysyon: why do I yet suffer persecutyon? For then had the offence whiche the crosse geueth, ceased.
Galatians 5:12 I woulde to God they were separated from you, whiche trouble you.
Galatians 5:13 Brethren ye were called into lybertye onelye let not youre lybertye be an occasyon vnto the fleshe, but in loue serue one another.
Galatians 5:14 For all the lawe is fulfylled in one worde: whiche is thys: thou shalte loue thyne neyghboure as thy selfe.
Galatians 5:15 Yf ye byte and deuour one another: take hede leaste ye be consumed one of another.
Galatians 5:16 I saye: walke in the spyryte, and fulfyl not the lustes of the fleshe.
Galatians 5:17 For the flesh lusteth contrarye to the spirite, and the spirite contrarye to the fleshe. These are contrarye one to the other, so that ye cannot do that which ye would.
Galatians 5:18 But and yf ye be led of the spyryte, then are ye not vnder the lawe.
Galatians 5:19 The dedes of the flesh are manyfeste, which are these aduoutrye, fornicacyon, vncleannes, wantonnes,
Galatians 5:20 Idolatrye wytchecrafte, hatred, varyaunce, zele, wrathe stryfe, sedityon, sectes,
Galatians 5:21 enuiynge, murther, drounkennes, glottonye, and suche lyke: of the whiche I tell you before, as I haue tolde you in tymes past, that they whiche commytte suche thynges shall not enheryte the kingdome of God.
Galatians 5:22 But the frute of the spiryte, is loue, ioye peace, longe sufferynge, gentylnes, goodnes, faithfulnes,
Galatians 5:23 mekenes, temperauncye. Against suche there is no lawe.
Galatians 5:24 They that are Christes haue crucyfyed the fleshe with the appetytes and lustes.
Galatians 5:25 If we lyue in the spyryte: let vs walke in the spyryte.
Galatians 5:26 Let vs not be vayne gloryouse, prouokynge one another, and enuyinge one another.

CHAPTER: 6

Galatians 6:1 Brethren, yf any man be fallen by chaunce into any faute: ye which are spyrytuall helpe to amende hym, in the spyryte of mekenes, consyderynge thy selfe leste thou also be tempted.
Galatians 6:2 Beare ye one anothers burthen, and so fulfyl the lawe of christ.
Galatians 6:3 Yf anye man seme to hym selfe, that he is somwhat, when in dede he is nothynge the same deceyueth hym selfe in hys ymaginacyon.
Galatians 6:4 Let euerye man proue hys owne worke, and then shall he haue reioysynge in hys owne selfe, & not in another.
Galatians 6:5 For euery man shal beare his owne burthen.
Galatians 6:6 Let hym that is taughte in the worde, mynyster vnto him that teacheth hym, in al good thynges.
Galatians 6:7 Be not deceyued, God is not mocked. For what soeuer a man soweth, that shal he reape.
Galatians 6:8 He that soweth in hys fleshe: shall of the fleshe reape corrupcion. But he that soweth in the spyryte, shall of the spyryte reape lyfe euerlastynge.
Galatians 6:9 Let vs not be werye, of wel doynge. For when the tyme is come, we shall reape withoute werynes.
Galatians 6:10 Whyle we haue therfore tyme, let vs do good vnto all men, and specially vnto them which are of the houshold of faythe.
Galatians 6:11 Beholde how large a letter I haue writen vnto you with myne owne hande.
Galatians 6:12 As manye as desyre with vtwarde apperaunce to please carnallye, they coustrayne you to be circumcysed, onelye because they woulde not suffer persecucyon with the crosse of Christe.
Galatians 6:13 For they them selues which are circumcysed kepe not the lawe: but desyre to haue you circumcysed that they myght reioyce in your fleshe.
Galatians 6:14 God forbyd that I shoulde reioyce but in the crosse of oure Lorde Iesu Christe, wherby the worlde is crucifyed as touchyng me, and I as concernynge the worlde.
Galatians 6:15 For in Christe Iesu neyther circumcisyon auayleth any thing at all, nor vncircumcysyon but a newe creature.
Galatians 6:16 And as many as walke accordynge to thys rule peace be on them, and mercye, and vpon Israel that pertayneth to God.
Galatians 6:17 From hence forthe let no man put me to busynes. For I bare in my bodye the markes of the Lord Iesu.
Galatians 6:18 Brethren the grace of oure Lorde Iesu Christe be with youre spyryte. Amen.

BOOK: Ephesians

CHAPTER: 1

Ephesians 1:1 Paule an Apostle of Iesu Christe by the wyll of God. To the Saynctes whiche are at Ephesus, & to them whiche beleue on Iesus Christe.
Ephesians 1:2 Grace be wyth you, and peace from God oure father, and from the Lorde Iesus Christe.
Ephesians 1:3 Blessed be God the father of oure Lorde Iesus Christe, which hath blessed vs wyth all maner of spyrytuall blessynges in heauenlye thynges by Christe,
Ephesians 1:4 accordynge as he had chosen vs in hym, before the foundacyon of the worlde was layde that we shoulde be Saynctes and wythoute blame before hym thorow loue.
Ephesians 1:5 And ordeyned vs before thorowe Iesus Christe to be heyres vnto hym selfe, according to the pleasure of hys wyll,
Ephesians 1:6 to the prayse of the glory of hys grace, wherewith he hath made vs accepted in the beloued.
Ephesians 1:7 By whome we haue redemption thorowe hys bloude, euen the forgeuenes of synnes accordyng to the ryches of hys grace
Ephesians 1:8 he shedde on vs aboundauntlye in all wysdome & perseueraunce.
Ephesians 1:9 And hath opened vnto vs the misterye of hys wyll accordyng to hys pleasure and purposed the same in hym selfe
Ephesians 1:10 to haue it declared, when the tyme were full come, that all thynges, bothe the thynges whiche are in heauen, & also thynges whiche are in earth shoulde be gathered together euen in Christ:
Ephesians 1:11 that is to saye in hym in whome we are made heyres, and were thereto predestinate accordynge to the purpose of hym which worketh all thynges after the purpose of hys owne wyll,
Ephesians 1:12 that we whiche before beleued in Christ shoulde be vnto the prayse of hys glorye.
Ephesians 1:13 In whome also ye (after that ye hearde the worde of trueth. I meane the Gospel of your saluacyon, wherein ye beleued) were sealed with the holye spiryte of promes,
Ephesians 1:14 whiche is the ernest of oure inheritaunce, to redeme the purchased possessyon, and that vnto the lande of hys glorye.
Ephesians 1:15 Wherfore euen I (after that I hearde of the faythe whiche ye haue in the Lorde Iesu, and loue vnto all the saynctes)
Ephesians 1:16 cease not to geue thankes for you: makyng mencyon of you in my prayers,
Ephesians 1:17 that the God of oure Lord Iesus Christ, and the father of glorye myghte geue vnto you the spyryte of wysdome, and open to you the knoweledge of hym selfe,
Ephesians 1:18 and lyghten the eyes of youre myndes that ye myght knowe what that hope is, where vnto he hath called you, and what the ryches of hys gloryous inheritaunce is vpon the saynctes,
Ephesians 1:19 and what is the excedynge greatnes of hys power to vs warde, whiche beleue accordynge to the workynge of that hys myghtye power,
Ephesians 1:20 whiche he wrought in Christe, when he raysed hym from the dead, and set hym on hys ryght hande in heauenly thynges,
Ephesians 1:21 aboue all rule, power, and myghte, and domynyon, and aboue all names that are named, not in thys worlde onely, but also in the worlde to come,
Ephesians 1:22 and hath put all thynges, vnder hys fete, and hath made hym aboue all thynges the heade of the congregacyon,
Ephesians 1:23 which is hys bodye, and the fulnes of hym that fylleth all in all thynges.

CHAPTER: 2

Ephesians 2:1 And you hath he quickened also that were deade in treaspas & synne,
Ephesians 2:2 in the whiche in time passed, yet walked accordynge to the course of thys worlde, & after the gouerner that ruleth in the ayer, the spyrite that nowe worketh in the chyldren of vnbelefe,
Ephesians 2:3 amonge whiche we also had our conuersation in tyme paste, in the lustes of oure fleshe, and fulfylled the wyll of the fleshe and of the mynde, and were naturallye the chyldren of wrath, euen as well as other.
Ephesians 2:4 But God whiche is ryche in mercye thorow his great loue wherewith he loued vs,
Ephesians 2:5 euen when we were dead by synne, hath quickened vs together in Christ (for by grace are ye saued)
Ephesians 2:6 and hath rayseth vs vp together, & made vs sitte together in heauenly thynges thorowe Christ Iesu,
Ephesians 2:7 for to shewe in tymes to come the excedinge riches of hys grace in kyndnes to vswarde in Christe Iesus.
Ephesians 2:8 For by grace are ye made safe thorowe fayth, and that not of youre selues. For it is the gyfte of God,
Ephesians 2:9 and commeth not of workes, leste anye man should bost him selfe.
Ephesians 2:10 For we are his worckmanshyp created in Christe Iesus to good workes, vnto the, whyche God ordeined vs before, that we should walke in them.
Ephesians 2:11 Wherfore remember that ye, beynge in tyme passed Gentyles in fleshe, and were called vncircumcision to them whiche are called circumcision in the fleshe, whiche circumcision is made by handes:
Ephesians 2:12 Remember I saye, that ye were at that tyme without Christe, and were reputed aliantes from the commen welth of Israel, and were straungers from the testamentes of promes, and had no hope and were wythout God in thys worlde.
Ephesians 2:13 But nowe in Christ Iesu, ye whych a whyle ago were farre of are made nygh by the bloud of Christe.
Ephesians 2:14 For he is our peace, whiche had made of both one, and hath broken doune the wall that was a stop betwene vs,
Ephesians 2:15 and hath also put awaye thorowe hys fleshe the cause of hatred (that is to saye, the lawe of commaundementes contayned in the lawe written) for to make of twayne one newe man in hym selfe, so makinge peace:
Ephesians 2:16 and to reconcile both vnto God in one body thorowe his crosse, and slew hatered therby:
Ephesians 2:17 and came and preached peace to you, whiche were a farre of, and to them that were nygh.
Ephesians 2:18 For thorowe hym we both haue an open waye in, in one spyrite vnto the father.
Ephesians 2:19 Nowe therfore ye are no more straungers and foreners, but citizyns with the sainctes, and of the houshold of God:
Ephesians 2:20 and are buylt vpon the foundation of the Apostles & Prophetes, Iesus Christe beynge the head corner stone,
Ephesians 2:21 in whom euerye buyldinge coupled together, groweth vnto an holye temple in the Lorde,
Ephesians 2:22 in whom ye also are buylde together, and made an habitacion for god in the spyryte.

CHAPTER: 3

Ephesians 3:1 For this cause I Paule am in the bondes of Iesu Christ for your sakes, whiche are heathen.
Ephesians 3:2 Yf ye haue hearde of the ministration of the grace of God, whiche is geuen me to youward.
Ephesians 3:3 For by reuelation shewed he this misterie to me as I wrote aboue in fewe wordes,
Ephesians 3:4 wherby when ye reade, ye maye knowe myne vnderstandinge in the misterye of Christe.
Ephesians 3:5 Which mysterye in tymes passed was not opened to the sonnes of men, as it is now declared vnto his holye Apostles and Prophetes by the spyrite
Ephesians 3:6 that the Gentyles shoulde be inheritours also, and of the same bodye, and partakers of hys promes that is in Christe, by the meanes of the Gospell,
Ephesians 3:7 wherof I am made a mynyster, by the gyfte of the grace of God geuen vnto me thorowe the workynge of hys power.
Ephesians 3:8 Vnto me the leaste of all sainctes is this grace geuen, that I shoulde preache amonge the Gentyls the vnsearcheable ryches of Christe,
Ephesians 3:9 and to make all men se what the fellowshyp of the mysterye is, whiche from the beginninge of the worlde hath bene hyde in God, whiche made all thinges thorowe Iesus Christ,
Ephesians 3:10 to the entente, that nowe vnto the rulers & powers in heauen myght be knowen (by the congregation) the manifolde wysedome of God,
Ephesians 3:11 accordinge to the eternal purpose, whiche he purposed in Christe Iesu our Lorde,
Ephesians 3:12 by whom we are bold to drawe nighe in that truste, whyche we haue by fayth on on him.
Ephesians 3:13 Wherfore I desyre that ye faynte not because of my tribulations for your sakes, whiche is your prayse.
Ephesians 3:14 For this cause I bowe my knees vnto the father of oure Lorde Iesus Christ,
Ephesians 3:15 whiche is father ouer all that is called father, in heauen and in earth,
Ephesians 3:16 that he woulde graunt you accordinge to the ryches of his glorie, that ye maye be strengthed wyth mighte by his spirite in the inner man,
Ephesians 3:17 that Christ may dwell in your hertes by fayth, that ye beinge roted and grounded in loue,
Ephesians 3:18 might be able to comprehende wyth all sainctes, what is the bread and length, deapt and height:
Ephesians 3:19 and to knowe, what is the loue of Christe, whyche loue passeth knowledge, that ye myghte be fulfylled wyth all maner of fulnes, whiche cometh of God.
Ephesians 3:20 Vnto hym that is able to do excedinge aboundantly aboue all that we are or thinke, accordinge to the power that worketh in vs,
Ephesians 3:21 be prayse in the congregation by Iesus Christe, thorowout al generacions, from time to time. Amen.

CHAPTER: 4

Ephesians 4:1 I therfore whiche am in boundes for the Lordes sake, exhorte you, that ye walke worthy of the vocation wherwyth ye are called,
Ephesians 4:2 in all humblenes of mynde, and mekenes, and longe sufferynge, forbearinge one another thorowe loue,
Ephesians 4:3 and that ye be diligente to kepe the vnitie of the spirite in the bounde of peace,
Ephesians 4:4 beynge one bodye, & one spirite, euen as ye are called in one hope of your callinge.
Ephesians 4:5 Let there be but one Lorde, one fayth, one baptysme,
Ephesians 4:6 one God and father of all, whiche is aboue al thorowe all and in you all.
Ephesians 4:7 Vnto euery one of vs is geuen grace accordinge to the measure of the gyfte of Christ.
Ephesians 4:8 Wherfore he sayth: He is gone vp on hye, and had led captiuitie captiue, and hath geuen gyftes vnto men.
Ephesians 4:9 That he ascended, what meaneth it, but that he also descended fyrste into the loweste parties of the earth?
Ephesians 4:10 He that descended, is euen the same also that ascended vp euen aboue all heauens, to fulfyll al thinges.
Ephesians 4:11 And the very same made some Apostles, some Prophetes, some Euangelistes, some sheperdes, some teachers,
Ephesians 4:12 that the saynctes myghte haue all thinges necessarye to worke and ministre wythal, to the edifiynge of the bodye of Christ,
Ephesians 4:13 tyl we euerie one (in the vnitie of fayth, and knowledge of the sonne of God) growe vp into a perfecte man, after the measure of age of the fulnes of Christ.
Ephesians 4:14 That we henceforth be no more chyldren, waueringe and caryed wyth euerye wynde of doctryne, by the wylynes of men and craftynes, wherby they laye awayte for vs to deceyue vs.
Ephesians 4:15 But let vs folowe the truethe in loue, and in al thinges growe in him which is the head, that is to saye, Christe,
Ephesians 4:16 in whom all the body is coupled and knyt together in euerye ioynt, wherwyth one ministreth to another (accordynge to the operation, as euerye parte hath hys measure) and encreaseth the bodye, vnto the edifiynge of it selfe in loue.
Ephesians 4:17 Thys I saye therfore and testifye in the Lorde, that ye henceforth walke not as other Gentyles walke, in vanitie of theyr mynde,
Ephesians 4:18 blynded in theyr vnderstandynge, beynge straungers from the lyfe whiche is in God thorowe the ignoraunce that is in them, because of the blyndnes of theyr hertes:
Ephesians 4:19 whiche beyng paste repentaunce, haue geuen them selues vnto wantonnes, to worke al maner of vncleanes, euen wyth gredines.
Ephesians 4:20 But ye haue not so learned Christ,
Ephesians 4:21 yf so be ye haue heard of hym, and are taughte of hym, euen as the trueth is in Iesu.
Ephesians 4:22 So then as concernyng the conuersacyon in tyme past, laye from you that olde man, whyche is corrupte thorowe the deceyueable lustes
Ephesians 4:23 and be ye renued in the spyrite of your mindes,
Ephesians 4:24 and put on that newe man, whyche after the Image of God is shapen in ryghteousnes & true holynes.
Ephesians 4:25 Wherfore put awaye lyinge, and speake euerye man trueth vnto hys neyghboure, for as muche as we are membres one of another.
Ephesians 4:26 Be angrye, but synne not, let not the sunne go doune vpon your wrath,
Ephesians 4:27 neyther geue place vnto the backebyter.
Ephesians 4:28 Let hym that stole, steale no more, but let hym rather laboure wyth his handes some good thynge, that he maye haue to geue vnto hym that nedeth.
Ephesians 4:29 Let no fylthy communication procede out of your mouthes: but that whiche is good to edefye wyth all, when nede is: that it maye haue fauoure with the hearers.
Ephesians 4:30 And greue not the holye spirite of God, by whom ye are sealed vnto the daye of redemption.
Ephesians 4:31 Let all bitternes, fearsnes and wrath, roring and cursed speakinge, be put awaye from you, wyth all maliciousnes.
Ephesians 4:32 Be ye courteouse one to another and mercyfull, forgeuynge one another, euen as God for Christes sake forgaue you.

CHAPTER: 5

Ephesians 5:1 Be ye folowers of God as deare children,
Ephesians 5:2 and walke in loue euen as Christe loued vs, and gaue hym selfe for vs, an offeringe, and a sacrifice of a swete sauoure to God.
Ephesians 5:3 So that fornicacion and vncleanes, or couetousnes be not ones named amonge you, as it becommeth sainctes:
Ephesians 5:4 neyther fylthynes, neyther folyshe talkinge, neither gestinge whiche are not comely: but rather geuinge of thankes.
Ephesians 5:5 For this ye knowe, that no whormonger, other vncleane persone, or couetous person, whyche is the worshypper of Images, hath anye inheritaunce in the kyngdome of Christe and of God.
Ephesians 5:6 Let no man deceiue you with vayne wordes. For thorowe suche thinges commeth the wrath of God vpon the children of vnbelefe.
Ephesians 5:7 Be not therfore companions wyth them.
Ephesians 5:8 Ye were ones darckenes, but are nowe lyghte in the Lorde. Walke as chyldren of lyghte.
Ephesians 5:9 For the fruite of the spirite is in all goodnes, ryghtuousnes and trueth.
Ephesians 5:10 Accepte that whiche is pleasinge to the Lorde:
Ephesians 5:11 and haue no fellowshyp wyth the vnfruitfull workes of darckenes: but rather rebuke them.
Ephesians 5:12 For it is shame euen to name those thinges, whiche are done of them in secrete:
Ephesians 5:13 but all thinges, when they are rebuked of the lyghte are manifeste. For what soeuer is manifeste, that same is lyght.
Ephesians 5:14 Wherfore he sayth: awake thou that slepest, and stand vp from death, and Christ shall geue the lyght.
Ephesians 5:15 Take hede therfore that ye walke circumspectlye: not as foles, but as wyse
Ephesians 5:16 redeminge the time, for the dayes are iuel.
Ephesians 5:17 Wherfore be ye not vnwise, but vnderstande what the wyll of the Lorde is,
Ephesians 5:18 and be not drounke wt wyne. wherin is excesse, but be fulfylled wyth the spirite,
Ephesians 5:19 speakinge vnto your selues in Psalmes, and Hymnes, and spiritual sounges, singing and makinge melodye to the Lorde in your hertes,
Ephesians 5:20 geuinge thankes alwayes for al thinges vnto God the father, in the name of oure Lorde Iesu Christe,
Ephesians 5:21 submittinge your selues one to another in the feare of God.
Ephesians 5:22 Women submitte youre selues vnto your owne husbandes, as vnto the Lorde.
Ephesians 5:23 For the husbande is the wyues head, euen as Christe is the heade of the congregation, and the same is the sauiour of the body.
Ephesians 5:24 Therfore as the congregation is in subieccion to Christe, lykewyse let the wyues be in subieccion to theyr husbandes in all thynges.
Ephesians 5:25 Husbandes loue youre wyues, euen as Christe loued the congregation, and gaue him selfe for it,
Ephesians 5:26 to sanctifye it, and cleansed it in the fountayne of water thorowe the worde
Ephesians 5:27 to make it vnto hym selfe a glorious congregation wythout spotte or wrinckle, or anye suche thinge: but that it shoulde be holy and wythout blame.
Ephesians 5:28 So ought men to loue theyr wyues, as their owne bodies. He that loueth hys wyfe, loueth him selfe.
Ephesians 5:29 For no man euer yet hated hys owne fleshe, but norisheth and cherisseth it euen as the Lorde doeth the congregation.
Ephesians 5:30 For we are members of his bodie, of his fleshe, and of hys bones.
Ephesians 5:31 For this cause shall a man leaue father and mother, and shall continue wyth hys wyfe, and two shalbe made one fleshe.
Ephesians 5:32 Thys is a greate secrete, but I speake betwene Christe and the congregation.
Ephesians 5:33 Neuerthelesse do ye so that euerye one of you loue his wyfe truely euen as hym selfe: And let the wyfe se that she feare her husbande.

CHAPTER: 6

Ephesians 6:1 Chyldren obeye youre fathers and mothers in the Lorde: for so is it ryght.
Ephesians 6:2 Honoure thy father and mother, that is the fyrst commaundemente that hath anye promes,
Ephesians 6:3 that thou mayeste be in good estate, and liue longe on the earth.
Ephesians 6:4 And ye fathers, moue not youre children to wrath, but bringe them vp with the norter and information of the Lorde.
Ephesians 6:5 Seruauntes be obedient vnto youre carnall maisters, wyth feare and tremblinge, in singlenes of youre hertes, as vnto Christe,
Ephesians 6:6 not wyth seruice in the eye sight, as men pleasers, but as the seruauntes of Christe, doynge the wyll of God frome the herte
Ephesians 6:7 wyth good wyll seruynge the Lorde, & not men.
Ephesians 6:8 And remembre that, whatsoeuer good thinge any man doeth, that shall he receiue agayne of the Lorde, whether he be bounde or fre.
Ephesians 6:9 And ye maisters, do euen the same thinges vnto them puttinge awaye threateninges: and remembre that euen your maister also is in heauen, neither is ther anye respect of person wyth hym.
Ephesians 6:10 Finally my brethren, be stronge in the Lord and in the power of his myghte.
Ephesians 6:11 Put on the armoure of God, that ye maye stande stedfaste agaynste the crafty assautes of the deuyll.
Ephesians 6:12 For we wrestle not againste fleshe and bloude: but against rule, agaynst power, and againste worldlye rulers of the darckenes of thys worlde, againste spyrytuall wickednes, for heauenly thynges.
Ephesians 6:13 For thys cause take vnto you the armoure of God, that ye maye be able to resiste in the euyl daye, and stande perfect in al thinges.
Ephesians 6:14 Stande therfore, and your loynes gyrde about wyth veritie, hauinge on the breste plate of rightuousnes,
Ephesians 6:15 and shoed with shoes prepared by the Gospel of peace.
Ephesians 6:16 Aboue all take to you the shelde of fayth, wherwith ye maye quench all the fyrie dartes of the wycked.
Ephesians 6:17 And take the helmet of saluacion and the swerd of the spyrite, which is the word of God.
Ephesians 6:18 And praye all wayes wyth all maner prayer and supplicacion: and that in the spirite, and watch therunto with all instaunce and supplication for all sainctes,
Ephesians 6:19 and for me, that vtteraunce maye be geuen vnto me, that I maye open my mouth bloudly, to vtter the secretes of the Gospel,
Ephesians 6:20 wherof I am a messenger in boundes that therin I may speake frely, as it becommeth me to speake.
Ephesians 6:21 But that ye maye also knowe what condicion I am in and what I do. Tichicus my deare brother and faythfull mynyster in the Lorde, shal shewe you of all thinges,
Ephesians 6:22 whom I sent vnto you for the same purpose, that ye myght knowe what case I stand in, and that he myght comforte your hertes.
Ephesians 6:23 Peace be with the brethren, and loue with fayth from God the father, and from the Lorde Iesus Christe.
Ephesians 6:24 Grace be with al them whiche loue oure Lorde Iesus Christe in purenes. Amen.

BOOK: Philippians

CHAPTER: 1

Philippians 1:1 Paule and Tymotheus the seruauntes of Iesu Christe. To all the sainctes in Christe Iesu, which are at Philippos, wyth the Bishops and Deacons.
Philippians 1:2 Grace be wyth you and peace from God oure father, and from the Lorde Iesus Christe.
Philippians 1:3 I thanke my God wyth all remembraunce of you,
Philippians 1:4 all wayes in al my prayers for you, and praye wyth gladnes,
Philippians 1:5 because of the fellowshyppe, whyche ye haue in the Gospell from the fyrste daye vnto nowe:
Philippians 1:6 and am surelye certifyed of this, that he whyche began a good worke in you, shall go forth wyth it vntyll the daye of Iesus Christe,
Philippians 1:7 as it becommeth me so to iudge of you al, because I haue you in my herte, and haue you also euerye one companions of grace wyth me, euen in my boundes as I defende and stablishe the Gospel.
Philippians 1:8 For God beareth me recorde howe greatlye I longe after you all from the very herte rote in Iesus Christe.
Philippians 1:9 And this I praye, that youre loue maye increase more and more in knowledge, and in al fealinge,
Philippians 1:10 that ye myght accepte thinges moste excellent, that ye might be pure and such as should hurte no mannes conscience, vntyll the daye of Christe,
Philippians 1:11 fylled with the fruites of rightuousnes, which fruites come by Iesus Christ vnto the glory and laude of God.
Philippians 1:12 I woulde ye vnderstode brethren that my busines is happened vnto the greater furtheringe of the Gospel.
Philippians 1:13 So that my boundes in Christe are manifeste thorowe out al the iudgement hal and in al other places:
Philippians 1:14 In so much that many of the brethren in the Lorde are boldened thorowe my boundes, & dare more largely speake the worde without feare.
Philippians 1:15 Some there are whiche preache Christ of enuie and stryfe, and some of good wyll.
Philippians 1:16 The one parte preacheth Christe of strife and not purelye supposinge to adde more aduersitye to my boundes.
Philippians 1:17 The other parte of loue, because they se that I am set to defende the Gospell.
Philippians 1:18 What then? So, that Christe be preached al maner wayes, whether it be by occasion, or of true meaninge, I therin ioye: ye & will ioye.
Philippians 1:19 For I knowe that this shall chaunce to my saluacion, thorowe your prayer and mynystringe of the spyryte of Iesu Christe,
Philippians 1:20 as I hertely loke for and hope that in nothinge I shalbe ashamed, but that wyth all confydence as alwayes in tymes paste, euen so nowe Christe shall be magnyfyed in my bodye, whether it be thorowe lyfe, or else death.
Philippians 1:21 For Christe is to me lyfe, and death is to me auauntage.
Philippians 1:22 Yf it chaunce me to lyue in the fleshe, that is to me frutefull for to worke, and what to chose
Philippians 1:23 I wote not. I am constrayned of two thinges: I desire to be lowsed and to be wyth Christe, whiche thinge is best of all.
Philippians 1:24 Neuerthelesse to abyde in the fleshe is more nedeful for you.
Philippians 1:25 And thys am I sure of that I shall abyde, and wyth you all continue for the furtheraunce and ioye of your faith,
Philippians 1:26 that ye may more aboundantly reioyce in Iesus Christe thorowe me, by my comminge to you again.
Philippians 1:27 Onlye let your conuersation be as it becommeth the Gospell of Christ, that whether I come and se you, or els be absent, I maye yet heare of you, that ye continue in one spyrite, and in one soule, labouring as we do, to mayntayne the fayth of the Gospell,
Philippians 1:28 and in nothing fearing your aduersaries: whiche is to them a token of perdicion, and to you of saluation, and that of God.
Philippians 1:29 For vnto you it is geuen, that not onely ye should beleue on Christ, but also suffre for his sake,
Philippians 1:30 and haue euen the same fyght, whiche ye sawe me haue and now heare of me.

CHAPTER: 2

Philippians 2:1 If there be amonge you anye consolation in Christ, yf there be anye comfortable loue, yf there be anye feloweshyp of spirite, yf there be any compassion or mercye,
Philippians 2:2 fulfyll my ioye that ye drawe one waye hauinge one loue, being of one accorde, and of one minde,
Philippians 2:3 that nothing be done thorowe stryfe or vaine glorye, but that in mekenes of mynde euerye man esteme other better then him selfe,
Philippians 2:4 & that no man considere his owne, but what is meate for other.
Philippians 2:5 Let the same mynde be in you that was in Christ Iesu:
Philippians 2:6 Whiche beinge in the shap of God, and thought it not robbery to be equal wt God.
Philippians 2:7 Neuerthelesse he made hym selfe of no reputation, & toke on him the shap of a seruaunt, and became lyke vnto men,
Philippians 2:8 and was founde in hys aparell as a man. He humbled hym selfe, and became obediente vnto the death euen the death of the crosse.
Philippians 2:9 Wherfore God hath exalted hym, and geuen hym a name aboue al names,
Philippians 2:10 that in the name of Iesus should euerye knee bowe, both of thinges in heauen and thinges in earth, and thinges vnder the earth,
Philippians 2:11 and that al tounges should confesse that Iesus Christ is the Lorde vnto the prayse of God the father.
Philippians 2:12 Wherfore my dearlye beloued, as ye haue alwayes obeyed, not when I was presente onelye, but nowe much more in myne absence euen so worke out your owne saluacion wt feare and trembling.
Philippians 2:13 For it is God, whyche worketh in you, both the wyll and also the dede, euen of good wyl.
Philippians 2:14 Do al thinge wythout murmuringe and disputynge,
Philippians 2:15 that ye maye be fauteles & pure, the sonnes of God wythout rebuke, in the middes of a croked and a peruerse nacyon, amonge whiche se that ye shine as lightes in the worlde,
Philippians 2:16 holding fast the worde of life, vnto my reioysing in the daye of Christe, that I haue not runne in vayne, neyther haue laboured in vaine.
Philippians 2:17 Yea, and though I be offered vp vpon the offeringe and sacrifyce of youre fayth: I reioyce, and reioyce wyth you al.
Philippians 2:18 For the same cause also, reioyce ye, and reioyce ye wyth me.
Philippians 2:19 I truste in the Lord Iesus for to sende Timotheus shortely vnto you, that I also maye be of good comforte, when I knowe what case ye stand in.
Philippians 2:20 For I haue noman that is so lyke mynded to me, whiche with so pure affeccion careth for youre matters.
Philippians 2:21 For al other seke theyr owne, and not that whiche is Iesus Christes.
Philippians 2:22 Ye knowe the profe of hym, howe that as a sonne with the father, so with me bestowed he his laboure vpon the Gospel
Philippians 2:23 Hym I hope to send assone as I knowe, howe it wyl go with me.
Philippians 2:24 I truste in the Lord I also my selfe shal come shortly.
Philippians 2:25 I supposed it necessarye to sende brother Epaphroditus vnto you, my companion in laboure and felow souldier, youre Apostle & my minister at my nedes.
Philippians 2:26 For he lounged after you, and was full of heauines, because that ye had hearde saye, that he shoulde be sycke.
Philippians 2:27 And no dout he was sicke, and that nye vnto death. But God had mercye on hym not on hym onely, but on me also, lest I should haue had sorowe vpon sorowe.
Philippians 2:28 I sent him therfore the diligentliar, that when ye shoulde se hym, ye might reioyce againe, and I myght be the lesse sorowfull.
Philippians 2:29 Receiue him therfore in the Lorde wyth al gladnes, and make muche of suche:
Philippians 2:30 because that for the worke of Christ he went so farre, that he was nye vnto death, and regarded not hys lyfe, to fulfyll that seruice, whiche was lackinge on your part towarde me.

CHAPTER: 3

Philippians 3:1 Moreouer my brethren, reioyce in the Lorde. It greueth me not to write one thinge often to you. For to you it is a sure thynge.
Philippians 3:2 Beware of dogges, beware of euyll workes. Beware of dyssencyon.
Philippians 3:3 For we are cyrcumcysion, whyche worship God in the spirite, and reioyce in Christe Iesu, and haue no confidence in the fleshe,
Philippians 3:4 though I haue wherof I might reioice in the fleshe. If any other man thinke that he hath wherof he mighte truste in the fleshe, much more I,
Philippians 3:5 circumcised the eighte daye, of the kynred of Israel, of the tribe of Beniamin, an Hebrue borne of the Hebrues: as concerninge the lawe, a pharisey,
Philippians 3:6 and as concerning feruentnes, I persecuted the congregation, & as touching the ryghtuousnes, whiche is in the lawe, I was vnrebukeable.
Philippians 3:7 But the thinges that were vauntage vnto me. I counted losse for Christes sake.
Philippians 3:8 Yea I thinke al thinges but losse for that excellent knowledge sake of Christ Iesu my Lord. For whom I haue counted al thinges losse, and do iudge them but dounge, that I myght wynne Christe,
Philippians 3:9 and might be founde in hym, not hauinge mine owne rightuousnes, which is of the lawe, but that whyche spryngeth of the fayth, is in CHRISTE. I meane the rightuousnes, whiche commeth of God thorowe fait
Philippians 3:10 in knowinge him and the vertue of his resurreccion, & the fellowshippe of hys passyons, that I myghte be conformable vnto his death,
Philippians 3:11 yf by anye meanes I myght atteyne vnto the resurreccyon from death.
Philippians 3:12 Not as though I had alreadie atteined to it, either were already perfecte: but I folowe yf that I maye comprehende that, wherin I am comprehended of Christ Iesu.
Philippians 3:13 Brethren I count not my selfe that I haue gotten it: but one thinge I say. I forget that, whiche is behinde, & stretche my selfe vnto that whiche is before,
Philippians 3:14 and prease vnto the marke appointed, to obteine the reward of the high callinge of God in Christe Iesu.
Philippians 3:15 Let vs therfore as many, as be perfect be thus wyse minded, & yf ye be other wise minded, I pray God open euen this vnto you.
Philippians 3:16 Neuertheles in the, whervnto we are come, let vs procede by one rule, that we may be of one accord.
Philippians 3:17 Brethren be folowers of me, and loke on them which walke euen so, as ye haue vs for an ensample.
Philippians 3:18 For many walke (of whom I haue tolde you often, and nowe tel you weping) that they are the enemies of the crosse of Christ,
Philippians 3:19 whose ende is dampnation, whose God is theyr belye, and whose glorye is to theyr shame, whiche are worldlye minded.
Philippians 3:20 But oure conuersation is in heauen, from whence we loke for a sauiour, euen the Lorde Iesus Christ,
Philippians 3:21 whiche shal chaunge oure vyle bodies, that they maie be fashioned like vnto his glorious bodie, accordinge to the working, wherby he is able to subdue all thinges vnto him selfe.

CHAPTER: 4

Philippians 4:1 Therfore my brethren dearlye beloued & lounged for my ioye & crowne, so continue in the Lord, ye beloued.
Philippians 4:2 I praye Euodias, & beseche Sintiches that they be of one accorde in the Lorde.
Philippians 4:3 Yea, and I beseche the faythfull yockefelowe, helpe the women, whiche laboured wyth me in the Gospell, and with Clemente also, and with other my labour felowes, whose names are in the boke of my lyfe.
Philippians 4:4 Reioyce in the Lorde alway, and agayne I say reioyce.
Philippians 4:5 Lette your softnes be knowen to all men. The Lorde is euen at hande.
Philippians 4:6 Be not carefull: but in all thinges shewe your petition vnto God in prayer and supplication, wyth geuinge of thankes.
Philippians 4:7 And the peace of God, whiche passeth al vnderstandynge, kepe your hertes and myndes in Chryste Iesu.
Philippians 4:8 Furthermore brethren, whatsoeuer thynges are true, whatsoeuer thinges are honest, whatsoeuer thinges are iuste, whatsoeuer thinges are pure, whatsoeuer thinges pertaine to loue, whatsoeuer thinges are of honeste report: yf there be anie vertuous thinge yf there be anye laudable thinge,
Philippians 4:9 those same haue ye in your minde, whiche ye haue both learned and receiued, hearde, and also sene in me: those thinges do, and the God of peace shall be wyth you.
Philippians 4:10 I reioyce in the Lorde greatly, that nowe at the last ye are reuiued agayne to care for me, in that wherin ye were also carefull, but ye lacked opportunitie.
Philippians 4:11 I speake not because of necessitie. For I haue learned in whatsoeuer estate I am therwyth to be content.
Philippians 4:12 I can both cast doune my selfe. I can also excede. Euery where, and in all thinges I am instructed, both to be ful, and to be houngrie, to haue plentie, and to suffre nede.
Philippians 4:13 I can do al thinges thorowe the helpe of Christe whiche strengtheth me.
Philippians 4:14 Notwithstandinge ye haue well done, that ye beare parte with me in my tribulation.
Philippians 4:15 Ye of Philippos knowe that in the beginninge of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no congregacion beare parte wyth me, as concerning, geuinge, and receiuinge, but ye onely.
Philippians 4:16 For when I was in Thessalonica, ye sente ones, and afterwarde agayne vnto my nedes:
Philippians 4:17 not that I desire gyftes, but I desire aboundaunte frute on youre part.
Philippians 4:18 I receiued al, and haue plentie. I was euen fylled after that I had receyued of Epaphroditus, that which came from you, & odour that smelleth swete, a sacrifyce accepted and pleasaunt to God.
Philippians 4:19 My God fulfill youre nedes thorowe hys gloriouse ryches in Iesus Christ.
Philippians 4:20 Vnto God and oure father be prayse for euermore. Amen.
Philippians 4:21 Salute all the sainctes in Christ Iesus. The brethren which are with me grete you.
Philippians 4:22 All the sainctes salute you, and most of all they, which are of the Emperours houshholde.
Philippians 4:23 The grace of our Lord Iesus Christe be wyth you all. Amen.

BOOK: Colossians

CHAPTER: 1

Colossians 1:1 Paule an Apostle of Iesu Christe by the wyll of God, and brother Tymotheus.
Colossians 1:2 To the sainctes, whiche are at Colossa, and brethren that beleue in Christe. Grace be wyth you and peace from God oure father, and from the Lorde IESVS Christe.
Colossians 1:3 We geue thankes to God the father of oure Lorde Iesus Christe, alwaies prayinge for you,
Colossians 1:4 sence we hearde of your fayth, which ye haue in Christ Iesu, and of the loue, which ye beare to all saynctes,
Colossians 1:5 for the hopes sakes, whiche is layde vp in store for you in heauen of whiche hope ye haue heard before by the true worde of the Gospe
Colossians 1:6 which is come vnto you, euen as it is into all the world, and is frutefull, as it is amonge you, from the fyrste daye in the, whiche ye hearde of it, and had experience in the grace of God in the trueth,
Colossians 1:7 as ye learned of Epaphra oure deare felowe seruaunte, whiche is for you a faythfull minister of Christe,
Colossians 1:8 whiche also declared vnto vs your loue, whiche ye haue in the spirite.
Colossians 1:9 For this cause we also, sence the daye we heard of it, haue not ceased prayeng for you, and desiring that ye myght be fulfilled with the knowledge of his will, in all wysdome, and spiritual vnderstandinge,
Colossians 1:10 that ye mighte walke worthy of the Lorde in all thinges, that please him beyng frutefull in all good workes, and encreasing in the knowledge of God
Colossians 1:11 strengthed wyth all myghte thorowe his glorious power, vnto al pacience & longe suffering with ioyfulnes,
Colossians 1:12 geuing thankes vnto the father, which hath made vs mete to be partakers of the inheritaunce of sainctes in lyght.
Colossians 1:13 Which hath deliuered vs from the power of darcknes and hath translated vs into the kyngdome of his deare sonne,
Colossians 1:14 in whom we haue redempcion thorowe his bloude, that is to saye: the forgeuenes of synnes,
Colossians 1:15 whyche is the ymage of the inuisible God, fyrste begotten of creatures.
Colossians 1:16 For by hym were all thynges created, thinges that are in heauen, and thinges that are in earth: thinges visible and thinges inuisible, whether they be maiestye or Lordeshyp, eyther rule or power. Al thynges are created by hym and in hym,
Colossians 1:17 and he is before all thinges, and in hym all thinges haue theyr beynge.
Colossians 1:18 And he is the head of the body, that is to wyt of the congregation: he is the beginning and fyrst begotten of the dead, that in all thinges he might haue the preeminence.
Colossians 1:19 For it pleased the father that in him shoulde all fulnes dwel,
Colossians 1:20 and by hym to reconcile all thinge vnto him selfe, and to set at peace by him thorowe the bloude of his crosse, both thinges in heauen, and thinges in earth.
Colossians 1:21 And you (which were in tymes past straungers and enemyes, because your myndes were set in euyl workes) hath he now reconciled
Colossians 1:22 in the body of his fleshe thorowe death, to make you holye vnblamable and without faut in his owne syght,
Colossians 1:23 yf ye continue grounded and stablyshed in the fayth, and be not moued away from the hope of the Gospell, where of ye haue hearde, how that it is preached amonge al creatures which are vnder heauen, wherof I Paule am made a minister.
Colossians 1:24 Nowe ioye I in my sufferinges which I suffer for you, and fulfyll that whiche is behinde of the passions of Christe in my fleshe for his bodies sake, which is the congregacion,
Colossians 1:25 wherof I am made a minister accordinge to the ordinaunce of God, whiche ordinaunce was geuen me vnto you warde, to fulfyll the worde of God,
Colossians 1:26 that mistery hyd sence the world beganne, and sence the begynnynge of generacyons: but now is opened to hys sainctes
Colossians 1:27 to whom God woulde make knowen the glorious riches of this misterye amonge the Gentyls, whiche ryches is Christ, in you the hope of glorye,
Colossians 1:28 whome we preache, warning all men and teachinge all men in all wisdom, to make all men perfect in Christ Iesu.
Colossians 1:29 Wherin I also labour and stryue euen as farforth as his workinge worketh in me mightely.

CHAPTER: 2

Colossians 2:1 I woulde ye knewe what fightinge I haue for your sakes, & for them of Laodicia, and for as many as haue not sene my person in the fleshe,
Colossians 2:2 that their hertes mighte be comforted and knit together in loue, and in all riches of full vnderstandinge for to knowe the mystery of God the father and of Christe,
Colossians 2:3 in whom are hyd al the treasures of wysdom and knowledge.
Colossians 2:4 This I saye leaste anye man shoulde begyle you with entisyng wordes.
Colossians 2:5 For though I be absent in fleshe: yet am I present with you in the spirite ioyenge and beholdinge the order that ye kepe, and your stedfast faith in Christ.
Colossians 2:6 As ye haue therfore receiued Christe Iesus the Lorde, euen so walke,
Colossians 2:7 roted and builte in him and stedfaste in the fayth as ye haue learned, and therin be plentuous in geuing thankes.
Colossians 2:8 Beware least anye man come and spoyle you thorowe philosophie and disceitful vanitie, thorowe the tradicions of men, and ordinaunces after the world, and not after Christ.
Colossians 2:9 For in him dwelleth al the fulnes of the Godhead bodely,
Colossians 2:10 and ye are complete in hym, whiche is the head of al rule and power,
Colossians 2:11 in whom also ye are circumcysed with circumcision made withoute handes, by puttinge of the synful body of the fleshe thorow the circumcision, that is in Christ,
Colossians 2:12 in that ye are buried, wt him thorow baptisme in whom ye are also risen again thorow fayth, that is wroughte by the operacion of God, which raysed hym from death.
Colossians 2:13 And ye which were dead in sinne thorow the vncircumcision of youre fleshe, hath he quyckened with him, and hath forgeuen vs al oure treaspases.
Colossians 2:14 And hath put out the hande wryttinge that was againste vs, contayned in the lawe wrytten, and that hath he taken out of the waye, and hath fastened it to his crosse,
Colossians 2:15 and hath spoiled rule and power and hath made a shewe of them openlye, and hath tryumphed ouer them in hys owne persone.
Colossians 2:16 Let no man therfore trouble youre consciences aboute meate and drincke, or for a peace of an holye daye, as the holy daye of the new mone, or of the Saboth dayes,
Colossians 2:17 whyche are nothinge, but shaddowes of thinges to come, but the bodye is in Christe.
Colossians 2:18 Let no man make you shoute at a wronge marke which after his owne ymaginacion walketh in the humblenes and holynes of aungels, thynges which he neuer sawe: causelesse puft vp with his fleshely minde,
Colossians 2:19 and holdeth not the head, wherof all the bodye by ioyntes and couples receyueth nouryshment, & is knyt together, & encreaseth wyth the increasynge that cometh of God.
Colossians 2:20 Wherfore yf ye be deade wyth Christe from the ordinaunces of the world, why as though ye yet liued in the worlde, are ye ledde wyth tradicions of them that saye?
Colossians 2:21 Touche not, tast not, handel not,
Colossians 2:22 whiche all perishe wyth the vsynge of them, and are after the commaundementes and doctrines of men,
Colossians 2:23 which thinges haue the symilitude of wysdome in chosen holines and humblenes, and in that they spare not the bodye, and do the fleshe no worship vnto his nede.

CHAPTER: 3

Colossians 3:1 If ye be then rysen agayn with Christ seke those thinges which are aboue where Christe sitteth on the right hand of God.
Colossians 3:2 Set youre affeccion on thinges that are aboue, and not on thinges, which are on the earth.
Colossians 3:3 For ye are dead and youre lyfe is hid with Christ in God.
Colossians 3:4 When Christ which is our life, shal shew him selfe then shal ye also appere wyth him in glorye.
Colossians 3:5 Mortifie therfore, youre members whiche are on the earth, fornicacion, vnclenes, vnnatural, lust euil concupiscence, and couetousnesse, which is worshippinge of Idolles,
Colossians 3:6 for which thynges sakes the wrathe of God commeth on the chyldren of vnbeliefe.
Colossians 3:7 In whyche thinges ye walked ones, when ye liued in them.
Colossians 3:8 But now put ye also awaye from you all thinges, wrath, fearnes, maliciousnes, cursed speaking fylthy speaking out of your mouthes.
Colossians 3:9 Lye not one to another, that the olde man wyth hys workes be put of,
Colossians 3:10 and the newe put on, whiche is renued in knowledge after the ymage of hym, that made hym
Colossians 3:11 where is neyther Gentile nor Iew, circumcysion nor vncircumcision, Barbarous or Sythian, bond or fre: but Christ is all in al thinges.
Colossians 3:12 Nowe therfore as electe of God, holy and beloued, put on tender mercye, kyndnes, humblenes of mindes, meaknes, longe sufferynge,
Colossians 3:13 forbearing one another, and forgeuing one another, yf anye man haue a quarel to another, euen as Christe forgaue you, euen so do ye.
Colossians 3:14 Aboue all these thynges put on loue, which is the bond of perfectnes.
Colossians 3:15 And the peace of God rule in your hertes, to the which peace ye are called in one bodye. And se that ye be thankfull.
Colossians 3:16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you plenteouslye in all wysdome. Teache and exhorte youre owne selues, in psalmes, and hymnes, and spirituall songes, whiche haue fauoure with them, singinge in your hertes to the Lorde.
Colossians 3:17 And all thinges (whatsoeuer ye do in word or dede) do it in the name of the Lorde Iesu geuinge thankes to God the father by hym.
Colossians 3:18 Wyues submitte youre selues vnto youre owne husbandes, as it is comly in the Lorde.
Colossians 3:19 Husbandes loue your wyues, and be not bitter vnto them.
Colossians 3:20 Chyldren obey your fathers & mothers in all thinges, for that is wel pleasynge vnto the Lorde.
Colossians 3:21 Fathers, rate not your children, leaste they be of a desperate mynde.
Colossians 3:22 Seruauntes, be obediente vnto your bodelye maisters in al thinges, not wyth eye seruice as men pleasers, but in synglenes of herte fearinge God.
Colossians 3:23 And what soeuer ye do, do it hertelye as though ye dyd it to the Lord, and not vnto men
Colossians 3:24 for as muche as ye know that of the Lorde ye shall receiue the reward of inheritaunce, for ye serue the Lorde Christ.
Colossians 3:25 But he that doeth anye wronge, shall receiue for the wronge that he hath done, for there is no respect of persons wyth God.

CHAPTER: 4

Colossians 4:1 Ye maisters do vnto your seruauntes, that which is iuste and equall, sayng: ye know that ye also haue a maister in heauen.
Colossians 4:2 Contynue in prayer & watch in the same wyth thankes geuynge,
Colossians 4:3 prayeng also for vs that God open vnto vs the dore of vtteraunce, that we maye speake the misterye of Christe (wherfore I am also in bondes)
Colossians 4:4 that I maye vtter it, as it becometh me to speake.
Colossians 4:5 Walke wiselye to them that are wythout and redeme the tyme.
Colossians 4:6 Let youre speache be alwayes well sauoured and poudred with salte, that ye maye knowe, howe to answere euery man.
Colossians 4:7 The deare brother Tichicus shal tell you of al my busines, whiche is a faithfull minyster, and felow seruaunt in the Lorde,
Colossians 4:8 whom I haue sent vnto you for the same purpose, that he mighte knowe howe ye do, & myght comforte your hertes,
Colossians 4:9 wyth one Onesimus, a faythfull and a beloued brother, whiche is one of you. They shall shewe you of al thinges, whiche are adoing here.
Colossians 4:10 Aristarchus my pryson felowe saluteth you and Marcus, Barnabas sisters sonne: touching whom ye receiued commaundementes. Yf he come vnto you, receiue him,
Colossians 4:11 and Iesus which is called Iustus, which are of the circumcision. These onely are my worke felowes vnto the kyngdome of God, whiche were vnto my consolacion.
Colossians 4:12 Epaphras the seruaunte of Christe, which is one of you, saluteth you, and alwaies laboureth feruentlye for you in prayers, that ye maye stande perfecte and full in all that is the wyll of God.
Colossians 4:13 I beare hym recorde, that he hath a feruent minde towarde you and towarde them of Laodicia and them of Hierapolis.
Colossians 4:14 Deare Lucas the Phisician greteth you, and Demas.
Colossians 4:15 Salute the brethren whiche are of Laodicia, and salute Nimphas, and the congregacion, which is in hys house.
Colossians 4:16 And when the Epistle is read of you, make that it be read in the congregacion of the Laodicians also and that ye lykewyse read the Epistle of Laodycya.
Colossians 4:17 And saye to Archippus: take hede to the offyce that thou hast receyued in the Lord, that thou fulfill it.
Colossians 4:18 The salutation by the hande of me Paule. Remembre my bondes. Grace be with you Amen.

BOOK: 1 Thessalonians

CHAPTER: 1

1 Thessalonians 1:1 Paule, Siluanus, and Tymotheus. Vnto the congregation of the Thessalonyans in God the father, and in the lord Iesus Christ. Grace be with you, & peace from God our father, & from the Lord Iesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians 1:2 We geue God thankes alwayes for you all, makinge mention of you in oure prayers
1 Thessalonians 1:3 wythoute ceasinge, and cal to remembraunce your worke the fayth, and laboure in loue & perseueraunce in the hope of our Lord Iesus Christ, in the syght of God oure father,
1 Thessalonians 1:4 because we know brethren beloued of God, how that ye are electe.
1 Thessalonians 1:5 For oure Gospell came not to you in worde onelye, but also in power, and in the holye Ghoste, and in muche certaintie, as ye know after what maner we behaued our selues among you, for your sakes.
1 Thessalonians 1:6 And ye became folowers of vs and of the Lord, and receyued the worde with much affliccion, with ioye of the holye ghoste:
1 Thessalonians 1:7 so that ye were an ensample to al that beleue in Macedonia and Achaia.
1 Thessalonians 1:8 For from you sounded out the worde of the Lord, not in Macedonia & in Achaia onelye: but your fayth also which ye haue vnto God, sprede her selfe abrode in all quarters, so greatlye that it neadeth not vs to speake any thynge at all.
1 Thessalonians 1:9 For they them selues shewe of you, what maner of entering in we had vnto you, and howe ye turned vnto God from Images, for to serue the liuing and true God,
1 Thessalonians 1:10 and for to loke for hys sonne from heauen, whom he raised from death. I meane Iesus which deliuered vs from wrath to come.

CHAPTER: 2

1 Thessalonians 2:1 For ye youre selues knowe brethren of oure entraunce in vnto you, how that it was not in vaine:
1 Thessalonians 2:2 but euen after that we had suffred before, and were shamefullye entreated at Philippos (as ye wel know) then were we bolde in our God to speake vnto you the Gospel of God wyth muche stryuynge.
1 Thessalonians 2:3 Oure exhortacyon was not to bringe you to erroure, nor yet to vnclennes, neyther was it wyth gile,
1 Thessalonians 2:4 but as we were allowed of God, that the Gospel shoulde be committed vnto vs, euen so we spake, not as though we entended to please men, but God whyche tryeth oure hertes.
1 Thessalonians 2:5 Neither was our conuersacyon at anye tyme wyth flatterynge wordes, as ye well knowe neyther in cloked couetousnes, god is record:
1 Thessalonians 2:6 neyther sought we prayse of men neyther of you, nor yet of anye other, when we mighte haue bene chargeable, as the Apostles of Christe,
1 Thessalonians 2:7 but we were tender amonge you, euen as a noursse cheryshed his children,
1 Thessalonians 2:8 so was our affeccion toward you, oure good wil was to haue dealte to you, not the Gospel of God onely, but also our owne soules because ye were deare to vs.
1 Thessalonians 2:9 Ye remember brethren our labour and trauayle. For we laboured day and night, because we would not be greuous vnto any of you, and preached vnto you the Gospel of God.
1 Thessalonians 2:10 Ye are wytnesses, and so is God, howe holily and iustlye and vnblameably we behaued our selues among you that beleue
1 Thessalonians 2:11 as ye know howe that we exhorted and comforted, and besoughte euerye one of you, as a father hys chyldren,
1 Thessalonians 2:12 that ye woulde walke worthye of God, whiche hath called you vnto his kingdome & glory.
1 Thessalonians 2:13 For thys cause thanke we God wythout ceasyng, because that when ye receiued of vs the word, wher with God was preached, ye receiued it not as the worde of man: but euen as it was in dede, the worde of God: whiche worketh in you that beleue.
1 Thessalonians 2:14 For ye brethren became folowers of the congregacions of God, which in Iewrye are in Christ Iesu, for ye haue suffred lyke thinges of your kinsmen, as we our selues haue suffred of the Iewes.
1 Thessalonians 2:15 Which as they kylled the Lorde Iesus and theyr owne prophetes, euen so haue they persecuted vs, and God they please not, and are contrarye to all men,
1 Thessalonians 2:16 and forbid vs to preache vnto the Gentyls, that they might be saued to fulfyll theyr synnes alwaye. For the wrathe of God is come on them, euen to the vtmost.
1 Thessalonians 2:17 For as muche brethren as we are kepte from you for a season as concernynge the bodely presence, but not in the herte we enforsed the more to se you personallye wyth greate desyre.
1 Thessalonians 2:18 And therfore we woulde haue come vnto you I Paule ones and agayne: but Sathan withstode vs.
1 Thessalonians 2:19 For what is oure hope or ioye, or crowne of reioysynge: are not ye it in the presence of our Lord Iesus Christ at hys coming?
1 Thessalonians 2:20 yes ye are our glory and ioye.

CHAPTER: 3

1 Thessalonians 3:1 Wherfore sence we could no longer forbeare, it pleased vs to remayne at Athens alone,
1 Thessalonians 3:2 & sente Timotheus our brother and minister of God, and our laboure felowe in the Gospel of Christe, to stablishe you and to comforte you ouer youre fayth,
1 Thessalonians 3:3 that no man should be moued in these afflicons. For ye your selues knowe that we are euen appointed there vnto.
1 Thessalonians 3:4 For verelye when I was wyth you, I tolde you before that we shoulde suffer tribulacion, euen as it came to passe, and as ye know.
1 Thessalonians 3:5 For this cause when I coulde no longer forbeare, I sente, that I might haue knowledge of your fayth, least haplye the tempter had tempted you, and that oure labour had bene bestowed in vayne.
1 Thessalonians 3:6 But nowe lately when Timotheus came from you vnto vs, and declared to vs youre fayth & your loue, & howe that ye haue good remembraunce of vs alwayes, desyring to se vs as we desyre to se you.
1 Thessalonians 3:7 Therfore brethren we had consolacion in you and in all our aduersyte and necessitie, thorow your fayth.
1 Thessalonians 3:8 For nowe are we alyue, yf ye stande stedfast in the Lorde.
1 Thessalonians 3:9 For what thankes can we recompence to God again for you, ouer al the ioy that we ioy for your sakes before oure God
1 Thessalonians 3:10 whyl we nighte and daye praye excedinglye that we mighte se you presently, and might fulfill that which is lackynge in youre fayth.
1 Thessalonians 3:11 God him selfe our father, and our Lord Iesus Christ guide oure iorney to you:
1 Thessalonians 3:12 and the Lorde increase you and make you flow ouer in loue one towarde another and toward all men euen as we do toward you,
1 Thessalonians 3:13 to make your hertes stable & vnblameable in holynesse before God oure father, at the comminge of our Lorde Iesus wyth al hys sainctes.

CHAPTER: 4

1 Thessalonians 4:1 Fvrther more we beseche you brethren and exhorte you in the Lord Iesus, that ye increase more and more, euen as ye haue receiued of vs, howe ye oughte to walke and to please God.
1 Thessalonians 4:2 Ye remember what commaundementes we gaue you in oure Lorde Iesu Christ.
1 Thessalonians 4:3 For this is the will of God, euen that ye shoulde be holy, and that ye shoulde abstayne from fornicacion,
1 Thessalonians 4:4 that euerye one of you should know, howe to kepe his vessell in holynes and honoure,
1 Thessalonians 4:5 and not in the luste of concupiscence, as do the heathen, which know not God,
1 Thessalonians 4:6 that no man go to far and defraude his brother in bargaining: because the Lorde is a reuenger of al suche thinges as we tolde you before tyme and testified.
1 Thessalonians 4:7 For God hath not called vs to vncleanes, but vnto holines.
1 Thessalonians 4:8 He therfore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, whiche hath sente his holye spirite amonge you.
1 Thessalonians 4:9 But as touchinge brotherly loue, ye nede not that I write vnto you. For ye are taught of God to loue one another.
1 Thessalonians 4:10 Yea and that thing verelye ye do vnto all the brethren, which are thorowout all Macedonia. We beseche you brethren, that ye encrease more and more,
1 Thessalonians 4:11 and that ye studye to be quyete, and to medle with youre owne busines, and to worke wyth youre owne handes, as we commaunded you:
1 Thessalonians 4:12 that ye may behaue your selues honestly towardes them that are wythout, and that nothinge be lackinge vnto you.
1 Thessalonians 4:13 I woulde not brethren haue you ignoraunt concerninge them whiche are fallen a sleepe, that ye sorowe not as other do which haue no hope.
1 Thessalonians 4:14 For yf we beleue that Iesus Christe dyed and rose agayne euen so them also, whyche slepe by Iesus, wyl God brynge agayn with hym.
1 Thessalonians 4:15 And thys saye we vnto you in the worde of the Lorde, that we whyche lyue and are remaynynge in the commynge of the Lorde, shal not come yerre they which slepe.
1 Thessalonians 4:16 For the Lord hym selfe shall descende from heauen with a shoute, and the voice of the Archangell and trompe of God. And the deade in Christ shall arise fyrste:
1 Thessalonians 4:17 then shal we which lyue and remayne, be caught vp with them also in the cloudes, to meate the Lorde in the ayer. And so shall we euer be with the Lord.
1 Thessalonians 4:18 Wherfore comforte youre selues one another with these wordes.

CHAPTER: 5

1 Thessalonians 5:1 Of the tymes and seasons brethren ye haue no nede, that I wryte vnto you:
1 Thessalonians 5:2 for ye youre selues knowe perfectly that the daie of the Lorde shall come euen as a thefe in the nyght.
1 Thessalonians 5:3 When they shal say peace and no daunger, then commeth on them soden destruccion, as the trauaylynge of a woman wyth chyld, and they shal not escape.
1 Thessalonians 5:4 But ye brethren are not in darckenes, that that daye shoulde come on you as it were a thefe.
1 Thessalonians 5:5 Ye are all the chyldren of lyght and the chyldren of the daye. We are not of the nyghte neither of darckenes.
1 Thessalonians 5:6 Therfore let vs not slepe as do other: but let vs watche & be sober.
1 Thessalonians 5:7 For they that slepe, slepe in the nyght: and they that be droncken, are droncken in the nyght.
1 Thessalonians 5:8 But let vs whiche are of the daye, be sober, armed wyth the breste plate of fayth and loue, and wyth hope of saluacyon as an helmet.
1 Thessalonians 5:9 For God hath not annoynted vs vnto wrath: but to obtayne saluacyon by the meanes of oure Lord Iesu Christ
1 Thessalonians 5:10 whyche dyed for vs: that whether we wake or slepe, we shoulde liue together wyth hym.
1 Thessalonians 5:11 Wherfore comforte your selues together, and edifye one another, euen as ye do.
1 Thessalonians 5:12 We beseche you brethren, that ye knowe them, whiche laboure amonge you, and haue the ouersight of you in the Lord
1 Thessalonians 5:13 and geue you exhortacyon, that ye haue them the more in loue for theyr workes sake, and be at peace wyth them.
1 Thessalonians 5:14 We desyre you brethren, warne them that are vnruly, comforte the feble minded, forbeare the weake, haue contynuall pacience towarde all men.
1 Thessalonians 5:15 Se that none recompence euyll for euyll vnto any man: but euer folowe that which is good, both among your selues, and to all men.
1 Thessalonians 5:16 Reioyse euer.
1 Thessalonians 5:17 Praye contynuallye.
1 Thessalonians 5:18 In all thinges geue thankes. For thys is the wyll of God in Christe Iesu towarde you.
1 Thessalonians 5:19 Quenche not the spyryte.
1 Thessalonians 5:20 Despyse not prophesyenge.
1 Thessalonians 5:21 Examen all thinges, and kepe that which is good.
1 Thessalonians 5:22 Absteyne from all suspicious thinges.
1 Thessalonians 5:23 The very God of peace sanctifye you thorowout. And I praye God that your whole spyryte, soule and bodye, be kept faultles vnto the comming of oure Lorde Iesus Christe.
1 Thessalonians 5:24 Faythfull is he whiche called you: which wyl also do it.
1 Thessalonians 5:25 Brethren, praye for vs.
1 Thessalonians 5:26 Grete all the brethren wyth an holy kysse.
1 Thessalonians 5:27 I charge you in the Lorde, that thys Epistle be read vnto all the holy brethren.
1 Thessalonians 5:28 The grace of the Lord Iesus Christ be wyth you. Amen.

BOOK: 2 Thessalonians

CHAPTER: 1

2 Thessalonians 1:1 Paule, Syluanus & Timotheus. Vnto the congregacyon of the Thessalonians, whiche are in God oure father, and in the Lorde Iesus Christe.
2 Thessalonians 1:2 Grace be with you and peace from God oure father, and from the Lorde Iesus Christe.
2 Thessalonians 1:3 We are bounde to thanke God alwayes for you brethren, as it mete, because that your fayth groweth excedingly, and euerye one of you swimmeth in loue towarde another betwene youre selues,
2 Thessalonians 1:4 so that we oure selues reioyse of you in the congregacions of GOD ouer youre pacience and fayth in al youre persecucyons and trybulacyons that ye suffer,
2 Thessalonians 1:5 whiche is a token of the ryghtuouse iudgement of God that ye are counted worthye of the kyngdome of God, for whiche ye also suffer.
2 Thessalonians 1:6 It is verely a ryghteous thing with God to recompence trybulacyon to them that trouble you:
2 Thessalonians 1:7 and to you whiche are troubled, reste wyth vs, when the Lorde Iesus shall shewe hym selfe from heauen wyth hys myghtye Aungels,
2 Thessalonians 1:8 in flammynge fyre, rendrynge vengeaunce vnto them that knowe not God, and to them that obeye not vnto the Gospel of our Lorde Iesus Christ,
2 Thessalonians 1:9 which shall be punyshed wyth euerlastyng dampnacyon from the presence of the Lorde, and from the glory of hys power,
2 Thessalonians 1:10 when he shall come to be gloryfyed in hys saynctes, and to be made marueylous in all them that beleue: because oure testimonye that we had vnto you, was beleued euen the same daye that we preached it.
2 Thessalonians 1:11 Wherfore we praye alwayes for you that oure God make you worthye of the callynge and fulfyll al delectacyon of goodnes and the worke of fayth, wyth power
2 Thessalonians 1:12 that the name of oure Lorde Iesus Christe maye be glorifyed in you, and ye in hym, thorowe the grace of oure God, and of the Lorde Iesus Christe:

CHAPTER: 2

2 Thessalonians 2:1 We beseche you brethren by the commynge of oure Lorde Iesu Christe, and in that we shal assemble vnto hym,
2 Thessalonians 2:2 that ye be not sodenly moued fome your mynd, and be not troubled, neyther by spirite neyther by wordes, nor yet by letter whiche shoulde seme to come from vs, as thoughe the daye of Christe were at hande.
2 Thessalonians 2:3 Let no man deceyue you by any meanes, for the Lord commeth not, except there come a departyng first, and that, that sinful man be opened, the sonne of perdicyon
2 Thessalonians 2:4 whiche is an aduersarye, and is exalted aboue all that is called God, or that is worshypped: so that he shall sytte as God in the temple of God, and shewe hym selfe as God.
2 Thessalonians 2:5 Remember ye not, that when I was yet with you, I tolde you these thynges?
2 Thessalonians 2:6 And nowe ye knowe what withholdeth: euen that he myght be vttered at his tyme.
2 Thessalonians 2:7 For the mysterye of that iniquitie doeth he al ready work whiche onelye loketh vntyll it be taken out of the waye.
2 Thessalonians 2:8 And then shall that wicked be vttered, whome the Lorde shall consume with the spirite of hys mouth, and shall destroye wt the aperaunce of hys commynge.
2 Thessalonians 2:9 euen hym whose commynge is by the workynge of Sathan, with all liynge power, signes and wonders:
2 Thessalonians 2:10 and in all deceyuablenes of vnryghtuousnes, amonge them that peryshe: because they receyued not the loue of the truethe, that they myght haue bene sayed.
